title: Dre Greenlaw, De'Zhaun Stribling, Osa Odighizuwa back at 49ers practice
summary: Things look a little better on the injury front at 49ers training camp on Thursday.
full_text: '' Things look a little better on the injury front at 49ers training camp on Thursday. Wednesday's practice ended with 20 of the players on the active roster out of action due to a variety of ailments, but a few of them were able to return to action. According to multiple reports from camp, linebacker Dre Greenlaw, defensive lineman Osa Odighizuwa, and wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling were back on the field. Greenlaw and Odighizuwa were dealing with soreness while the rookie wideout missed several days with a hamstring issue. Defensive end Sam Okuayinonu was also back. He left Wednesday's session with an ankle injury. That still leaves a long list of injured players, but those were a few steps in the right direction as the 49ers continue getting ready for the regular season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Mike McCarthy raves about Mason Rudolph
summary: Beyond Aaron Rodgers as the obvious starting quarterback for the Steelers, the rest of the depth chart has questions.
full_text: '' Beyond Aaron Rodgers as the obvious starting quarterback for the Steelers, the rest of the depth chart has questions. There's no question, apparently, in the mind of coach Mike McCarthy that veteran Mason Rudolph can be trusted with the No. 2 job. "Mason Rudolph, I can’t tell you how pleased I am with him," McCarthy told reporters on Thursday, via Chris Adamski of the Pittsburgh Tribune-Review . "He throws the ball better than I thought . . . . He's been impressive." A third-round pick of the Steelers in 2018, Rudolph has 34 career regular-season appearances and 19 starts. The bigger question for the Steelers is the number of quarterbacks they'll keep on the 53-man roster. Unless they're going to carry four (which is not unprecedented but unusual), one of the three behind Rodgers will be released — Rudolph, Will Howard, or Drew Allar. Howard and Allar would have to pass through waivers before being signed to the practice squad. They could get creative and cut Rudolph, with a wink-nod that they'll sign him to the practice squad and routinely elevate him for games. Or, as some cynics are suggesting, McCarthy is trying to create a trade market for Rudolph. Regardless, Rudolph has plenty of experience in NFL games. Howard and Allar have none. They'll need someone who can play, in the event Rodgers can't go. Rudolph is the only option who brings that to the table.
author: Mike Florio

title: 49ers sign OT Kion Smith
summary: The 49ers announced a pair of roster moves on Thursday.
full_text: The 49ers announced a pair of roster moves on Thursday. Offensive tackle Kion Smith has signed a contract with the team. Wide receiver Colton Dowell was waived to open up a spot for Smith. Smith signed with the Falcons after going undrafted in 2021 and moved on to the Dolphins later that year. He remained in Miami through the 2025 season and appeared in 23 games. Smith's only two starts came during the 2025 season. Dowell signed with the 49ers in January. He was a Titans seventh-round pick in 2023 and caught one pass for three yards in 10 games during his rookie season.
author: Josh Alper

title: With a new contract due, Puka Nacua makes agent change
summary: On the surface, Rams receiver Puka Nacua isn't clamoring aggressively for a new contract.
full_text: On the surface, Rams receiver Puka Nacua isn't clamoring aggressively for a new contract. With a new contract inevitable, Nacua has made some changes behind the scenes. Nacua has switched agents in advance of something other than the non-negotiable, slotted deal he signed as a fifth-round pick in 2023. “I did change agencies I think it was something for me, looking at the offseason and where I feel like I've been at in this past year," Nacua told reporters on Wednesday. "Trying to reset and be able to refocus and reprioritize some of the things that I feel like are best for me. I’m grateful to feel like I have a team supporting me in all facets.” Nacua will make $5.767 million in 2026. Seahawks receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, drafted the same year as Nacua, set a new bar at $42.15 million in new-money APY earlier this year. Nacua's off-field situation does indeed complicate things. The lawsuit alleging that he bit a woman on New Year's Eve could, in theory, spark a suspension — especially if he enters a diversion program in lieu of a possible prosecution. A new deal done before that would have to account for a possible suspension, since suspensions typically void any remaining guarantees. Nacua's camp would want a carve-out for that incident. The Rams, in turn, may want to pay him less in order to get it. Regardless, he's grossly underpaid for 2026. And he's risking every day the kind of injury that would delay a second contract indefinitely.
author: Mike Florio

title: Josh Jacobs out of practice with groin injury, not expected to be long-term
summary: One of Green Bay’s top offensive players is not practicing on Thursday, but he should be back on the field soon.
full_text: One of Green Bay’s top offensive players is not practicing on Thursday, but he should be back on the field soon. According to multiple reporters on the scene, Packers running back Josh Jacobs is not participating due to a groin injury. But this is not expected to be a long-term absence. Jacobs, 28, dealt with multiple injury concerns in 2025. He finished the year with 929 yards rushing with 13 touchdowns, along with 36 receptions for 282 yards with a TD. A first-round pick in the 2019 draft, Jacobs has taken 1,840 carries and tallied 2,109 total touches with 76 total touchdowns so far in his career.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Texans, Henry To’oTo’o agree to two-year extension
summary: The Texans and linebacker Henry To’oTo’o have reached a new deal.
full_text: The Texans and linebacker Henry To’oTo’o have reached a new deal. To'oTo'o has agreed to terms on a two-year, $16 million extension, his agents told Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport. The 25-year-old To'oTo'o has played with the Texans since they drafted him out of Alabama in the fifth round of the 2023 NFL draft. Last year To'oT'o played in all 17 games and was on the field for 79 percent of the Texans' defensive snaps, as well as 17 percent of special teams snaps. He also started both playoff games.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Braxton Jones, Montez Sweat left Bears practice early
summary: The Bears had players on both sides of the line of scrimmage leave practice early on Thursday.
full_text: The Bears had players on both sides of the line of scrimmage leave practice early on Thursday. Left tackle Braxton Jones and defensive end Montez Sweat both exited with members of the training staff. According to multiple reports, Jones is believed to have avoided a serious injury. There is no update on Sweat's condition or on how long either player might be off the field at training camp. Sweat opened camp on the non-football injury list, but returned after missing one practice. Defensive backs Dallis Flowers and Gervarrius Owens also made early exits from the workout. There has been no word on the severity of either player's issue.
author: Josh Alper

title: Fox will stand pat with its current NFL deal through 2029 season
summary: The NFL entered the offseason with a plan to approach its broadcast partners to discuss extensions that would entail paying more money immediately to televise games.
full_text: '' The NFL entered the offseason with a plan to approach its broadcast partners to discuss extensions that would entail paying more money immediately to televise games. At least one partner won't be doing that. Via Drew Lerner of Awful Announcing, Fox CEO Lachlan Murdoch said during a Thursday quarterly earnings call that Fox “ will not be making any amendments ” to its current arrangement with the NFL until after 2029, the last year of Fox's contract (if/when the NFL exercises an opt-out provision). The NFL can end after the 2029 season its current deals with Fox, NBC, Amazon, and YouTube. The ESPN/ABC deal can be exited early after the 2030 season. The CBS contract also runs through 2029, but the NFL could invoke a change-in-control provision and end the deal given the recent Skydance-Paramount merger. “We don’t see any changes to our contractual terms until the 2030 season,” Murdoch said. “Our relationship with the NFL is an incredibly positive one. We engage with them all the time.” He said there's “a clear path forward” with the NFL after the current deals end. It doesn't mean Fox won't negotiate with the league for 2030 and beyond. It only means that Fox won't be paying more than what it is committed to pay for the next four seasons. The NFL, reportedly miffed at the massive NBA deals signed after the NFL's latest round of contracts, had hoped to get more from the broadcast partners over the remaining years of the existing deals. That prompted an effort by Fox to push political buttons as to the broadcast antitrust exemption. After Fox mounted thinly-disguised resistance to an effort to get it to pay more from 2026 through 2029, the league found itself in need of a win-win off ramp. It could be that the league will simply act as if it never tried to get more money before the expiration of the current contracts. If the other networks follow suit and stand on the existing contracts, the stage could be set for chaos in the next wave of deals. But with all major broadcast networks currently having a full-season package — and with plenty of pressure from Congress on the league to not freeze out the FCC-regulated operations — the NFL may be less inclined to, for example, remove one or both of the Sunday afternoon packages from three-letter networks and sell them to a streamer. Our prediction? In the end, new deals will be done. The NFL will be fully compensated for its product, which is more valuable than any other property. And the eyebrow-raising numbers will allow all parties to continue to work together in a way that allows everyone to profit.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jason Licht: We love Baker Mayfield, our feelings for him haven't changed
summary: Baker Mayfield made his feelings about his contract clear when he told reporters last week that he was feeling "disrespected" and "undervalued" by the Buccaneers.
full_text: Baker Mayfield made his feelings about his contract clear when he told reporters last week that he was feeling “disrespected” and “undervalued” by the Buccaneers. But with Mayfield pledging to be focused on “all ball” going forward, General Manager Jason Licht is not concerned about the state of things between the front office and the club’s quarterback. Speaking to reporters on Thursday, Licht said the team still feels Mayfield is a franchise quarterback. “Well, I’m not going to get into the specifics about the contract and all that stuff. But yeah, we think he is,” Licht said, via Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times . “We love Baker. Our feelings for Baker haven’t changed .” Licht also seemed to be understanding of Mayfield’s comments from last week. “Baker, as we all know here, is a very fiery competitor who’s not afraid to speak his mind ,” Licht said, via Greg Auman of FOX Sports. "I'm sure he's disappointed, frustrated; we were too. We're in a good place. He's focused on having the best year of his career." Mayfield is entering the last season of a three-year, $100 million deal he signed with the Bucs in March of 2024. He was offered a two-year contract extension , which did not rise to the level of him feeling valued by the organization. Last year, Mayfield completed 63.2 percent of his passes for 3,693 yards with 26 touchdowns and 11 interceptions.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Bengals activate TE Josh Kattus
summary: The Bengals got tight end Josh Kattus back at practice on Thursday.
full_text: The Bengals got tight end Josh Kattus back at practice on Thursday. Kattus was placed on the non-football illness list before the start of training camp last month. The team announced that he has passed a physical and been activated from the list. Kattus signed with the Bengals after going undrafted in April. He had 38 catches for 505 yards and six touchdowns in 44 games over four seasons at Kentucky. Kattus started 26 of those contests. Mike Gesicki, Drew Sample, Erick All, Tanner Hudson, Cam Grandy and seventh-round pick Jack Endries are the other tight ends on the 90-man roster in Cincinnati.
author: Josh Alper

title: Titans sign LB Dominique Hampton, waive LB Shad Banks
summary: The Titans made a change to their linebacker group on Thursday.
full_text: The Titans made a change to their linebacker group on Thursday. They announced that they have signed Dominique Hampton to the active roster. Shad Banks was waived with an injury designation in a corresponding move. Hampton was a fifth-round pick by the Commanders in 2024 and he moved from safety to linebacker as a rookie. He played six special teams snaps in his only regular season appearance with the team and spent time with the Bears this offseason. Banks signed with the Titans after going undrafted out of UTSA this April. If he clears waivers, he will revert to the team's injured reserve list.
author: Josh Alper

title: Buccaneers GM Jason Licht: We have no plans to trade Vita Vea
summary: Buccaneers defensive tackle Vita Vea's agent said this week that he doesn't see Vea's contract impasse with the team "ending in anything but a trade at this point," but the team is taking a different view of things.
full_text: Buccaneers defensive tackle Vita Vea's agent said this week that he doesn't see Vea's contract impasse with the team "ending in anything but a trade at this point," but the team is taking a different view of things. Vea requested a trade ahead of training camp after spending the offseason working to land a new contract in Tampa and the team said it didn't intend to make a move at the time. On Thursday, General Manager Jason Licht reiterated at a press conference, via multiple reporters, that he has "no plans" to make a trade. Licht acknowledged that he doesn't know how things will end with the longtime Buc defender, but that they have "engaged" with Vea's representatives. Vea has not been practicing at camp, which some have called a hold-in despite head coach Todd Bowles saying Vea tweaked his back during a conditioning test. Licht said that the team does not want Vea to aggravate the issue and that there's no timetable for when Vea might start practicing this summer.
author: Josh Alper

title: Steelers sign DB Israel Mukuamu
summary: The Steelers have brought in a defender that Mike McCarthy knows well.
full_text: The Steelers have brought in a defender that Mike McCarthy knows well. Pittsburgh announced on Thursday that the club has signed defensive back Israel Mukuamu to a one-year deal. Mukuamu, 26, was a Cowboys sixth-round pick in 2021 when McCarthy was Dallas’ head coach. He appeared in 50 games with three starts for the Cowboys over his first four seasons, mainly playing special teams. He was with the Panthers in 2025, appearing in one contest for the club. As a corresponding move, the Steelers released cornerback Ahmari Harvey.
author: Myles Simmons

title: OL Greg Van Roten visits the Patriots
summary: The Patriots are taking a look at a veteran offensive lineman on Thursday.
full_text: '' The Patriots are taking a look at a veteran offensive lineman on Thursday. Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that guard Greg Van Roten is visiting the team . Van Roten spent the last two seasons with the Giants and started every game over that period. He entered the league as an undrafted free agent with the Packers in 2012 and has also played for the Panthers, Jets, Bills and Raiders. Van Roten has appeared in 148 games and made 105 starts across all of those stops. The Patriots signed Alijah Vera-Tucker as a free agent this offseason and he is expected to start at guard with Mike Onwenu.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jets first-round pick Kenyon Sadiq out a couple more weeks after core muscle surgery
summary: Jets rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq remains out of practice after core muscle surgery in May, but he's getting closer to a return.
full_text: Jets rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq remains out of practice after core muscle surgery in May, but he's getting closer to a return. Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said today that he's optimistic about Sadiq, who should be on the practice field in a couple weeks and ready to go well before Week One. "We actually got pretty good news the other day," Glenn said. "I'm just crossing my fingers, I'm going to say it's a couple weeks still, but it's not anything that's going to keep him out of the regular season." The 16th overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft, Sadiq played through the injury during his final season at Oregon last year and had the surgery in May. Glenn indicated that once he's fully healed, Sadiq won't need another surgery and the injury will be a non-issue for him going forward.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Raiders sign RB Dare Ogunbowale
summary: The Raiders have added a veteran running back.
full_text: '' The Raiders have added a veteran running back. Las Vegas announced on Thursday that the club has signed Dare Ogunbowale. Ogunbowale, 32, spent the last four seasons with Houston, mainly playing special teams. In 2025, he also ran it 11 times for 25 yards with a touchdown while catching 10 passes for 76 yards. In all, Ogunbowale has appeared in 114 games with nine starts since entering the league as an undrafted free agent in 2017 out of Wisconsin. With an open roster spot, the Raiders did not need to make a corresponding move.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Steve Belichick takes medical leave from UNC football
summary: As North Carolina coach Bill Belichick prepares for his second season at the college level, one of his top assistants (and one of his sons) is currently not with the team.
full_text: As North Carolina coach Bill Belichick prepares for his second season at the college level, one of his top assistants (and one of his sons) is currently not with the team. Via Andrea Adelson of ESPN, Belichick announced on Thursday that defensive coordinator Steve Belichick is on medical leave indefinitely . Bill Belichick shared no other details. As to whether Steve Belichick will be back for the season opener on August 29 in Ireland, Bill Belichick said only that the Tar Heels "look forward to getting him back as soon as possible." No interim defensive coordinator will be named, for now. "We coach defense collectively as a staff and we will continue to do that," Bill Belichick said. Also on leave, due to an internal investigation, is North Carolina G.M. Michael Lombardi. Steve Belichick worked for Bill with the Patriots from 2012 through 2023. In 2024, Steve served as the defensive coordinator at the University of Washington. He joined UNC when Bill took the job in 2025.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bengals plan to play starters in their preseason opener
summary: The Bengals will kick off their preseason schedule next Thursday and head coach Zac Taylor shared some of his plans for that game against the Lions at a Thursday press conference.
full_text: The Bengals will kick off their preseason schedule next Thursday and head coach Zac Taylor shared some of his plans for that game against the Lions at a Thursday press conference. Taylor was asked if he is planning to play the team's starters against Detroit and Taylor said that those players will see action. "They will play a little bit . We'll just determine how much at a later date," Taylor said. It's a similar approach to the one the Bengals took to start the 2025 preseason. After leaving starters on the bench for several years in August, the Bengals changed course by putting Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and others on the field. Burrow went 9-of-10 for 123 yards and two touchdowns, including one to Chase, before heading to the bench. The shift in approach was designed to help the team get off to a faster start in the regular season and it looked successful as the Bengals opened with a pair of wins, but an injury to Burrow helped send them to a 4-11 record the rest of the way.
author: Josh Alper

title: Sean McVay on Aaron Donald's tryout: I think he could make the team
summary: Aaron Donald did not intend to create more comeback speculation, but the defensive tackle did just that.
full_text: Aaron Donald did not intend to create more comeback speculation, but the defensive tackle did just that . Donald worked out at the Rams' training cap with Rams equipment, requiring the team to report his visit as a "tryout" on the NFL's personnel notice Wednesday. " Did it come across as a tryout ?" Rams coach Sean McVay asked NFL Network. "Best tryout we've ever had. "I think he could make the team." The third-time Defensive Player of the Year wanted to see how he felt in a helmet as he considers a return to the NFL after a two-year absence. "That was honestly our way of being able to get a workout with him within the parameters of what's necessary," McVay told NFL Network. "[Defensive line coach] Giff Smith said it's the greatest tryout he's ever had." The Rams' acquisition of two-time Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett in June prompted Donald to consider unretiring. Donald, 35, made 10 Pro Bowls in his 10 seasons and has 111 career sacks.
author: Charean Williams

title: Chris Foerster: 49ers are "very healthy," bumps and bruises come from practicing hard
summary: Chris Foerster, the San Francisco assistant who is filling in while head coach Kyle Shanahan recuperates from a car accident, says the narrative that the 49ers have been devastated with training camp injuries is incorrect.
full_text: '' Chris Foerster, the San Francisco assistant who is filling in while head coach Kyle Shanahan recuperates from a car accident, says the narrative that the 49ers have been devastated with training camp injuries is incorrect. On the same day that the 49ers ended practice without 20 players , Foerster said his team is actually very healthy, and that players who are sitting out are mostly dealing with the kinds of minor injuries that naturally arise during a tough training camp. "It seems like we're very healthy. We have injuries and bumps and bruises and guys are missing practices," Foerster said. "If you're not practicing football hard you can get through camp easily without injuries." Foerster added that the 49ers are "practicing hitting, contact-style of football" in camp. Injuries have been a major issue for the 49ers in the last two seasons, and an issue they're eager to avoid this year. Foerster says that so far, they are staying healthy, even if it doesn't always look like it on the practice field.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Michael Penix Jr.: I'm doing everything I can to help my knee get better faster
summary: To this point, the Falcons' quarterback competition has not truly begun in earnest because Michael Penix Jr. has not been fully medically cleared.
full_text: To this point, the Falcons' quarterback competition has not truly begun in earnest because Michael Penix Jr. has not been fully medically cleared. Penix, who suffered a torn ACL in November, is still recovering and told reporters in his Wednesday press conference that he feels like he’s getting better every day. While Penix’s original timetable for recovery had him being cleared in late August, he said that he could be cleared “any day.” “I'm not really chasing a timeline. I'm just chasing trying to be better every day,” Penix said, via transcript from the team. “Each and every day I get out there, I look forward to being better than I was the day before. That comes with obviously just the reps, time on task, and also just what I'm doing in the rehab and the treatment room as well, so I can get to where I want to be.” Penix noted he doesn’t yet have a scheduled date to get re-examined by his doctor to be cleared, but that’s a step he’ll need before he’s able to fully participate. That also means he won’t truly be a part of a QB competition until that time. “I mentioned it before, I can't worry about a starting job until I'm worried about getting back on the field,” Penix said. “If I can't be on the field, how am I going to be the starter? That's all my focus is right now — just trying to get back and get healthy so that whenever that time comes, then we can talk about the whole starter thing, but that's not my focus right now. “I'm just getting stronger and getting more confident in my knee and everything. My body has been feeling really good. I'm hitting all my weight goals and making sure I'm taking my diet seriously. I'm doing everything I can to help my knee get better faster. I'm definitely better than where I was last week.” But as Penix continues to make progress, Tua Tagovailoa will have the ability to put some separation between himself and Penix’s base level in the new offense under head coach Kevin Stefanski.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Jahmyr Gibbs suits up for Lions practice Thursday
summary: There's been no word of an agreement on a new contract for Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs, but there has been a change to his approach to practice at training camp.
full_text: There's been no word of an agreement on a new contract for Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs, but there has been a change to his approach to practice at training camp. Multiple reporters at Thursday's practice sent word that Gibbs was in uniform and taking reps during early drills. After the walkthrough period of practice came to an end, Gibbs moved to a side field to do individual work. It is the first time that Gibbs has been on the practice field since camp started last month. Gibbs is looking for a contract extension and that was seen as the reason why he was not participating in practices with the rest of the team. Gibbs said that was not the case in brief comments to reporters earlier this week, but declined to say why he wasn't practicing or when he might get on the field. The reason for the shift in participation is also currently unknown, but the extensions that Bijan Robinson and Jonathan Taylor agreed to over the last few days could have created some momentum toward a new deal for Gibbs. Whatever the reason, the Lions have one of their best players practicing and that's a positive sign for the offense in Detroit.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jonathan Taylor agrees to two-year extension with Colts
summary: Taylor is set to make $44 million under the terms of his new deal.
full_text: Colts running back Jonathan Taylor didn't need to hold in to get a new contract. According to multiple reports on Thursday morning, Taylor has agreed to a two-year extension. PFT reported earlier this week that signs were pointing to an extension of that length as Taylor moves into his seventh season in Indianapolis. Taylor is set to make $44 million over those two years with a maximum contract value of $47 million. There is $39 million in guaranteed money. The $22 million average annual salary is just behind the $22.25 million that Bijan Robinson agreed to with the Falcons this week. Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs — who joined Robinson in holding in at training camp and is still out of practice — is now the biggest name looking for a contract extension at the running back spot.
author: Josh Alper

title: Mike Macdonald provides update on Zach Charbonnet's rehab
summary: Zach Charbonnet underwent surgery to repair the torn anterior cruciate ligament in his left knee on Feb. 20.
full_text: Zach Charbonnet underwent surgery to repair the torn anterior cruciate ligament in his left knee on Feb. 20. He started training camp on the active/physically unable to perform list, and it seems likely he will begin the season on the reserve/PUP list. Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald provided an update on the running back's rehab. "It’s just a progression that you’ve got to be able to do to get your body ready to play, especially at the running back position," Macdonald said, via video from Brian Nemhauser of hawkblogger.com. "He’s going through it, hitting his hurdles, and we’re rolling. "We’ll see what the timetable is and how quickly he comes back.” Charbonnet injured his knee on his fifth carry in the divisional round of the playoffs after running for 730 yards and 12 touchdowns on 184 carries in the regular season. The Seahawks drafted running back Jadarian Price in the first round as a replacement for Kenneth Walker, who won the Super Bowl MVP award before leaving for Kansas City in the offseason.
author: Charean Williams

title: 49ers release DL Kevin Givens, DL Cameron Sample
summary: The 49ers made their two Wednesday signings official, which also means they had to make a pair of corresponding roster moves.
full_text: '' The 49ers made their two Wednesday signings official, which also means they had to make a pair of corresponding roster moves. In announcing the club had officially added receiver KhaDarel Hodge and defensive lineman Ogbo Okoronkwo to one-year deals, the club also noted veteran defensive linemen Kevin Givens and Cameron Sample have been released. Givens, 29, has been with the 49ers since entering the league as an undrafted free agent in 2019. He’s appeared in 70 career games for the franchise, tallying 8.0 sacks with 18 tackles for loss and 18 quarterback hits. He played five games last year, registering two total tackles. Sample joined the 49ers in April on a one-year deal after spending his first five seasons with the Bengals. In 2025, he tallied 17 total tackles with 2.0 sacks, two TFLs, and six QB hits in 14 games with two starts. San Francisco’s first preseason game will take place next Thursday against Tennessee in Santa Clara.
author: Myles Simmons

title: C.J. Gardner-Johnson returns to practice for Bills
summary: Safety C.J.
full_text: '' Safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson's exit from practice on a cart last weekend caused a scare for the Bills, but word that he only suffered a calf strain allowed everyone a sigh of relief. There was cause for another one at practice on Thursday. Gardner-Johnson was in uniform as the team took the practice field and reporters at the session share that he has participated without issue during the workout. Gardner-Johnson is wearing a sleeve on his right calf for added protection. Reporters also note that defensive tackle Deone Walker is taking part in practice Thursday. Walker has missed time with an elbow injury.
author: Josh Alper

title: DeMeco Ryans: Jadeveon Clowney is "fitting right in"
summary: Jadeveon Clowney is back in Houston, where his NFL career began 12 years ago.
full_text: Jadeveon Clowney is back in Houston, where his NFL career began 12 years ago. He's already making a good impression on head coach DeMeco Ryans. "Clowney is bringing what he's always done," Ryans told reporters on Wednesday. "He's explosive off the edge and he finds a way to get to the quarterback. He's been very productive throughout his career of getting to the quarterback and causing havoc, which is what I love. So he fits our style. He fits our brand of football. "He came in late yesterday and he's been picking up the scheme, picking up things we're asking him to do and he's fitting right in. He made a couple plays today, he’s in the backfield a lot as I'm standing back there, so that's encouraging to see. We'll continue to give him more. He'll get caught up to speed here pretty quickly, but we're excited with the type of player we're able to add and continue to add depth to our defensive line. We want to rotate a lot of guys there, so that we don't wear any one guy out. We want those guys to be able to last throughout the duration of the season and Clowney definitely gives us that flexibility that we were looking for at the defensive end spot.” As linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair said Tuesday, “Rich get richer, man. The rich get richer." And the Texans' dominant defense gets better. If the offense can improve just a bit, the Texans could be the team to beat in a conference that is still top heavy with contenders.
author: Mike Florio

title: Injuries left 49ers without 20 players by the end of Wednesday's practice
summary: Injuries have been a major storyline at 49ers camp so far this summer and Wednesday's practice was no exception.
full_text: Injuries have been a major storyline at 49ers camp so far this summer and Wednesday's practice was no exception. The team opened the session without 18 members of their 90-man roster on the field and the number of injured players grew to 20 when defensive end Sam Okuayinonu (ankle) and guard Nick Zakelj (elbow) made an early exit. Per multiple reports, the 49ers were also without offensive lineman Carver Willis (concussion), fullback Kyle Juszczyk (finger), wide receiver Jacob Cowing (hip flexor), offensive lineman Brett Toth (undisclosed) defensive end Nick Bosa (soreness), defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa (soreness), linebacker Dre Greenlaw (soreness), wide receiver Christian Kirk (calf), wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling (hamstring), wide receiver Mike Evans (quad), safety Malik Mustapha (hamstring), running back Kaelon Black (adductor), running back Jordan James (ribs), defensive end Keion White (adductor), and offensive tackle Vederian Lowe (ankle). Tight end George Kittle (Achilles), defensive end Mykel Williams (knee), and running back Isaac Guerendo (pec) have not practiced at all in camp and remain on the physically unable to perform list. They have also placed five players, including wide receiver Ricky Pearsall, on injured reserve and head coach Kyle Shanahan has not resumed a full workload following a pre-camp car accident.
author: Josh Alper

title: Todd Monken clarifies comments about QB plans for the preseason
summary: Monken responded to a report that Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders will each start a preseason game.
full_text: Browns head coach Todd Monken opened a Wednesday press conference by responding to a question about the team's plans for their starting quarterback in their first two preseason games. Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network reported on Tuesday that Monken told him either Deshaun Watson or Shedeur Sanders would start the preseason opener against the Bears on August 15 and that the other one would start against the Bills on August 22. On Wednesday, Monken said that was not an entirely accurate representation of the team's plans at this point. "Basically talked about that the quarterbacks are gonna play in the preseason," Monken said. "Obviously if it’s still a competition at that time, why wouldn’t you start one and start the other and then we would go from there. That was really what the conversation was. He wasn’t wrong in what we talked about, which you’ve all known that they’re gonna play in the preseason. Someone has to go out there for the first snap thus they would be the one that starts. At this point we’re so far from that, that it’s not really as important as what it got made out to be." Monken said that Watson and Sanders will continue rotating with the first team as long as the competition continues and gave no indication that there's a specific date he has in mind to make a decision on a starter. It seems likely that both Watson and Sanders will wind up starting a preseason game if that continues for a few more weeks, but it's not the sure thing it may have seemed on Tuesday.

title: Why you should watch Panthers-Cardinals in Hall of Fame Game, plus ranking the NFL's top 10 play-callers
summary: Here's everything you need to know about the NFL for Aug. 6
full_text:
Hello football friends, and welcome to the Thursday edition of the Pick Six newsletter!
After 179 days of waiting, football is finally back. Have I been counting down since February? Yes, and yes, I clearly need a hobby.
The Hall of Fame Game kicks off tonight, and sure, there's a good chance that you won't be able to name a single player on the field in the fourth quarter, but that's the beauty of preseason football . If you need a reason to watch tonight's game, don't worry, we're going to give you a few reasons why you should tune in. With that in mind, let's get to the rundown.
As always, here's your daily reminder to tell all your friends to sign up for the newsletter. To get them signed up, all you have to do is click here .
The first game of the 2026 season is officially here, which is a good thing, because I was starting to experience football withdrawal symptoms. The game tonight will feature the head coaching debut of Arizona's Mike LaFleur, who was hired in January to take over for Jonathan Gannon.
The game will be kicking off from Canton, Ohio, at 8 p.m. ET on NBC and the fact that NBC has the game is one reason why you should be watching. Tonight's game will mark the NBC debut of former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin, and it will be interesting to see how he handles his new job.
Besides Tomlin, here are a few other things to know heading into tonight's game and a few reasons why you might want to watch:
Breech's pick: Cardinals 20-17 over Panthers (Cardinals cover +1). It's the bottom of the Panthers roster against the bottom of the Cardinals roster, so it's hard to pick a winner here, but I'm going with Arizona, only because I think Mike LaFleur would like to start his career off with a win.
The Hall of Fame Game is just an appetizer when it comes to the festivities this weekend. The main course will be coming on Saturday with the enshrinement of the Pro Football Hall of Fame's class of 2026. If you're planning to watch induction ceremony this weekend, you better clear your schedule on Saturday afternoon because that's when the ceremony will be kicking off. After years of holding the enshrinement ceremony in prime time, the Hall of Fame moved the ceremony to noon ET in 2022, and that's where it will be once again this year. (The ceremony will be televised by both ESPN and NFL Network.)
The Hall of Fame's Class of 2026 consists of five players, including a KICKER. Let's take a look at the class:
Vinatieri is just the third pure placekicker ever to make the Hall of Fame, joining Jan Stenerud and Morten Andersen. One other notable fact about this weekend is that Kuechly will become the second-youngest Hall of Famer ever when he's inducted on Saturday. The 2013 NFL Defensive Player of the Year just turned 35 in April. The only player who was younger at the time of his induction was Gale Sayers, who was 34 when he was enshrined in 1977.
If you're wondering who might make the Hall of Fame in the future, Bryan DeArdo went through and identified one active player from each team who could eventually end up in Canton and you can check that out here .
After ranking the top 10 head coaches in the NFL earlier this week, you might have thought that we were done ranking things, but we're not, we're never done. Today, we're going to rank the top offensive and defensive play-callers in the NFL.
We rounded up 12 of our NFL experts and had them vote on the top play-callers and I'm going to unveil our ranking for the top 10 defensive play-callers.
1. Mike Macdonald ( Seahawks head coach) 2. Steve Spagnuolo ( Chiefs defensive coordinator) 3. Jesse Minter ( Ravens head coach) 4. Vic Fangio ( Eagles defensive coordinator) 5. Brian Flores (Vikings defensive coordinator) 6. Robert Saleh ( Titans head coach) 7. Chris Shula ( Rams defensive coordinator) 8. Vance Joseph ( Broncos defensive coordinator) 9. Anthony Campanile (Jaguars defensive coordinator) 10. Matt Burke ( Texans defensive coordinator)
It's kind of crazy to think that Macdonald and Minter were on the same staff in Baltimore for four seasons (2017-20).
As for the top ranked guys on the offensive side of the ball, you'll have to check out our full story here if you want to see that part of the list.
If there's one thing you can count on every year in the NFL, it's that your going to see multiple new playoff teams during the upcoming season. There have been at least four new playoff teams in every season played since 1990, so it almost feels like a lock that we'll once again see that happen this year.
With that in mind, Zach Pereles decided to take a look around the AFC to try and figure out which teams might make the postseason this year after missing out last year.
Here are the top three teams on his list:
Pereles also made a prediction on several teams that could take a step back after making the playoffs last year and you can check out that list here .
NFL owners aren't allowed to gamble on the NFL, but apparently, they can tell you what they would bet on if they were allowed to gamble and that's what Jimmy Haslam did recently.
The Browns owner has apparently been paying close attention to the Over/Under total that his team has been given and we know that because he specifically mentioned it during a recent press conference.
"I would say this, and we never do this, but I think the odds are for us to win five and a half games," Haslam said. "I'll take the over."
Taking the over on the Browns might seem slightly crazy, but I think I actually agree with him and there's one big reason why: The schedule.
I'm not sure if I've gone completely crazy, but I do think the Browns will top 5.5 wins in 2026. You can read my full breakdown of the situation here .
It's been a busy few days around the NFL, and since it's nearly impossible to keep track of everything, I put together a quick roundup for you.
author: John Breech

title: Renner's 2027 NFL Draft scouting series: Ranking top 10 defensive tackles
summary: After only one defensive tackle cracked Round 1 in 2026, the 2027 class already looks much deeper
full_text:
After a 2026 class that only saw one defensive tackle, Clemson's Peter Woods, sneak into the back end of Round 1, early tape suggests big changes in 2027. Talent abounds throughout this class, with the top six prospects all having a real chance to end up as first-rounders. What makes it so intriguing is the youth. Three of the top four on this list are rising juniors, and all have well-rounded skill sets. That means there will be a lot of competition to track who DT1 will be throughout the season.
Positional rankings: IOL • S • LB • DT • TE • OT • RB • CB • EDGE • WR • QB
Note: ⭐️ represents each player's 247Sports star rating as a high school recruit
For a true sophomore, Stone has some prodigious pop behind his hands. He is a pure power defensive tackle already and ragdolled some of college football's best in the SEC last season. The scary thing is that strength can improve throughout a collegiate and even an NFL career in a way that explosiveness and speed cannot. For him to be this imposing this early on is a strong signal.
David Stone (6’3 310) Oklahoma ✅ Quick to shoot gaps ✅ Reported 35” arm length ✅ 26 pressures during 2025 ✅ 13.0% stop rate was among the highest for any defender in the country during the 2025 season pic.twitter.com/rB4ZScvIA3
This isn't terribly surprising for the former 5-star recruit and top-10 overall player in the 2024 recruiting class. While I'd like to see more production as a pass-rusher than his 28 pressures last season, he doesn't need to improve much to end up a first-rounder.
Trying to block the 6-foot-3, 330-pound Washington doesn't seem like it would be a lot of fun. That's because a. He's very explosive off the line for his size. He's excellent and maintains a low center of gravity into contact. You're not going to be able to keep him out of the backfield if he wants to go there, but you can only hope to get him off-balance enough to keep him from making plays. That combination gives him a high floor vs. the run when projecting him to the NFL.
Oregon DT A’Mauri Washington (6-3, 330) would’ve been my DT2 in THIS NFL Draft Firmly in DT1 talks. So quick off the 🏈w/ridiculous athleticism. Moves like he’s 300 🦆8 batted passes led FBS 🦆12 QB hurries in 2024 🦆18 in 2025 1st Round Bound for 2027 pic.twitter.com/O7VGqPz8mM
He needs more than if he's going to be a consistent pass-rushing threat in the league, though. His ability to separate off blocks once engaged is easily the biggest hole in his game. Most of his wins come at the snap, and his ability to string together moves with his hands still remains to be seen.
While there are a lot of different body types that can play defensive tackle in the NFL, Echoles possesses one that could really only fit at defensive tackle. At 6-foot-2, he is thick from head to toe. The kind of build where I'm not sure he could reach 250 pounds, even with Tony Horton personally training him. It makes moving him in the run game a tall task for opposing linemen.
Will Echoles Cut Ups https://t.co/fTASIhlnhz pic.twitter.com/tnydrCBsbW
At that size, I love that he almost never comes off the field still. He played the most snaps of any Power-4 defensive tackle last season and the third-most in the FBS. Despite the heavy workload, it's rare to see him gassed, and he has a knack for making plays. He finished with the second-most run stops among Power-4 defensive tackles behind only second-rounder Kayden McDonald. That's incredibly impressive for a player who was only 19 years old all season. In what looks like an extremely talented defensive tackle class, Echoles will have a real case for the top player at his position next spring.
Scott got lost in one of the best defensive lines in modern college football history, but he's a dynamic playmaker in his own right. He was an afterthought for the Hurricanes staff to start the season, but by the year's end, he played a career-high 52 snaps in the National Title against Indiana.
I am officially a big Justin Scott fan pic.twitter.com/QlRKaGwQo0
What gets me excited about Scott's sophomore tape is the pass-rushing potential. He had 17 pressures in his final seven games. His two-hand strike stuns most linemen, and then he's quick enough to slip by en route to the quarterback. Obviously, I'd like to see it for a full season, but there's more than enough on tape last year to know Scott has the goods.
Gadson was a backup for two seasons in Lexington after suffering a knee injury in the spring of his freshman year. He broke out in a big way last fall with 20 pressures. He's got high-end traits to be a pass-rush threat at the next level with long limbs and a swift first step. Unfortunately for his draft prospects, Gadson often played out of position at nose tackle for the Wildcats last fall, when he's much more of a 3-4 defensive end. Hopefully, that changes under the new coach, Will Stein.
I was floored when Moten decided to return to school this fall, as he had the kind of twitchy athleticism for a defensive tackle that the 2026 draft class was short on. That could have seen him boosted to a top-50 selection, but now he's back for a fifth season to take a swing at the first round.
Moten's calling card is his light feet as a pass-rusher that allow him to dance past opposing linemen. He pairs them with active hands and good body control to be a consistent pass-rushing threat on the interior.
I've been known to overvalue undersized, athletic 3-techniques in the past, and Brewu is precisely that. What separates Brewu's game from your average 6-foot-1, 285-pound collegiate defensive tackle is his strength through contact. He doesn't get jostled around nearly as much as you'd expect from an undersized tackle and can really do damage with his hands. Make no mistake, however, Brewu is a three-technique only in the NFL. Being as productive as he was in only two seasons at Pittsburgh before transferring makes me excited about where his game could end up by the time he declares for the draft.
Notre Dame DT Francis Brewu: Extremely strong individual pic.twitter.com/ySvO2UfaZ9
Horace Lockett (6’5 362) UCF ✅ Massive frame ✅ 76.9 run defense grade in 2025 ✅ Power to push the pocket ✅ 7.0% career missed tackle rate pic.twitter.com/pqUDpZsZpP
Alexander will forever be known as the transfer portal poster boy after his Instagram post in a Penn State jersey (on a visit) flexing his right biceps featuring a Georgia tattoo (his original school) with a USC profile picture (where he spent 2023-24).
His talent has never been in question as a former top recruit, but his development did not take hold until his first season with the Ducks. You really saw him unlock the high-end strength he possesses throughout his frame. He was far more violent getting off blocks, and he finished with the second-most run stops of any returning defensive tackle.
Oregon DT Bear Alexander really lives up to his name with the violence he brings on every snap. His hands are legitimate weapons. pic.twitter.com/Og5mo1Im0C
Holmes isn't that physically imposing with a slight frame for a defensive tackle and limited length, but he makes up for it with a quick first step and consistent hand placement. No one on this list caught shoulder pads as consistently in the run game as Holmes did last season. Even on a loaded defensive line, I'd argue he was clearly the best run defender. The only question is how that will translate to the NFL, given less-than-prototypical traits at the position? He has another year to prove it's not a fluke.
Note: These aren't necessarily the next three players in my rankings, but rather three prospects who caught my eye for one reason or another.
Sigler isn't an uber-traitsy prospect by any means, but he dominated his competition at Arkansas State last year. That came after three years at West Alabama, where he started his career. If he can be similarly productive in the SEC, he'll get on radars very quickly.
Abasiri looks like a lab-built defensive tackle with incredibly long arms…

title: Predicting every NFL team's best current Hall of Fame candidate: Aaron Rodgers, Travis Kelce among locks
summary: Which player from your favorite team has the best chance to eventually earn a bronze bust in Canton?
full_text:
There is no official criterion when determining who is enshrined in the Pro Football Hall of Fame. That being said, based on who has and who hasn't been enshrined over the past 50 years, it's safe to say that there are certain obvious characteristics when determining bronze busts and gold jackets. And there is no better time to examine those than the 2026 Hall of Fame Game.
Using the interpretation of some of the unspoken criteria used when determining who gets into the Hall of Fame, we've created a list of each NFL team's current player who has the best shot at being enshrined in Canton once their career is over. Here was the criteria used when selecting the most likely players on each NFL team that could be considered a "lock" if their careers ended today:
Did your team's best player make the cut? Let's find out.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No
The hard-hitting safety enters the 2026 season as an eight-time Pro Bowler and two-time first-team All-Pro. It's hard to make the Hall of Fame as a safety, though, so for Baker to truly have a legitimate shot at Canton one day, either he or the Cardinals need to win some hardware in the coming years. Baker is responsible for 1,021 career tackles in 138 regular-season games, including 678 solo tackles. He's exceeded 100 tackles six times, including 164 in 2024.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No
Last season, Robinson unofficially supplanted Saquon Barkley and Derrick Henry as the NFL's best running back. At 24 years old, Robinson is just getting into his prime seasons. If he continues to mimic the success he had in the previous two seasons, Robinson will have a strong argument for his future Hall of Fame candidacy.  Robinson's 3,910 rushing yards through his first 51 games represent an impressive Hall of Fame trajectory.
Current Hall of Fame lock: Yes
Henry punched his future ticket to Canton during his first two seasons with the Ravens, when he hit several career milestones that included 100 career touchdown runs and 13,000 career rushing yards. Henry enters the 2026 season ranked fourth all-time in career touchdown runs and 10th in both career rushing yards and career total touchdowns.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No, but getting closer
Allen has had a great career so far, but he'll need to have a few more Pro Bowl-caliber seasons before he can be considered a future Hall of Famer. With a league MVP in tow, a Super Bowl win may be all Allen needs to be considered a lock for future induction. Allen boasts 30,102 career passing yards and 220 touchdowns. He will also break 5,000 rushing yards and 80 rushing touchdowns by October of this season.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No
A former first-round pick, Brown had the most complete year of his career in 2023, setting career highs with 103 tackles in addition to two sacks, an interception and six pass breakups. After an injury wiped out virtually his entire 2024 season, Brown returned to form last season while helping the Panthers capture the NFC South.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No
Joe Burrow received consideration, but there's no denying that Chase is more deserving of this spot given what he has done in his career up to this point. He's a five-time Pro Bowler who, in 2024, won the coveted "triple crown" after leading the league in receptions, receiving yards and touchdown catches. Chase is certainly off to a Hall of fame start thanks to his 520 catches, 6,837 receiving yards and 54 touchdowns in addition to his individual honors.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No
Thuney's career has included two Super Bowl wins with the Patriots, two more Super Bowl wins with the Chiefs and three consecutive Pro Bowl berths entering this season. Now 33, Thuney will need to continue to rack up Pro Bowl selections if he is going to have a serious Hall of Fame case someday.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No
Ward, who recently received a hefty contract extension, has been one of the league's top cornerbacks since his rookie season back in 2018. Some All-Pros nod, and team success would greatly increase Ward's future Hall of Fame chances. Ward has 18 picks and 104 pass defenses in 110 career regular-season games.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No
Oddly, Lamb's success in Dallas has somewhat gone under the radar. He's been a Pro Bowler each of the last five years and, in 2023, broke Michael Irvin's single-season franchise receiving record. For Lamb's career to seriously merit Hall of Fame consideration someday, he'll probably need to get more All-Pro nods. A receiving title or two wouldn't hurt, either. Lamb has 571 career catches for 7,416 yards and 41 touchdowns.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No
Surtain has quickly blossomed into one of the NFL's premier cornerbacks. He's earned five Pro Bowl nods and two All-Pro selections. In 2024, he became the first defensive back this decade to win Defensive Player of the Year.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No
Hutchinson got the nod over Amon-Ra St. Brown and Penei Sewell , who are also enjoying strong starts to their careers. Less than a year after breaking his leg, Hutchinson recorded a career-high 14.5 sacks in 2025. Barring injury, there's a very good chance that Hutchinson will join the short list of players who have reached 100 career sacks before turning 30.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No, but trending in that direction
Parsons was in the middle of another banner season until he suffered a torn ACL in Week 14. If Parsons can return to his preinjury form, he should be considered a future Hall of Fame lock. Primarily as a member of the Dallas Cowboys, Parsons registered 65 career regular-season sacks and 297 tackles over 77 games.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No, but on the cusp
Hunter would crack any list naming the NFL's most underrated players. The 31-year-old is a five-time Pro Bowler and is currently tied with J.J. Watt on the NFL's career sack list. Hunter is fewer than 10 sacks away from cracking the top-30 in career sacks.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No, but trending in that direction
You can't have a better start to a career than the one that Nelson has enjoyed. Through eight seasons, Nelson has earned eight Pro Bowl and three All-Pro nods. He's two selections away from becoming only the 13th offensive lineman in history with double-digit Pro Bowl nods.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No
Hines has had an impressive career so far, including two Pro Bowl nods and a career-high 17.5 sacks in 2023. He'll have to start stacking up Pro Bowls, however, if he is going to have a legitimate shot at making the Hall of Fame someday. While 2023 has been his signature season to date, he boasts 61 overall career sacks since his arrival from Kentucky.
Current Hall of Fame lock: Yes
The Chiefs have two slam-dunk future Hall of Famers in Kelce and quarterback Patrick Mahomes . Kelce was picked here largely because of the fact that his career is winding down, whereas Mahomes is still adding chapters to his career. Kelce's legacy includes three Super Bowl wins, 11 consecutive Pro Bowl nods and being the postseason's all-time leading pass catcher.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No
Still only 28 (he'll turn 29 later this month), Crosby has been one of the league's most destructive defenders since his rookie season. He's made the Pro Bowl each of the last five years and has led the NFL in tackles for loss twice. Crosby already has 69.5 sacks to his name, including five seasons with double digits.
Current Hall of Fame lock: No, but close
While he is on the downturn of his career, Mack has nonetheless put together a career worthy of future Hall of Fame consideration. His list of career milestones includes a DPOY, nine Pro Bowls, three All-Pros and an All-Decade Team selection. Here are the numbers: 662 career tackles, 481 solo tackles, 113 sacks and 36 forced fumbles.
Current Hall of Fame lock: Yes
Davante Adams and Myles Garrett both have strong Hall of Fame arguments, but Stafford has the edge after winning his first league MVP in 2025. Stafford has also won a Super Bowl ring and is top-10…
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Steelers training camp overreactions: Drew Allar outplaying Will Howard? Is Rico Dowdle the new RB1?
summary: Sorting out what's fact and what's fiction from Steelers training camp
full_text:
LATROBE, Pa. -- For a team that is bringing back most of its starters, there remain a lot of unknowns as it relates to the Pittsburgh Steelers as they continue to move through their second week of training camp.
Who will be backing up Aaron Rodgers when the Steelers open the regular season? Who is the starting running back? Are the new receivers making an impact? Will Mike McCarthy regret his decision to have a tackling-free training camp?
Pittsburgh's two most recent open practices provided insight regarding each of the above questions. And while things could obviously change between now and Week 1, here is what we currently know based on sideline observations from Saint Vincent College earlier this week.
Overreaction or reality: Reality
Allar was slightly more impressive than Howard during this week's practices. He was more decisive in his decision-making, took more chances downfield and was often successful whenever he did stretch the field. He also made some tight throws in traffic that included several impressive completions for scores during red zone drills.
Howard, who has a long history of being entrenched in position battles, is clearly game for the competition. On Monday, two plays after Allar completed a deep pass downfield, Howard decided to go deep himself. The pass wasn't completed, but Howard's decision to test himself in that situation was more notable than the result.
Drew Allar and Will Howard during a recent practice. #Steelers pic.twitter.com/Z0ADAqyz5v
As far as intangibles are concerned, Howard has the leg up in that department. He was the last player off the field on both Monday and Tuesday. In 2024, his leadership helped Ohio State overcome a devastating loss to archrival Michigan to go on an improbably national title run. And speaking of Ohio State, Howard shared the many similarities between Ryan Day and McCarthy following Monday's practice.
Will Howard on similarities between Ryan Day & Mike McCarthy. pic.twitter.com/MaHYpSVpg0
Allar may have the edge now, but the ultimate test will come in the preseason. Furthermore, in addition to competing against each other, Allar and Howard are also competing against Mason Rudolph , the team's veteran backup. McCarthy hasn't ruled out having four quarterbacks on his roster, but it's safe to assume that he is hoping that two of his three backup quarterbacks play well enough during the preseason to convince him that he only needs three on the 53-man roster.
One can also assume that McCarthy would rather keep two young quarterbacks on the roster, which could very well lead to Rudolph being the odd man out. For that to happen, though, Allar and Howard have to take full advantage of their opportunities during the preseason.
Overreaction or reality: Reality
Despite rotating first-team reps with Jaylen Warren , it's clear that Dowdle is the front-runner to be Pittsburgh's starting running back when the regular season starts.
Dowdle, who ran for 1,000 yards during his final season with McCarthy in Dallas, has quickly developed a rapport with Rodgers as a safety valve in the passing game. He is embracing the opportunity to play with and catch passes from Pittsburgh's future Hall of Fame quarterback.
"The best quarterback I've stepped on a field with," Dowdle told CBS Sports following Tuesday's practice. "Smartest quarterback. It's just been get getting out there, getting beside him and working with him. Definitely looking forward to getting out there during the regular season with him."
“That’s the best quarterback I’ve stepped on a field with.” Rico Dowdle on Aaron Rodgers pic.twitter.com/qoKH41HKls
As impressive as Dowdle has been, the Steelers are going to need him and Warren in order to be successful this season. Warren, despite setting career highs last season with 958 rushing yards, 1,291 all-purpose yards and eight total touchdowns, continues to carry a chip on his shoulder after not being selected in the 2022 NFL Draft .
"I don't think that will ever go away," said Warren, who made the Steelers' initial 53-man roster in 2022 after going undrafted. "Whether it's Year 5 or Year 11, I'll still carry that."
Warren's individual goal for 2026 is to rush for over 1,000 yards for the first time. He was asked whether or not he and Dowdle can become the eighth pair of teammates to both rush for 1,000 yards in the same season.
"Oh yeah, for sure," he said. "Our O-line, they've definitely built that chemistry. Everybody's on the same page, and I'm excited for the season to start."
#Steelers Jaylen Warren’s individual goal is to run for 1K for the first time, and he thinks that Rico Dowdle can do so as well. Steelers have had one pair of teammates to each hit 1K in the same season: Franco & Rocky back in 1976. pic.twitter.com/4uoDsvAJXg
While the Steelers' running game appears to be primed for success, that wasn't the case during this week's first two practices as Pittsburgh's backs seldom reached the third level of the defense. That is something to keep an eye on when the Steelers kick off the preseason.
Overreaction or reality: Reality
After an impressive opening week of camp, Wilson was just as impressive during this week's first two practices.
Wilson has received the majority of the reps with Pittsburgh's first-team offense, and he's taken full advance of those reps. Throughout both practices, Wilson was consistently targeted by Rodgers, who is clearly developing trust in Pittsburgh's former third-round pick.
It's easy to see how Wilson has found a way to move up the depth chart. He's spent time with the jugs machine before practice and has continued to catch passes after practice.
Roman Wilson getting some work in before #Steelers first padded practice. pic.twitter.com/mTcabwlQl9
Along with Wilson, Rodgers' top targets thus far have been Dowdle, DK Metcalf , and tight end Pat Freiermuth . Michael Pittman , one of the Steelers' big offseason acquisitions, was noticeably quiet during both practices. So was rookie Germie Bernard , who is clearly still getting acclimated to life in the NFL .
Overreaction or reality: Overreaction
Defensively, the Steelers don't appear to be negatively impacted by the fact that they no longer have a defensive-oriented head coach. In fact, it appears to be the opposite.
Led by new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham, the Steelers' defense made a bevy of notable plays during the first two days of padded practice. That was the case even with the absence of defensive backs Joey Porter Jr . and Jalen Ramsey .
Ironically, two other defensive backs, Brandin Echols and newcomer Jaquan Brisker , have been two of Pittsburgh's biggest defensive standouts thus far. Brisker has made his presence felt both in the secondary and up on the line of scrimmage. Echols made several notable plays earlier this week that included an interception of Rodgers during the early portion of Monday's practice.
Echols' playmaking was complemented by his constant chirping at the offense, a subtle reminder that the Steelers, at their core, are still about being physical and intimidating.
"I've been like that since high school," Echols said. "It's crazy. I used to watch a lot of Jalen Ramsey [going back to] his rookie year when he was with Jacksonville. All the trash talking it, seeing everything he was doing, it just like motivated me. I was like, 'When I get to the NFL, I want to be just like that.'"
Ironically, Echols said one of his favorite receivers in the NFL to exchange banter with is one of his teammates.
"DK," Echols said. "DK brings it out of me. Me and DK are kind of from the same area. He's from Mississippi. I'm from Mississippi. We've got that relationship. We're just trying to make each other better."
As far as the 2026 season is concerned, Echols said that the Steelers' defense is motivated to prove their naysayers wrong.
"We're gonna come out with a chip, especially coming off last year," he said. "You know, just looking at some of the rankings, how they had us placed, we know some…

title: Colts signing Jonathan Taylor to two-year, $44 million extension as another NFL RB gets paid, per reports
summary: Taylor's new deal checks in just behind Falcons' Bijan Robinson
full_text:
Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor is now a much richer man. The star seventh-year back will sign a two-year contract extension with his team that pays him a base value of $44 million, $39 million of which is guaranteed, according to multiple reports . The contract has a maximum value of $47 million.
The deal comes together just days after Atlanta Falcons star Bijan Robinson signed a new deal with a base value of $22.75 million per year, which clearly set the market for running back contracts. Taylor now becomes the second-highest-paid running back in the NFL in terms of average annual value, jumping ahead of Philadelphia Eagles star Saquon Barkley , who sits at $20.6 million.
Christian McCaffrey ( 49ers )
De'Von Achane ( Dolphins )
Kenneth Walker III ( Chiefs )
The $39 million full guarantee, meanwhile, slightly surpasses Robinson for the most ever for a running back, excluding Jeremiyah Love's fully guaranteed rookie-scale contract as the No. 3 pick in this year's NFL Draft , according to Over the Cap.
Taylor had been heading into the final season of the three-year, $42 million extension he signed in 2023. He is set to draw a base salary of $11.98 million in 2026 while counting for $15.562 million against the cap.
Taylor led the NFL in both carries (323) and rushing touchdowns (18) last season, and has run for at least 1,400 yards and 11 touchdowns in each of the last two years. He's heading into his age-27 season and is the clear centerpiece of the Indianapolis offense.
The Colts started last season absolutely on fire offensively under quarterback Daniel Jones , leading the league in scoring for the first half of the season. They slowed down a bit after Jones suffered an initial leg injury, then suffered further after Jones tore his Achilles and the team had to turn to Philip Rivers , whom they signed off the street. With Jones back healthy in time for training camp, they are trying to recapture the form they had at the start of last year, and Taylor is clearly one of the keys to their doing so.
Of course, the Colts also spent a bunch of money to retain Jones this offseason, handing him a two-year, $88 million contract to return to the fold. Field-stretching wide receiver Alec Pierce also received a big-money contract, with the Colts re-signing him for $114 million over four years. Indianapolis is now clearly counting on that trio to hold down the fort down the offense over the next couple of years.

title: 2026 Hall of Fame Game: Carson Beck heads top 10 players to keep an eye on in preseason opener

Football is back. The Carolina Panthers and Arizona Cardinals will kick off the preseason in the Pro Football Hall of Fame Game tonight in Canton, Ohio. Those two teams will play four preseason games while the rest of the league will play just three.
Panthers head coach Dave Canales has already made his intentions known not to play the starters. However, the term "starters" is relatively subjective at this stage of the preseason. Some starters may be in competition with others whereas others may only be in a starting role due to injury.
The Cardinals have been less direct in their intentions, but are expected to operate under similar guidelines. Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love expressed his desire to play Thursday night, but coach Mike LaFleur seemed to dismiss that idea in media availability earlier this week. For that reason, wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. , cornerback Will Johnson and defensive tackle Walter Nolen III were among the notable names left off the list.

Starting safeties Nick Scott and Tre'von Moehrig have a combined 14 years of service in the NFL . The team is comfortable with that duo but second-year safety Lathan Ransom and Wheatley will push for a larger role. Wheatley is a long athlete (6-foot-3) who can muddy passing windows and get his hands on the football; as evidenced by his four interceptions over the past two seasons.
Offensive line was high on the list of offseason priorities for Arizona, but offensive guard Chase Bisontis and Williams were the only two drafted. The team did sign veterans Isaac Seumalo and Elijah Wilkinson in free agency, but Williams has starting-caliber traits that may lead to him receiving more playing time as the season progresses. The preseason gives the Cardinals an opportunity to test and establish a baseline for their rookie.
When Taylor-Demerson was drafted, the thought was that he could be the heir apparent to Budda Baker . However, Jalen Thompson is now gone from that secondary and Baker remains. The team signed Andrew Wingard in free agency despite Taylor-Demerson intercepting two passes in just 12 games. Can he continue his development and take ownership of a starting role in Arizona's young secondary?
Under the current coaching staff, a new cornerback emerges every year. Mike Jackson is coming off his best season and Jaycee Horn has become the player Carolina had expected when it selected him in the first round of the 2021 NFL Draft . Undrafted free agent Corey Thornton played 11% of the team's defensive snaps after breaking out last offseason. The team's track record of development, as well as its fourth-round investment in Lee, give reason for optimism.
Harrison-Hunte showed a lot of promise dating to his freshman season at Miami. Although he has yet to reach his full potential, Harrison-Hunte possesses great size. He may get a longer look alongside two other young defensive tackles: Cam Jackson and Lee Hunter .
Kuwatch plays the game sideline to sideline with reckless abandon. Carolina signed Devin Lloyd in free agency so the preseason may be Kuwatch's best opportunity for live-game repetitions, but do not be surprised if the Miami (Ohio) product becomes a key contributor on special teams this season.
Bisontis, a second-round pick, has cross-trained at left and right guard thus far. It sounds as though he will begin the season as a key reserve so preseason repetitions are invaluable. Bisontis is an athletic lineman who was playing his best football toward the end of his final season at Texas A&M, but remains a bit rough around the edges. Will he eventually take a starting role from either Isaiah Adams or Seumalo?
Umanmielen was a third-round pick a year ago and a recent season-ending injury to Nic Scourton places even more pressure on the Ole Miss product to elevate his game. Last season, Umanmielen recorded 1.5 sacks and a forced fumble for the Panthers. Jaelan Phillips was a big ticket free agent signing, but Umanmielen is competing with Patrick Jones II and Trevis GIpson for more playing time.
Hecht was a personal favorite during the pre-draft process. He was viewed as a top 100 overall prospect with starting capabilities but lasted until the fifth round. The Kansas State lineman is now embroiled in a competition with veteran Luke Fortner for the starting center job.
Beck will start for the Cardinals. It will be the first extended look of the third-round pick as a professional and the nation's first impression of LaFleur as a head coach. The game plan is unlikely to express more than a surface level look at the offense, but the opportunities to see Beck this season may be limited. Veteran Jacoby Brissett is the anticipated Week 1 starter and there is no timeline for the Miami product to take over.
