title: Should Buffalo Bills fans be worried about kicker Tyler Bass?
summary: The Buffalo Bills were without the services of kicker Tyler Bass for the entire 2025 season as Bass dealt with a painful pelvic injury, but the expectation was that Bass would be healthy and ready to go as the Bills got ready for training camp at St. John Fisher University. It has been nearly a […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills were without the services of kicker Tyler Bass for the entire 2025 season as Bass dealt with a painful pelvic injury, but the expectation was that Bass would be healthy and ready to go as the Bills got ready for training camp at St. John Fisher University. It has been nearly a year since Bass kicked a football for the Bills—during the 2025 preseason finale against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers—but so far, through the first five practice sessions at camp, Bass has yet to publicly attempt a field goal. Nearly eight months after Bass had surgery to repair a sports hernia, the kicker has not suffered any setbacks as he works his way back onto the field, according to special teams coordinator Jeff Rodgers. That thought was echoed by Bass, who said his body is “feeling good, we’re excited to get back and the process has been really kind of recovering, strengthening.” During a Q&A with the media on Tuesday, Rodgers said that, despite a lack of kicks during the team’s sessions that have been open to the media and fans, Bass has been working on his kicking in situations outside of team practices. The reason why fans haven’t been able to watch Bass attempt field goals and extra points so far at camp? The team hasn’t reached the step in their training camp schedule where they want to work extensively on field goals in game scenarios. “It has been by design,” Rodgers told WGR 550’s Paul Hamilton . “It’s not ‘Don’t let him kick just yet,’ there’s a finite number of things that we can get done on the field and field goal protection is not going to be as competitive in practice as it is in a game, so we take advantage of the walk through time because of the tempo that it requires, but at some point guys have got to start working on that stuff.” Rodgers revealed that, starting with today’s practice, fans curious about how Bass’ recovery can watch him handle field goals and extra point scenarios at camp. Rodgers told reporters that during Thursday’s practice sessions, the Bills will work on field-goal protection scenarios as a team for the third time since gathering at Fisher, and for the first time in pads to replicate game scenarios. Through the first five practices, Buffalo’s special teams units have prioritized working on their kickoffs and punts, while work on field-goal protection has been addressed during walkthrough sessions. “We just go step-by-step with it and try to put him environments that he’s going to be in, we build from there. We’ve done some individual and team stuff, but it hasn’t worked out for us to be on the field quite yet, but that will happen later on this week and then again at the stadium,” Rodgers said. “I don’t think you skip steps, it starts from ground zero and he’s working with two new holders right now (Mitch Wishnowsky and Tommy Doman) and that’s a part of that comfort, so it’s going to be a rep thing, but he looks like he did on tape and everything is going well so far.” The last time Bass kicked in a game was on Aug. 23, 2025, when he converted on three of his four field goal attempts and made both extra points in Buffalo’s preseason finale vs. Tampa Bay. Though Bass attempted to play through the pain he experienced last preseason, he was never able to shake off the discomfort and was eventually placed on injured reserve before the season began. Prior to his injury-plagued 2025 campaign, Bass had appeared in all 83 games since being selected with the No. 188 overall selection in the sixth round of the 2020 NFL Draft. Rodgers said Bass is looking forward to his first opportunity to kick in Buffalo’s new Highmark Stadium, which will occur Saturday night during the team’s annual “Return of the Blue & Red” practice starting at 7 p.m. Bills fans are hoping Bass is able to make a full recovery and return to being an effective offensive weapon. Through his first five seasons, Bass made 131 of his 155 field goals during the regular season (84.5%) and converted 264 of his 274 extra point attempts (96.4%).

title: Plays That Defined 2025: New York Jets, Week 18

For any newcomers, first and foremost; welcome! When it comes to […]
full_text: The 2025 Buffalo Bills’ season has been written, but the book is incomplete. Before we cast our full attention toward the 2026 season, let’s take one last glance back over our shoulder for our annual look at the Plays That Defined the prior campaign. For any newcomers, first and foremost; welcome! When it comes to the “rules” of this exercise, we’re not voting for our favorite highlight necessarily, but the one that best captures the essence of the game. Put differently, if you had to choose just one play to show someone to explain as much of the contest as possible, which would you choose? Week 18: New York Jets at Buffalo Bills Sometimes a game is more than a game. Sometimes a game is a milestone. Sometimes a game is a farewell. This is all of those things. The Buffalo Bills ended the 2025 regular season at home. Due to the standings, there would be no home playoff game. title: Buffalo Bills 2026 scouting reports: C/OG Austin Corbett
summary: The Buffalo Bills lost left guard David Edwards in free agency this offseason, as the veteran signed a lucrative contract with the New Orleans Saints. Edwards was a stabilizing force for a very good Buffalo offensive line, serving almost as the command center in pass protection and blitz pickup. Especially in hostile road environments, you […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NC - AUGUST 26: Carolina Panthers guard Austin Corbett (63) during a NFL preseason football game between the Buffalo Bills and the Carolina Panthers on August 26, 2022 at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, N.C. (Photo by John Byrum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Buffalo Bills lost left guard David Edwards in free agency this offseason, as the veteran signed a lucrative contract with the New Orleans Saints. Edwards was a stabilizing force for a very good Buffalo offensive line, serving almost as the command center in pass protection and blitz pickup. Especially in hostile road environments, you could always count on seeing Edwards pointing out potential threats incoming from opposing defenses. Those are pretty large shoes to fill for whomever ends up winning the starting gig at left guard for the 2026 NFL season. In today’s installment of our “91 players in 91 days” series, we discuss a well-traveled veteran looking to fill Edwards’ shoes this fall. _____________________________________________________________________________ Name: Austin Corbett Number: 63 Position: C/OG Height/Weight: 6’4”, 306 pounds Age: 30 (31 on 9/5/2026) Experience/Draft: 9; selected by the Cleveland Browns in the second round (No. 33 overall) of the 2018 NFL Draft College: Nevada Acquired: Signed with Buffalo on 3/26/2026 Financial situation (per Spotrac): Corbett signed a one-year contract worth a total of $1,487,500. Thanks to the veteran’s salary benefit, his cap hit will be slightly less than that, coming in at $1,262,500 for the season. That number is also what Buffalo will carry in a dead-cap charge if they release him prior to Week 1. As a vested veteran, his entire base salary — $1.3 million — becomes fully guaranteed if he’s on the team for that first week. 2025 Recap: Corbett spent last season with the Carolina Panthers, which is where he’d played from 2022 onward. He began the season as Carolina’s starting center, but a Week 2 MCL injury led to the Panthers placing him on Injured Reserve. When he returned for Carolina’s Week 7 victory over the New York Jets, Corbett started, but this time, he started at left guard. Corbett did not start the following week against the Bills, but after Cade Mays suffered an ankle injury early in the game, Corbett went right back into the lineup at center. He ended up playing in 13 total games for the Panthers, starting 11 games combined at center, left guard, and right guard. According to Pro Football Focus , he was flagged for just one penalty during the season. He allowed two sacks while earning a 67.8 grade overall, which was No. 29 among 81 qualified guards. Positional outlook: Corbett is one of four players listed at center/offensive guard on the current roster. Alec Anderson, Sedrick Van Pran-Granger, and Connor McGovern are the others. Lloyd Cushenberry is listed solely at center. Tylan Grable and Jude Bowry are listed at tackle/guard. Bruno Fina, Da’Metrius Weatherspoon, O’Cyrus Torrence, Ar’Maj Reed-Adams, and Nick Broeker are listed at guard. 2026 Offseason: Corbett is in the mix to replace David Edwards in the starting lineup at left guard. He has seen reps with the first team during early training camp practices, rotating with Alec Anderson in that role as the starting left guard. 2026 Season outlook: Throughout his career, Corbett has been an above-average performer at multiple positions. He was a starter at right guard for a Super Bowl team, as he held down that role for the Los Angeles Rams when they won the title during the 2021 NFL season. The Bills could do far worse than someone with Corbett’s ability and experience in the starting lineup. However, Corbett’s versatility and veteran savvy also makes him an ideal interior line reserve. Whether he wins the left guard competition or not, Austin Corbett is someone the Bills would love to keep on the roster. There were plenty of people, myself included, who assumed that the left guard gig this season would be Alec Anderson’s to lose given the time Buffalo has taken in developing him; however, this is a win-now league, and for the Bills, 2026 is a win-now season. They don’t have time to wonder whether the player they’ve developed is going to be good enough to start, and they certainly won’t give the job to Anderson merely because he’s been here longer. The NFL is a business, and the main goal in this business is winning. If Austin Corbett is better than Alec Anderson, he’ll start at left guard this season for the Bills. If he isn’t, then he’ll likely be an active reserve on game days given that he can slot into all three of the interior positions along the offensive line. Buffalo could decide that they like another young player that they have developed, Sedrick Van Pran-Granger, enough to use Corbett as trade bait, but SVPG has really only played center in his pro career despite his C/G listing. It’s too early to tell which player has the upper hand in the left guard competition, but it wouldn’t surprise me at all if Corbett were to earn the starting gig. He’s started 78 regular season games and six playoff games in his career, which is more than all of the other players vying to replace David Edwards have even played in, let alone started, combined. Corbett is talented enough to win a starting gig with the Bills this season.

title: What will Buffalo Bills turnover battle look like in 2026?
summary: For the last… well I can’t really remember how long it’s been now actually, I’ve been examining the Buffalo Bills takeaways and giveaways for quite some time. I think it’s time to look back at the Sean McDermott in totality, and try to make some guesses for the 2026 season; the dawn of the Joe […]
full_text: For the last… well I can’t really remember how long it’s been now actually, I’ve been examining the Buffalo Bills takeaways and giveaways for quite some time. I think it’s time to look back at the Sean McDermott in totality, and try to make some guesses for the 2026 season; the dawn of the Joe Brady era… McDermott era giveaways We all know the narrative around Josh Allen. He’s turnover prone. That’s not precisely wrong. It’s also not precisely right. Let’s look at a chart. I’m sorry to say it, but it’s a valid statement to say that in general, quarterbacks are a primary culprit of a team’s giveaways. That said, when it comes to Allen the phrase “your mileage may vary” is an apt one. His first year was frankly, abysmal. Then he improved drastically, with the team hovering around average from 2019 – 2021. Then we got a couple years of spikes in 2022 and 2023. Since this is a predictive feature ultimately, I should point current head coach, Joe Brady was the quarterbacks coach and interim offensive coordinator for those two seasons. In 2024 and 2025 Brady was the offensive coordinator and we had an elite year with barely any giveaways, and then a pretty average year. The team’s identity shifted toward the run under Brady’s OC tenure, but it should be noted that the 2024 season with the scant turnovers featured a balanced offense where passing attempts did edge out rushing ones. Of course we also have no idea if this was Brady’s plan or McDermott’s plan, but we’ve gotta make some kind of prediction for the season so my take is… The seasons with Brady seeing a heavier influence were both good ones. Allen and company have the potential for a disastrous season (2023 data), but those do appear to be the outliers with recent upturns coming under the Ken Dorsey era of offensive coordination. Are you curious about the splits in the 2023 season where Dorsey was ousted and Brady became the interim? Of course you do. Under Dorsey, the Bills had 18 turnovers. With Brady at the helm as OC, it went down to 10. That’s not quite the full story though as Dorsey had 10 games that season with Brady only coordinating seven. That equates to 1.8 turnovers per game vs. 1.4 turnovers per game. Brady still has the advantage, but not quite as drastic. I’ll hold off on a numeric predictor for right now. McDermott era takeaways If there was one side of the ledger that constantly had me looking foolish, it was the takeaway side. Like before, let’s consult the chart. The term “regression to the mean” is pretty much built for turnovers, where it’s tough to stay on top consistently. I predicted regression to the mean plenty of times for the Buffalo Bills and as you can see, aside from the 2025 season and the 2019 one it simply just wasn’t happening under Sean McDermott. I should also note for full disclosure that last season I penned several articles where the main premise was that the Bills’ defensive roster was less talented than many of McDermott’s squads. I mention that because I don’t think the coach is out there looking for a pick-six personally, so talent matters. This side of the ball is a bigger question mark with McDermott gone and the defensive scheme likely shifting, if not outright changing under Jim Leonhard. It’s unlikely Joe Brady will look to be a dominant influence on the defense either, with his history strongly on the offensive side of things. Like above, let’s hold off on predictions for a moment. Turnover differential As is tradition, a chart. Anything on the positive side of the ledger is a good thing, as turnover differential is strongly correlated with success. The 2024 season is preposterous so we should 100% dismiss it as an outlier. That aside, the Bills only had a negative differential one time, Josh Allen’s rookie season which was the most catastrophic one on the board for giveaways. That leads me to predictions, which of course I’ll start with last year’s. I predicted 28 takeaways as I finally learned to bet on McDermott. Just in time for an average season. Whoops. I was off by eight. For giveaways, I predicted regression to the mean with 16 turnovers on the wrong side of the ledger. That was only three off, so not too terrible. For this season, I like the Joe Brady influence to be a stabilizing one and I think the Josh Allen narrative is overblown. I’m going to predict 18 giveaways as the team emphasizes risk mitigation and careful football to support a defense going through growing pains. On the giveaways, I just don’t have much faith in the team immediately gelling. I hate to say it, as I know feelings on the man are mixed, but Sean McDermott was a masterful conductor, orchestrating ways to take the ball away. The data supports this knack and Jim Leonhard will need to prove himself to earn that rep. Until then, I have to assume he’s part of the pack. I also don’t want to assume Leonhard will be terrible at prepping the team, and there are many McDermott era starters who will still carry on what they learned. I like the Bills to still be on the positive side of the differential, but barely. I’m predicting 19 takeaways as the Bills remain at the mean.

title: 2026 Season Opener Countdown: 38 Days Remaining
summary: Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NC - OCTOBER 25: Star Lotulelei #98 of the Carolina Panthers defends a pass by Sam Bradford #7 of the Philadelphia Eagles in the first half during their game at Bank of America Stadium on October 25, 2015 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Streeter Lecka/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change that up a bit by counting down our own list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time. This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial. #38. Star Lotulelei The Panthers wished upon a falling Star in the first round of the 2013 NFL Draft. Star Lotulelei, considered by most pundits to be one of the best defensive prospects in the draft that year, played his college ball at Utah. He filled a major hole in the Panthers defense at that time, but most people thought he would be long gone before the Panthers picked at 14th overall, especially since that draft was notoriously thin for top tier quarterback prospects. A concerning heart condition made some teams at the top of the draft skittish, passing on Lotulelei in favor of “safer” picks. The Panthers pounced, taking Lotulelei and not looking back. In the end, his heart was never an issue. Star would go on to play the entirety of his rookie contract with the Panthers, coming in and starting immediately in the middle of the Panthers defensive line. His 42 tackles and three sacks his rookie year earned him enough votes to finish fourth in the Defensive Rookie of the Year voting. The following four years as a consistent presence up front for the Panthers defense. While defensive tackles not named Aaron Donald rarely get the flashy stats, Lotulelei was a coaching staff favorite who sacrificed his own box score to eat double teams and let other players make plays. Near the end of the 2014 season, Lotulelei suffered a broken foot, requiring surgery. He reaggravated the injury in training camp of 2015 and was never quite the same player afterwards. After his five years in Carolina, he signed with the Buffalo Bills (Panthers North) and played there for three seasons before retiring. Nose tackles rarely get the credit they deserve from fans and the media, and Star was no exception. His presence in the middle of the defensive line, especially during the Super Bowl run of 2015, allowed other players to make names (and tons of money) for themselves. Those players, like Luke Kuechly, Kawann Short, etc., would undoubtedly agree that while he wasn’t a star, Star definitely earned this spot in our countdown.

title: Cash, Stash, or Slash: Montez Sweat
summary: As we continue through this series, we continue to look at veteran players on the Chicago Bears roster and what they should do with them over the next 12 months. Should they extend them (cash), should they cut them (slash), or should they wait and see how the next year plays out (stash)? Next up, […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - JANUARY 10: Montez Sweat #98 of the Chicago Bears lines up before the snap during an NFC Wild Card Playoff game against the Green Bay Packers at Soldier Field on January 10, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images As we continue through this series, we continue to look at veteran players on the Chicago Bears roster and what they should do with them over the next 12 months. Should they extend them (cash), should they cut them (slash), or should they wait and see how the next year plays out (stash)? Next up, let’s look at Montez Sweat. Sweat is an interesting player to look at because he is by far the most productive player on the Bears’ defensive line, but many fans don’t think he has lived up to the contract that Ryan Poles gave him when the Bears traded for him from the Washington Commanders. Sweat’s contract expires after the 2027 season. What should the Bears do with him? Montez Sweat: Cash Baring a catastrophic injury or a massive drop-off in play, there’s close to no reason to slash Sweat, but there are plenty of reasons to stash him and see what happens after a couple of seasons. If I’m the Chicago Bears, I give Sweat an extension after this season. Some fans may be surprised at this stance, and I get it; Sweat turns 30 in September, extending him (let’s say 2 years) would be committing dollars to a player in their age 32 and 33 seasons. And it’s not like Sweat is a dynamic edge like a Micah Parsons or a Myles Garrett, but while you look at negatives, more so, look at the reasons why it should happen. First of all, you have to keep someone on the defensive line. It’s not like Ryan Poles is going to be able to go out after this season and just find 4 new DL to play, maybe three with Austin Booker. You need some stability there. Sweat is a reliable pass rusher, a strong run defender, and plays almost every Sunday and turns in a solid game. For fans who want Sweat to terrorize a game, he isn’t going to do that, but he is going to provide steady play and not let his side of the line get destroyed. Ideally, on a great defensive line, Sweat would be your second-best player. He would complement a stud opposite him or in the interior. But the Bears don’t have that, at least not right now. Sweat’s contract has also aged quite well. Sweat is now making half (literally half) of what the top edges in the game are being paid, and you would have to think if the Bears try to extend a solid but not spectacular player in his early 30s, there’s very little reason to think he would be looking for a massive raise in salary. Keeping Sweat around at his current price would be great for the Bears, who need to rework a lot of their defensive line if they are going to elevate this defense into a unit that belongs in the top half of the league. If the Bears want a solid D, you need more players like Sweat, not less. Sweat is not the type of guy who should be the best defensive player on a roster; it’s not his fault that the Bears don’t have better defenders than him. The durability Sweat has and the way he plays, I believe that he should be able to maintain this level of play at least for another three or four years, and if that’s the case, keeping him around as a building block piece on the defense with Devin Bush, Dillon Thieneman, and hopefully some guys like Austin Booker makes sense. Keep Sweat and add around him; subtracting him does very little to strengthen the Bears defense. It makes too much sense: keep Sweat, and fix the mistakes around him; don’t make another by letting him walk.

title: Cash, Stash, or Slash: Joe Thuney
summary: As we continue to look at some key veterans on the Chicago Bears roster and whether the Bears should sign them to an extension (Cash), cut ties with them sooner rather than later (Slash), or play out another year and see where the player is at (Stash), we shift back to the offensive line and […]
full_text: SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - FEBRUARY 05: Joe Thuney during the 15th Annual NFL Honors at the Palace Of Fine Arts on February 05, 2026 in San Francisco, California. (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images) | Getty Images As we continue to look at some key veterans on the Chicago Bears roster and whether the Bears should sign them to an extension (Cash), cut ties with them sooner rather than later (Slash), or play out another year and see where the player is at (Stash), we shift back to the offensive line and look at Joe Thuney. After the trade with the Carolina Panthers that netted Caleb Williams, at this point I think you would have to say that Joe Thuney is Ryan Poles’ best acquisition. Thuney was acquired from the Kansas City Chiefs for just a fourth-round pick, and he helped rejuvenate a line that had been towards the bottom of the league for years and transform it into a top 5 line. Not only that, he was the recipient of the first-ever Protector award, given to the league’s best offensive lineman. In short, he was awesome. Joe Thuney: Cash This article is probably going to be shorter than a lot of others in this series just because there isn’t much debate here. Thuney is under contract through the 2027 season. That makes Thuney a prime extension candidate after this season. The Bears should sit Thuney down after this season and ask him how much longer he wants to play. There is no decision on the Bears’ side if they should keep Thuney or move on. They should keep him. The question is that Thuney will be 35 when this current contract expires, and you have to wonder how much longer he wants to play. Thuney hasn’t said much about his future in football; it may be that he will play out his current contract and retire after 2027, or it may be that he wants to sign another deal and stay in Chicago for a few more years. Nobody really knows what Thuney wants to do except for Joe Thuney. If Thuney wants to return, inking him to a 2-year extension after the 2026 season seems like a no-brainer for the Bears. Thuney has been remarkably durable, but if in his mid-to-late 30s his body starts breaking down and the contract doesn’t age well, you don’t worry about that one bit. It’s still worth the contract to try to keep him around, and like it was stated previously, there are no signs that Thuney is slowing down or becoming less durable. There are plenty of offensive linemen that excel late into their careers. Trent Williams is still elite at 38. Lane Johnson is still elite at 36 (although you have to wonder if the body is starting to break down). There are plenty of examples. Heck, the Bears stabilized their line a few years ago when they brought in 40-year-old Jason Peters to play LT. If Thuney wants to play, you pay him. At 34 or 35, Thuney isn’t going to be looking to make a massive contract. He will want fair market pay, and I expect negotiations would go pretty smoothly. Joe Thuney should be a Bear as long as Joe Thuney wants to play football. There really isn’t any other argument that holds a grain of salt.

full_text: After two physical practices in full gear, the Chicago Bears were just in shorts and shells today. It was a shorter practice, including some walk-through in the red zone, but the crispness from the offense definitely picked up after a rough outing on Tuesday. “Caleb Williams in 7 on 7 drill today so far: 8/9 with TDs to Kyle Monangai, Luther Burden, Colston Loveland, and Kaden Davis,” per the Bear Report . “Very sharp in 7 on 7 today overall. Davis has been mentioned a few times during the first seven practices of camp, so he’s likely to be that “guy” this preseason. Even more so if the Bears share the video of today’s catch. Defensive end Dayo Odeyingbo is aware of the “Motivated Dayo” trend circulating on social media, and he laughed and said he was fine with it, saying , “It’s entertainment at the end of the day. That’s what football is about.” He added that rehabbing from an injury reminds him how much he wants to be out there and that “Being able to play football is a blessing.” Wideout Luther Burden III, who took a big shot yesterday, was at practice, and it was business as usual for him. Also, don’t forget that we’re just talking ’bout practice . A few other nuggets from the day. Left guard Joe Thuney and defensive tackle Grady Jarrett received veteran rest days today. With Thuney out, it was second-year pro Luke Newman filling in with the starters. ( link ) Braxton Jones had the bulk of the work at left tackle with the first string. title: Bears’ Offense Seeking Explosives Over Efficiency
summary: Bears Offensive Coordinator Press Taylor met with the media this morning before training camp practice and gave everyone a glimpse into the mind of Head Coach Ben Johnson, along with some other noteworthy mentions of some key players. “I don’t think Ben has ever mentioned the word efficiency. We talk about explosive. We are trying […]
full_text: Aug 5, 2026; Lake Forest, IL, USA; Chicago Bears offensive coordinator Press Taylor speaks during training camp at Halas Hall. Mandatory Credit: Kamil Krzaczynski-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Bears Offensive Coordinator Press Taylor met with the media this morning before training camp practice and gave everyone a glimpse into the mind of Head Coach Ben Johnson, along with some other noteworthy mentions of some key players. “I don’t think Ben has ever mentioned the word efficiency. We talk about explosive. We are trying to attack a defense,” Taylor said. “I think there’s a perception by a lot of people [that] we’re going to run the ball, we’re going to stay efficient, we’re going to control the clock. We are looking to attack a defense.” “We’re looking to attack fronts, to expose space, to create run lanes, to create explosives.” Taylor reiterated. “I mean, we don’t look at the run game as a way to stay on track. We look at the run game as a way to attack defenses and really be explosive and continue to just put our foot on the gas the entire game.” Our own Jeff Berckes recently wrote a spectacular piece on the topic of explosives, and after watching the Bears offense last season, it’s no surprise to hear that our head coach is relaying the message of importance to his entire staff. Last season, Chicago was one of the most explosive teams in the league despite being near the bottom in 2024. #NFL Offensive Explosive Play Rates 2025 Explosive Rush Leaders: BAL, CHI Explosive Pass Leaders: NE, BUF pic.twitter.com/2tw9zczHAA — SFdata9ers🏈📊 (@sfdata9ers) January 13, 2026 #NFL Explosive Play Rates 2024 Despite all the injuries, #SF remained an elite team in explosive plays on both sides of the ball. The #49ers finished the season with the 4th-highest offensive explosive play rate and the 3rd-lowest allowed on defense. pic.twitter.com/VigIpOOvgL — SFdata9ers🏈📊 (@sfdata9ers) January 8, 2025 As you can see from the charts above and in reading JB’s article, and as we all saw last season with Swift and Monangai, explosives are far more than flea-flickers and Hail-Mary’s. The run game can create chunk plays, which keep defenses honest and exploit mismatches. Which leads me to the two players Press highlighted. Cole Kmet and Darnell Wright. This is the second coach to praise Kmet’s team-first mentality and laud his behavior and leadership. Easy to see why for those that have followed Kmet his entire career, but important, no less. Especially with two very young tight ends in his position room. TE Cole Kmet epitomizes what this #Bears Offense and Team is all about. The value of his versatility is matched only by his selflessness. Watch the two clips below…. • Cole Kmet on wanting to win more than he wants the ball. • OC Press Taylor on just how important Cole is… pic.twitter.com/YimFfCWzw9 — Herb Howard (@HerbHoward411) August 5, 2026 Surely, selflessness and ability contribute to more explosive plays. Which brings me to our newly extended STUD of a right tackle, Darnell Wright. Coach Taylor referred to Wright as one of the team’s best players and admitted to wanting to feature him and get behind he and right guard Jonah Jackson, but admitted even when plays aren’t designed to go behind those two behemoths, that “the ball tends to find its way back there because of the things he does well.” For the first time in a long time, Bears fans not only have a roster capable of taking the top off the defense and putting points on the board, but also has a mindset among their coaches to be explosive. Every. Single. Play. Bear down, everyone.

title: Bengals training camp Day 7 discussion and news
summary: Many fans probably would have been shocked to hear that the defense is holding its own in training camp so far. There have even been days when defenders have dominated. The presence of defensive lineman Dexter Lawrence and safety Bryan Cook has really changed the feel of this entire defense. That isn’t to diminish players […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 27: Barrett Carter #49 and Demetrius Knight Jr. #44 of the Cincinnati Bengals hold up turkey after the game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on November 27, 2025 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Ishika Samant/Getty Images) | Getty Images Many fans probably would have been shocked to hear that the defense is holding its own in training camp so far. There have even been days when defenders have dominated. The presence of defensive lineman Dexter Lawrence and safety Bryan Cook has really changed the feel of this entire defense. That isn’t to diminish players like Boye Mafe constantly pressuring quarterback Joe Burrow. You can see how much the offense has to account for those guys, and also how easy it is for them to absolutely blow things up. It would be nice to see the offense go off more than a few plays during practice, but it’s safe to say most fans will take this change of pace. At least for now, that is. Bengals News Will Wagner Looks to Engineer Uneventful Year Two “I use my mechanical engineering degree pretty much every day in long snapping,” Wagner said in an interview while at Michigan. “In engineering, I have to know how matter is going to react if I put force in one place compared to another, and it’s the same in long snapping — how is the ball going to fly if I snap it one way versus another?” A very interesting look into the mind of a long snapper. If you have been a Bengals fan long enough you do not take for granted having a quality long snapper in the fold. Training Camp Report | New-Look Defense Turning Heads It was Carter who had a day Tuesday, playing downhill and, for the most part, helping bottle up an inside running game that had gouged holes the day before. Featuring some collisions with tight end Erick All Jr. as fullback. Knight was good, too, but Carter is the guy talking to Golden in his helmet before every play and getting them lined up. The defense as a whole had some really nice things to say about Barrett Carter and his performance so far in training camp. It is something fans will hope to see during the season. I sure I am not alone in that I would willingly eat crow if Carter turns things around. Bengals’ offensive players and coaches say Dexter Lawrence is dominating practices “There’s certain guys in this league like Dexter who wreck a whole game play and you have to do everything around them and you change everything you’re doing,” Risner said. “You’re going to have to change how you block against certain guys. He’s just making us do it really early and really often.” It certainly isn’t surprising to see Lawrence do these kinds of things. When the trade happened many were worried we might be getting a player on decline. It seems like that could not be further from the truth the way the offense is talking. Bengals Legend Anthony Muñoz Ranked Among 100 Greatest Players in NFL History The man truly deserves all the flowers he recieves. He was such a foundational piece over his career, and for too long, he was the only Bengals player in the Hall of Fame. Even though he has some company now, Muñoz will always be the player fans should think of when talking about the best Bengals of all-time. Who would you put on the Bengals Mount Rushmore?

title: Bengals safety Bryan Cook is embracing his leadership role
summary: At practice on Tuesday, cornerback DJ Turner was beaten deep by Ja’Marr Chase on what ended up being an incomplete pass. Turner didn’t have time to get down on himself because free-agent safety acquisition Bryan Cook was quickly by his side to give him a word of encouragement. Then, on the very next play, Boye […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals safety Bryan Cook (6) cheers after breaking up a play during practice at the Paycor Stadium practice facility in downtown Cincinnati on Tuesday, Aug. 4, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co At practice on Tuesday, cornerback DJ Turner was beaten deep by Ja’Marr Chase on what ended up being an incomplete pass. Turner didn’t have time to get down on himself because free-agent safety acquisition Bryan Cook was quickly by his side to give him a word of encouragement. Then, on the very next play, Boye Mafe, another free agent acquisition, beat Orlando Brown Jr. around the edge and forced Joe Burrow to throw an errant pass earlier than he wanted. Cook stepped in front of the pass, picked it off, and took it back for what would have been a touchdown had it been a real game. Later in the locker room, Cook reflected on the moment, showcasing his leadership, not only verbally, but with action. “For the most part, it’s just being aggressive, attention to detail, flying around, playing as one, and also being my brother’s keeper,” he said in the locker room after practice . “I know we’re all tired, but make a play. Any given moment, it could happen. I can be tired and have a great break at the post, and then Dexter Lawrence can get a sack. Things like that, it boosts the whole morale of a defense.” The Bengals’ defense has largely been to blame for the team missing the playoffs over the last two seasons. Sure, if they bounced their way one or two times in either season, they could have backed their way into the playoffs, but a team can win if they allow opposing teams to score 30 or more points as often as they did. This offseason, though, the Bengals’ front office took the big swing generations of fans have been asking for. They not only traded the No. 10 pick to the Giants for Lawrence, but they signed Cook, Mafe, Jonathan Allen and Kyle Dugger. Combined with this year’s draft class, the entire defense, except for linebacker, has been reshaped. With Cook’s leadership in the secondary and with the monster that is Lawrence soaking up blockers meant to get to linebackers, the defense will hopefully transform from a liability to a strength.

full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 16: Myles Murphy #99 of the Cincinnati Bengals pressures Mason Rudolph #2 of the Pittsburgh Steelers during the third quarter at Acrisure Stadium on November 16, 2025 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals went all-in on fixing their defense this offseason. Despite losing Trey Hendrickson to the Baltimore Ravens, the Bengals made several additions all across the defense to try to fix the unit that shouldered the blame for missing the postseason the last two seasons. Included in those acquisitions was pass rusher Boye Mafe, who was basically signed as a replacement for Hendrickson. They will also return 2025 first-round pick Shemar Stewart when he returns from his hyperextended knee suffered early in training camp. 2023 first-rounder Myles Murphy is also back and likely motivated after his fifth-year option wasn’t picked up. Also joining the rotation is rookie and former SEC Defensive Player of the Year, Cashius Howell. CBS Sports’ Carter Bahns isn’t very confident in the Cincinnati pass rush this season. He recently released his rankings of all 32 pass rush groups in the NFL and slotted the Bengals near the bottom of the league at 29th. “While the rest of the Bengals’ defense improved on paper this offseason, the edge rusher group said farewell to its leader, Trey Hendrickson. Mafe is an upside-oriented addition who will not fully replace Hendrickson’s pass-rushing prowess, but who displayed flashes of greatness as a young starter for the Seattle Seahawks. The rest of the crew, plus second-round pick Cashius Howell, is extremely young. Cincinnati is banking on its last few drafts starting to pay off. It just might pay dividends, but it is impossible to know for sure until it actually happens,“ Bahn wrote. To be fair, there are quite a few unknowns along the defensive front and specifically at pass rusher, but 29 still feels awfully low when you consider the drastic improvements to the interior defensive line. Dexter Lawrence II should draw a lot of double teams and free up pass rushers to get home. Preseason rankings are just that, preseason predictions. In just over a month, the Bengals’ defense will have a chance to change that narrative on the field.

title: Dexter Lawrence is already making life miserable for the Bengals’ offense, and they couldn’t be happier
summary: When the Cincinnati Bengals traded a first-round pick to acquire Dexter Lawrence this offseason, the expectation was that the three-time Pro Bowler would transform a defense that desperately needed a game-wrecker in the middle. One week into training camp, it sounds like that transformation is already underway. From Joe Burrow to Ja’Marr Chase to the offensive line […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - JULY 29: Dexter Lawrence II #97 of the Cincinnati Bengals signs autographs during the Cincinnati Bengals Training Camp at Kettering Health Practice Fields on July 29, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images When the Cincinnati Bengals traded a first-round pick to acquire Dexter Lawrence this offseason, the expectation was that the three-time Pro Bowler would transform a defense that desperately needed a game-wrecker in the middle. One week into training camp, it sounds like that transformation is already underway. From Joe Burrow to Ja’Marr Chase to the offensive line tasked with blocking him every day, the reviews have been remarkably consistent: Lawrence has been every bit as disruptive as advertised. And while it has made practices far more difficult for Cincinnati’s offense, it’s exactly the kind of challenge the Bengals believe will make them a better football team when the games begin. The loudest endorsement came from Chase, who didn’t mince words when describing the veteran defensive tackle’s impact. “Honestly, he’s been terrorizing practice,” Chase said, via Yahoo! Sports. “I can honestly say that.” That’s about as glowing a compliment as a wide receiver can give a defensive tackle. Joe Burrow has already felt Lawrence’s presence Burrow echoed that sentiment after practice when asked about the newest centerpiece of Cincinnati’s defensive front. The franchise quarterback admitted Lawrence has forced the offense to speed up its operation because the pocket simply doesn’t stay clean for very long. "Dex is just so big, he makes throwing over the middle a little more difficult." Joe Burrow has had to adjust to the addition of Dexter Lawrence on the Bengals' D-line 😂 🎤: @EvanWashburn pic.twitter.com/mOzDifZHq4 — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) August 3, 2026 As Burrow explained in the NFL on CBS interview clip via Evan Washburn, the offense has to “get that thing out” faster when Lawrence collapses the middle of the pocket, adding that the All-Pro defensive tackle has looked the part during the opening days of camp. It’s the type of praise that carries extra weight coming from one of the NFL’s premier quarterbacks. Burrow has faced elite interior defenders throughout his career, and Lawrence has quickly reminded everyone why he has long been considered among the league’s most dominant defensive tackles. The offensive line is embracing the challenge Perhaps no Bengal has had a tougher assignment than center Ted Karras, who has lined up across from Lawrence throughout camp. Rather than complain about the impossible task, Karras has welcomed it. Earlier this week, Karras called Lawrence “probably the best nose tackle in the last 30 years,” explaining that practicing against a player of that caliber every day will only sharpen Cincinnati’s offensive line heading into the season. He also compared the challenge to practicing against some of the dominant New England Patriots defenses from earlier in his career, saying Lawrence has immediately elevated the competitiveness of practice. Cincinnati offensive guard Dalton Risner echoed Karras’ sentiments about Lawrence’s presence through camp. “There’s certain guys in this league like Dexter who wreck a whole game play, and you have to do everything around them, and you change everything you’re doing,” Risner said, via Yahoo! Sports. “You’re going to have to change how you block against certain guys. “He’s just making us do it really early and really often.” That’s exactly what the Bengals envisioned when they made the blockbuster trade. A defense that suddenly looks different The Bengals spent much of the offseason overhauling a defense that struggled throughout 2025. Lawrence’s arrival has quickly become the centerpiece of that rebuild. Reports from camp have consistently highlighted a defense winning its share of team periods, with Lawrence creating havoc in both the running and passing game while helping open opportunities for the linebackers and edge rushers around him. That impact extends beyond the stat sheet. When elite offensive players like Burrow and Chase are openly talking about how disruptive one defender has been, it says plenty about what Lawrence has brought to Cincinnati. Offensive Coordinator Dan Pitcher added that Lawrence is a “nightmare” for units going up against “Sexy Dexy”. Training camp is designed to make teams uncomfortable. Through the first week, nobody has embodied that philosophy more than Dexter Lawrence. If his practice performances are any indication, opposing offenses may soon find themselves echoing the same sentiment Ja’Marr Chase delivered so succinctly: He’s been terrorizing people. “Better bring your f-ing shit when you’re going against Dexter Lawrence.” Ted Karras being tested daily against the stud DT. Karras compared it to going up against the 2016 Patriots in practice. pic.twitter.com/j2GMQscxmB — Mike Petraglia (@Trags) August 1, 2026

title: Buying Browns owner Jimmy Haslam’s optimism? Some are
summary: Front offices in professional sports will often be asked hard questions and, oftentimes, the front office will dodge those questions and give a response that is deemed “professional.” We’ve all heard the “coach speak.” Sports fans will ask for honesty and transparency from their favorite team, but nine times out of ten, it’s unlikely that […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JUNE 09: Executive vice president, football operations & general manager Andrew Berry of the Cleveland Browns talks with managing and principal partners Jimmy Haslam and Dee Haslam during the Cleveland Browns Mandatory Minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on June 09, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images Front offices in professional sports will often be asked hard questions and, oftentimes, the front office will dodge those questions and give a response that is deemed “professional.” We’ve all heard the “coach speak.” Sports fans will ask for honesty and transparency from their favorite team, but nine times out of ten, it’s unlikely that the fans will get that. The Cleveland Browns are entering Year 2 of a rebuild and, on paper, this team is nowhere near contention for a playoff spot. The looming QB question continues to be a concern for many. Despite that, Browns owner Jimmy Haslem spoke to the media a few days ago and gave interesting comments surrounding the team this season. As it stands, the Browns win total for the year is at 5.5 on multiple sports betting sites. Fans will likely roll their eyes at this statement, but Haslem seems to have some form of confidence that this Browns team will be better than last year. Jimmy Haslam and JW Johnson speaking to reporters after practice. Haslam: “I think the odds are for us to win 5.5 games. I’ll take the over.” pic.twitter.com/pyLh3Lkhpy — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) July 31, 2026 Haslem also gave another comment surrounding this season: Haslam: "We want to be a contending playoff team in ’27." Johnson: "I just want to say we're not punting on this season by any means. ’27, whatever, that's great. But we have high expectations for this team." https://t.co/7ny3kasJq4 — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) July 31, 2026 Ownership has a clear vision for the upcoming season, but they also have a clear vision for what this team wants to be the following season. Likely, their expectations are: 2026: Year 2 of a rebuild: Competitive but not contending 2027: Year 3 of a rebuild: Competitive, contending team in the AFC Ownership is not alone in having some confidence in taking the over on Cleveland’s win total: Jimmy Haslam would take the over on the Browns' projected win total of 5.5. It's not as crazy as it sounds. pic.twitter.com/co4mNVMNrE — PFT Live (@PFT_Live) August 3, 2026 It’s clear that the ownership wants to see noticeable progress for the team, but they also know that this team isn’t going to be in the playoff conversation this season. Trading star defensive end Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams might have sped up the team to potentially “punt” the season, but instead of selling, the team chose to retain key players. Cornerback Denzel Ward received a new extension; the same can be said for safety Grant Delpit. Considering that the Browns have an easier strength of schedule, the odds of the team winning more than 5.5 games are plausible; however, many things have to go their way for that to happen. Offensively, the unit has talent but major question marks; defensively, the unit lacks a true alpha, and head coach Todd Monken is entering his 1st year as a head coach. Rebuilding teams can often be ahead of schedule, as we’ve seen before, but don’t expect Cleveland to be one of those teams. It’s possible that this team is a fringe playoff contender next season, but this season expect more of what happened last season, even if they add a win or two. The team will not be good enough to be in playoff contention but not bad enough to be a top 3 team picking in the upcoming NFL Draft. Young, competitive, but just not good enough, just as Haslam seems to be alluding to. Join the conversation! title: Browns get a stray diss from current Eagles defender
summary: Seven days into the 2026 NFL free agency period, Cleveland Browns GM Andrew Berry signed a very good pass rusher in DE A.J. Epenesa away from the Buffalo Bills. The deal was for one-year at $5 million. At the time of the signing, it was assumed that the corner opposite Myles Garrett needed a dynamic […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - JULY 30: Philadelphia Eagles defensive end A.J. Epenesa #57 runs a drill during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on July 30th, 2026 at Jefferson Health Training Complex in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Seven days into the 2026 NFL free agency period, Cleveland Browns GM Andrew Berry signed a very good pass rusher in DE A.J. Epenesa away from the Buffalo Bills. The deal was for one-year at $5 million. At the time of the signing, it was assumed that the corner opposite Myles Garrett needed a dynamic pass rusher who was decent against the run but had a lot of presence in the opponent’s backfield. RELATED: BROWNS FEEL GOOD ABOUT DEFENSIVE END POSITION The signing got average grades of “B-.” Matt Warren, NFL Community Director for SB Nation and Buffalo Rumblings contributor, gave this note on the Epenesa signing: “Played significant snaps for the Bills. Seems cheap to me.” And so, it was assumed that Berry had gotten a good pass rusher who would compete for snaps with Alex Wright and Isaiah McGuire on that left side. Quality depth was about to come to Cleveland after the franchise lost DE Cameron Thomas to the Atlanta Falcons. Then, 11 days later, Cleveland decided to rescind the contract due to issues with the player when he visited the Berea facility and concerns after he took his physical, a source informed ESPN . After visiting the facility and undergoing a standard medical evaluation, team officials opted not to finalize the paperwork. Similar, but on a much smaller level, to the Baltimore Ravens rescinding their trade for DE Maxx Crosby. Epenesa had played six years in the NFL and was a second-round draft pick of the Bills in the 2020 NFL draft. His forte is being a pass rusher. Last year, he had only 2.5 sacks in 16 games played, but from 2022-2024, he had 19 combined sacks and 31 QB hits. Epenesa kicks the INT to himself! BUFvsCAR on FOX/FOX One https://t.co/HkKw7uXnxV pic.twitter.com/qx0HUbD2PN — NFL (@NFL) October 26, 2025 It generally surprised most folks when Cleveland backed out of the arrangement after being uncomfortable with the medical findings. It wasn’t like Epenesa had ended the 2025 season on any list or was injured in any way. He wasn’t. He appeared in all 17 regular-season games plus the playoffs. The Browns never really stated what the medical issue was with Epenesa. They just announced they had rescinded the deal, and that was that. It wasn’t like the franchise quoted the “Lemon Law” or anything. At the time, Epenesa called it “a weird situation.” On June 10, Epenesa signed with the Philadelphia Eagles but did not disclose terms other than that he inked a one-year deal. Now, Epenesa is discussing his brief time of almost being a Cleveland Brown : “I don’t necessarily want to go back and talk about that. I’ll just leave that in the past and just be happy that I’m not a Brown and that I’m an Eagle. Very healthy, feeling good, and happy to be here.“ Epenesa, age 27, appeared in 91 games over six seasons in Buffalo, including 19 starts.

title: Browns QB Dillon Gabriel quietly putting in the work at camp
summary: Cleveland Browns quarterback Dillon Gabriel has been the invisible man in the early days of training camp as the third man in a depressing two-man quarterback competition. Some of that is to be expected given that veteran Deshaun Watson is healthy enough to participate after missing all of last year with a twice-torn Achilles tendon. […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - AUGUST 03: Dillon Gabriel #6 of the Cleveland Browns throws a pass during the Cleveland Browns Training Camp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on August 03, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Cleveland Browns quarterback Dillon Gabriel has been the invisible man in the early days of training camp as the third man in a depressing two-man quarterback competition. Some of that is to be expected given that veteran Deshaun Watson is healthy enough to participate after missing all of last year with a twice-torn Achilles tendon. And Gabriel did not exactly light up the NFL in his six starts as a rookie, completing just 59.5 percent of his passes and seeing the Browns win just one of his starts. Gabriel was statistically better than fellow rookie Shedeur Sanders in just about every metric that matters, however, so one could begrudge him for feeling a bit left out with the spotlight shining so brightly on Watson and Sanders. But Gabriel does not seem wired that way, at least outwardly, as on Wednesday he said he never felt “disrespected” and that he understands the NFL is a business. He also spoke confidently about being able to pick up what head coach Todd Monken wants from the offense given the similarities to what Gabriel ran in college (quote via a team-provided transcript): “I don’t think picking up an offense has ever been a problem for me. I think conceptually, if you see it, a lot of people are on the same (stuff); it’s just how you call it and how you get to things. In man versus zone, or a two-high one-high, do you want an all-call where you can play it split field on one play, or do you want to get to a premier play where there are multiple winners against a certain coverage? “I think I take that kind of attitude toward it, plus my time with Coach (Dan) Lanning — whatever that Georgia tree is — and Coach Monken being there, I think there’s some similarities. Even in practice and how we’ve seen our offense, it’s kind of similar to Oregon.” Being comfortable in the offense could conceivably give Gabriel a leg up on the competition, and the fact that he is going about his business has not gone unnoticed by Monken, as he explained on Wednesday : “One thing Dillon does a really good job of is he’s very even-keeled. First of all, he’s got a great personality; he’s fun to be around. You wouldn’t know it unless you’ve been around him. He seems stoic, but no, he’s actually very funny, has a great personality, and he’s handled this situation with unbelievable class. “Every player wants to compete, and he hasn’t really had the opportunity in terms of the number of reps. He’s had a chance to compete just with a different number of reps. So, I think he’s done an unbelievable job that way, and for the lack of reps, he does a great job carrying over the meetings to the field. He does a great job with a limited amount of reps, which is a credit to him.” The competition to be the Week 1 starter for the Browns will still likely come down to Watson or Sanders unless something drastic happens between now and the opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars. But given that this is the Browns, they will likely need multiple quarterbacks once again this fall, and Gabriel staying ready could pay off for him at some point before the end of the regular season.

title: Unexpected surprises at Cowboys training camp
summary: The Dallas Cowboys have now completed one week of training camp out in Oxnard. It hasn’t just been the California sun that has shined, but also several players and position groups are looking extremely sharp right out of the gate. Dak Prescott is already looking in mid-season form as the 11-year veteran has been wheeling […]
full_text: OXNARD, CALIFORNIA - JULY 30: Javonte Williams #33 of the Dallas Cowboys runs with the ball during training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields on July 30, 2026 in Oxnard, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys have now completed one week of training camp out in Oxnard. It hasn’t just been the California sun that has shined, but also several players and position groups are looking extremely sharp right out of the gate. Dak Prescott is already looking in mid-season form as the 11-year veteran has been wheeling and dealing on a daily basis. Rookie safety Caleb Downs is everything that people said he was, and his versatility is going to bring a different element to what the Cowboys do defensively under Christian Parker. Also, Qunnien Williams and Kenny Clark are showing how disruptive they can be. While all those things are great to see, they aren’t shockers by any means. However, there been several things that have stood out that most people didn’t see coming. Let’s take a look at three surprises so far at camp. Several RBs are having great camps early Javonte Williams is the undisputed RB1 in Dallas. Don’t tell him that though, because he’s been playing with his hair on fire. He looks explosive running between the tackles, and he’s even been featured in the screen game, which is something that head coach Brian Schottenheimer talked about before camp. With that said, he’s not alone. Jaydon Blue didn’t have the rookie season he wanted in 2025, but he has put that in his rear view. He looks very confident in what he’s doing, and his speed has been on full display with several huge plays so far. Add Phil Mafah’s name to this as well. He worked on his explosiveness during the offseason, and positive results have come about already. Williams had a very good season a year ago with over 1,200 yards, proving that he can be a bell-cow. Dallas needs for him to be fresh at the end of ball games, and the best way to do that is having other reliable options. Blue and Mafah are showing early that this group has the potential to cause a lot of headaches for opposing defenses. Jaishawn Barham looks ahead of schedule Jaishawn Barham was picked in the third round by Dallas back in April, and there was buzz about what he could potentially bring to the Cowboys revamped defense. None if that mattered until he got camp, which is when he would really have to prove if he wanted early playing time. Not only is he showing that he’s going to be a big factor, but Barham looks like a guy who has already been in the league for years. The former Michigan Wolverine has shined in individual drills and during team periods against the likes of All-Pro guard Tyler Smith and the aforementioned Blue. He brings linebacker and edge skills to the table, and Parker intends to take full advantage of that versatility in his philosophy. Needless to say, Barham is undoubtedly ahead of where people thought he’d be right now. Otito Ogbonnia is standing out The Cowboys decided to trade defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa to the San Francisco 49ers on March 11th. The day before that, they added Ogbonnia to the roster, who played in 41 games with 20 starts over his four years with the Los Angeles Chargers. He has some injury history, including missing eight games with an elbow issue last season. Ogbonnia also has a reputation for stopping the run, and its been no different in camp. In the Cowboys base look, Ogbonnia has been on the field with Qunnien Williams and Kenny Clark, and the trio have been effective consistently. Stopping the run has been a huge issue for Dallas over the years, and Ogbonnia and his 6’4″, 320-pound frame can be a big difference maker. It wasn’t a flashy signing, but Ogbonnia could end up being an impact offseason addition in Dallas.

summary: We are a week into training camp. So far, the Dallas Cowboys have had five practices, and two of them have been with pads on. full_text: OXNARF, CA - JULY 28: Workers drive a cart while setting up for the opening of Dallas Cowboys training camp on Tuesday, July 28, 2026, in Oxnard, Calif. (Smiley N. Pool/The Dallas Morning News via Getty Images) We are a week into training camp. So far, the Dallas Cowboys have had five practices, and two of them have been with pads on. Even during this brief window, we have some answers to some of the many questions we had going into camp. Today we’ll explore a few of those answers. Caleb Downs is a student of the game This may not come as a surprise but the rookie from Ohio State, who received rave reviews from past coaches including Nick Saban, is as studious and focused as advertised. Typically, rookies have growing pains, and while Downs hasn’t been perfect, usually the types of mistakes that are endured when bringing a first-year pro along are those that happen when teaching a rookie a pro system and bone-headed errors that usually take weeks to iron out. Yet, Downs has received nothing but rave reviews for his work ethic and focus, particularly from his head coach, Brian Schottenheimer. TRENDING: Caleb Downs has been a NIGHTMARE for the Cowboys offense. One NFL scout reportedly believes Downs “showcases” similar abilities to Ed Reed (Former Ravens S). The Cowboys rookie safety is going to be a PROBLEM in this league 🔒😳 pic.twitter.com/zomo2IqXSS — Rookie Watch (@RookieWatxh) August 5, 2026 As we continue to progress in camp and see some field action in the preseason, Cowboys fans can only be hopeful that Downs is going to be everything they had wished for (if he plays). The secondary is much improved The secondary unit was terrible last year. Between the entire secondary, only four interceptions were secured by this position group in 2025. In the offseason, the Cowboys addressed these concerns by bringing in the likes of Cobie Durant and Jalen Thompson and, as mentioned earlier, drafting the highly touted Downs in the first round, along with hiring new defensive coordinator Christian Parker, who is also receiving rave reviews from players and coaches alike. Now, as practice gets underway, we’ve gotten a glimpse of this unit in action, and the difference seems to be night and day from last year, both in production on the practice field and in intensity. Watch two things closely: 1. Dak no-looked the throw 2. Cobie Durants instincts beat what otherwise would have been an easy Touchdown Imma say it again… GIVE CHRISTIAN PARKER the keys to the city if a healthy & effective Daron Bland is the 3rd best CB on this Cowboys… pic.twitter.com/vO3dRmUrw4 — Landon Holifield ✭ (@TheLandoShow) August 5, 2026 Durant, Daron Bland and Shavon Revel have been sticky and have made plays, and they’ll need that, along with the fiery attitudes they’ve shown thus far in practice, to make the leaps necessary to turn this unit into a quality unit in 2026. Tyler Guyton is the Cowboys’ starting left tackle Yes, most of us could see right through Schottenheimer’s shrewd motivational tactic when he “opened up” the left tackle position for competition. Even still, given Guyton’s struggles in his first few years, it seemed the competition might be open. Nope, the door was slammed shut on that Tuesday, August 4. Now, again, there may not have been much of a competition between Guyton and seventh-round pick Nate Thomas. Guyton still had to do enough to secure the nomination from Schottenheimer, which isn’t nothing. The Cowboys have an opportunity to put together what could be a special offensive unit in 2026. Guyton, along with fellow offensive tackle Terence Steele, is one of the linchpins for whether or not GOTI (Greatest Offense There Is) is. title: 3 players pushing for a roster spot at Cowboys training camp
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are at training camp and some of the players have given the coaches a lot to think about so far. There are a few who need a really strong camp to even have a shot at being considered for the team. Some of that has been the result of circumstances out of […]
full_text: May 1, 2026; Frisco, TX, USA; Dallas Cowboys tight end Michael Trigg (46) goes through a drill during practice at the Ford Center at the Star Training Facility in Frisco, Texas. Mandatory Credit: Chris Jones-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Cowboys are at training camp and some of the players have given the coaches a lot to think about so far. There are a few who need a really strong camp to even have a shot at being considered for the team. Some of that has been the result of circumstances out of their control, and sometimes it’s their own efforts. Next Saturday the team plays its first game of the preseason, and it presents a chance for the fringe players to shine. Who are the fringe guys that have impressed so far? Furthermore, who are the players that are taking advantage of a fast start to make moves toward earning a spot on the roster? Here are the players who are angling for a spot on the team. Michael Trigg Following the draft, Michael Trigg signed with the Cowboys as an undrafted free agent. Dallas signed Trigg to a three-year contract worth up to $3.1M. Trigg was a finalist for the Mackey Award and was named an All-American in his final year at Baylor. Trigg is more like a big wide receiver than a traditional tight end. Because of this, he is a mismatch for linebackers and a handful for them to keep up with him in coverage. He has flashed his talents at training camp, and everyone is starting to take notice. The Michael Trigg hype train is off and running pic.twitter.com/QUsZ5nunYN — RJ Ochoa (@rjochoa) August 3, 2026 The Cowboys also got word that fellow tight end Princeton Fant went down with a season-ending knee injury. Fant may have already been on the fringe, but his absence opens a door that Trigg’s talent could see him run through. With Fant out of the picture, Trigg is going to get extended looks to build on what he’s already done. Two solid preseason games, and the Cowboys may not want to risk losing him. Sam Williams Although Sam Williams has been a part of the team since 2022, it’s very clear that nothing will be guaranteed to him. Williams rejoined the Cowboys on a one-year contract with a base salary of only $1.4M. Obviously, the team has much more invested in the players ahead of him on the roster. To the detriment of the team but also to the benefit of Williams for the time being, the collective pass rush hasn’t done so well. This has allowed Williams to stand out from the rest of the pack. Williams has terrific athleticism relative to the edge rusher position. We have seen him showcase his talents as a gunner and, at times in camp, has looked fairly good in coverage. Sam Williams meets Jaydon Blue in the backfield pic.twitter.com/jIoYArkkLt — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 4, 2026 Sam Williams vs Drew Shelton pic.twitter.com/6898cHCJH3 — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 4, 2026 Williams and James Houston appear locked into a hotly contested roster battle, and Houston had a solid day Monday as well as picked up a sack in practice. Williams can earn a spot not only by his own merits but also in some part by default if others don’t step it up to keep serve with Williams. Now in his fifth year, if the lights do come on for him, it could be the perfect time for the team and for Williams. Curtis Robinson Curtis Robinson hasn’t played much in the NFL since going undrafted in 2021. He’s mostly maintained his spot in the NFL as a core special teams player. Yet, the Cowboys have given him a little more responsibility. He, along with others, has been entrusted with wearing the defensive green dot to relay defensive signals to the defense. Unlike his other linebacker counterparts like Justin Barron, for example, he has a little more in-game experience on defense and has logged a lot of time on special teams coverage. PICK-6! Curtis Robinson takes it to the 🏠 Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/8P3YGE8sAT — NFL (@NFL) August 24, 2025 That alone has given him a leg up on the competition as he battles for one of the lower spots on the depth chart. There’s still a long way to go, but if Robinson can stay the course and continue to validate the coaches’ faith in his cognitive abilities, he might make it out of camp with a roster spot.

title: Why the Cowboys left tackle battle is over
summary: Tyler Guyton is the left tackle for the Dallas Cowboys. This has always been the hope since he was selected late in the first round of the 2024 NFL draft, and his job security was brought into question after head coach Brian Schottenheimer announced in early June that the position was up for grabs between […]
full_text: Tyler Guyton is the left tackle for the Dallas Cowboys. This has always been the hope since he was selected late in the first round of the 2024 NFL draft, and his job security was brought into question after head coach Brian Schottenheimer announced in early June that the position was up for grabs between Guyton and Nate Thomas. For now, the decision has been made with the former Oklahoma tackle keeping the starting spot. The left tackle position has been a little up in the air for the last couple of months, with lingering factors creating uncertainty. Most of which stems from the availability and progress of Guyton. He’s dealt with injuries in each of his first two seasons in the league, and when he has played, he hasn’t shown enough consistency to give the coaching staff confidence that he is the long-term plan at the position. Thomas’ name was thrown into the hat after a promising debut last season. A seventh-round pick in the same draft as Guyton, Thomas missed his entire rookie season dealing with knee tendinitis, landing him on injured reserve. He returned last year and played all 17 games, including making four starts when Guyton got hurt. He put together a decent rookie campaign, showing good things as a run blocker, but he also struggled in pass protection. He allowed 23 pressures, three sacks, and four penalties. A promising start made this a supposed open battle to start the camp as the coaching staff initially planned to evaluate both tackles in four-day cycles. This evaluation period was short-lived as the team appears to have already made its decision. Thomas showed some nice spurts, but Schottenheimer stated that he wasn’t showing enough consistency. His ongoing struggles with pass protection have created enough separation between him and Guyton, making the choice easy for the coaching staff. It’s not just the fading of Thomas that’s driving this decision. Guyton has looked impressive in camp. The coaches have praised him for his technical growth, and it has shown up in his performance over these first training camp practices. His footwork has looked sharp. He’s popping out quickly, setting well in his stance, and showing a lot more control and balance. He’s putting himself in good spots early and has shown nice leverage on several reps in camp. These improvements are huge for Guyton. His dedication is noted as he returned to the weight room in early February. His hand punching and physical power have been evident as he’s been seen driving defenders back. All the signs are pointing to him finally turning a corner this season. Guyton was selected on Day 1 because of his elite athletic traits accompanying his prototypical frame of an NFL left tackle. The potential has always been there, but he just hasn’t made the right strides in his development to be a player one can count on to protect the blindside of your franchise quarterback. But now these strides are more evident, and things are looking up for the Cowboys’ young offensive tackle. I don't care what anyone says. I believe Tyler Guton will be special this year. Not just good but special. He looks amazing. I see change. Real change. He already had the heart and work ethic!!!! Year 3 blow up coming. pic.twitter.com/vP6k7mDZKJ — Boss *Show Me (@BossCowboySport) August 4, 2026
