summary: One thing is for certain for the Dallas Cowboys, second-year running back Jaydon Blue is on a mission to be a contributor after a rough rookie campaign. Linebackers DeMarvion Overshown and rookie Jaishawn Barham are having good training camps, and the versatility of both will be used a lot in 2026. Christian Parker is gearing […]
full_text: Jun 16, 2026; Dallas, TX, USA; Dallas Cowboys running back Jaydon Blue (23) goes through a drill during practice at the Ford Center at the Star Training Facility in Frisco, Texas. Mandatory Credit: Chris Jones-Imagn Images | Chris Jones-Imagn Images One thing is for certain for the Dallas Cowboys, second-year running back Jaydon Blue is on a mission to be a contributor after a rough rookie campaign. Linebackers DeMarvion Overshown and rookie Jaishawn Barham are having good training camps, and the versatility of both will be used a lot in 2026. Christian Parker is gearing up for his first year of calling plays as a defensive coordinator, and according to him, his unit is taking the right steps. Ryan Flournoy is the WR3 in Dallas, but he’s poised to elevate his play this year. Here’s your Cowboys’ news for Thursday. Cowboys’ Jaydon Blue understands his Year 2 assignment: ‘I took the lessons to heart’ – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com Jaydon Blue had high expectations as a rookie, but things didn’t go as planned for multiple reasons. Now, he’s ready to be a difference maker in 2026. “I’m just [focused on] stacking these good days out here,” said Blue, following the second Cowboys’ padded practice in which he shined again. “I’ve just been more intentional. Like I said, this offseason, my main priority was making sure that I stayed in the playbook and was doing things that the coach was asking me to do.” Cowboys MLB DeMarvion Overshown has rave reviews for new DC Christian Parker at training camp – SportsDay Staff, Dallas Morning News Christian Parker has a lot of support in his defensive coordinator position, but it is his first year calling plays. However, linebacker DeMarvion Overshown says believe the hype. DeMarvion Overshown: “He’s a competitor, just like us. He feels like he’s putting on a helmet and shoulder pads as well when we come out here to get ready for practice. In meeting rooms, he’s challenging us to know what the rest of the defense is doing, like he wants everyone to be able to think like they’re a coach out there. What stood out after Cowboys’ padded practices? 2 players who could elevate the offense – Jon Machota, The Athletic The Cowboys have one of the top offenses in the NFL. It may be even better this season if a few players take a leap. Ryan Flournoy Everyone knows the importance of CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens to Dallas’ passing game. But Flournoy has shown that he’s ready to build on what he did after his breakout performance in Week 5 last year against the New York Jets. In 16 games last season, Flournoy had 40 catches for 475 yards and four touchdowns. He’s got a chance to be closer to the 700-800 yard range this season as Dallas’ clear No. 3 wide receiver. Christian Parker pleased with Cowboys defense’s progress early in training camp – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com The Cowboys had one of the worst defenses in team history in 2025. This prompted them to hire Christian Parker as their new defensive coordinator, and things are running smoothly so far in training camp. “I think we’re embracing the play style that we want to stay with,” Parker said. “I think guys are really just trying to harp on the details and get the next level of knowledge to the defense that we’re really focusing on. We talked about getting your undergraduate degree in OTAs, and now we’re working towards our masters. That’s more of an accelerated program, so we’ve got to get going quick. The guys are doing a great job.” It looks like the Dallas Cowboys have a secret pass rushing weapon, and they’re showing it in training camp – Mauricio Rodriguez, AtoZ Sports Dallas didn’t blitz linebacker DeMarvion Overshown that much last season like they did in 2024 under Mike Zimmer. Christian Parker wants to take advantage of that part of his game again. There’s still plenty to figure out with Overshown. The biggest question remains whether he can play middle linebacker with the physicality the position requires. Can he take on climbing offensive linemen at the second level, something far more common at MIKE than at weakside linebacker where he had more open space to operate? There was a play earlier this week where left tackle Tyler Guyton climbed to the second level and swallowed Overshown whole. That part of his game remains to be answered. But one thing is clear: Overshown as a blitzer is back. Cowboys rookie Jaishawn Barham’s versatility becoming a ‘cheat code’ for Christian Parker – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News Jaishawn Barham has done a nice job making himself known at training camp. He played both linebacker and edge at Michigan, and defensive coordinator Christian Parker is salivating over he’s versatility. “Him playing both is one of his cheat codes that he has,” Parker said. “He’s played equal amount of snaps almost at Maryland and Michigan [at inside linebacker], so he’s been exposed to it. So it’s not like he’s seeing things that he hasn’t seen before from that perspective. … I think that he is a fast processor.” Daily discussion question: How much will you watch of the HOF game?

title: Christian Parker takeaways so far at Oxnard
summary: When the Cowboys hired Christian Parker as defensive coordinator, they weren’t just seeking a new coach. They wanted someone capable of rebuilding a defense that finished 2025 as one of the NFL’s worst units, while also developing a young secondary packed with potential. Just over a week into training camp in Oxnard means it’s still […]
full_text: Jul 29, 2026; Oxnard, CA, USA; Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker at training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect When the Cowboys hired Christian Parker as defensive coordinator, they weren’t just seeking a new coach. They wanted someone capable of rebuilding a defense that finished 2025 as one of the NFL’s worst units, while also developing a young secondary packed with potential. Just over a week into training camp in Oxnard means it’s still early, but many of the first signs have been extremely encouraging. Christian Parker coaching up Cobie Durant and Daron Bland #Dallascowboys pic.twitter.com/vltsKrsspK — Nicole Hutchison (@nhutchisontv) August 1, 2026 The biggest takeaway has been how quickly players have embraced Parker’s coaching style. Rather than creating a passive practice environment, Parker has encouraged constant competition between the offense and defense. Players have described practices as iron sharpening iron, with the defense feeding off the challenge of facing Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens every day. That competitive atmosphere has noticeably increased the energy level of camp and has created an environment where every rep matters. Sam Williams sniffing out the Jaydon Blue run #Dallascowboys pic.twitter.com/MrNud6i100 — Nicole Hutchison (@nhutchisontv) August 4, 2026 KaVontae Turpin vs. Shavon Revel pic.twitter.com/XQeDKZZcAu — Jon Machota (@jonmachota) August 4, 2026 One of the first things that stands out about Christian Parker’s defense is the importance he places on communication. Every player in the secondary is expected to know not only their own assignment but also how the coverage changes based on motion, formations and offensive adjustments. That has created a defense where players are constantly talking before the snap instead of waiting for the play to unfold. Parker’s experience developing defensive backs is showing through the way Dallas is using its personnel, with safeties and cornerbacks moving into different roles rather than being limited to a single position. Rookie Caleb Downs has been one of the biggest examples of that flexibility, spending time as a deep safety, working closer to the line of scrimmage and lining up in the slot depending on the situation. Malachi Lawrence with the pressure, Caleb Downs with the near INT. The two first round picks on the play. pic.twitter.com/S9UJDcgSQE — Joseph Hoyt (@JoeJHoyt) August 1, 2026 The secondary has arguably been the biggest success story of camp so far. After struggling through much of last season, the defensive backfield has looked far more confident and competitive in Oxnard. Shavon Revel is slowly showing why the Cowboys are so excited about his future by matching receivers physically throughout practice, while DaRon Bland looks fully recovered and back to playing with the instincts that made him one of the league’s most dangerous ballhawks. Cobie Durant has wasted little time making an impression after arriving in Dallas, and Julius Wood has consistently shown his willingness to play downhill and finish through contact. Those performances carried into the first padded practice, where the defensive backs repeatedly challenged throws, closed passing windows and highlighted the day with Durant’s interception in the red zone. Cobie Durant downfield PBU pic.twitter.com/Gj8rp3xDhN — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 4, 2026 pic.twitter.com/oXoBKFyU2O — Clarence Hill Jr (@clarencehilljr) August 5, 2026 Another encouraging development has been how comfortable the entire group already looks despite learning a new defensive system. Mistakes that often accompany a scheme change have been relatively limited, with the secondary playing faster because players appear confident in what they are being asked to do, and that’s thanks to the work Parker has done preparing the guys upfront. Rather than making tackles after completions, defenders have frequently been in position to contest passes before receivers can secure the football. The safety group has also demonstrated far more flexibility, regularly changing responsibilities based on offensive looks instead of remaining in static alignments. Parker’s personality has also left an impression on the practice field. He coaches with energy, demands attention to detail and isn’t afraid to hold players accountable when standards aren’t met or things fall out of line, we’re looking at you Donovan Ezeiruaku. At the same time, he’s quick to celebrate effort, turnovers and winning reps, creating a competitive atmosphere that has spread throughout the defense. His message has been simple from the start, improvement has to happen every day, because standing still means falling behind Donovan Ezeiruaku was pulled from practice by Brian Schottenheimer after getting into it with Terence Steele. He spoke with Will McClay for a moment before Todd Williams walked him off the field. pic.twitter.com/RhPIGKAhEY — Bobby Belt (@BobbyBeltTX) August 4, 2026 Even with all the positive signs, there is still plenty of work to do. Training camp practices can only reveal so much, and preseason games will provide the first real opportunity to see how the defense performs against unfamiliar opponents and how the down roster guys can find a place on the defense. The Cowboys’ offense has still produced explosive plays at times, particularly when Prescott has been well protected, reminding everyone that the installation process is far from complete. The next step for Parker’s unit will be proving that the communication, versatility and aggressive style on display in Oxnard translate once the games begin to count. Caleb Downs and Christian Parker getting in some work after practice pic.twitter.com/ra1Tt9l1En — Jon Machota (@jonmachota) August 1, 2026 Even so, the early signs are difficult to ignore. The secondary looks more connected, younger players are developing rapidly, veterans appear fully invested in Parker’s message, and the overall energy surrounding the defense feels dramatically different from a year ago. If those trends continue once the games begin, the Cowboys may finally have found the defensive leader capable of unlocking a defense that should hold its own and create one of the most talented secondaries they’ve assembled in years. Dak Prescott and Christian Parker sharing some laughs before practice pic.twitter.com/hF3xcVNy1d — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) July 30, 2026

title: Malik Davis is falling behind in Cowboys’ RB competition

He has quickness and can see the hole quickly. — Todd Archer (@toddarcher) August 3, 2026 I think this was Israel Abanikanda https://t.co/0HvQk2qMAN — Tom Downey (@WhatGoingDowney) August 4, 2026 Davis has been down this road before. In fact, four times before. While Davis always looks solid with the ball in his hands, it’s never been enough to outshine some of the other RBs in camp. In his early years, Davis kept losing out to Rico Dowdle because he couldn’t match Dowdle’s abilities as a blocker and special teamer. Unfortunately for him, Davis’ blocking woes have already been on display this summer. Probably a sack from Shemar James here vs Malik Davis. https://t.co/VDQB96ccSG — Mauricio Rodríguez (@MauNFL) August 3, 2026 Turning 28 this November, Davis is obviously not a developmental guy anymore. He has to be clearly better than these younger prospects, probably winning the RB2 job outright if he wants to make the roster. But with Blue off to a hot start in camp and guys like Abanikanda and Mafah also showing well, it’s hard to imagine Davis faring any better in this camp than he has in the ones before it. It’s going to sting for fans who rightfully developed a soft spot for Davis after last year’s heroics. Finding his way back on the roster after Miles Sanders’ injury and Blue’s delayed development, Davis had a big play in Dallas’ Thanksgiving victory over Kansas City, then led the rushing attack in the Christmas win over Washington. In front of huge national audiences, Davis shined and did a lot to raise his profile, at least with Cowboys fans. Still, for the last four years, the Cowboys have consistently decided not to put Malik Davis on the 53 unless injuries forced their hand. As long as the RB room doesn’t have a sudden run of bad medical luck, we seem to be trending in that direction again in 2026. It’s going to sting for some, but we can find comfort in the probability that Davis’ fall means younger guys with broader skills are moving up the ladder, and hopefully improving Dallas’ overall depth at running back.

title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 39
summary: It is Day 39 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA - NOVEMBER 8: Quarterback Tony Romo #9 of the Dallas Cowboys scrambles during the game against the Philadelphia Eagles on November 8, 2009 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The Cowboys won 20-16. (Photo by Drew Hallowell/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is Day 39 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. Get ready Cowboys fans for Day 39 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit an exorcism game for an entire generation of Cowboys fans. Dallas entered the 2009 postseason carrying 13 years of January frustration, six consecutive playoff defeats and all the baggage attached to Tony Romo’s previous postseason failures. By the end of the night, none of that mattered. Saturday, January 9, 2010 — 8:00 p.m. ET Cowboys Stadium, Arlington, Texas Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 34, Philadelphia Eagles 14 The matchup itself felt unusual because the teams had played in the same stadium only six days earlier. Dallas had shut out Philadelphia 24-0 in the regular-season finale to win the NFC East, dropping the Eagles from a potential first-round bye to the sixth seed. That created an immediate rematch in the Wild Card round, with Philadelphia returning to Arlington and insisting the previous result would not be repeated. The first quarter ended scoreless, but Dallas had already established control through long possessions and defensive pressure. The Cowboys finally broke through early in the second quarter after a deep throw toward Miles Austin drew a 40-yard pass-interference penalty against Sheldon Brown. From the one-yard line, Romo found reserve tight end John Phillips for the opening touchdown and a 7-0 lead. Philadelphia answered almost immediately. Andy Reid brought Michael Vick into the game, and Vick launched a deep pass to rookie Jeremy Maclin. Cornerback Mike Jenkins lost his footing, allowing Maclin to complete a 76-yard touchdown that tied the score at 7-7. It was the Eagles’ first meaningful offensive success against Dallas in nearly six quarters, but it did not change the direction of the game for long. The Cowboys responded with an impressive 85-yard drive, showcasing their composure. However, an apparent Philadelphia interception was overturned on replay, revealing that the ball had hit the ground, thus preserving the drive. Romo then orchestrated crucial gains by finding Jason Witten and Patrick Crayton. Tashard Choice capped off the drive with a one-yard touchdown run, giving Dallas the lead at 14-7. The Eagles were unable to recover and ultimately lost the game. The second quarter became increasingly lopsided. Crayton returned a punt 31 yards, and Romo quickly connected with Austin for 36 yards, putting Dallas in scoring range. Shaun Suisham’s 25-yard field goal gave the Cowboys a 17-7 lead. On Philadelphia’s next possession, Vick mishandled an exchange with Leonard Weaver, leading to Bobby Carpenter recovering at the Eagles’ 18-yard line. Three plays later, Romo found Austin for a six-yard touchdown, extending Dallas’s lead to 24-7. Before halftime, the Eagles gave the ball away again. Bradie James forced a fumble from Weaver and recovered it at the Philadelphia 42. Suisham converted from 48 yards as time expired, completing a 27-point second quarter and sending Dallas into halftime with a commanding 27-7 lead. In just under 14 minutes, the Cowboys had turned a tied rivalry game into a rout. Any remaining doubt vanished midway through the third quarter. Felix Jones took a handoff, burst through the right side, and outran the Philadelphia secondary for a 73-yard touchdown. This run gave Dallas a commanding 34-7 lead and solidified its status as the longest rushing touchdown in Cowboys postseason history. Jones’ performance was nothing short of spectacular, finishing the night with 148 yards on just 16 carries, impressively averaging over nine yards per attempt. The Cowboys finished with 426 total yards, including 198 on the ground, while forcing four Philadelphia turnovers. Dallas possessed the ball for more than 39 minutes and scored on five consecutive second-quarter possessions. It was not a fortunate escape or a narrow breakthrough. It was complete control of a division rival on the postseason stage. This game belongs on the countdown because it released years of pressure. The Cowboys hadn’t won a playoff game since December 1996, and every postseason failure since then had added another layer of frustration. Romo had carried the team through the 2006 snap disaster and the home defeat to the Giants in 2007. Wade Phillips had faced his own questions about winning in January. Although beating Philadelphia didn’t erase everything that followed, for one night, Dallas looked like a genuine contender and finally stopped living under the weight of its postseason drought. #Cowboys vs #Eagles 2009 Wildcard Round Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 34, Philadelphia Eagles 14 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/rO5WXQZLAb — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) August 5, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game This was the first playoff game played at Cowboys Stadium, which had opened at the beginning of the 2009 season. The announced crowd of 92,951 was, at the time, the largest attendance for an NFL postseason game outside of the Super Bowl. title: Jake Ferguson shines in second padded practice
summary: Jake Ferguson had a very productive 2025 season for the Dallas Cowboys. In fact, he had his best year overall as his 82 receptions and eigth touchdowns were both career highs, and his 600 yards were the second most most he’s produced. Unfortunately, he also had three fumbles, which gave him seven over a two-year […]

(Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jake Ferguson had a very productive 2025 season for the Dallas Cowboys. In fact, he had his best year overall as his 82 receptions and eigth touchdowns were both career highs, and his 600 yards were the second most most he’s produced. Unfortunately, he also had three fumbles, which gave him seven over a two-year span, and his 7.3 per catch were a career low. Despite undoubtedly being the top tight end on the team, Ferguson came into training camp needing to show that he put his up-and-down season behind him. On Tuesday, he was one of the best performers at practice Ferguson was able to make several good plays in the passing game. One of them was a beautiful seam ball he caught in front of cornerback Shavon Revel. His biggest play of the day yardage-wise saw Ferguson turn on the jets with rookie safety Caleb Downs trailing. To top it off, Ferguson also beat safety Markquese Bell for a touchdown in the back of the end zone after a beautiful throw from Dak Prescott. SeamGod. 4 to 87. #Cowboys pic.twitter.com/sRbgOpNXaB — Patrik [No C] Walker (@VoiceOfTheStar) August 4, 2026 Jake Ferguson pic.twitter.com/F009CG8wga — Jon Machota (@jonmachota) August 4, 2026 Dak finds Jake Ferguson in the back of the end zone pic.twitter.com/ruWLRRpFFd — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 3, 2026 His name doesn’t get the needle moving like CeeDee Lamb or George Pickens, but Ferguson is a key element to the Cowboys’ passing game. The threat to make plays in the middle of the field helps Lamb and Pickens carve up opposing defenses and also gives Ryan Flournoy opportunities to eat. Ferguson is a chain mover as he’s racked up 95 first downs over the last three seasons. Ferguson looks more explosive so far in camp. Granted, he’s not a burner or anything, but adding a little quickness can certainly make him a bigger weapon. He’s in the second year of his four-year, $52 million deal, and after somewhat mixed results a season ago, Ferguson is looking to remind Dallas why they extended him last July.

title: 3 questions that have developed at Cowboys training camp
summary: The Dallas Cowboys have done some good things to start training camp. The stars of camp have been the usual suspects, but others have been breaking into the spotlight, especially some of the rookies. When players that you aren’t counting on to contribute immediately start showing up, it’s like finding hidden money. Yet, there are […]
full_text: May 1, 2026; Frisco, TX, USA; Dallas Cowboys linebacker Malachi Lawrence (57) goes through a drill during practice at the Ford Center at the Star Training Facility in Frisco, Texas. Mandatory Credit: Chris Jones-Imagn Images | Chris Jones-Imagn Images The Dallas Cowboys have done some good things to start training camp. The stars of camp have been the usual suspects, but others have been breaking into the spotlight, especially some of the rookies. When players that you aren’t counting on to contribute immediately start showing up, it’s like finding hidden money. Yet, there are questions that have come up that may worry some fans and possibly even make the team break the piggy bank. Here are three questions that have cropped up so far in training camp. Do they have enough pass rush? While the back seven has made plays, especially defending the pass at training camp, the pass rush has been slow to develop. Dallas’ interior defensive line is built to stop the run, but for where the Cowboys were last year, they aren’t showing consistent ability to pressure the passer outside of blitzes. Donovan Ezeiruaku and Malachi Lawrence are young but the hope was they would ignite the pass rush. Ezeiruaku was sent out of practice today for his role in a scuffle, perhaps also some frustration on his part. Rashan Gary is a veteran in the edge rusher group, but his calling card is more akin to stopping the run. The front office has teased about getting more veteran help, but do they stoke the embers on reigniting talks regarding Las Vegas Raiders edge rusher Maxx Crosby? The Cowboys know that Crosby isn’t happy with the Raiders, and what would be the point of prolonging hanging on to a disgruntled player? The Cowboys and the Raiders have an excellent working relationship, so the two sides coming together isn’t far-fetched. Or, maybe the Cowboys stay the course, and Christian Parker finds ways to generate more pressure ahead of the preseason and joint practices with the Los Angeles Rams and New Orleans Saints. It’s not time to panic, but you couldn’t fault fans for being somewhat antsy about the defense getting to the quarterback so far. Does Dallas still need a veteran linebacker? For weeks, if not longer, the Cowboys have been connected to veteran linebackers on the market, whether that be via trade or free agency. The names Jordyn Brooks and Bobby Wagner have been thrown around. At one point, that felt like a need, but in the weeks that have passed, it seems like adding another linebacker to the mix may be more of a luxury than anything else. Everyone is raving about rookie Jaishawn Barham and justifiably so. He has been outstanding. When you look beyond him, you have DeMarvion Overshown, who seems like he is on the cusp of greatness if he can stay healthy. DeMarvion Overshown with the first big pad pop of training camp. Hits Hunter Luepke and forces a cut back from Jaydon Blue. pic.twitter.com/Zx7erQSxm0 — Joseph Hoyt (@JoeJHoyt) August 3, 2026 Luke Schoonmaker likely thought this was a walk-in TD, but Shemar James hawks him down to stop him short of the goal line. #Cowboys defense is flying around. pic.twitter.com/yam8jTpFo9 — Patrik [No C] Walker (@VoiceOfTheStar) August 3, 2026 Dee Winters is a great fit with the team and should command a starting spot to open the season. Plus, you have Shemar James in his second season. Also, don’t lose track of Justin Barron. The Cowboys have a good chunk of change tied up in the former undrafted Syracuse linebacker and have flashed the last few days. When you further assess the inside linebacker room, the need at linebacker doesn’t feel as strong as it did during the offseason. Has Jaydon Blue already taken the RB2 two job, and if so, what does that also mean? Talk about getting off to a fast start. Now in his sophomore season, Jaydon Blue looks hungry to carve out a bigger role for himself. In the early portion of training camp, he has shown to be electric with his speed and agility in the open field, breaking one big run after another. Jaydon Blue pic.twitter.com/eDJ5Iq1mG5 — Jon Machota (@jonmachota) August 4, 2026 On Tuesday, he made another explosive play as he took a short screen pass for a big gain. It’s hard to ignore just how good he has looked, which makes you think: Is the RB2 spot his to lose? Phil Mafah is doing his best to challenge for the spot, and Malik Davis hasn’t popped. While for Blue, it would be great if he, in fact, had lapped the other runners for the primary spot behind Javonte Williams, what does that also mean for the rest of the running backs on the roster? Assuming Blue is the second option, where does that leave Mafah? Has he done enough to be in serious consideration of pushing Davis, who made a few big plays himself last year? The first preseason game in less than two weeks against the Arizona Cardinals will be very telling with how much or little Blue plays and who gets the majority of the work between Mafah, Davis, and Israel Abanikanda.

title: Troy Franklin feels more comfortable in third season with Broncos
summary: One of the most intriguing storylines unfolding at Denver Broncos training camp is the competition at wide receiver. Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton are slated to be the top tandem in the Broncos’ aerial attack this season. Yet the continued development of their young receiving corps will also be critical for the offense to ascend […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 16: Troy Franklin #11 of the Denver Broncos reacts after catching a pass during the third quarter against the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High on November 16, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the most intriguing storylines unfolding at Denver Broncos training camp is the competition at wide receiver. Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton are slated to be the top tandem in the Broncos’ aerial attack this season. Yet the continued development of their young receiving corps will also be critical for the offense to ascend to new heights in 2026. Entering his third season with the franchise, Troy Franklin is coming off the best season of his career. After a relatively quiet rookie campaign , Franklin took flight in 2025 and was the Broncos’ second leading receiver. He trailed only Sutton in target share and production. He finished his second season with 65 catches for 709 yards and 6 touchdowns. It’s unlikely that Franklin will see as much volume in year three compared to last year. Nevertheless, he figures to play an important role in Denver’s passing game. Yesterday, Head Coach Sean Payton took time to discuss Franklin’s progression to date and what he has improved upon since his rookie season in 2024. “His understanding of the formations, the details. Maybe in a different offense where he’s lining up outside right, now all of the sudden he’s getting used to the different roles that he’s playing and the alignments on the field,” stated Payton. “He has really good burst. That would be the one thing: he’s comfortable within the framework. It’s so much different than the system he had in college.” It usually takes several seasons for wide receivers coming out of the collegiate ranks to finally hit their stride as pros. Last season, we saw tremendous growth from the former Oregon standout. While there were some issues with drops and downfield tracking, he made a lot of big plays that helped Denver earn several key victories. After yesterday’s practice, Franklin noted he is better prepared this training camp compared to his first two years with the team. His knowledge of the offense is far more immense. Moreover, his chemistry with quarterback Bo Nix continues to get better each and every day. “I would say a lot. It’s my third year in it, so I’m comfortable. I don’t really have to think anymore, so I can just go and play,” stated Franklin. With Sutton and Waddle poised to earn the most looks in Denver’s passing endeavors, how the rest of the target share winds up being divided up remains a mystery. Franklin is competing alongside Marvin Mims Jr. and Pat Bryant for playing time during training camp. With no clear leader in the competition thus far, how Payton and Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb choose to attack opposing defenses on a weekly basis will be fascinating to watch. Their bevy of talented receivers has a lot of potential. If they can live up to it and be more consistent in ‘26 compared to ‘25, Denver certainly has the ability to be one of the best offenses in the NFL.

title: Eyioma Uwazurike hype hits fever pitch early on at Broncos training camp
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country. To win and play at a high level in the National Football League, you have to hold your own at the line of scrimmage. Over the past several seasons, the Denver Broncos have performed outstanding in the trenches. It’s a key reason why they are championship caliber team. The Broncos are […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 7: Eyioma Uwazurike #96 of the Denver Broncos stands on the sidelines during the nation anthem prior to an NFL football game against the Tennessee Titans at Empower Field at Mile High on September 7, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country. To win and play at a high level in the National Football League, you have to hold your own at the line of scrimmage. Over the past several seasons, the Denver Broncos have performed outstanding in the trenches. It’s a key reason why they are championship caliber team. The Broncos are set to return virtually every player on their offensive and defensive fronts with the exception of John Franklin-Myers. Those are some big shoes to fill, but thankfully, Zach Allen, D.J. Jones, and Malcolm Roach are the incumbent top three at the position. However, the competition for the next spot in the rotation is ramping up. Several players on rookie contracts are in a heated battle for increased playing time in 2026. Earlier in the offseason, some had pegged fourth-year defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike as a potential breakout player for the Broncos’ defense. While it’s still very early on in camp, Uwazurike is starting to make some noise. Yesterday, Head Coach Sean Payton spoke highly of his career arc and progression to date. “I’m proud of him because, you guys know this, in our sport, any sport really to just be out for a year can be difficult. He’s really come back, developed,” stated Paton. “He’s strong, he’s big and he’s having a real good start to camp. I think you have to look at it as one less year than what’s listed because of the year out. He’s doing really well.” Uwazurike played in eight games as a rookie before missing his entire second season due to violating league policy on gambling. After a relatively quiet year back in 2024, the former Iowa State standout earned a lot of playing time last year. He finished the 2025 season with a career high 39 tackles, 5 tackles for loss and 3.5 sacks. While Payton lauded his unteachable physical traits, veteran defensive tackle D.J. Jones spoke to what he has seen up close and personal as key reasons why Uwazurike performed well last year, and why he is ready to take his game to the next level in ‘26. “His hands and his eyes. This game is fast. It’s physical, which he has. But if you don’t have good eyes on the defensive line, then you’ll be lost. The leap he’s taking right now is pretty scary. He can play every position, very physical and his eyes are 10 out of 10 now,” remarked Jones. Replacing Franklin-Myers’ production won’t be easy, but if we can trust Payton and Jones, Uwazurike appears poised to be huge part of the Broncos’ defensive plans this season. As always, thank you for reading. Here is today’s slate of articles for Horse Tracks .

title: Denver Broncos: Notes from the quotes — August 5th 2026
summary: Any time you listen to a player or a coach give an interview in the NFL, you have to not only listen to what they say, but also what they DON’T say. Along with head coach, Sean Payton, wide receiver, Troy Franklin, and interior defensive lineman, D.J. Jones, gave interviews. Sean Payton offers several important […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL , CO - JUNE 4: Troy Franklin (11) of the Denver Broncos stretches during OTAs at the Broncos Park in Centennial, Colorado on Thursday, June 4, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Any time you listen to a player or a coach give an interview in the NFL, you have to not only listen to what they say, but also what they DON’T say. Along with head coach, Sean Payton, wide receiver, Troy Franklin, and interior defensive lineman, D.J. Jones, gave interviews. Sean Payton offers several important updates Injury updates are always a critical point of interest during questions with Sean Payton and Wednesday was not exception. Coach Payton mentioned that Drew Sanders is fully healthy, there were questions about whether he would be playing inside or outside and he said that Drew’s position “will sort itself out. It always does. That’s a lot better question than, ‘Who’s going to take the three reps?’ It’s an important position in this defense. Those edge positions, they’re hard to find. It’s a big reason why we’re staying with the positions these guys played a year ago. I think it’s one of the strong suits of our front.” So it would appear that Sanders will be mostly used at OLB in a crowded and highly talented group that includes Nik Bonitto, Jonathan Cooper, Jonah Elliss, Dondrea Tillman, and Que Robinson. With the lack of depth at ILB, and ability to play some snaps at ILB, which Elliss or Sanders could do, could be critical to making the 53-man roster. Additionally “the special teams stuff” will be critical. “Those guys are going to play a lot of snaps if they’re not playing snaps on defense. So all of that will factor in.” Que Robinson has been a pleasant surprise so far in camp and Sean Payton offered him some praise. Payton mentioned “he’s a real good technician, and he’s one of those guys that we know has been coached hard. We felt coming into this defense from what he was playing in, there were some similarities to what we were going to ask him to do.” The continued development of Que could make one of the other edge guys, like Cooper, a tradeable asset. Payton mentioned that Que is “competing for those reps in the line of scrimmage. I think it’s going really well, and again, we’ve had pads on for two days now.” The Broncos can never have too many good edge guys. Discussion of the WR room There were some interesting tidbits about the WR room offered yesterday both from Troy Franklin and Sean Payton. Payton offered high praise for the continued progress of Pat Bryant who he calls “one of those congested ball catchers.” The ability to go over the middle and catch the ball will be critical for the continued development of Bo Nix who did use the middle of the field very much last season. Having Jaylen Waddle who is “fine” as he just had some muscle tightness yesterday. Payton mentioned that Troy Franklin has made some progress during the offseason in terms of understanding the formations and the details of what is going on with the rest of the offense on a given play. “Now all of the sudden he’s getting used to the different roles that he’s playing and the alignments on the field. He’s comfortable within the framework. It’s so much different than the system he had in college.” A familiarity with the offense and with the Bo Nix can only help to improve the production from Troy Franklin who has “really good burst” according to Sean Payton. In Troy’s own words “I don’t really have to think anymore, so I can just go and play.” Coming down with more of his targets in 2026 will be critical for Troy. He was generally getting deep targets (ADOT, average depth of target, was 12.7 yards with was 27th highest in the NFL), but his catch rate of 53 percent leaves plenty of room for improvement. For comparison, Jaxson Smith-Njigba had an ADOT of 11.2 last season and a catch rate of 73 percent while Christian Watson had an ADOT of 17.8 and a catch rate of 64%. Lil’Jordan Humphrey also received praise from San Payton as one of the guys who does all of the little things to help the team win. He plays special teams at a high level, he blocks, and he doesn’t complain if he isn’t getting targetted, he is a big target, and he is extremely smart according to Sean Payton. He also mentioned that LJH has lost some weight relative to last season and he is moving better. “We do all the metrics and they wear the chips, but his weight’s down. His movement on the field, acceleration, top-end speed is higher last season and now than it was when he was here earlier.” Troy Franklin also sang the praises of new WR coach, Ronald Curry, who “has been great for us. I think he’s bringing a lot of new options on how we can get open. He’s taking a really good time in meeting rooms and making sure we know everything we need to do [with] our spots. Same thing with ‘Johnny Mo’ (Offensive Pass Game Coordinator John Morton), too. All those guys are helping us—[Offensive Quality Control Coach] Willie Snead [IV]. They’ve been a great addition for sure.” I’m excited about the WR room for this season. Marvin Mims will be playing for a free agent contract, which is usually when guys have career years. Pat Bryant, if he can stay healthy, is the possession guy that can thrive with all the attention Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle will draw. Troy Franklin and LJH can both contribute in significant ways, so at least on paper, the Broncos have a really strong WR group. Discussion of the defense DJ Jones mentioned the progress that Eyioma Uwazurike has made during the past year. “His hands and his eyes. This game is fast. It’s physical, which he has. But if you don’t have good eyes on the [defensive] line, then you’ll be lost. The leap he’s taking right now is pretty scary. Like I said, he can play every position, very physical and his eyes are 10 out of 10 now.” Having EU as a dominant force on the DL, even if it is just in run-stuffing, will be critical since he is the largest IDL player that the Broncos have and much of the group relies more of quickness than mass. At the team roster site, he is listed as 320, which is the second heaviest player on the team. Only Tyler Miller, 6-9 335 lbs, is heavier. Sometimes on the DL, you just need that mass to stand up against double teams from the OL. Our next heaviest IDL guy is Jordan Miller at 307. DJ also mentioned how the return of almost every starting defender from last season will help the 2026 defense. While familiarity with the guys playing next to you and their abilities is not as critical as it is on the OL (since the OL plays every snap and the DL rotates), it is a plus for any defense.

title: Jonah Coleman is turning heads, and Sean Payton is taking notice
summary: Few aspects of the Denver Broncos training camp top the risers and fallers. Everyone knows the players who have their spots on the roster scribbled in ink. But it’s the players who are fighting for a spot or clawing their way up the depth chart that creates the best storylines. That’s especially true for rookies. […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL , CO - JUNE 16: Jonah Coleman (20) of the Denver Broncos works out during minicamp at the Broncos Park in Centennial, Colorado on Tuesday, June 16, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Few aspects of the Denver Broncos training camp top the risers and fallers. Everyone knows the players who have their spots on the roster scribbled in ink. But it’s the players who are fighting for a spot or clawing their way up the depth chart that creates the best storylines. That’s especially true for rookies. After Broncos practice on Wednesday, Sean Payton was asked if there has been a pleasant surprise at this point. “Fair question. I think the young runner, you don’t feel a rookie with (running back) Jonah (Coleman). He’s playing. It’s been harder with some of the linemen because we haven’t been in pads in fairness to them. Then a couple of these young linebackers, we’re getting to see them move around, make the calls. There’s a lot to that position, a lot of it is key and diagnose. That’s been good.” The fact that Payton singled out Coleman is no doubt a positive sign (thanks, John Madden). When Denver selected the running back out of Washington in the fourth round, the pick was widely celebrated. Adding his running style and abilities to this offense gives the running back room another element and a different running style. Now Coleman is getting praise from Payton as a pleasant surprise at this point in training camp. But the compliments from Payton on Wednesday didn’t stop there. He was also asked about second-year receiver Pat Bryant and what area he’s progressed the most in since last year. “(I’m) really pleased with how he’s doing,” Payton said to the media on Wednesday. “He’s just one of those congested ball catchers. His feet stay on the ground. So when receivers catch the ball with their feet on the ground, they’re usually pretty good run after the catch. You don’t see him skipping in the air or jumping. That means he has a lot of confidence in catching this thing the right way. “I think in college in that final year (at Illinois), I think he had three walk-off touchdowns. Like literally last play of the game in-cuts where he caught it and didn’t … He was full stride when he caught it. If you’re breaking stride for a catch, there’s that tick of a second everyone gets a little bit of leverage on you. He’s extremely smart. He’s doing really well.” We all know the players who are projected to make the biggest impact for the Broncos this season. Seeing the younger players shine at this point is what will make the team better.

title: 2026 Denver Broncos Training Camp: Day 5 News and Notes
summary: Today was one of the more important practices of training camp. It was another fully padded practice, but the intensity was ramped up, and they had their longest practice session thus far. Unfortunately, for the third straight day, another Broncos starter left practice early with an injury, and today it was wide receiver Jaylen Waddle. […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL , CO - AUGUST 5: J.K. Dobbins (27) of the Denver Broncos works out with teammates during training camp at Broncos Park in Centennial, Colorado on Wednesday, August 5, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Today was one of the more important practices of training camp. It was another fully padded practice, but the intensity was ramped up, and they had their longest practice session thus far. Unfortunately, for the third straight day, another Broncos starter left practice early with an injury, and today it was wide receiver Jaylen Waddle. Thankfully, like Wattenberg and Bonitto, it seems like he avoided anything significant, but he was absent for most of the practice. Same with Courtland Sutton, who received back-to-back veteran rest days, so the Broncos offense was down their top two targets. #BroncosCamp work zone 🚧 pic.twitter.com/rzBrjb6FnR — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) August 5, 2026 For the third straight padded practice, the Denver Broncos defense, specifically their defensive line/ front 7, dominated the practice. DJ Jones, Malcolm Roach, Jonathon Cooper, Uwazurike, and the rest simply created havoc all practice. Sam Ehlinger took QB2 reps again today and looked good, but Payton said there’s no official competition happening there, and we have updates on select players from Sean Payton. Plus, as always, news and notes, injury updates, tweets from camp, quotes, and more! Defense and front 7 win again The offense started camp hot and had fans and media excited because we haven’t seen an offense come out firing like this in a long time in training camp. Well, that excitement was short-lived, because when the pads came on, the Denver Broncos front 7 came alive. Today it was Malcolm Roach, Jonathon Cooper, DJ Jones, and Uwazurike just absolutely dominating the Denver Broncos offensive line and limiting their overall production. It didn’t help that the offense did not have Waddle, Sutton, Wattenberg, and at times, McGlinchey and Powers, but still, the defense dominated. Roach, Jones, Uwazurike, and the rest of the Denver Broncos defensive line dominated the run game and were also able to get after the quarterbacks. It was a strong performance from three players who will be very important to the success of this team this upcoming season and potentially replacing John Franklin-Myers in this defense. "We've tasted it, now it's time to cook the meal, eat it, and take a break… we're about to eat again, it's time!" DJ Jones on the Denver Broncos' defense HUNGER going into this season 🔥 pic.twitter.com/rKdvLBFiru — DNVR Broncos (@DNVR_Broncos) August 5, 2026 Speaking of replacing JFM, veteran starting nose tackle DJ Jones believes the competition is already over and thinks Malcolm Roach will run away with the job, and that would make sense. Roach earned the contract extension from the Broncos last season while also flashing his pass rush upside. So, we could see Roach take over that JFM role, but there are a number of other defensive linemen on this team pushing for those reps. Given that depth, Jones believes the Broncos can break the NFL team sack record. He told reporters, We got what it takes and “We’ve tasted it, and now it’s time to cook the meal, eat it, and take a break”. He added, “We about to eat again” and that they have the numbers, the men, the willpower and the freewill to go out and do that, and he believes they will. The Broncos pass rush, even without John Franklin-Myers, is deep. Upfront they have Zach Allen, Malcolm Roach, the ascending Eyioma Uwazurike, Sai’vion Jones, rookie Tyler Onyedim, Jordan Jackson, Matt Henningsen, and on the edges you have Bonitto, Cooper, Elliss, Robinson, Tillman, Sanders and so on. The sack potential on this team is immense, and they should lead the NFL in sacks once again and push for that team sack record. Speaking of Uwazurike, he appears to be taking that next step in his career and becoming a problem for offensive linemen. Uwazurike taking that next step? After a not-so-great rookie year followed by a year-long suspension, it appeared Eyioma Uwazurike’s tenure with the Broncos and potentially even his football career could be over. However, he returned in 2024 and not only saved his career, but he became a key rotational player for this top-ranked Denver Broncos defense. Now, he’s looking at taking that next step and becoming a dominant defensive lineman and someone the team could count on to replace the role and snaps John Franklin Myers had wiith this team the past few seasons. "Speaking of Enyi, he can't be blocked… he's scary" 🔥 DJ Jones has some BIG praises for Eyioma Uwazurike 👀 pic.twitter.com/SIjKdEO8Xf — DNVR Broncos (@DNVR_Broncos) August 5, 2026 Jones was asked about Uwazurike’s development; he told reporters that Enyi “cannot be blocked”, he can play every position, and that “he’s scary”. “His hands and his eyes. This game is fast. It’s physical, which he has. But if you don’t have good eyes on the [defensive] line, then you’ll be lost. The leap he’s taking right now is pretty scary. Like I said, he can play every position, very physical and his eyes are 10 out of 10 now.” Head Coach Sean Payton also had high praise for the Broncos’ massive defensive lineman. He told reporters that he is proud of Enyi for bouncing back from his year-long suspension, knowing that it can end players’ careers. He also added that he has developed; he’s strong, big, and having a really good start to camp. “I’m proud of him because, you guys know this, in our sport, any sport really to just be out for a year can be difficult. He’s really come back, developed. He’s strong, he’s big and he’s having a real good start to camp. So I think you have to look at it as one less year than what’s listed because of the year out. Yes, he’s doing really well.” There’s a lot to like about Uwazurike, especially if he’s putting his entire game together. First, he’s listed at 6’6, 320 pounds (and he might be bigger than that), he’s athletic (played edge rusher at Iowa State), and he can play every position, as Jones stated and apparently cannot be blocked. If Enyi can turn into a really good player on top of the rest of the Broncos defensive line depth, this front seven could be even more dangerous and disruptive than they were last season. Updates on select players Sean Payton spoke about several players after today’s practice, so I decided to lump them all together here and give you all the updates in one place. HC Sean Payton on CB Kris Abrams-Draine “One thing about him is he’s smart. We felt that right away his rookie year. He’s one of those players, the ball kind of finds him too with his instincts. I would say he has tremendous hands. So he’s gotten stronger since his first year. He has real good key and diagnose, and a lot of traits that with his ball skills that serve him well at corner.” HC Sean Payton on EDGE Que Robinson “There were certain traits you saw on film. He’s a real good technician, and he’s one of those guys that we know has been coached hard. We felt coming into this defense from what he was playing in, there were some similarities to what we were going to ask him to do. I think that’s a help.” “I think it’s going well. He’s certainly competing for those reps in the line of scrimmage. I think it’s going really well, and again, we’ve had pads on for two days now.” HC Sean Payton on WR Lil’Jordan Humphrey “Good. It’s unusual for someone his age. We do all the metrics and they wear the chips, but his weight’s down. His movement on the field, acceleration, top-end speed is higher last season and now than it was when he was here earlier. They’re able to measure that with the Catapult. So he’s extremely smart, that’s probably one of his superpowers. He can play all three positions, and he’s a big target. HC Sean Payton on rookie TE Justin Joly “Yes, he’s coming. It’s a big jump for all those young tight ends. He’s certainly someone we feel like is better with…

title: Jaylen Waddle embracing a team-first mindset early on with the Broncos
summary: The biggest addition the Denver Broncos made this offseason was trading for wide receiver Jaylen Waddle. It came at a hefty cost. Nevertheless, the Broncos are confident they will see an immediate return on their big-time investment. Denver’s ultimate goal this season is the Super Bowl. Few teams can realistically say that, but for them—it’s […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL , CO - JULY 31: Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (17) of the Denver Broncos sign autographs for young fans after practice on Friday, July 31, 2026, at Broncos Park in Centennial, Colo.(Photo by Timothy Hurst/MediaNews Group/The Denver Post via Getty Images) | Denver Post via Getty Images The biggest addition the Denver Broncos made this offseason was trading for wide receiver Jaylen Waddle. It came at a hefty cost. Nevertheless, the Broncos are confident they will see an immediate return on their big-time investment. Denver’s ultimate goal this season is the Super Bowl. Few teams can realistically say that, but for them—it’s true. In order to accomplish that, the team will have to be much better on offense and unleash untapped dimensions of their aerial attack in 2026 that were missing last year. Throughout the offseason, Waddle has earned praise from his coaches and teammates for what he brings to the table. However, he knows it will take more than just him to get the Broncos’ offense to the next level. After yesterday’s practice, Waddle approached the aforementioned with humility and embraced a team-first attitude when asked about making the offense more dynamic. “I wouldn’t even say it’s just me. We have a lot of playmakers around us, so they want to get playmakers in space. They want us to get the ball in a hurry, get the ball out fast and just allow us to create plays. I don’t necessarily think it’s just me. We have a lot of playmakers, so just designing different things to get us in space,” added Waddle. SI's @AlbertBreer on Waddle and Mims: "Jaylen Waddle has arrived as advertised. The most noticeable and unique quality he brings to the table from Miami is his combination of elite long speed and sudden stop-and-start ability." "And Marvin Mims Jr. has had an outstanding… pic.twitter.com/8S7lTxM4Xu — SleeperBroncos (@SleeperBroncos) August 4, 2026 Transitioning to a new team isn’t always easy. Though for Waddle, heading from Miami to Denver has been a relatively smooth process. While he is still learning the ropes and getting acclimated to the area, the sixth-year pro gave rave reviews about the team’s culture. Moreover, expressed gratitude for how everyone in the organization treated him from the day he arrived in the Mile High City. “It’s just the team. They welcomed me with open arms since Day 1. I kind of grew to know not just Pat, but my receiver group, and the defense and everyone. It’s like a big family here. It just makes it easy to come to work. It makes it easy to come to work, go out there and compete in front of the fans on days like this.” In his first three years in the NFL, Waddle surpassed the 1,000-yard mark. The past two seasons, there has been some statistical regression. That’s by no fault of his own and can mostly be attributed to the quarterback issues with the Dolphins. In his first year with the Broncos, the sky is the limit for Waddle. He expressed confidence and optimism for the upcoming season. One of those reasons is because of who he is going up against on a daily basis. The Broncos boast one of the league’s best secondaries that will present him with more challenges leading up to the start of the season. Iron sharpens iron, and Waddle believes going up against Denver’s high-caliber defense will improve his play. “Our defense is definitely top in the league. Just having that back and forth with them, front to the back end, to the linebackers. It just makes us play true. We try to go out there, give them good looks and compete really hard against them. Our defense is hard to get a yard on, I can tell you that.”

title: Detroit Lions training camp injury report: Gibbs, Conklin back
summary: After a day off, the Detroit Lions were back on the field Thursday for Day 7 of training camp. It was a very hot and balmy day at Allen Park, and it forced a lot of players to either be limited or miss practice entirely. The Lions even offered the following update regarding players after […]
full_text: ALLEN PARK, MICHIGAN - JUNE 17: Jahmyr Gibbs #0 of the Detroit Lions works out at mandatory minicamp at Detroit Lions Meijer Performance Center on June 17, 2026 in Allen Park, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a day off, the Detroit Lions were back on the field Thursday for Day 7 of training camp. It was a very hot and balmy day at Allen Park, and it forced a lot of players to either be limited or miss practice entirely. The Lions even offered the following update regarding players after practice: “Several player absences/limited time related to the heat/cramping etc. Won’t have official updates on those.” So as you see some of the unexpected absences, early departures or limited playing times of the players below, keep in mind some of them may not be injury related. Return to practice: RB Jahmyr Gibbs (hold-in, back) TE Tyler Conklin (calf) G Ben Bartch (undisclosed) Gibbs was back on the field with a helmet, going through walkthroughs with his teammates for the first time. But when the team broke for positional and team drills, he split from the group and worked with a trainer. He stayed on the field for the entire practice, but did no team work after walkthroughs. Conklin officially came off the PUP list and did some walkthrough and individual drills on Thursday. He was not cleared for team drills yet, though. That left Jackson Meeks and Thomas Gordon to get most of the TE3-4 reps for the day. After solely working with trainers for the past couple of days, Bartch was back on individual drills, but he has still yet to participate in any team drills this training camp. For someone expected to contend for the starting left guard job, he needs to get out there soon. Out, but working with trainers: S Brian Branch (PUP, Achilles) Branch spent a significant amount of time working with a trainer on Thursday. I would estimate he did about an hour of work, up from about 15 minutes he did earlier in the week. He stayed on the field all day and hung out with his teammates, but he remains on PUP, with the last estimate on his return being late August, early September. Appeared to be limited: LB Derrick Barnes (undisclosed) Barnes appeared to be on a bit of a pitch count on Thursday, leaving Trevor Nowaske to get the majority of the first-team SAM linebacker reps when Detroit was in base defense. Not practicing: QB Teddy Bridgewater (undisclosed) RB Isiah Pacheco (undisclosed) RB Sione Vaki (eye, broken nose) OT Giovanni Manu (NFI) G Juice Scruggs (undisclosed) EDGE Derrick Moore (groin) EDGE Payton Turner (back) LB Malcolm Rodriguez (ankle) LB Jimmy Rolder (leg) CB D.J. Reed (undisclosed) S Kerby Joseph (PUP, knee) Bridgewater was nowhere to be seen on Thursday, leaving undrafted rookie quarterback Luke Atlmyer to take all of the second and third-team reps. He got a ton of work in Thursday, which is obviously good for his development. He did not look out of place, either. Some reporters believe they saw Pacheco during warmups (I hadn’t started attendance yet), but he was not present for the rest of practice. With Pacheco, Vaki, and Gibbs not participating in team drills, the first-team reps were split pretty evenly between Jacob Saylors and Jabari Small. No word on why Juice Scruggs was out. But with him out and Bartch still limited, Christian Mahogany took all of the starting left guard reps that I saw. Michael Niese stepped in for Scruggs as the backup center, as well. With Reed out for undisclosed reasons, it was primarily Rock Ya-Sin and Nick Whiteside as the starting cornerbacks, with a heavy day of nickel reps for Ennis Rakestraw. Left practice early EDGE Tyler Lacy (undisclosed) DT Mekhi Wingo (groin) CB De’Shawn Rucker (ankle) We did not get an update on Lacy, suggesting his early exit was heat related. In his place as the starting big end, Detroit utilized both Ahmed Hassanein and some Levi Onwuzurike with the ones. But with a lot of nickel looks on Thursday, DJ Wonnum got a significant workload opposite Aidan Hutchinson. With Wingo out, rookie Skyler Gill-Howard got the bump up at three-tech, playing with both the first and second-team defenses. Onwuzurike also took some of those reps. Rucker appeared to suffer an injury during 7-on-7 red zone drills.

title: Jahmyr Gibbs returns to practice; contract extension could ‘get done this week’
summary: Detroit Lions superstar Jahmyr Gibbs has returned to training camp practices, according to Pride of Detroit’s Jeremy Reisman. Gibbs reported for Lions training camp last week, and while he has been participating in meetings and with his teammates, he had yet to practice while he waits for a new deal to arrive. On Thursday, he […]
full_text: Sep 14, 2025; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (0) looks on during warmups prior to the game against the Chicago Bears at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Detroit Lions superstar Jahmyr Gibbs has returned to training camp practices, according to Pride of Detroit’s Jeremy Reisman. Gibbs reported for Lions training camp last week, and while he has been participating in meetings and with his teammates, he had yet to practice while he waits for a new deal to arrive. On Thursday, he was in full uniform and participated in warm-ups, but when the team shifted to individual drills, he stepped off to the side to work with a trainer, suggesting he is going through an acclimation process. Gibbs is not going through individual drills with the team. Currently working to the side with a trainer. — Jeremy Reisman (@DetroitOnLion) August 6, 2026 This return to the field for Gibbs is another optimistic sign that he could be nearing a contract extension with the Lions, which lines up with a recent report from The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones. Before Thursday’s practice, Jones expressed optimism surrounding a new deal, based on conversations with sources, and reported that a deal could “get done this week for Gibbs.” Gibbs has not formally met with the media in camp, and while reporters—Pride of Detroit included—have attempted to ask him about his situation, he’s kept things very close to the vest. When asked when he plans to rejoin his teammates on the practice field, he simply responded: “Time will tell.” On Tuesday, coach Dan Campbell was asked how other NFL running backs getting extensions could help facilitate the process of getting a deal done with Gibbs; he noted how it could help and that he was excited to get the star running back on the field. “I think it certainly’s not going to hurt,” Campbell said. “It’s not going to hurt, but we’ll see. I’m anxious to get Gibbs back out there. Every day that goes by, that’s another day that you feel like you miss with him and getting him out there with the guys and him doing his part. But, there again, it’ll get done when it gets done.” On Wednesday, general manager Brad Holmes was also asked for his thoughts on the situation by SiriusXM radio hosts Pat Kirwan and Jacob Hester, and Holmes noted that the two sides remain in communication. “Look, obviously we love Jahmyr,” Holmes said. “Me and Dan (Campbell) have always been believers in that one-two punch. I just think that’s how this league is going now. But, you know, we’re having dialogue. We’ll see where it goes.“ Will continue to update this situation as it progresses.

title: Discussion: What’s the proper concern level for Jahmyr Gibbs’ hold-in?
summary: Jahmyr Gibbs’ hold-in for a new contract officially enters Week 2 on Thursday, as the Detroit Lions will participate in their seventh training camp practice this offseason. Thus far, there have been no tangible signs of progress between the Lions and Gibbs, but there haven’t been any reports of stagnation or sticking points with negotiations, […]
full_text: Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (0) on field after practice during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Monday, August 3, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Jahmyr Gibbs’ hold-in for a new contract officially enters Week 2 on Thursday, as the Detroit Lions will participate in their seventh training camp practice this offseason. Thus far, there have been no tangible signs of progress between the Lions and Gibbs, but there haven’t been any reports of stagnation or sticking points with negotiations, either. Really, all the evidence we have about negotiations are the scant details we’re getting from the team itself. Both Lions coach Dan Campbell and general manager Brad Holmes have expressed public interest in getting a deal done, and on Wednesday, Holmes said they are engaged in talks. So this isn’t a situation in which the Lions are refusing to pay Gibbs or closed to any talks. However, there have been a few signs that are relatively discouraging. A week ago, Campbell said he “wasn’t sweating” Gibbs’ hold-in, but he also admitted he was surprised the contract hasn’t been finalized yet. “I thought we’d have been done by now,” Campbell said. On Wednesday, Holmes told SiriusXM they’re “having dialogue” with Gibbs , but his body language did not scream optimistic, and when reassured by the radio host that it’ll get done, his response was an uninspiring “that’s the hope.” So today’s Question of the Day is: What’s your concern level regarding Jahmyr Gibbs’ hold-in? My answer: I’m still pretty low. Let’s call it a 2/10 total. Admittedly, we’re entering uncharted territory with the Lions. Any time they’ve publicly expressed an interest in extending a player, they’ve been able to do so in a very timely manner. So, on the surface, it’s a bit concerning that’s not how negotiations are going this time around. Additionally, I figured as soon as Bijan Robinson signed his three-year extension with the Atlanta Falcons, that Gibbs’ deal would come about almost immediately. It’s been around 48 hours since, and all has been quiet. That all being said, I’m still not that concerned. We’re still very early in training camp, and while I’d certainly like Gibbs to be out there in a new offense with a new offensive line, there is more than enough time for him to enter the picture and be ready by Week 1. I trust that Gibbs’ appearance at practices is a sign of good faith and no ill-will, and I do expect the Robinson deal to move things along relatively quickly. And with Campbell’s mostly-optimistic comments on the situation, I’m assuming things will be just fine. Simply put, if Campbell isn’t sweating it, there’s no reason I should be. That said, if we’re beyond the first preseason game and Gibbs is still sidelined, that’s when the worry starts to creep up into the 4-6 range, and if we’re nearing the end of preseason, that’s when I’d jump to a 8-10. But, for now, it’s early. It’s okay to be patient here. What is your concern level for the Jahmyr Gibbs contract negotiations? title: Detroit Lions veteran TE to return from injury
summary: According to the NFL transaction wire, veteran tight end Tyler Conklin has passed his physical after missing the first week of training camp with a calf injury suffered in the spring. That almost certainly means Conklin will come off the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list when the Lions return to practice on Thursday. His […]
full_text: Detroit Lions tight end Tyler Conklin (83) practices a drill during OTAs at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Friday, May 29, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co According to the NFL transaction wire, veteran tight end Tyler Conklin has passed his physical after missing the first week of training camp with a calf injury suffered in the spring. That almost certainly means Conklin will come off the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list when the Lions return to practice on Thursday. His return comes just in time, as the Lions’ tight end room has suffered several injuries already in camp. Veteran tight end Anthony Firkser has already been placed on injured reserve with a broken leg. And the Lions also placed Miles Kitselman on injured reserve with a leg injury of his own. To help out, Detroit has added Nick Muse and re-signed Zach Horton. But the return of Conklin figures to be the biggest impact of all the Lions’ maneuvering in the tight end room. Conklin is an eight-year veteran who has put up at least 400 receiving yards on four different occasions. Detroit signed him to a one-year, $1.3 million deal this offseason to compete for the tight end depth behind Sam LaPorta and Brock Wright. Though Conklin is coming off a tough year with the Chargers, he caught at least 50 passes in each of the four previous seasons. He brings a strong blend of receiving skills and physical play to a room that struggled with its depth last season. Additionally, the Lions re-signed wide receiver Tarik Black to fill the roster spot left after placing Kitselman on injured reserve. And receiver Lawrence Keys reverted to the Lions’ injured reserve after the team waived him with an injury designation earlier in the week.

title: Detroit Lions announce new president, CEO Richard Haddad
summary: The Detroit Lions announced on Wednesday they’ve hired a new team president and CEO, and he doesn’t have to move too far for work. The new team president is Richard Haddad, a Michigan native who has served as the Chief Operating Officer and Chief Legal Officer of the Detroit Pistons since January of 2022. Prior […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - DECEMBER 05: A detailed view of the Detroit Lions logo on a helmet on the field before the game against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field on December 05, 2024 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions announced on Wednesday they’ve hired a new team president and CEO, and he doesn’t have to move too far for work. The new team president is Richard Haddad, a Michigan native who has served as the Chief Operating Officer and Chief Legal Officer of the Detroit Pistons since January of 2022. Prior to that, he served as the Executive Vice President of business affairs/administration and general counsel for the Pistons. “Rich is a proven leader who understands what it means to steward an iconic sports franchise in the city of Detroit, and we are thrilled that he is bringing that experience to the Lions,” Sheila Hamp said in a written statement. “Throughout our process, Rich’s experience, steady leadership style, and grasp on the present and future state of team sports were clear differentiators. My family and I are excited to work with Rich on driving the Lions forward in our continued pursuit to bring a championship to Detroit.” Haddad made Sports Business Journal’s “Forty Under 40” list in 2022 . Here’s what he had to say to the publication back then: “Detroit declared bankruptcy within a year and a half of my moving here, which is probably the bottom,” Haddad said. “It’s been incredible over the few years since then to see the city’s resurgence, and to have the opportunity through the Pistons to try to play a small role in accelerating all that.” In addition to his work with the Pistons, he was part of the effort to bring back a WNBA team to Detroit ( currently scheduled for 2029 ), “I am thrilled to join the Detroit Lions organization as its next President and CEO,” Haddad said via a press release. “I want to thank Sheila Hamp and the Ford family for their trust in me, along with Tom Gores and Arn Tellem for 14 great years with the Pistons. As a lifelong Lions fan, I understand firsthand how much this team means to this city and state, and I’m honored and humbled to lead this franchise. Sheila, Rod [Wood], Brad [Holmes] and Dan [Campbell] have built an incredible foundation, and I can’t wait to work with them to build on that and deliver for our fans and our community.” Haddad replaces Rod Wood, who announced he was retiring earlier this offseason. Per the Lions’ official story on the hire, Wood, Hamp, Bill Ford, Chris Spielman, and Lindsay Verstegen were involved with the hiring, along with the advisory firm Russell Reynolds. Wood will remain in place until Haddad completes his work with the Pistons and his transfer to the Lions is complete. Haddad is expected to take over in early September.
