title: Los Angeles Chargers Roster: Trey Pipkins, OL, scheme fit, 2026 outlook
summary: Next up in our 90-in-90 series is veteran offensive lineman Trey Pipkins! Will the seven-year veteran find his way back into the starting lineup for the Chargers this year? Let’s take a look at his chances! Basic Info Height: 6’6Weight: 307College: Sioux FallsExperience: 7 A native of Apple Valley, Minnesota, Pipkins starred on the offensive […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - JANUARY 11: Trey Pipkins III #79 of the Los Angeles Chargers looks on during the national anthem prior to an NFL wild card playoff game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on January 11, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Next up in our 90-in-90 series is veteran offensive lineman Trey Pipkins! Will the seven-year veteran find his way back into the starting lineup for the Chargers this year? Let’s take a look at his chances! Basic Info Height: 6’6 Weight: 307 College: Sioux Falls Experience: 7 A native of Apple Valley, Minnesota, Pipkins starred on the offensive line for Apple Valley High School. As a junior, he helped lead his team to a 8-3 record and the school’s first appearance in the state playoffs in over 19 years. As a senior, he blocked for a quarterback that set school records in single-season passing yards and passing touchdowns. Pipkins stayed fairly close to home by committing to play at the University of Sioux Falls where he was a three-year starter for the Cougars. After redshirting in 2014, Pipkins saw time in 10 games while playing mainly on special teams and sparingly on the line. In those limited snaps, he managed to allow zero sacks. As a first time starter in 2016, he got the nod for all 10 games the team played and earned his first All-NSIC honor with the second team. He repeated the postseason accolade after starting 12 games the following year, as well. In 2018, Pipkins put the cherry on top of his lengthy college career by earning not only a First-Team All-NSIC selection, but he was also voted to the AP’s Division II All- American First Team. This was the season that helped him catch the eye of NFL scouts and it earned him an invite to the East-West Shrine Game to play against some of the best talent in the country. In March of 2019, Pipkins also became the first player from Sioux Falls to be invited to the NFL Scouting Combine and he certainly did not disappoint. At 309 pounds, he ran a 5.12 forty-yard dash and jumped 33.5 inches in the vertical which was a top mark among all offensive linemen at the event. Following Pipkins’ selection with the 91st pick, the Chargers had no intentions of having him see the field as a rookie. However, thanks to a string of injuries, Pipkins was called upon to start three games, including the final two of the season. During his sophomore campaign, Pipkins lost the training camp battle to Sam Tevi for the starting left tackle spot. However, with nagging injuries to right tackle Bryan Bulaga, Pipkins ended up starting five games last year, mainly at right tackle. During the 2021 season, Pipkins lost the starting right tackle job to Storm Norton in training camp. Norton started the majority of games but Pipkins still recorded a pair of starts due to injuries to the former. In 2022, Pipkins finally broke through to win the starting job which he held for 14 games during the regular season. A nagging MCL injury kept him out of three contests, but overall Pipkins had his best season as a pro. Following the season, the Chargers signed him to a three-year contract to keep him as the team’s starting right tackle for the foreseeable future. Zion Johnson, Trey Pipkins, and Donald Parham parted the red sea at the goal line 😤 pic.twitter.com/9mcorO9Jkn — Steven Haglund (@StevenIHaglund) December 20, 2022 In 2023, Pipkins stayed healthy and started all 17 games for the Chargers. The 2024 season brought with it a position change for Pipkins who started 15 games at right guard following the drafting of Joe Alt to hold down the right edge. After beginning the 2025 season looking like he be the team’s swing tackle, Pipkins was forced into starting duties following injuries to both Rashawn Slater and Alt. The veteran saw starts at multiple spots, but spent most of his 10 starts that year at right tackle. The Good Pipkins is the longest-tenured offensive lineman on the Chargers and he’s managed to keep his value high as a versatile blocker who could play both tackle and guard spots in a pinch. He’s always been an athletic lineman and that could serve him well as a potential starter in Mike McDaniels’ outside zone scheme. The Bad Pipkins has always been “fine” when he’s been on the field for the Chargers, but his games where he’s been impactful have always been few and far between. After seven years with the Chargers, I believe we’ve come to what Pipkins is and will continue to be in the NFL which is a dependable backup who can be a starter when needed. 2026 Outlook Pipkins is currently in the running for the starting left guard job, but that also happens to be a competition that features four other players in Kayode Awosika, Jake Slaughter, Trevor Penning, and Branson Taylor. Pipkins’ athletic profile should fit well, but it’s been mostly Awosika and Slaughter who have been earning reps with the first team. If Pipkins does not earn a starting job, he’d then look to earn the swing tackle role which may not be a sure-thing given Penning’s experience there for the team in 2025.

title: Can Myles Garrett Lead the Rams to the NFL Sack Record?
summary: The Denver Broncos have already set the bar. This week, Broncos defensive tackle D.J. Jones boldly predicted that Denver can break the NFL record for sacks in a season. After falling four sacks shy last year, the Broncos have the record on their mind. But now that they have Myles Garrett, and possibly Aaron Donald, […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - JANUARY 04: Myles Garrett #95 of the Cleveland Browns celebrates breaking the NFL single-season sack record after the game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos have already set the bar. This week, Broncos defensive tackle D.J. Jones boldly predicted that Denver can break the NFL record for sacks in a season. After falling four sacks shy last year, the Broncos have the record on their mind. But now that they have Myles Garrett, and possibly Aaron Donald, can the Los Angeles Rams also challenge for the league’s all-time sack record? Currently, the Chicago Bears hold the record with 72, set one season before their legendary and historic Super Bowl run. If the Rams are going to attempt to break the record, they have an uphill climb. Denver fell four sacks shy of tying the mark, making their goal of breaking the record far more realistic in 2026. L.A. finished seventh in the NFL with 47 sacks, only 21 behind the league-leading Broncos. As far as we know, no Rams player has boasted about the team challenging the record. Even with Garrett leading the pass rush, it’s still a long shot, but not impossible. The most sacks the Rams have had in a season was 57, unsurprisingly set during the 1999 campaign . Despite all of Aaron Donald’s success with the franchise, the most sacks the defense achieved with him in the lineup was 53 in 2020. So yeah, remember when I said this was going to be an uphill climb? The ‘99 team wasn’t loaded with dominant sack masters, because several guys contributed. Thirteen players finished with a sack that season, led by All-Pro Kevin Carter’s 17. No other player on the defense had double-digit sacks. For reference, D’Marco Farr had the second-most sacks on the team with 8.5. If Los Angeles hopes to challenge for the NFL record, guys beyond Garrett must step up. The Broncos were so dangerous last season because, like that iconic Rams team, they had several contributors. Eight players had at least four sacks, including four with seven sacks or more. Looking at L.A. now, they have plenty of capable players. Byron Young led the team with 12 sacks, and Kobie Turner added seven. Swapping Jared Verse for Garrett should undoubtedly help the unit, given the Florida State product had 12 sacks in two seasons. Myles Garrett joins the Rams after setting the NFL single-season sack record with 23 sacks in 2025, despite facing a league-high 139 chip blocks. Over the last five seasons, no player has recorded more sacks (83) or generated more quick pressures (218) than Garrett. #RamsHouse https://t.co/anLo4NHKYa pic.twitter.com/DtTZpK9Yrq — Next Gen Stats (@NextGenStats) June 1, 2026 The Rams are unlikely to challenge for the NFL’s all-time sack record, but the franchise record is well within their sights. L.A. should be aiming for that goal first, and with the reigning Defensive Player of the Year on defense, potentially Aaron Donald as well, it’s perhaps inevitable that mark will fall. Should the team get enough production from several guys, not just the stars, they could finish with the best pass rushing season in franchise history.

He joined The Jim Rome Show to talk about his experience. "When you get a chance to see someone who is really good at what they do, you can just soak it in. I was a sponge, soaking it in." Sean McDermott on his recent visit with Sean McVay and the Rams. pic.twitter.com/MN3HLjw7UD — Jim Rome (@jimrome) August 5, 2026 McDermott was highly complimentary of Sean McVay’s operation in Los Angeles. It seemed to be an enlightening experience for someone who will likely be back in the head coach cycle as soon as next year. Quarterback Matthew Stafford and others have said that the team’s recent practices are as competitive as they’ve seen . The Rams are performing at a high level ahead of the regular season. Expectations are sky-high, and McVay deserves credit for helping the roster cut through media narratives and staying focused on the mission. Some notable quotes from the interview: On McVay: When you get a chance to see someone who is really good at what they do, you can just soak it in. I was a sponge—soaking it in. Did McVay try to hire McDermott? Well, you know, I thought for a second there the visit was going so well. I’m like, if he asks me to stay, I might consider it but only if I get to stay at his house. I’m done living in dorm rooms (for camp)… It was a great visit. It’s probably unlikely that McDermott would join McVay’s staff at this point of the season—or at least it would be rare for a hiring for someone of this public profile. Whether McDermott is a longer term fit for Los Angeles is the better question. Rams defensive coordinator Chris Shula garnered attention this past offseason for teams with an opening at head coach. His name is certain to be included in the rumor mill again for 2027. Bringing in a former head coach would mitigate a potential downturn if McDermott can’t find his way back to a head seat. The Rams have no shortage of big personalities on the defense, including Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie, and others. This might not be a role well-suited for a first-time coordinator. Stay tuned at Turf Show Times for updates on all news coming out of training camp.

title: The Toughest Roster Battle on the Rams Might Be at Defensive Tackle
summary: The Los Angeles Rams may have one of the NFL’s deepest defensive tackle rooms entering 2026, even without adding Aaron Donald. Kobie Turner has already developed into one of football’s premier interior pass rushers. Poona Ford helped transform the Rams’ run defense. Braden Fiske is looking to rebound, Tyler Davis earned a larger role last […]
full_text: The L.A. Rams defensive line is ready for a lot of celebrating in 2026 (Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams may have one of the NFL’s deepest defensive tackle rooms entering 2026, even without adding Aaron Donald. Kobie Turner has already developed into one of football’s premier interior pass rushers. Poona Ford helped transform the Rams’ run defense. Braden Fiske is looking to rebound, Tyler Davis earned a larger role last season, and several young players are battling for what could be the final two roster spots. With training camp underway, here’s a complete look at every Rams defensive tackle, how each player fits Chris Shula’s defense, and who has the best chance to make the 53-man roster. Who’s locked into the roster? Who’s on the bubble? Which players have breakout potential? Here’s a player-by-player breakdown of the Rams’ defensive tackle room. Versatility in Defensive Linemen One reason the Rams value depth so highly is the way defensive line coach Giff Smith and defensive coordinator Chris Shula deploy their front. Rather than assigning players to fixed roles, Los Angeles asks its interior defenders to move throughout the formation, creating one of the NFL’s most versatile defensive line rotations. The Rams put a lot of weight on the shoulders of the defensive interior, gone are the days when they made due with their 5-2 base and high shell coverages. Last year, according to Sharp Football Analysis , L.A. used sub defensive packages at a 75 percent clip. The defensive front was expected to provide the pass rush pressure without a lot of blitz calls, 18 percent, second fewest in the NFL. They were also expected to hold their mud against the run, with Shula using light boxes 56 percent of the time to lure opponents into running the football. 2026 sees the return of all six of seven snap recipients from last year, only Jack Heflin (8 reps) is gone. It will be a tough room to bust into for the few newcomers. Let’s meet them all. Meat on the bone Kobie Turner – 6’2” 290 lb. 32” arms In his three pro seasons, Turner has been a steady force in the Rams interior. He’s put up consistent production numbers up and proven to be very durable, seeing action in all 51 regular season games as well as every playoff matchup. Pro Football Focus recently ranked him as the 59th best player in the NFL and 4th best defensive tackle. His 69 pressures in 2025 was second-best in the NFL. Even though Turner lacks prototypical mass and has adequate arm length, his build is stout and powerful. He’ll have problems if opposing blockers latch on to him, but he eludes them with nimble footwork, short area agility, and change of direction. Plays with low pads and a constant motor. Follows the ball in pursuit and a good tackler. Has very good hand fighting skills, a bevy of pass rush moves, and is bursty and powerful on stunts/loops/twists. Poona Ford – 6’ 314 lb. 33” arms Built like a fireplug with good arm length, Ford was brought in last season as a free agent to help re-build the Rams run defense and did exactly that. According to Pro Football Focus , the L.A. run defense improved from 27th in Expected Points Added (EPA) per play in 2024 to 8th in 2025. Ford was a huge part of the upgrade. As part of the Rams interior rotation, he was in on about 50 percent of reps, down from his past work, but that seems about right for a 31 year-old that has spent eight seasons in the middle of a gang fight. His thick build, strong lower half, and low pad level gives him leverage, as well as a strong anchor. When matched against double team’s, he engages from underneath and corkscrews his leg into the turf to hold his ground. Ford’s also sneaky quick through gaps, if not briskly squared up. A power-based pass rusher, best-suited to collapsing the pocket than chasing down quarterbacks. Poona Ford ( @PoonaF_95 ) with the swipe swim. Gets the sack to force OT! #PassRush #InteriorRusher #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/Wluqm1LILb — DLineVids (@dlinevids1) December 19, 2025 Braden Fiske – 6’4” 294 lb. 31” arms Fiske looks to bounce back after battling the sophomore jinx in 2025. His production in snaps, tackles, and sacks were substantially down. To be fair, he got a late start after knee surgery in his rookie off-season and was hit-and-miss on the 2025 injury lists with ankle and oblique woes. He did however, play well in the playoffs. Wins with get-off, nimble feet, and effort. Strong hand fighter. Very impressive is how he keeps opposing linemen from squaring him up, he plays on their shoulders, abating their balance and power. When he has an edge, he really bursts to the ball. Conversely, his average arm length and relative lack of low mass can allow linemen to stick to him. His burst is not only evident as a pass rusher, Fiske gets through gaps or backdoors in a hurry, particularly against zone runs. His upper body strength allows him to stack/shed well. Tyler Davis 6’2” 305 lb. 31 3/8” arms Compact, blocky frame, his build starts him with good leverage. Davis plays a very disciplined game, consistently maintaining his gaps. Shows the ability to control and stack/shed or drive blockers with constantly moving feet and strength. He generally has good awareness as to what’s going on around him, reacting and flowing towards the ball. A better run defender than pass rusher, when he stays low he is very hard to move off his spot, even versus double teams. Not a lot of pass rush moves, but Davis can be explosive off the snap and strikes a powerful punch. He can pressure opposing linemen when shooting gaps Last year, Davis nearly doubled his snaps from his rookie season and stat production was commensurate. His toughness versus the run makes him one of the “dirty work” players on the interior, he’s accountable, disciplined, and tough. Roster battle: youth and exuberance vs. age and treachery Ty Hamilton – 6’3” 301 lb. 32 1/4” arms Re-watching Hamilton’s film, his work as a rookie didn’t fully match up to his college traits. He did show a quick and accurate punch and plays with low pad leverage. It was his get-off that didn’t show up. In college, his twitch and leg drive were explosive. He stacks blockers well, but lacked in shedding them. Held his ground pretty well, even on double teams. Pursues to the ball well. His pass rush is bullrush-based, didn’t show a lot of different moves, although he did hand fight well. A 2025 Round 5 draftee, Hamilton played in 14 regular season games with 138 snaps. Well-put together frame and tested quite well for athleticism, strength, and explosiveness. Big, strong hands and adequate arm length. Year 2 will be the litmus test for how much value Hamilton will offer going forward. The traits are right, he will just need to apply them. This is one play by Ty Hamilton that is pretty good. They have been playing him mostly at NT. Here in a near 4-point stance in a shade technique. He steps and fights pressure and keeps his legs at a good leverage angle step, then control step, keeping eyes up pic.twitter.com/D35XTWdvuc — Jim Youngblood 53 (@53_jim70721) August 18, 2025 Larrell Murchison – 6’3” 297 lb. 32 5/8”arms Originally a Round 5 selection (Tennessee Titans) in the 2020 NFL Draft, Murchison came to L.A. off waivers in December 2022. He made the Rams opening roster in 2023 and 2025. He was destined to make it in 2024, but two separate injuries, a late-camp broken arm and right after coming off the Injured Reserve List, a broken ankle kept him on the sidelines for the whole season. Murchison has carved out a role as a depth player. In 2 1/2 active seasons, he’s played in 34 games with 432 snaps. Ofttimes his work was mop up duty, but he did make three starts. Plays with veteran savvy and 100 percent effort, fairly well-rounded game, just no outstanding traits. Adequate arm length to keep distance, plays low, and has good contact balance. Best in short area…

title: Trent McDuffie Got Mad When He Found Out He Was Traded
summary: The Los Angeles Rams were one of the busiest teams of the offseason, trading for Trent McDuffie in the spring and then Myles Garrett in the summer, and both deals had players upset that they were changing teams unexpectedly. In the case of the Garrett trade, it was Jared Verse who got caught off-guard, and […]
full_text: Trent McDuffie at the Sports Illustrated Beyond the Pitch Los Angeles held at the Hollywood Palladium on June 12, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Chad Salvador/Variety via Getty Images) | Variety via Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams were one of the busiest teams of the offseason, trading for Trent McDuffie in the spring and then Myles Garrett in the summer, and both deals had players upset that they were changing teams unexpectedly. In the case of the Garrett trade, it was Jared Verse who got caught off-guard, and McDuffie says that Sean McVay let the pass rusher stand up in front of the whole team to say goodbye. The room was in shock, according to McDuffie during an appearance on the Bussin’ with the Boys podcast on Wednesday . “We didn’t even meet, we just talked. The coaches were like ‘Get your feelings out’…I could tell, (Jared Verse) was loved in that building.” McDuffie also said on the show that he couldn’t believe the Chiefs had traded him instead of paying him, but then he was happy when he found out he was going to the Los Angeles Rams. “I can’t hold on to the past,” McDuffie explained. “This happened, let’s just move on as fast as we can. And honestly having that conversation with Sean McVay and our defensive backs coach Jimmy Lake, who was my DB coach at Washington, already just calmed me.” McDuffie may not have expected the Chiefs to under-value him, but he was happy that the one team that appreciated his talent was a Super Bowl favorite. That’s just one of the many Rams stories from Wednesday. Here are the rest. Trent McDuffie Reveals Surreal Moment About Chiefs-Rams Trade (heavy.com) “The whole time they’re telling me ‘we’re going to get it situated and we’re going to get the contract done.’ So the whole offseason, I’m going to chill. Knowing the Chiefs, they’re going to drag this out,” McDuffie told former NFL offensive lineman Taylor Lewan. Both later referred to the Tyreek Hill situation. The one that ultimately led to KC dealing him to the Miami Dolphins before the Chiefs’ Super Bowl 58 run. He later revealed he learned of his fate through his Apple Watch while during a workout. Plus became confronted by his mother and future wife. McDuffie later described that the world stop. “Just that moment of being traded, and you’re like ‘what’s going on?!’” McDuffie said, who added that he didn’t hear from his agent or even anyone on the Chiefs’ side. “It was surreal.” Puka Nacua hires a new agent (Bleacher Report) The Rams’ star receiver is looking for a new contract, and the first step was changing his agency. Rams standout wide receiver Puka Nacua, who is entering the final year of his four-year rookie contract, has hired @winsportsgroup to represent him in contract negotiations. pic.twitter.com/vnPWuIzuZZ — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) August 5, 2026 Win Sports Group just made two powerful WR deals: “Win Sports Group also represents Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Baltimore Ravens wideout Zay Flowers , both of whom landed lucrative extensions this offseason. Smith-Njigba inked the most lucrative deal for any wide receiver in NFL history when he signed a four-year deal, $168.6 million extension including $120 million in guaranteed money in March.“ What will they do for Puka? NFL offseason power rankings: No. 1 Los Angeles Rams move all in to win another Super Bowl (sports.yahoo) “As Rams general manager Les Snead has said through the years, it’s more complicated than the “(forget) them picks” phrase that has become attached to him and the franchise. It’s just an aggressive mindset that Snead picked up when he was in the Falcons’ front office with then-GM Thomas Dimitroff. “You could see his mentality, our mentality of why,” Snead told ESPN in 2022. “We’re aware of this window. Let’s make a bet that we can make the most of this window.” Aaron Donald update: “This kid has a shot” (Sean McVay) The Rams head coach was asked about Donald (again) on Wednesday. Here’s what he had to say about Donald’s tryout with the team: Aaron Donald “tried out” for the Rams Wednesday. Sean McVay says the kid has a shot pic.twitter.com/1mqd8f8CoC — Gregg Rosenthal (@greggrosenthal) August 5, 2026 Aaron Donald playing for a spot in history (Andscape) A poetic imagining of what Donald could bring to the Rams if and when he returns. “A haunted house. The room of a thousand mirrors. Every carnival has a ride or attraction rooted in awe and fear. Ask Geno Smith . Ask Joe Burrow . Ask any quarterback who lined up in front of Donald. Ask any offensive lineman or coach. To be in awe and to be in fear is twisted euphoria. Sometimes the most charming individual in the room is the bully. American culture has long been enamored with figures who became mythical because their reputations preceded them.“ McVay’s ‘Love’ training camp strategy is winning over players (LA Times) McVay trades old-school punishment for a more precise, player-friendly grind that has become a hit. 49ers injury problems mount Yet another injury problem for the 49ers, L.A.’s Week 1 opponent. This time, it’s Kyle Juszczyk. No practice today for Kyle Juszczyk, who broke his finger — David Lombardi (@LombardiHimself) August 5, 2026 The 49ers had 20 players out of practice recently. Seahawks on Hard Knocks The Rams’ biggest division rivals right now are the Seahawks and their training camp is featured on Hard Knocks. Rookie running back Jadarian Price will have a big role this season and the cameras were rolling, but is the position still a weakness for Seattle? Rookie RB @Jadarian15 is impressing at Seahawks camp 👀 Watch the first episode of Hard Knocks: Training Camp with the @seahawks now on @hbomax pic.twitter.com/Uz7hiZz82y — NFL (@NFL) August 6, 2026 Matthew Stafford’s best friend visits While Justin Herbert’s camp visitor was pop star wife Madison Beer, Stafford had a different kind of famous Hollywood friend. High school teammate Clayton Kershaw was in the house at Rams camp on Wednesday. Who has the better arm? Let us know what you think in the comments. LA icon (and apparently Matthew Stafford’s high school teammate) Clayton Kershaw in the house! 👋 pic.twitter.com/votnvtn3ir — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) August 5, 2026 Rams building “Dodgers-like super team” (Deadspin) Speaking of the L.A. Dodgers, Deadspin compared the Rams to the NFL’s version of that. “If Dodgers manager Dave Roberts can manage a full constellation of his sport’s main stars, why shouldn’t Rams head coach Sean McVay be able to do the same? Garrett isn’t even the only Pro Bowl addition on defense this past offseason. Cornerback Trent McDuffie arrived from the Kansas City Chiefs in a March trade. The offense is led by no less than reigning MVP Matthew Stafford. And while first-team All-Pro Puka Nacua went through a bevy of offseason issues that put his character in question, he is in camp and seemingly motivated to get all the talk back on his play again.“ Will the Rams represent the NFL as well as the Dodgers represent MLB? title: Which Ram falls off the roster if Aaron Donald returns?
summary: With each passing day, Aaron Donald’s return to the Los Angeles Rams seems more and more likely. Donald worked out with team equipment on Wednesday, which required the Rams to report his activity to the league office. Sean McVay and the team have maintained that Donald would not return unless he was confident he could […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - JANUARY 14: Aaron Donald #99 of the Los Angeles Rams runs around the edge during an NFC Wild Card Playoff football game against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on January 14, 2024 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Ryan Kang/Getty Images) | Getty Images With each passing day, Aaron Donald’s return to the Los Angeles Rams seems more and more likely. Donald worked out with team equipment on Wednesday , which required the Rams to report his activity to the league office. Sean McVay and the team have maintained that Donald would not return unless he was confident he could play at the elite level we are accustomed to from him. Donald wouldn’t come back to be a part-time player or live off his reputation. He wants to make a difference on the defensive line next to Myles Garrett. While Donald’s return would largely be positive news for the Rams organization, it would also in turn be bad news for someone on the back of the roster. LA would need to cut someone from training camp in order to make room for the future hall of famer. So who becomes the odd man out? Here are some options: Defensive line The most logical place to start. It’s purely a numbers game and if Donald is added to the roster, the most likely place to trim would be his same position group. These are the players on uncertain ground: Larrell Murchison Jaxson Moi Payton Zdroik Bill Norton One benefit working in Norton’s favor is that he is more of a defensive tackle while the other aforementioned names are more ends. Still, the Rams have plenty of backups at tackle even though Norton did show promise last preseason. Kobie Turner, Poona Ford, Tyler Davis are locks to make the roster. Recent draft choices in Ty Hamilton and Tim Keenan may be competing for a spot. Murchison is also likely safe for now, though he’s bounced on and off the roster multiple times in recent years. Moi and Zdroik don’t bring much name recognition to the table. That isn’t a positive in training camp. Other names to watch Matthew Caldwell, QB LA may need Caldwell just to make it through the three preseason games. We still don’t know how much or if at all we will see each of Stetson Bennett and/or Ty Simpson in the exhibitions. But the main question is whether the Rams keep two or three quarterbacks. Caldwell has a remote chance to make the team. Why not sever ties now?

title: Aaron Donald has official ‘workout’ with Rams
summary: For the first time in two years, Aaron Donald is officially involved in Rams training camp. Donald, who has been mulling a return from retirement over the last couple of months, worked out with the team on Wednesday. The “workout” was submitted by the team to the NFL, per league rules, because Donald was using […]
full_text: For the first time in two years, Aaron Donald is officially involved in Rams training camp. Donald, who has been mulling a return from retirement over the last couple of months, worked out with the team on Wednesday. The “workout” was submitted by the team to the NFL, per league rules, because Donald was using team equipment at their facilities at Loyola Marymount University. It’s not a return yet. But it is the closest thing fans have had so far as proof that Donald has one foot back in the door. Aaron Donald wanted to do a workout in a football helmet, and even though he did not wear pads during it, he used Rams’ team equipment at their facility during training camp, requiring them to report his activity to the NFL. https://t.co/4egBgDAiLH — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) August 5, 2026 The Aaron Donald saga continues to move forward. Earlier this week, it was reported that Aaron Donald would not rejoin the team until the team returned back to Woodland Hills . However, today’s news certainly accelerates the timeline of Donald’s potential return to the team for the 2026 season. There is also the issue of the $30 million that needs to be worked out . Speculation on Donald’s return has been a daily recurrence, from one day when he may return midseason to the next when he’s supposedly going to join the team any minute now and go full, 100-percent when the season starts. Can confirm that Aaron Donald's workout at the team facility in Woodland Hills today was reported on the daily NFL transactions as a "tryout." Just another sign that Donald is getting closer to a return to the LA Rams. pic.twitter.com/i9tk4afHaf — Michael J. Duarte (@michaeljduarte) August 5, 2026 And what will Donald’s return do to the players expected to play his position before this all started? Should the team trade Braden Fiske if they’re just going to push him to the side for Donald? Donald’s return is exciting, but anything other than simple. If there’s anything that’s not confusing though, it’s that every single news item and rumor that has come through since the beginning has gotten Donald closer to return, with not one of those reports suggesting he’s not coming back.

title: Rams predicted to win NFC West in 14-3 tiebreaker
summary: The Seattle Seahawks may have won the NFC West by two games last year, but that alone doesn’t paint a clear picture of just how close both the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers came to winning the division and earning the number one seed. The 12-5 Rams had multiple opportunities to beat the […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - DECEMBER 18: Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams avoids a tackle from Leonard Williams #99 of the Seattle Seahawks during overtime at Lumen Field on December 18, 2025 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks may have won the NFC West by two games last year, but that alone doesn’t paint a clear picture of just how close both the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers came to winning the division and earning the number one seed. The 12-5 Rams had multiple opportunities to beat the Seahawks and virtually lock up the NFC West in Week 16, then the 12-5 just had to beat Seattle in Week 18 to do it. What if this year’s division doesn’t just feature one 14-3 team like it did last year, but two? And what if the Rams come out ahead and win the tiebreakers this time? That could be their ticket back to the Super Bowl because nothing is as powerful as the number one seed. At least one writer thinks that will happen. USAToday’s Nate Davis not only predicted that the Rams would win the Super Bowl , but that they would win the division in a tiebreaker of the 14-3 Seattle Seahawks, prior to defeating the Seahawks, Cowboys, and Bills in the playoffs. (1) Los Angeles Rams (14-3): What else needs to be said about this would-be juggernaut? Sure, reigning MVP Matthew Stafford, 38, must continue to defy Father Time. WR Puka Nacua needs to stay out of the off-field headlines as he tries to convince the organization he’s worthy of a bodacious bag. DC Chris Shula has those significant new parts to mesh – and maybe an old one if Donald unretires. At the very minimum, the special teams can’t be an Achilles heel. And the Seahawks remain a bugaboo. Still, the Rams have won 20 of their last 28 games, many of the losses over that stretch of the fluky variety, and have more star power than any team in the league. Anything less than a Lombardi would be a disappointment – especially since Stafford’s age and several expiring contracts, Nacua’s chief among them, could necessitate a drastically altered roster in 2027. It would be one thing for Davis to cop out and say that no other NFC teams were a real challenge to L.A., and that could certainly happen, but instead he set up a situation in which Sean McVay and Matthew Stafford need every last second of the NFL season to earn the number one seed and win the Super Bowl because he also has the Seahawks going 14-3 this season. That’s far more exciting. Especially because the Rams and Seahawks face each other twice in the last three weeks. The No. 1 Rams are the Super Bowl favorites, and for great reason. They're the most aggressive team in the NFL, and it has paid off with the top roster in the sport. https://t.co/tdMsibJSCx — Frank Schwab (@YahooSchwab) August 5, 2026 Consider the massive implications of Week 16 and Week 18 if the Rams and Seahawks both go 14-3. Presumably if the Rams win the division, they must beat Seattle at least once in that span. Let’s say it’s Week 18. Then the Week 18 game would be a 13-3 team against a 14-2 team and the 13-3 team wins the Super Bowl. 14-2 vs. 13-3 would be the second-biggest such game in history, only defeated by the time that the 15-2 Lions beat the 14-3 Vikings two years ago for the NFC North and the number one seed. L.A. vs Seattle could be even bigger than that. Davis also has the 49ers going 11-6, but losing in the first round to the Bears. He has Seattle beating the Saints and the Cowboys beating the Lions in the first round. Then the Rams beat the Seahawks and the Cowboys beat the Bears, setting up Roger Goodell’s dream matchup of the Rams vs the Cowboys in the NFC Championship. In the AFC Championship, the Bills beat the Ravens. Do I think this will happen? It’s all pretty chalky to me. Davis shies away from any surprises, which is never the case. I like at least one team to shock the world this year, and my pick is the Tennessee Titans. Maybe the Titans won’t win a playoff game, but I’ll say that they can reach the playoffs and Cam Ward becomes one of the NFL’s biggest stars. Having the Saints in the playoffs is a bit surprising, but less so because of the division they play in; although Tyler Shough could also become a star. The Rams already have many stars of their own. That’s why many expect them to win the NFC West and the Super Bowl, even if for the second year in a row, the division has both of the league’s two best teams.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Rams making different travel plans than 49ers
summary: The Los Angeles Rams are taking a completely different approach in their travel plans to Melbourne, Australia than the San Francisco 49ers are for their season-opening game. Whereas the Niners will leave nine full days before the game, the Rams will reportedly arrive just one day before kickoff, according to ESPN’s Dan Graziano. This lines […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 09: Kyren Williams #23 of the Los Angeles Rams runs the ball against Dee Winters #53, Drake Nugent #66, and Renardo Green #0 of the San Francisco 49ers in the first quarter of a game at Levi's Stadium on November 09, 2025 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams are taking a completely different approach in their travel plans to Melbourne, Australia than the San Francisco 49ers are for their season-opening game. Whereas the Niners will leave nine full days before the game, the Rams will reportedly arrive just one day before kickoff, according to ESPN’s Dan Graziano . This lines up with something Sean McVay said four months ago on the Up and Adams show : “We were like SEAL Team 6,” coach Sean McVay said of the team’s trip to London. “We’re in and out before you know what happened.” How will those plans impact the players in Australia? For clarity, when I was researching this piece, I found it much simpler to ignore mentions of days of the week. There is a 17-hour time difference at that time of year which is all you need to know. Circadian rhythms and two ways to balance them Your circadian rhythm is your body’s natural 24-hour internal clock. It controls when you sleep, wake, eat, and release hormones. Schedule changes, such as shift work or jet lag from travel, or when you eat and exercise, can affect this natural rhythm, resulting in poor sleep quality and daytime fatigue. Kyle Shanahan wants to give his players ample time to acclimate to the time change: “Usually when you travel with a [16]-hour flight, you don’t want to get there the day before because you lose like a whole day there or two and you’re just messed up,” Shanahan said. “The people we’ve talked to, you don’t feel normal until like the third or fourth day,” Shanahan said. “So, we’d like to go out seven days early. But since it takes a day and a half to travel there, we’re going to go nine. I think we leave on Wednesday and land on a Friday. And so, then we get there about seven days before our game.” The issue with this approach is that they’ll face the same acclimation period when they return stateside. Will they be fully recovered for their Sunday afternoon game 10 days later? McVay and the Rams are taking the opposite strategy: “It’ll be a similar approach, and really the goal for us is to try to keep guys in as close to a rhythm and routine as possible,” McVay said. “This is new to us, even going this far. I trust our group and most importantly, what’s going to be best for our players. We always try to take that into consideration.” A possible Rams itinerary All times are PST Leave 5:00 am Wednesday Arrive 9:00 pm Bed 11:00 pm Breakfast 8:00 am Thursday Game 5:35 pm With the exception of weights and some treatments, the typical gameday routine can be followed with some modifications. The players can follow their typical sleep routines on the flight home, and they shouldn’t upset their circadian rhythms. As an added bonus, the Rams have an extra 28 hours, compared to the Niners’ prep time, to prepare for their Giants game. The only real obstacle should be finding rooms with blackout curtains and quiet rooms so the players can sleep during their body clocks’ hours. Oh…and having Matthew Stafford’s back hold up over the two 16-hour flights.

title: Matthew Stafford is QB under the most pressure in 2026
summary: Despite winning a Super Bowl and MVP honors, Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford still has plenty to prove. In fact, it’s fair to label him as the signal caller facing the most pressure ahead of the 2026 season. Yep, more than Dak Prescott, who has yet to guide the Cowboys to the NFC Championship […]
full_text: Westchester, - August 01: Quarterback Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams during the Los Angeles Rams training camp on the campus of Loyola Marymount University in Westchester on Saturday, August 1, 2026. (Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images Despite winning a Super Bowl and MVP honors, Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford still has plenty to prove. In fact, it’s fair to label him as the signal caller facing the most pressure ahead of the 2026 season. Yep, more than Dak Prescott, who has yet to guide the Cowboys to the NFC Championship and beyond. More than Justin Herbert, who has yet to win a playoff game. More than Jalen Hurts, who has won a Super Bowl, but most everyone is still unsure about him. Heck, more than even Josh Allen, who has failed in his mission (thus far) to lead the Bills back to the Super Bowl. Stafford is facing the heat more than any of those other QBs simply because he’s the face of a super team. Los Angeles improved its defense by adding Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson, and decided to throw in Myles Garrett for the hell of it. The veteran recently called the Garrett acquisition a “shot in the arm,” which is definitely underselling it. Garrett is more than a “shot in the arm” — he’s what pushes a contender into title favorite status. The Rams were considered one of the best teams in the NFL before his arrival, and with him in tow, they’re clear favorites to win it all in February. TST’s own JB Scott noted L.A.’s Super Bowl odds improved by at least 200 points following the trade. FanDuel Sportsbook has the team at +550 odds to win the 2027 Super Bowl, way ahead of Seattle at +1100. Winning a Super Bowl was the goal all offseason after falling short against the Seahawks in the NFC Championship. Now, thanks to the all-in moves for Garrett and company, winning the big game is the only acceptable outcome. As we know, quarterbacks face the brunt of the heat whenever they fall short of expectations. In a team sport like football, I guess it’s only fair to do so. That’s the cost of playing QB in the NFL. You hear that, Stafford? You asked for this! Look, Stafford has already been in this position before. He faced pressure to guide a loaded Rams team to the Super Bowl in Year 1, and he delivered. Stafford doesn’t need another MVP season. His legacy and Hall of Fame chances will only be helped if he can secure another title. However, what he needs is to avoid the key mistakes that derail a title run while also providing the steady leadership expected of a veteran quarterback. Simply put, he must be the leader his team needs if they have any hope of meeting their lofty goals. Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk said it correctly: the Rams cannot allow themselves to get complacent despite the high expectations. Stafford will be tasked with keeping his hungry young team in check and ensuring they don’t get too ahead of themselves. View this post on Instagram The Rams traded for Garrett to win the Super Bowl, and anything less than a Lombardi Trophy will certainly be disappointing. Stafford already owns a ring, but this season isn’t about proving he can win another one. It’s about proving he can lead a different loaded roster back to the promised land, rather than another talented team that falls short.

title: Rams are limiting their time in Australia for Week 1 game
summary: It is being reported that the Los Angeles Rams will arrive in Australia for their pivotal Week 1 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers one day before the contest kicks off. Meanwhile, the 49ers will reportedly spend about a week in The Outback as they prepare to start their season off on the right foot. […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 29: Head coach Sean McVay of the Los Angeles Rams shakes hands with head coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers after the San Francisco 49ers defeated the Los Angeles Rams 23-20 at SoFi Stadium on November 29, 2020 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is being reported that the Los Angeles Rams will arrive in Australia for their pivotal Week 1 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers one day before the contest kicks off. Meanwhile, the 49ers will reportedly spend about a week in The Outback as they prepare to start their season off on the right foot. Fans, and media personalities attending the Week 1 international game are likely to end up spending more time in Australia than the Rams do. The Rams will arrive in Australia the day before their Week 1 matchup against the 49ers and depart Melbourne immediately after the game, per @DanGrazianoESPN . San Francisco will arrive a full week earlier so players and coaches can adjust to the time difference. pic.twitter.com/JfuhQ0CVcx — Yahoo Sports (@YahooSports) August 5, 2026 It’s two different approaches by two very successful franchises. For the Rams, this was perhaps to be expected since last year when they went to London, they limited their time across the pond, and ended up having their best game of the year against the Jacksonville Jaguars as L.A. won by a final score of 35 to 7. The traditional idea is that teams acclimate themselves to whatever area they have to travel to before gameday. The Rams are basically saying we don’t need to acclimate to anything, just give us a football field, and we’ll play. If the Rams win this game against SF, then their travel plans will be studied, if they aren’t being studied already. Keep an eye out for any changes to the Rams plans, but at this point, what they are planning in August is likely what they will do in September, with regard to their travel plans. Now, in terms of gameplans, expect Kyle Shanahan and McVay to dial it up. We’ll have to tune in on gameday to see which team’s travel plans seemingly worked out better, and which unit is ultimately able to find a way to secure the victory.

title: Las Vegas Raiders Summer Scouting: SAF Rankings
summary: I broke down the 2027 scouting classes in my early summer scouting series, and the room has a ton of potential with a long list of potential standout players. I broke down the offense and defense in articles and I suggest reading those for a broad aspect of the room. The Raiders do have some […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - JANUARY 01: Kewan Lacy #5 of the Ole Miss Rebels is chased by Kj Bolden #4 of the Georgia Bulldogs during the first quarter during the 2025 College Football Playoff Quarterfinal at the Allstate Sugar Bowl at Caesars Superdome on January 01, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images) | Getty Images I broke down the 2027 scouting classes in my early summer scouting series, and the room has a ton of potential with a long list of potential standout players. I broke down the offense and defense in articles and I suggest reading those for a broad aspect of the room. The Raiders do have some talent on the interior OL, and I’d expect Las Vegas to add more in 2027 as John Spytek does. The Raiders will see Jeremy Chinn possibly hit free agency, and they did add rookies Treydan Stuke & Dalton Johnson this last year, though Stukes likely will play a diverse bandit safety role leaving some holes in the FS and SS positions. The 2027 draft class is exceptional at safety, and Las Vegas could really use a rangy over the top free safety that they have lacked for a long time. These rankings are extremely early, and they will evolve over not only the summer but the next 8-10 months throughout the season, and into draft season. Some lists will feature 10, 15, 20, or more ranked prospects but I’ll include others on the list below to note. Tae Johnson, Notre Dame – 6’3/195, R-So Elite. Johnson is coming off a 2025 where in his first year as a starter he logged 51 tackles, 4 INT, and 7 PBU with another 2 TD and a FF. Johnson allowed a 51.7 QBR, is an elite tackler, and he’s an uber athlete. He has a phenomenal first step and continues to show sideline to sideline ability. Johnson plays physical, has elite hip flexibility, and he uses his full body in most reps with an ability to consistently turn and run and take away passing lanes. Johnson is smart, he has an ability to read and react well, and with his first step quickness Johnson can close passing lanes quickly to jump routes. As a run defender, Johnson is able to drive downfield, he’s shown good great tackling angles, and is just a strong tackler overall. There’s a lot of potential for Johnson to be even better than Xavier Watts, Alohi Gilman, and Kyle Hamilton. KJ Bolden, Georgia – 6’0/190, Jr KJ Bolden and Tae Johnson are going to be 1a & 1b all year long and I might end with them just tied for number one. He’s logged a career 135 tackles, 3 INT, and 7 PBU and while not elite production, Bolden just hasn’t been targeted. Bolden has elite hip flexibility to pair with strong first step explosiveness, and he’s just an elite athlete overall. Bolden is average in size, he isn’t the strongest and it does show at times with him getting boxed out by bigger tight ends and receivers in situations. Bolden shows sideline to sideline skill, elite instincts, and he pairs these with a good first step to take away passing concepts, routes, and he’s extremely knowledgably in the backend working to manipulate quarterbacks eyes. Bolden also shows good tackling ability, but the lack of strength does knock him at times, as does average tackling form where he’ll ankle bite. He’s aggressive, which can get him flagged, and he’ll bite on double moves but Bolden shows a high level recovery speed to take routes away. Bray Hubbard, Alabama – 6’2/215, R-Jr Bray Hubbard is a traditional SS but he shows some tendencies to play a FS role, though I like him a lot in a BANDIT role or box safety. Hubbard is coming off a 2025 with 79 tackles, 5 TFL, 4 interceptions, 7 PBU, and 3 FF for Alabama & his elite frame/athleticism works in his favor a lot. Hubbard is super aggressive, and playing near the line of scrimmage helps him avoid being susceptible to big plays over the top due to biting on double moves/play action. Hubbard is an elite athlete, drives on the ball well, and he’s consistently able to take away route combinations and lanes due to his length. The Alabama product also shows good tackling angles, he’s physical, and he has an ability to work off blocks but I’d like to see him clear up his form with a high missed tackle rate. Overall, Hubbard is versatile, and it’s rare to find strong safeties with his level of athletic ability and ball skills. Corey Myrick, Clemson – 6’3/205, R-So Myrick is an exceptional athlete, and he’s played at Marshall then Southern Miss before transferring to Clemson. The Junior has true sideline to sideline range, a quick first step, and elite hip flexibility. Myrick does a good job working the sideline to his advantage, and he uses his size to consistently to box out defenders. Myrick does need to improve as a tackler where he can be slow to react at times, and there’s also some inconsistent angles which will not succeed at Clemson compared to the SunBelt. Myrick’s athleticism is elite, and he pairs that with good football IQ at the position, Myrick tracks the ball well, shows an ability to break and take away route concepts, and overall projects as a long-term starting FS with an ability to play in single high coverage. In his lone year at Southern Miss, Myrick logged 92 tackles, 5 TFL, 2 INT, and 6 PBU. Tao Johnson, UCLA – 6’1/195, Sr Johnson transferred to UCLA from Utah after 51 tackles, 2 TFL, 2 INT, and 4 PBU in 2025. Johnson isn’t the best athlete, and he’s shown some issues at times in downfield coverage due to his lack of long speed and inconsistent first step. That said, Johnson is a phenomenal run defender, he takes good fluid angles, has strong hip movements, and he’s physical. Johnson isn’t an ankle biter, shows good form in his tackling, and he’ll deconstruct blocks well. Additionally, Johnson does show an ability to play the ball in space, and wins with his instincts where he’s extremely smart, able to bait quarterbacks, and understands leverage well to force defenders to the sideline. Johnson is likely going to push into the strong safety or closer to the line of scrimmage role in the NFL, and he’s a good mover in space but limited athletically overall though his instincts make up for it. Jelani McDonald, Texas – 6’2/200, Sr Koi Perich, Oregon – 6’1/200, R-Jr Perich is going to play a similar role to Dillon Thieneman as a single high safety, and the former Minneosta standout could excel in the role. Perich is instinctual, he’s a great tackler, and he drives on the ball well. There’s times he’s very aggressive and abandons his passing lanes to try and make a play on the ball, leaving a big play opportunity open. Perich does have a ton of inconsistency on his film, but the natural ball skills, aggressiveness, and instincts will get looks in the NFL. Ty Bartrum, UCF – 6’1/195, R-Sr Harvard standout, good athlete, extremely intelligent player. Shows ability to play the nickel, strong/free, and single high safety. Interested how it adapts to UCF compared from FCS Harvard. Peyton Bowen, Oklahoma – 6’0/201, Sr Amare Ferrell, Indiana – 6’2/205, Sr HIGHLY instinctual single high safety, shows good ball skills. Versatile safety, good hip flexibility, limited range at times but does a good job driving on the ball and taking away route concepts. Ferrell can rise quickly, he’s smart, a stable athlete, and does his job in the run game. There’s a lot to like, despite limitations in his lower body movement. He’s coming off back to back seasons with 50 tackles, 4 TFL, and 4 interceptions though he added 8 PBU in 2025 compared to 2 in 2024. Other Names To Watch: Adon Shuler, Notre Dame – Aggressive, physical strong safety. Needs to refine his play, likely won’t commit, can play SS/FS/Nickel. Good tackler Marcus Neal, Penn State Keon Sabb, Alabama Faletau Satulala, BYU – Sneaky riser in the class. Great size, good ball skills. Tackles well, will take over Tanner Wall’s FS role and could see a lot of production. SMART player. Ty Benefield, LSU Qua Moss, Tennessee – Athletic, 6’3 safety. Tons of plays on the ball, smart but inconsistent. Rod Moore, Michigan – Former…

full_text: Roger Craig #22, Running Back for the Los Angeles Raiders in motion carrying the football during the American Football Conference West game against the San Francisco 49ers on 29th September 1991 at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, Los Angeles, California, United States. The Raiders won the game 16 - 13. (Photo by Ken Levine/Allsport/Getty Images) | Getty Images Once a Riader, always a Raider, right? That’s how the franchise treats their players and that is always evident when they celebrate the success of players who enter the Pro Football Hall of Fame even if they played just a brief time for the Silver and Black. That will be the case this weekend when running back Roger Craig will be inducted into the Canton, Ohio musuem as a senior committee candidate. The induction ceremony starts Saturday at 11:30 a.m. PT. Craig joined the Los Angeles Raiders in 1991 after starring for the San Francisco 49ers for eight years. He played for the Raiders for one season before spending the final two seasons of his career with the Minnesota Vikings. Craig made the Hall of Fame, of course, because of his vital role on the 49ers’ championship teams. But he did contribute for the Raiders as he was a teammate of Hall of Fame running back Marcus Allen. Craig started 13 games for the Raiders and he had 590 yards and 17 catches for the Raiders, who went 9-7. And now he will be inmortalzied in Canton forever.

title: Segun Olubi’s special teams prowess, speed difficult to knock off roster
summary: It’s easy to overlook Segun Olubi’s addition to the Las Vegas Raiders. The linebacker isn’t as big of a name as his fellow free agent additions like Quay Walker and Nakobe Dean. The former Green Bay Packer and Philadelphia Eagle, respectively, are set to be the faces of the Raider recalibration at the starting linebacker […]
full_text: May 28, 2026; Henderson, NV, USA; Las Vegas Raiders linebacker Segun Olubi (50) during organized team activities at Intermountain Health Performance Center. Mandatory Credit: Candice Ward-Imagn Images | Candice Ward-Imagn Images It’s easy to overlook Segun Olubi’s addition to the Las Vegas Raiders. The linebacker isn’t as big of a name as his fellow free agent additions like Quay Walker and Nakobe Dean. The former Green Bay Packer and Philadelphia Eagle, respectively, are set to be the faces of the Raider recalibration at the starting linebacker spots, after all. Then came the announcements of center Tyler Linderbaum, edge rusher Kwity Paye, and wide receiver Jalen Nailor being as official acquisitions shortly after the NFL’s transaction wire kicked into gear at the start of the new league year on March 11. Five days after the flurry of money deals were made amongst the 32 teams in the league, Las Vegas made official the signing of Olubi. Like his former Indianapolis Colts and current Raiders teammate Paye, the 26-year-old linebacker was brought in for specific reasons. And in the San Diego State product, the Silver & Black land an elite, high-impact special teams ace. “He’s a difference maker-type guy,” Raiders special teams coordinator Joe DeCamillis said of Olubi back in June after one of the team’s minicamp sessions. “He’s blocked punts in the league. He obviously had one against the Raiders last year. He’s a guy that is twitchy, he’s a guy that has already shown what he can do on the field, and he’s brought a lot to the to the group for us already. So, it’s going to be good to coach him. I’m excited we have him.” Olubi’s special teams prowess and speed is going to be hard to knock off the Raiders roster this offseason. By The Numbers Segun Olubi, Linebacker, 5th Year 2025: 17 games (zero starts), 11 total tackles, 1 forced fumble, 1 blocked punt; 362 snaps on special teams, 6 on defense Career: (2022-25) 51 games (2 starts), 50 total tackles, 1 interception, 1 pass deflection, 2 forced fumbles, 2 fumble recoveries, 2 blocked punts; 1,095 snaps on special teams, 141 on defense #RAIDERS ROSTER MOVE: – Signed LB Segun Olubi #RaiderNation | @Raiders pic.twitter.com/gAB6wvL5Ka — Raiders PR (@RAIDERS_PR) March 16, 2026 Luring DeCamillis out of the collegiate ranks — the veteran special teams boss spent the last three seasons in the SEC coaching at Texas and South Carolina — was a task but the connection with the Kubiak family was too strong to turn down. “There’s a lot of similarities between him and his dad, but there’s some differences too,” DeCamillis said of Klint and his father Gary Kubiak “Both are very, very detail-oriented. They love ball, which I think is huge, and he’s done a great job of organizing things since he’s been here, which I knew he would. It’s great to be with him, for sure, and the whole staff. I’ve worked with a few guys that are on the staff also.” That attention to detail meant reconstituting all three phases of the Raiders’ game: Offense, defense, and special teams. Hence signing Olubi and fellow special teams dynamo wide receiver Dareke Young (who Klint Kubiak is all too familiar with during their respective time with the Seattle Seahawks last season). It’s never a bad idea to add elite or upper echelon talent — even on special teams. DeCamillis and his assistant coaches, Marquice Williams and Tim McConnell, are charged with providing the defibrillator to a Las Vegas special teams group that flatlined last season. From blocked kicks ( Daniel Carlson’s game-winning try thwarted by the Chicago Bears in Week 4; AJ Cole III’s two punts in Week 5 and Week 10 , respectively), to awful coverage (Washington Commanders rookie receiver Jaylin Lane torching the team for a 90-yard punt return touchdown in Week 3 , chief among them), and kicking instability (large portion to why Carlson is gone and veteran Matt Gay and undrafted rookie Kansei Matsuzawa are competing for the place kicker gig), the Silver & Black were a case study in breakdowns and blunders. And this is for a special teams group that historically flourished while the rest of the team floundered. In order to do a 180-degree turn, bringing in proven impact players like Olubi is the way to go about it. That Week 5 punt block that ended up hobbling Cole was Olubi. The 6-foot-1 and 233-pound difference maker still exhibits the 4.44 speed he clocked in at San Diego State’s pro day heading into the league in 2022 and brings a tremendous chip on his shoulder, frenetic energy tailor made for special teams work, and all-important work ethic and accountability. Yep, this is the guy the #Raiders just signed. pic.twitter.com/59oEdMlvWw — Levi Edwards (@theleviedwards) March 16, 2026 Look at the block Olubi had of Cole’s punt in the above tweet. That kind of game-altering screaming off the edge impact play has been sorely missing for Las Vegas as takeaways have become a rarity. He paced the Colts with 30 special teams tackles including a highly efficient 2025 campaign where he notched 11 stops on special teams — including a forced fumble — and a blocked punt putting him in select company as only one of a baker’s dozen (13) to achieve the same stat line last season. Don’t expect a drastic role change for Olubi in Silver & Black. He compiled 1,095 special teams snaps during his time in Indianapolis and he’s expected to be a core special teamer in Las Vegas. The linebacker notched 362 special teams snaps in 2025 to just six defensive snaps. And his heaviest workload in both groups occurred in his second season in 2024 where Olubi tallied 334 special teams and 114 defensive snaps. Olubi’s competition in DeCamillis’ department are fellow young linebackers Tommy Eichenberg and Cody Lindenberg. That duo accounted for 371 and 362 snaps on special teams in 2025 and it’s the former that showcased some jarring hitting ability in coverage. But neither of the Bergs bring what Olubi has: Explosiveness and unadulterated speed. Couple that with a resume of impact plays, and it’s difficult to see the Bergs knock off the latest addition off the roster. Although, there’s plenty of special teams work to be had. “Like you said, he’s very energetic, and I think that for special teams at this level, I think that’s very, very critical, because the reality is most people don’t grow up wanting to play left tackle on punt team. They want to be the starting linebacker,” Cole said of DeCamillis’ importance to the special teams room. “Most people don’t grow up saying, ‘Oh, I want to be the wing.’ They want to be the starting running back, but we need those guys to do that job at a high level. And so, when he comes into the room with that energy and that fire and that passion, I think it lights it in a bunch of other people. And so, hopefully, I mean, I’m confident that that will bring the best out of the group.” Olubi certainly matches that energy, fire, and passion. And barring an injury or sudden plummet to ineffectiveness, he’ll not only make the final 53-man roster, but likely be worth more than the one-year, $1.145 million contract he inked with the Raiders.

title: Malik Benson making strong push for role on Las Vegas Raiders’ offense during training camp
summary: It’s no secret that the third wide receiver spot on the Las Vegas Raiders’ depth chart is up for grabs during training camp. While 2025 second-round pick Jack Bech is the logical choice to win the job, Bech had an underwhelming rookie season and is far from a heavy favorite to earn the role on […]
full_text: HENDERSON, NEVADA - AUGUST 03: Malik Benson #19 of the Las Vegas Raiders practice during the team's training camp at the Las Vegas Raiders Headquarters/Intermountain Health Performance Center on August 03, 2026 in Henderson, Nevada. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s no secret that the third wide receiver spot on the Las Vegas Raiders’ depth chart is up for grabs during training camp . While 2025 second-round pick Jack Bech is the logical choice to win the job, Bech had an underwhelming rookie season and is far from a heavy favorite to earn the role on offense. That opens the door for a dark horse to factor into the mix, and 2026 sixth-rounder Malik Benson has turned some heads early in camp. “Another late-round rookie who’s put veterans on notice this camp is Benson,” The Athletic’s Sam Warren wrote on Aug. 3. “The sixth-round draft pick has found good chemistry with No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza so far, earning him more opportunities as camp has gone on.” With plenty of eyes on Mendoza this summer, developing a connection with the future of the franchise will certainly help the Oregon product make a name for himself and climb up the depth chart. But Benson hasn’t just caught the media’s attention; he’s drawn good reviews from the coaching staff and his teammates as well. Head coach Klint Kubiak was asked about the rookie receiver’s performance so far, and, in typical stoic Kubiak fashion, the coach said Benson has had a “good head start” and is “playing good football” while also noting that he still has a lot to prove to the coaching staff (h/t SleeperRaiders on X/Twitter ). The latter is certainly a fair statement. The Raiders only have about a week’s worth of practices under their belts, and the pads just came on at the time of writing. So, the first-year wideout still has plenty of checkpoints to clear before reaching the finish line and winning the race. But he’s out to an early lead and has drawn praise from his potential running mates, veteran wide receivers Tre Tucker and Jalen Nailor. “Man, I’m so excited for him because as an older guy coming to the league with the guys that I had in my room, the one thing you want to see is a young guy that wants to get better,” Tucker replied when asked about Benson. “They’re not going through the motions, and Leek (Malik) comes in every single day and wants to get better. And he is getting better every play, every rep, and he can run all day. “That’s something that I tell him that makes you super here in a way because if you can run all day, you can play fast, like there’s a spot for you here. So, I’m excited for him. I have him under my wing just to keep him going because I know what it’s like to be a rookie. I’m very excited for him, and I think he’s going to be a very big part of us this year too.” Nailor shared a similar statement on the sixth-rounder’s performance. “He’s a young kid; he has a ways to go, but he’s asking questions, he’s asking the right questions,” Nailor said. “He wants to be better, he wants to play, he wants to be on this team, he wants to show himself. So, just having that type of mindset as a young rookie, it means a lot. Just to have him asking questions, to me, it shows that he cares. I care as well, so I want to give him all the pointers that I can with whatever he’s asking.” It will be interesting to see what Kubiak and Co. want to do with the wide receiver rotation moving forward. The passing game will likely be run through two-time Pro Bowl tight end Brock Bowers, and Kubiak leaned heavily on 12 personnel as the Seattle Seahawks’ offensive coordinator last year. Also, Tucker, Nailor and Benson have similar skill sets while Bech can bring something different out wide. Of course, the Raiders’ coaching staff doesn’t have to have that figured out right now, as the season opener against the Miami Dolphins is still more than a month away. Additionally, it’s still early in training camp, so there’s time for Benson’s hype train to slow down. But that doesn’t change the fact that the Raiders’ sixth-round pick appears to be ahead of schedule and has a chance to take on a bigger role than previously expected.

(Photo by Fred Kfoury III/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins claimed rookie tight end Jeremiah Fanklin off waivers on Wednesday, the team accounted. He originally entered the league as an undrafted free agent out of Illinois, signing with the Seattle Seahawks. He spent time last year on the Indianapolis Colts’ practice squad. title: Dolphins add defensive lineman after injury
summary: The Miami Dolphins added defensive lineman Fatorma Mulbah to the roster on Wednesday, according to his agent Brett Tessler. The move comes a day after rookie defensive tackle Rene Konga suffered a serious injury. The specifics of the injury were not released, but head coach Jeff Hafley left no doubt that it would be season-ending. […]
full_text: Aug 16, 2025; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; New York Jets defensive tackle Fatorma Mulbah (62) following the game against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Rich Barnes-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Miami Dolphins added defensive lineman Fatorma Mulbah to the roster on Wednesday, according to his agent Brett Tessler . The move comes a day after rookie defensive tackle Rene Konga suffered a serious injury. The specifics of the injury were not released, but head coach Jeff Hafley left no doubt that it would be season-ending. Hafley, after answering questions about injury status of some of the other players on the roster, added, “[Konga]’s the one [injury] that will be long term. He’ll be out for the season…But Konga will be done for the year, and that’s unfortunate because he’s a young guy who was working really hard and he’ll have to view this as a redshirt year.” Konga joined the Dolphins as an undrafted free agent this year. He started his college career at Rutgers before transferring to Louisville for the last two seasons. During the 2025 season, he recorded 29 tackles, 1.5 sacks, and six passes defensed in 12 games for Louisville; he was named Second-Team All-ACC after the season. The Dolphins have a lot of depth at defensive tackle, but Konga could have been fighting for a developmental spot on the roster or practice squad. Mulbah originally entered the league last year as an undrafted free agent out of West Virginia, signing with the New York Jets. He was cut by the team, but then returned to their practice squad in October before being released again in January. He spent the start of his college career at Penn State.

title: Dolphins shake up leadership group with new CEO named
summary: The Miami Dolphins on Tuesday shook up the top levels of the franchise in a move that probably should not have come as a surprise. After 13 years as the Dolphins’ President and Chief Executive Officer, Tom Garfinkel stepped down, paving the way for owner Stephen Ross to name Daniel Sillman to the top spot […]
full_text: Miami Dolphins owner Stephen M. Ross and Dolphins Vice Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer Tom Garfinkel talk before the start of an NFL football game against the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday, Sept. 8, 2019 at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Fla. (David Santiago/Miami Herald/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) | TNS via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins on Tuesday shook up the top levels of the franchise in a move that probably should not have come as a surprise. After 13 years as the Dolphins’ President and Chief Executive Officer, Tom Garfinkel stepped down, paving the way for owner Stephen Ross to name Daniel Sillman to the top spot of football operations. Sillman, who led the team’s search for new general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan and new head coach Jeff Hafley this offseason, has been named in the succession plan for the Dolphins should anything happen to Ross. Sillman was named the CEO of Ross Sports & Entertainment, a newly formed entity that brings the Dolphins, Hard Rock Stadium, the Miami Grand Prix, the Miami Open tennis tournament and the Precision Drive Club under one umbrella for Ross. Several members of Ross’s leadership team will now report to Sillman, which for the Dolphins including Sullivan, Hafley, and Executive Vice President of Football Operations Brandon Shore. While Garfinkel is stepping away from his day-to-day role with the Dolphins, he will remain as Vice Chairman for the Dolphins and Hard Rock Stadium. He will also remain as the managing partner for the Miami Grand Prix. Garfinkel’s work since becoming the President and CEO of the Dolphins was highlighted in the press release from the team. It read, “Since joining the Dolphins in 2013, Garfinkel spearheaded the business turnaround of the organization, including increasing annual revenues by more than 400 percent and securing more than $3 billion in future contractually obligated sponsorship income. Garfinkel led the vision and execution of the privately funded $550 million transformation of Hard Rock Stadium, oversaw the development of the $135 million Baptist Health Training Complex, and helped grow the Dolphins Cancer Challenge into the NFL’s largest charitable fundraiser, generating more than $100 million for cancer research. ” Garfinkel was also responsible for creation of the Miami Grand Prix for Formula 1 racing around Hard Rock Stadium and for bringing the Miami Open tennis tournament to Hard Rock Stadium. His efforts also resulted in the Dolphins’ home stadium hosting a Super Bowl, two College Football National Championship games, and seven matches during the 2026 World Cup including the third place game. “I love the Dolphins and the people here, but after 13 years it was just the right time for me to make this decision,” said Garfinkel via the press release. “The business has never been in a better place and the team of people we have here is second to none in sports. I want to thank the South Florida community and Dolphins fans for all of their support over the years and especially Steve Ross for the opportunity to be a part of this great organization. He is a visionary leader and a team owner who always strives to be best-in-class, and he provides his people all the trust and resources needed to be successful. I have every confidence in where this organization is headed on and off the field under Danny’s leadership, and I’m excited about the new challenges that will come moving forward.”

I just see them, have an opportunity to watch them interact, and I just see how comfortable they are with each other. They have different characteristics that I think all of us can decide how that works,” Wilf continued about Teasley and O’Connell. “But from my perspective, it’s working well. Coach can focus on what he has to focus on, [and] Nolan can focus on what he focuses on, and they share and they collaborate, and everyone in the building feels that.” Here are three other takeaways from Wilf’s press conference Wednesday: Anticipation of hosting 2028 NFL Draft The Vikings in May were selected to host the 2028 NFL Draft, which will be just over a decade after hosting Super Bowl LII. Wilf described being “thrilled” about the honor and “tremendous opportunity” for the state of Minnesota. “As you know, the draft has become one of the league’s premier events, and hosting it here means hundreds of thousands of fans will descend on this community, and our state will be placed squarely in the global spotlight,” Wilf said. “And like we’ve done many times in the past, the community will of course deliver. Minnesota has proven its ability to host national and international events at the highest level. “We have tremendous partners across the state, and I’m confident we’re going to put on another first-class event in 2028,” he added. Ownership continues appreciating stewardship opportunity Wilf was asked during his media availability if, considering the recent sale of the Seahawks and the numbers involved, he’s entertained the idea of selling the team down the road. “Well, the business side of it is not what got us into the Minnesota Vikings,” he emphasized. “We love football. We’re honored and privileged to be stewards of an incredible franchise. “Our ultimate goal is to bring championships to the fans of the Minnesota Vikings; they really…
