summary: The Minnesota Vikings completed Day 7 of training camp — their second day in pads at TCO Performance Center — and the quarterback battle between Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy is beginning to look less like a competition and more like a coronation. On the latest episode of The Real Forno Show, host Tyler Forness, […]
full_text: EAGAN, MINNESOTA - MAY 27: Kyler Murray #1 of the Minnesota Vikings participates in a drill during an OTA workout at Twin Cities Orthopedics Performance Center on May 27, 2026 in Eagan, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings completed Day 7 of training camp — their second day in pads at TCO Performance Center — and the quarterback battle between Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy is beginning to look less like a competition and more like a coronation. On the latest episode of The Real Forno Show , host Tyler Forness, who was live at TCO, broke down everything Vikings fans need to know alongside co-host Dave Stefano. Key Points from This Episode: QB Battle: Murray Pulling Away — Forness, who has attended the last four practices, said Murray is separating from McCarthy in the areas that matter most: processing speed, consistency, and explosive downfield throws. Murray connected on two deep post touchdowns — a 40-yarder in 7-on-7 and a 60-yarder in team drills. “I think it’s now becoming a matter of time that Kyler Murray is going to be named the starter,” said Forness. J.J. McCarthy: Best Day, But Not Enough — McCarthy had his sharpest processing day of camp but couldn’t sustain it. “He’ll drop back, he’ll have a really clean process, and he’ll rip a 15-yard out route — but two plays later it feels like it’s unraveling,” Forness noted. Tai Felton Turning Heads — Forness compared Felton’s emergence to K.J. Osborn’s 2021 breakout. “I’m very impressed with Tai Felton. He’s showcasing a lot.” Felton hauled in a 60-yard touchdown bomb from Murray on a deep post in team drills. Chuck Demmings Is the Real Deal — The fifth-round rookie cornerback is winning reps against Justin Jefferson. “He is winning against Justin Jefferson… This dude has the perfect brain for a cornerback,” Forness said. Demmings is a legitimate steal. Demond Claiborne Struggling — The return specialist has logged multiple drops in his first two camp days and was laid out by Jamal Adams. “Very, very unimpressed so far with Demond Claiborne,” Forness said plainly. Dallas Turner Flashing — The pass rusher tallied multiple pressures and sacks during team drills. Running Game Looks Different — With Frank Smith brought in to revamp the run game, Forness believes Jordan Mason will eventually earn a larger share of the backfield over Aaron Jones in wide zone sets. Jordan Addison Thumb Injury — A jammed thumb kept Addison out, but imaging cleared him and it’s not considered serious. Listen: Or on your favorite podcast aggregator. title: Vikings Training Camp Notes: 8/5 Edition
summary: The Minnesota Vikings had the most physical practice of training camp today, in full pads, and this one seemed to take on more importance than others as kind of the final test of the first week of training camp. Tomorrow is an off-day- no practice- but I wouldn’t be surprised if the coaching staff was […]
full_text: The Minnesota Vikings had the most physical practice of training camp today, in full pads, and this one seemed to take on more importance than others as kind of the final test of the first week of training camp. Tomorrow is an off-day- no practice- but I wouldn’t be surprised if the coaching staff was hard at work with evaluations and updated plans for the next part of training camp. So, let’s get into it. Quarterback Competition If you look at the readout of attempts and completions (below, compiled by Judd Zulgad) for Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy, you’d probably come to the conclusion that it was a pretty even day in the quarterback competition. It wasn’t. Murray: 14/21, including 11/15 in 11 on 11 and 3/6 in 7 on 7. McCarthy: 13/20, including 10/14 in 11 on 11 and 3/6 in 7 on 7. In fact, after today’s practice, I would not be surprised if Kevin O’Connell declares Kyler Murray the starting quarterback sometime in the next few days, perhaps even tomorrow. We’ll see. Kyler Murray The reason the quarterback competition wasn’t close today, despite the completion percentage stats indicating so, is first of all Kyler Murray threw for about a hundred more yards than J.J. McCarthy in 11-on-11 team drills, which are what really counts. Murray had two bombs- one to Tai Felton who was wide open on a post route that went for a long (50 yard-ish) touchdown, and another one later to Justin Jefferson that was really kind of a jump ball that Jefferson came down with over Isaiah Rodgers and Theo Jackson. Jefferson ran it in for a touchdown. . @JJettas2 ✈️✈️ pic.twitter.com/kOoqRGafil — Minnesota Vikings (@Vikings) August 6, 2026 Looking at this video, it looked like Rodgers might have been a bit more cautious to avoid a collision/injury than he might have been in a real game, but still a nice play by Jefferson to come down with it. Kyler Murray to Tai Felton for the DEEP touchdown 👀 (Via Vikings mobile app) pic.twitter.com/iYFMG9f1vJ — VikingzFanPage (@vikingzfanpage) August 6, 2026 This last throw by Murray- hitting a receiver deep and in-stride- we haven’t seen since 2024 Sam Darnold. It looked like Isaiah Rodgers again in coverage but whether he was supposed to have help over the top is a question. If so, it looked like Josh Metellus, who came running late, missed the assignment. Murray’s other passes were mostly short, but a couple intermediate ones too including a TD pass to Jauan Jennings. His incompletions were on a middle screen that got blown up, an intermediate pass to Hockenson that was a bit low but Hockenson dropped it, a PBU by Charles Demmings on an intermediate pass targeting Jefferson, and a throw-away after a scramble in the red zone with nobody open. Murray again looked calm in the pocket- he actually held the ball a bit longer today than in other practices looking for the deep ball- and was able to move the offense well. No miscommunications or bad snaps or other mishaps today. He also scrambled and ran a few times after not finding an open receiver in team drills- once left, once right, and once up the middle. I didn’t see a would-be sack of Murray today either. J.J. McCarthy McCarthy’s completions in 11-on-11 team drills were mostly of the short variety, with a few intermediate passes mixed in. He also had two or three would-be sacks where the rusher broke it off because hitting quarterbacks is not allowed. But going back to my training camp notes on Monday , this was another McCarthy performance that looked very similar to his training camp performances last year. On most pass attempts, it simply looks like a struggle for him processing. There are some quick hitters when he does fine, but on most longer route concepts he holds the ball too long, waiting for a receiver to come open until he’s under pressure and opts for a checkdown. I don’t think he’s even attempted an over-the-top bomb since the start of training camp in 11-on-11 team drills. Last year in training camp there were usually one or two attempts each practice. Toward the end of 11-on-11 drills Kevin O’Connell talked to him a few times in-between plays. Judging by what happened on the previous play, it looked like O’Connell was trying to get him to speed up his processing. At one point he raised his hand to his head with his finger pointed toward his head moving in a circular motion indicating speed it up. There was even a completion over the middle to Jennings late in the down where O’Connell talked to him after the play seemingly to get him to speed things up. So, for the most part, 2026 training camp McCarthy is the same as 2025 training camp McCarthy, except no deep balls. His completion percentage may look fine, but it’s mostly screens and checkdowns. And the reason it’s mostly screens and checkdowns is because he’s too slow processing and isn’t able to throw with anticipation. Accuracy can be an issue on occasion- mostly on the longer throws he attempts, but that hasn’t been as big an issue in team drills this year primarily because he’s not throwing down the field much. There were no layered throws again today. What we are seeing is McCarthy having reached a plateau that isn’t high enough to be a quality starter. And until the light comes on and he’s able to process faster, he’s likely to remain at this level. So, Murray continues to separate himself and the first-team reps have been following that separation over the last 3-4 practices. I don’t know how much more Kevin O’Connell needs to see before he names Murray the starter, but I wouldn’t be surprised if he does so soon. That would allow Murray to get all the first-team reps going forward and help him continue to learn the offense and build rapport with the receivers he’ll be throwing to in the regular season. For McCarthy, the question becomes whether he or Carson Wentz would be the best backup. Battle in the Trenches Offensive and defensive linemen faced off today in full contact drills that were fun to watch- almost as fun as the special teams gunner drills- which I’ll get into later. The trench battles began with one-on-one pass rush/block drills. The Vikings website broke it down like this: Christian Darrisaw and Dallas Turner set the tone and traded blows out of the gate. On their initial rep, Darrisaw locked up a bull rush by the third-year OLB; Turner got him right back, winning with speed. Defensive lineman Levi Drake Rodriguez, who turned 26 Tuesday, took home the make-believe Best Move Award with a silky spin move past center Blake Brandel that landed him smack dab in the lap of an assistant coach acting as QB. Second-year DL Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins and guard Will Fries went back and forth, just like CD and DT, with the former executing a nice push-pull rush, and then the latter resetting his feet to win take No. 2. The strongest two-rep sequence belonged to 2025 UDFA Joe Huber, who shut down back-to-back rushes by 2026 first-round pick Caleb Banks. Huber sat down in his seat and cranked his feet on both occasions. Toward the end of the drill, Jalen Redmond and Turner stunted left down the line to squeeze past guard Donovan Jackson and Darrisaw and reach the QB in a timely manner. Earlier, Jackson outlasted Redmond twice. I would also add: Brandel won a rep against LDR as well Andrew Van Ginkel got by Brian O’Neill Caleb Tiernan held off Bo Richter Elijah Williams got the better of Henry Byrd Tomas Rimac (at tackle) held off Arden Walker twice Big Citrus Domonique Orange gave Henry Byrd all he could handle Eric Johnson and Vershon Lee battled to a draw, more or less Rimac and Richter each won a rep against each other Caleb Banks and Big Citrus Joe Huber holding off Caleb Banks twice in a row is notable here and kind of summarizes where things are at right now overall with both Banks and Big Citrus when also including 11-on-11 reps. With both Banks and Big Citrus, they don’t get a lot of reps in team drills- they’re usually in for just a couple reps and then are rotated out. That has led to more reps for…

title: Wonder About the Over/Under
summary: The crew at the Daily Norseman is doing its usual stellar job covering the opening days of training camp, including an increasingly intriguing quarterback competition. The same goes for the news that the Vikings brought in safety Jamal Adams and extended offensive tackle Brian O’Neill. We’re so back. This allows me to vent a little. […]
full_text: EAGAN, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 01: Head coach Kevin O'Connell of the Minnesota Vikings looks on during Training Camp at Twin Cities Orthopedics Performance Center on August 01, 2026 in Eagan, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images The crew at the Daily Norseman is doing its usual stellar job covering the opening days of training camp, including an increasingly intriguing quarterback competition . The same goes for the news that the Vikings brought in safety Jamal Adams and extended offensive tackle Brian O’Neill. We’re so back. This allows me to vent a little. The topic? The Vikings’ head-scratching over/under of 8.5 wins for the upcoming season. I’ve noted several times over the past year or so how astute the oddsmakers are. They tend to know what they’re doing, whether it’s good or bad for the team(s) you root for. This time, I’m truly at a loss. Take last year, when the over/under was 8.5 wins early in the offseason and 9.5 wins in some places just before Week 1. Did I agree with it? Nope. Chugging a gallon or 12 of purple Kool-Aid (as always) was a contributing factor. Did I understand it? Absolutely. Rolling with a first-time, unproven starter at quarterback alone was enough to justify a healthy drop from 14 wins the year prior. Known unknowns were there. And guess what? The oddsmakers were right on, and yours truly was wrong. I had them at 12, while it took a Week 18 home win over a Green Bay Packers team already locked in the 7th seed for the over to hit at 9-8… or not, if you didn’t get in early. TOO MUCH NEEDS TO HAPPEN FOR THE UNDER Fast-forward to now, and the Vikings are again staring at an 8.5 over/under for the 2026 season. That is dead last in the NFC North, behind the Lions at 10.5, the Packers at 9.5, and the Bears at 9.5. Gross. Unlike last year and most years before it, I can’t get my head around the logic this time. The Vikings entered the 2025 season with a strength of schedule ranked 4th- to 7th-hardest, depending on the metrics used (e.g., opponents’ prior-year winning percentage vs. projected over/under). This year, it’s ranked 11th to 17th. As I noted previously, the overall quarterback play in 2025 was the worst since at least 2013, probably 2007. And those offenses were run-first, Adrian Peterson-led units. The numbers tell the story. Last year, per Statmuse, the McCarthy- (mostly injured) Wentz- Brosmer trifecta managed only 3,200 gross passing yards, about 1,200 fewer than in 2024. Gross is the keyword here. This ranked 30th in passing yards per game. Meanwhile, the Vikings ranked 28th in EPA per play. We went 9-8 and missed the playoffs by ½ game. For the Vikings to not match that mark and therefore not hit the over for 2026, most, if not all, of the following will need to occur: QUARTERBACK/OFFENSIVE PERFORMANCE (REGARDLESS OF STARTER) Kyler Murray, a former #1 overall pick with over 20,000 career passing yards, a 67% completion percentage, and a 2:1 TD-INT ratio, will need to be so bad in this offense that he gets benched. This would defy historical precedent, given what KOC has done with veterans such as Sam Darnold and Nick Mullens. J.J. McCarthy, who was 6-4 as a starter despite the struggles, will have to make zero improvement during an offseason when he made it a priority to do just that. No additional comfort or growth in KOC’s offense in his third year. No progress in mechanics. No development. Zilch. Nada. Carson Wentz, if called upon for whatever reason, healthy and with a full offseason in the system, will somehow not be able to reach the level of “passable” when he had little trouble getting the ball to Justin Jefferson when he could actually move last season. The best WR trio in the NFL – and the Vikings’ best since Carter-Moss-Reed – will not only fail to live up to the hype but also embrace mediocrity. This says nothing of the depth advantage of having three receivers with experience in the #1 role (Addison in 2023, when Jefferson got hurt; Jauan Jennings on the 49ers in 2024). The offensive line will need to regress a year after its best player, Christian Darrisaw, was nowhere near 100% and is now, by all accounts, healthy. Donovan Jackson’s development will need to stall. Will Fries and Brian O’Neill would both need to have subpar seasons. Blake Brandel underperforming as the starting center – despite a full offseason of work – is a far more likely scenario, but nowhere near an insurmountable obstacle. The Vikings have been navigating less-than-stellar center play for years. DEFENSIVE PERFORMANCE Question marks along the defensive line are real. The Vikings could have kept either Jonathan Allen or Javon Hargrave, but the internal calculations clearly led them to pursue the current course. Both Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange will need to make limited contributions, while Jalen Redmond and the established depth will need to perform worse than expected for it to reach crisis level. It could happen, but a slight regression is more likely. Allen and Hargrave didn’t exactly have All-Pro seasons, either. Dallas Turner will need to be a far worse and more inconsistent replacement for Jonathan Greenard than expected. I’ve been on record as not favoring the decision to trade Greenard away (especially given the return), and I assume regression. Still, I don’t expect the pass rush to collapse in a way that would dramatically impact overall defensive performance. Brian Flores is adept at finding unique and unpredictable ways to pressure the quarterback. Which leads me to… Brian Flores would need to forget how to coach defense. He came here and promptly turned an atrocious defense that ranked 28th in points and 31st in yards into one that ranked 13th and 16th, respectively. The following two seasons brought Top 10 finishes in points (5th and 7th) and defensive DVOA (2nd and 6th). Adding a schematically versatile player like Jamal Adams not only addresses a potential Harrison Smith retirement but also an underwhelming Dallas Turner showing (Adams has 22.5 career sacks). Of course, as we’re the Vikings, there is always precedent for awful things. We watched Mike Zimmer lose his fastball in rapid, dramatic, 2015 Peyton Manning-esque fashion. I could write another 1,000 words on why I don’t think this will happen with Flores, but let’s say it would be… a stretch. MAKE IT MAKE SENSE I can’t understand it. Far, far, far more would have to go wrong for the Vikings not to hit the over on 8.5 wins. Can it happen? Definitely. This franchise has watched its stadium roof collapse, missed its first-round draft pick, inadvertently created the 1990s Dallas Cowboys dynasty, and remains the pacesetter for improbable, gut-wrenching, heartbreaking playoff losses. Going 8-9 or worse and missing the playoffs would be nothing for us. That said, this team is too well-coached and has too much talent. The Vikings have effectively taken out an insurance policy against the only thing that could prevent 9 wins by how they’ve assembled the quarterback room. Or maybe I’m just delusional.

A free agent since March, Van Roten spent the past two seasons with the New York Giants. […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 02: Greg Van Roten #74 of the New York Giants is introduced against the San Francisco 49ers before their game at MetLife Stadium on November 02, 2025 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images A veteran of 144 NFL games made a midweek stop in Foxborough. The New England Patriots hosted guard Greg Van Roten on a visit Thursday morning, according to a report from Ian Rapoport of NFL Network and ESPN . A free agent since March, Van Roten spent the past two seasons with the New York Giants. The 36-year-old has started 105 games on the interior offensive line during his NFL run, including 51 in a row. He spent the previous two campaigns with the New York Giants, finishing both as the organization’s ironman and logging a career-high 1,150 offensive snaps in 2025. Originally entering the league as an undrafted free agent out of Penn in 2012, Van Roten has also been a member of the Green Bay Packers, Seattle Seahawks, Jacksonville Jaguars, Carolina Panthers, New York Jets, Buffalo Bills and Las Vegas Raiders. A CFL stint arrived along the way with the Toronto Argonauts. Primarily a right guard, the 6-foot-4, 295-pound former All-Ivy League offensive tackle has also eclipsed 2,000 downs between left guard and center. The Patriots currently carry a full 91-man roster . The interior offensive line heads further into training camp with Alijah Vera-Tucker, Jared Wilson, Mike Onwenu, Ben Brown, Andrew Rupcich, Mehki Butler, Caedan Wallace, James Hudson as well as undrafted rookies Jacob Rizy and JonDarius Morgan in the fold. The preseason opens next Thursday night at Gillette Stadium with a 7:30 p.m. ET kickoff versus the Indianapolis Colts.

title: Patriots training camp recap: Defense caps day with 3 straight interceptions
summary: The New England Patriots were back in full pads on Thursday following a day of walkthrough work. With the tempo picking back up, the Patriots worked both full-field and red zone work. Here’s what went down throughout the session on the humid fields behind Gillette Stadium. Attendance Absent: WR Romeo Doubs, CB Carlton Davis III, […]
full_text: Jul 25, 2026; Foxborough, MA, USA; New England Patriots safety Kevin Byard III (31) makes a catch at training camp at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New England Patriots were back in full pads on Thursday following a day of walkthrough work. With the tempo picking back up, the Patriots worked both full-field and red zone work. Here’s what went down throughout the session on the humid fields behind Gillette Stadium. Attendance Absent: WR Romeo Doubs, CB Carlton Davis III, TE Jack Westover, WR Cameron Dorner Injured: DL Christian Barmore, CB Charles Woods Limited: OT Will Campbell, OG Caedan Wallace PUP/NFI: ED Harold Landry III, S Brenden Schooler The Patriots attendance list largely remained the same on Thursday as Romeo Doubs and Carlton Davis again highlighted the absentees. New England saw depth offensive lineman Caedan Wallace return to the practice fields in a limited fashion. On a hot, humid day, the defense did see Christian Barmore and Charles Woods depart with head athletic trainer Jim Whalen. Takeaways Defense ending strong: It was a strong day in general for the Patriots defense, but the unit put the cherry on top with three straight interceptions in two-minute situations to end the session. With 1:20 on the clock from the 40-yard line, Drake Maye found a trio of completions — including a strong hands catch from A.J. Brown with Christian Gonzalez all over him — before a short pass to Kayshon Boutte saw Marcus Jones jump the route for the interception. Allowing Maye’s unit to then stay on the field, the quarterback’s next pass down the seam to Hunter Henry was intercepted by Kevin Byard. As Tommy DeVito’s unit then took over, a similar result follow. Facing pressure on his first drop back, DeVito moved to his left before firing an interception to safety John Saunders Jr. The defensive sideline was rightfully rowdy while Mike Vrabel ended practice. A.J. vs Gonzo: It’s been a highly competitive back-and-forth summer between cornerback Christian Gonzalez and wide receiver A.J. Brown. On Thursday, advantage Gonzalez. After a downfield target to Brown with Gonzalez in coverage fell incomplete in full-team work, the duo matched up twice against each other in 2-on-2 goal line work. Gonzalez was on the winning side of both reps, which included a pass breakup in the corner of the end zone to end the drill that sparked back-and-forth trash talk — with the two almost needing to be separated as work transitioned to a new period. Christian Gonzalez with a smile as he recalls some trash talk between him and A.J. Brown from today’s practice … where the two almost needed to be separated after one pass breakup in the end zone. pic.twitter.com/bQBeIOZTeg — Brian Hines (@iambrianhines) August 6, 2026 Campbell limited: Starting left tackle Will Campbell did not participate in any competitive periods on Thursday as he again wore a Rob Gronkowski-like arm brace on his left arm that he debuted in Wednesday’s walkthrough. Without their top left tackle, fellow second-year pro Marcus Bryant repped in his place with the top offense as first-round pick Caleb Lomu continued to train at right tackle with the second unit. That then elevated rookie Dametrious Crownover to backup left tackle. Jacas’ ramping up: Rookie pass rusher Gabe Jacas worked in with the first-team defense on Thursday as he continues to ramp up following his offseason knee procedure. While Jacas’ size and power stand out, the rookie won multiple times with speed on Thursday while working against the second unit. That first came when he dipped around Lomu to register a pressure (and a likely holding penalty) before beating Crownover in two-minute to help force an interception. Other notes: With Romeo Doubs sidelined, increased reps were split between Mack Hollins, Kayshon Boutte, and Efton Chism III. Kyle Williams worked in with all three offenses and caught a downfield corner route from Behren Morton while DeVito missed him on a goal line fade. Mack Hollins and DeMario Douglas caught touchdowns from Drake Maye in red zone work. In 2-on-2 goal line work both Hunter Henry and Eli Raridon had multiple wins while Kyle Williams smoked Kevin Byard on a slant. Efton Chism saw a pair of passes uncharacteristically hit the turf before ending with a win. The Patriots worked their QB/option run game in the red zone. Their regular run game largely continued to struggle. Terrell Jennings was the first running back up behind Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson. Morgan Moses had a false start. Quintayvious Hutchins continues to flash along the edge as he was in the backfield for a potential sack. Jesse Luketa also logged a would-be sack with the third unit. Joshua Farmer added another run stuff to his impressive summer resume. Brandon Crossley had a late pass breakup guarding Nick DeGennaro along the goal line. The Patriots will be back on the practice fields on Friday for their fifth and final practice of the week, which is set to begin at 10:15 a.m. ET. Mike Vrabel will speak beforehand.

title: Bryce Baringer aiming for more consistency entering Year 4
summary: The New England Patriots held tryouts for two punters during rookie and mandatory minicamp this offseason. Neither was signed. Instead, the team entered training camp with confidence in Bryce Baringer. The 27-year old is coming off a season in which he punted a career-low 51 times in the regular season before a busy playoff run. […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA- JUNE 11: Bryce Baringer #17 of the New England Patriots ready for the snap during New England Patriots Minicamp on June 11, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Summer Lamont/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New England Patriots held tryouts for two punters during rookie and mandatory minicamp this offseason. Neither was signed. Instead, the team entered training camp with confidence in Bryce Baringer. The 27-year old is coming off a season in which he punted a career-low 51 times in the regular season before a busy playoff run. Baringer continued to showcase his big leg by again eclipsing the 70-yard longest punt mark and recording a career-best 4.41-second average hang time, but remained hampered by the occasional mishit — such as a 22-yard punt in Week 13 against the Giants. That’s why Baringer’s offseason focus was centered on one thing. “I want to be more consistent,” he said. “No. 2, big emphasis was hang time and distance. Kind of having that relationship. Just knowing what I’m capable of doing, trusting myself, my process. Like I said, [Jeremy Springer], [Tom Quinn], [Mike Vrabel], they all know what I’m capable of. It’s just going out and being able to do it, and just trusting myself wholeheartedly.” In addition to slight tweaks to his mechanics, Baringer is hoping a new mental approach can help him find more consistency on a kick-to-kick basis. “Looking at it more holistically. If it was a punt that I didn’t like, rather than being upset about it — obviously I’m going to be upset about it, I’m very hard on myself — flip it to the 180. ‘Okay, what did I do wrong there? And how can I not do it again?’,” Baringer said. “Rather than coach has talked about in squad meetings, if you’re in a rut or a lull, don’t let it bleed into further reps or plays. And that’s kind of what I’m working on right now.” As Baringer enters the final year of his rookie contract, he stands without direct competition on the roster during training camp. Head coach Mike Vrabel also praised the punter for his work as a holder and the positive impact he has on kicker Andy Borregales. “Bryce is such a calming piece for Andy and does a nice job,” Vrabel said. “Really, we want our punters to be great holders and excellent at plus-50 punts. If we punt, we want them to be plus-50. That means we are moving the football and giving me a decision whether we are going to go for it on fourth down or we are going to punt. So, again, we cannot take those guys for granted, and the reason when they do their job, you never hear about them.” Through the early portion of training camp, Baringer has seemingly struck the ball well while Borregales has been nearly perfect, connecting on 28-of-30 field goal attempts. The specialists — which also includes second-year long snapper Julian Ashby — have set a high standard for themselves, and Baringer believes the coaching staff continues to push them because it knows what the group is capable of. “[The coaches] have a large amount of trust in us, they know what we’re capable of, and that’s why they’re hard on us, because they know what we’re capable of doing,” Baringer said. “Coach talked about it yesterday. He’s trying — if you squeeze an orange, you’re going to get orange juice out of it. Like, whatever you squeeze is what you are. That’s you. And so, he’s just trying to pull that out of us, which is awesome.”

title: Patriots 2026 scouting report for TE Hunter Henry
summary: The New England Patriots’ 2021 free agency class was one for the ages, but five years later only one of the high-profile signings remains with the team. And for good reason: Hunter Henry has been a model citizen since coming to Foxborough (and before that as well), and will go down as one of the […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - JANUARY 25: Hunter Henry #85 of the New England Patriots celebrates a touchdown during the AFC Championship Playoff game between the New England Patriots and the Denver Broncos at Empower Field At Mile High on January 25, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots’ 2021 free agency class was one for the ages, but five years later only one of the high-profile signings remains with the team. And for good reason: Hunter Henry has been a model citizen since coming to Foxborough (and before that as well), and will go down as one of the better tight ends in franchise history. Heading into his sixth season with the Patriots, there is nothing to suggest that he won’t again be an imporant piece of the club’s offensive puzzle. Hard facts Name: Hunter Henry Position: Tight end Jersey number: 85 Opening day age: 31 (12/7/1994) Measurements : 6’4 7/8”, 249 lbs, 9 1/4” hand size, 32 3/4” arm length, 78” wingspan, 4.68s 40-yard dash, 7.16s 3-cone drill, 4.41 short shuttle, 31 1/2” vertical jump, 9’5” broad jump, 13 bench press reps, 6.28 Relative Athletic Score Experience NFL: San Diego/Los Angeles Chargers (2016-20), New England Patriots (2021-) | College: Arkansas (2013-15) Henry drew considerable interest as a four-star college recruit out of Pulaski Academy in Little Rock, AR, but he decided to stay in his home state and joined the University of Arkansas in 2013. He was named All-SEC in all three of his seasons as a Razorback (first team 2014, 2015; second team 2013) and also was named an unanimous All-American as well as the winner of the. John Mackey Award as the nation’s top tight end in 2015. After catching a combined 116 passes for 1,661 yards and nine touchdowns his first three seasons, Henry decided to forgo his final year of eligibility to enter the NFL. He was a highly-regarded prospect and ended up as the first tight end off the board: the Chargers brought him to San Diego as the 35th overall selection in 2016. Henry made an impact on the Chargers offense from his rookie season on, and together with veteran Antonio Gates formed one of the league’s better tight end duos during his first two seasons with the organization. While a torn ACL limited him to just one game in 2018 — a divisional playoff loss to the eventual Super Bowl champion Patriots — he still managed to appear in 56 games with 50 starts during his five-year career in San Diego and Los Angeles. After receiving the franchise tag in 2020, however, he left the organization the following spring: the Patriots signed him to a three-year, $37.5 million free agency pact, and he quickly picked up where he left off. Setting a new career high in touchdowns (9), he was one of quarterback Mac Jones’ favorite targets and therefore instrumental to New England qualifying for the postseason. The next few years were more challenging from a team success perspective, but Henry nonetheless was one of the top performers and most reliable players on New England’s roster — a status that did not change with the arrivals of new starting QB Drake Maye in 2024 and head coach Mike Vrabel in 2025. As a consequence, Henry has now played 86 games with 72 starts for the club and been on the receiving end of 269 total passes for 3,115 yards and 27 touchdowns. Scouting report Strengths: Standing at 6-foot-5, 249 pounds, Henry has the size and length NFL teams are looking for in an inline/Y-tight end. He uses his size and naturally soft hands to haul in passes at a high rate and make receptions outside of his frame or in a contested manner. He readjusts his body well in the air, and has a good feel for not committing too early to incoming plays. In general, his football IQ is immense and he is able to find soft spots in zone defense or maneuver through traffic effectively; he also knows how to stay alive on scramble drills. Henry also is a very good route runner, especially in the short and intermediate parts of the field. He moves efficiently without any wasted lower-body movement and quickly gets into his patterns. He also possesses the short-area quickness to make hard cuts and shake defenders in man-to-man coverage. A quarterback’s best friend, he has handled a volume role well as a receiver and also has been competitive as a blocker on the edge; he identifies his targets well and knows how to position himself to maximize his chances of coming away victoriously. In addition, leadership has been a key part of Henry’s presence ever since he arrived in New England. The 2025 season was his third being voted a captain by his peers, and his teammates regularly praise him for his demeanor on and off the field. Weaknesses: Henry is a crafty blocker more so than a talented one. He carries out his assignments but is not a game-changer at the point of attack; he lacks the core strength and leg drive to consistently free up the edge in the run game and can get mispositioned against speed and power. In general, his consistency has been on and off since joining the Patriots: especially late in seasons, there has been a drop-off in his ability to maintain his typical high level of play. As a receiver, Henry lacks the explosiveness to be a consistent deep threat. He also won’t break many tackles, despite overall being a solid if unspectacular run-after-the-catch producer. 2025 review Stats : 21 games (21 starts) | 1,067 offensive snaps (78.6%), 11 special teams snaps (2.0%) | 98 targets, 69 catches (70.4%), 880 receiving yards (12.8/catch), 8 TDs, 6 drops | 4 QB pressures surrendered (2 sacks, 2 hurries) | 3 penalties (incl. 0 declined/offsetting) Season recap: Even though the Patriots offense as a whole struggled in 2024, Henry produced a career year in terms of catches (66) and receiving yards (674). Naturally, there was plenty of optimism when the team under new head coach Mike Vrabel hired Josh McDaniels to call the offense: Henry had looked good during their lone season together, and there was little to suggest that their second go-around would be any different. And indeed, it was not. Henry was once again one of New England’s top performers on the offensive side of the ball and a safety blanket for quarterback Drake Maye. As a consequence, he was on the field for more than three quarters of offensive snaps, ranking first among the Patriots’ skill position players. He also managed to set new career marks in games against the Steelers and Bengals. The first contest saw him tie his personal best with eight catches and two touchdowns, while the latter ended with him reeling in seven passes for a career-high 115 yards as well as another score. All in all, Henry was once again a pivotal part of the Patriots’ offensive operation. He finished the season ranked second on the team in targets (98), receptions (69) and receiving yards (880) — all eclipsing his 2024 numbers — while ranking first in touchdowns (7). One of those TDs came during New England’s wild card playoff win over his former team, the Chargers. THIS IS GORGEOUS 🎯 @DrakeMaye2 | @Hunter_Henry84 📺 NBC pic.twitter.com/7TYUczWj3q — New England Patriots (@Patriots) January 12, 2026 The base-line statistics tell only part of the story, though. Henry’s season was much more nuanced than “career high after career high” en route to his first Super Bowl appearance. While, yes, he also posted his best yards after the catch (5.4) and yards per route run (1.54) since joining the Patriots, and moved the chains on half of his 32 third- and fourth-down targets, he also dropped a career worst six passes and was uneven as a run blocker. In general, he was again not able to sustain what had been a strong start to the season. In the postseason especially, he failed to elevate his game against the top defenses the Patriots faced. While solid in that aforementioned game against the Chargers, he only had six receptions for 48 yards in the final three playoff games combined. So, was Henry’s 2025 season a success or…

title: Drake Maye weighs in on Kayshon Boutte’s future with Patriots
summary: New England Patriots wide receiver Kayshon Boutte has been at the center of trade speculation throughout the offseason. The 24-year-old enters the final year of his rookie contract and requested a trade during the spring after the Patriots acquired A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs this offseason. For now, though, Boutte remains in New England. Throughout […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - JANUARY 18: Drake Maye #10 of the New England Patriots celebrates with Kayshon Boutte #9 after his touchdown catch against the Houston Texans during an NFL divisional playoff game at Gillette Stadium on January 18, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts.(Photo By Winslow Townson/Getty Images) | Getty Images New England Patriots wide receiver Kayshon Boutte has been at the center of trade speculation throughout the offseason. The 24-year-old enters the final year of his rookie contract and requested a trade during the spring after the Patriots acquired A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs this offseason. For now, though, Boutte remains in New England. Throughout training camp, the wide receiver has continued to flash his big-play ability while rotating with the first- and second-team offense as the Patriots wide receiver depth chart remains seven deep. That could still result in Boutte being elsewhere by Week 1. Following Wednesday’s walkthrough, quarterback Drake Maye was asked about Boutte’s future with the team. “I think just the way Kayshon is approaching it, man. He’s here now,” Maye said. “He’s where his feet are at, and I’m having fun throwing it to him out there in practice. He’s doing a great job, and he makes plays when the football’s in the air. And I think he can speak for that, and that speaks for itself. So, I’ve had a lot of great times with Kayshon, and I’m looking forward to us getting better each and every day.” After Boutte posted back-to-back 500-yard season, the Patriots added Brown and Doubs to the roster this season to join him, Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism III. Speaking earlier this week on SiriusXM NFL Radio, Maye broke down his top seven wide receivers and mentioned Boutte last. “Probably the last one is Boutte,” Maye said. “He’s a comforting receiver to throw to. You get to know him – same thing as Pop, this is my third year with Boutte and I was throwing to him on scout team when I was a rookie. Now we’re making plays; I threw my first touchdown to him. He’s just one of those guys that is quiet, does everything the right way, cares about his teammates, and he just puts his head down and works. There’s a lot of talk about whatever you want to say with Boutte, but he just continues to make plays. He’s going to be in the right spot and make a play on the football.” Maye’s comments echo what Boutte has shown throughout training camp. But the business side of the NFL could still result in him playing elsewhere before the regular season — something Boutte remains open to as he looks to secure the first significant payday of his career.

title: 7 performances of note from the Patriots’ 10th training camp practice
summary: The New England Patriots toned down the tempo on Wednesday. Coming off five practices in full pads, they went to bucket hats and T-shirts instead — an attire that reflected the intensity: the Patriots’ 10th session of training camp was a walkthrough. To recap the action, please check out our practice recap. In the meantime, […]
full_text: Jul 28, 2026; Foxborough, MA, USA; New England Patriots cornerback Channing Canada (29) walks to practice for training camp at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New England Patriots toned down the tempo on Wednesday. Coming off five practices in full pads, they went to bucket hats and T-shirts instead — an attire that reflected the intensity: the Patriots’ 10th session of training camp was a walkthrough. To recap the action, please check out our practice recap . In the meantime, here is who caught our eyes for better or worse. Standout of the day N/A: Unlike the last few days, the focus on Wednesday was not on competition. We did get a look at the depth chart and where the camp competitions currently stand, but the nature of the session prevents us from crowning a standout of the day. Other performances of note RB Terrell Jennings: After returning from the non-football injury list earlier this week, Jennings has been used quite prominently. On Wednesday, he was with the starting offense alongside Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson — an honor not reserved for any of the other backup RBs — and also lined up with the top kickoff return unit and the top punt block squad. The third-year man appears to be carving out an advantage in the race for the third running back spot. WR Efton Chism III: With Romeo Doubs missing the session, the Patriots had an opening in their starting lineup. It went to sophomore Efton Chism, whose ability to line up all over the formation has made him a valuable presence in the wide receiver room. Chism was with the starting wide receiver group during the first period of 11-on-11s and often was on the field in Doubs’ place alongside A.J. Brown and DeMario Douglas. It will be seen how his role evolved once Doubs is back, but his usage on Wednesday was definitively noteworthy. WR Kyle Williams: Even with Romeo Doubs absent, Kyle Williams was not among the group of wideouts repping with Drake Maye and the starters during the aforementioned 11-on-11s. He did join the top unit later, but did not line up against the starting defense. What he did do, however, was lining up as the first-unit kickoff returner alongside Terrell Jennings. The more you can do. CB Channing Canada and CB Karon Prunty: When the Patriots split into 11-on-11 work, the rookie pair was among the five cornerbacks to work with the defensive starters; Christian Gonzalez, Charles Woods and Marcus Jones were also part of the group. Both youngsters took the field behind Woods, the current CB4 and a top-level perimeter player with Carlton Davis still out, and are perhaps in the process elevating themselves beyond the other backups at the position. S Dell Pettus and S Mike Brown: The fight for the third safety spot saw Pettus and main competitor Mike Brown on different fields Wednesday. Whereas Pettus was with the first-teamers on defense, Brown was with the second unit. Both also served as the personal punt protectors, with Brown the top option at the position and Pettus — who filled that role during his 2024 rookie season — serving as the No. 2. The Patriots will hold their 11th practice of training camp on Thursday, and it will once again take place behind closed doors. Of course, Pats Pulpit will be on hand to report from the session.

title: Patriots training camp recap: Walkthrough provides look at depth chart
summary: After five straight fully padded practices the New England Patriots dialed it back on Wednesday with another walkthrough style practice. While the tempo was slowed, the session did provide an updated look at the depth chart as work was split between two fields. Here’s what went down throughout the session. Attendance Absent: WR Romeo Doubs […]
full_text: Jun 9, 2025; Foxborough, MA, USA; New England Patriots wide receiver Efton Chism III (86) warns up during minicamp at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After five straight fully padded practices the New England Patriots dialed it back on Wednesday with another walkthrough style practice. While the tempo was slowed, the session did provide an updated look at the depth chart as work was split between two fields. Here’s what went down throughout the session. Attendance Absent: WR Romeo Doubs (new), CB Carlton Davis III, TE Jack Westover, OG Caedan Wallace, WR Cameron Dorner Returnee: FB Reggie Gilliam (rest), TE C.J. Dippre (PUP) PUP/NFI: ED Harold Landry III, S Brenden Schooler Wide receiver Romeo Doubs was a new absence during Wednesday’s walkthrough while the rest of the attendance list remained the same beyond fullback Reggie Gilliam (rest) returning. Gilliam shared his managed workload this summer was due to nagging injuries from recent years. Tight end C.J. Dippre was present at practice in uniform for the first time this summer indicating that he has been activated off the PUP list . Takeaways Chism and the WRs: With Romeo Doubs sidelined, Efton Chism III was the biggest beneficiary seeing plenty of snaps in the veteran’s place with the first-team offense — often sharing the field with A.J. Brown and DeMario Douglas. Chism’s ability to play/backup multiple wide receiver spots in the offense and him being counted on for his run blocking ability in packages with the first-team offense this camp has him on the path towards a roster spot. Drake Maye largely worked with A.J. Brown, Mack Hollins, Kayshon Boutte, Douglas, and Chism, while Kyle Williams originally started on the opposite field before working with Maye later on as the entire offense gathered together. RB rotation: Two days after being activated off the NFI list, Terrell Jennings joined Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson with Maye’s offense. Jennings is New England’s only depth running back with NFL experience and may have an early lead on the RB3 spot. Lan Larison, Jam Miller, and Myles Montgomery then repped on the opposite field. Rookie corners: As Carlton Davis remained absent, Charles Woods continued to operate as the top cornerback opposite of Christian Gonzalez. A pair of rookies in Karon Prunty and Channing Canada then worked in behind them with the first-team defense. Since the pads came on, Prunty has been around the ball often while Canada has also been competitive in coverage — although was on the wrong side of multiple completions in Tuesday’s session. Both seem to be trending upward as the team looks for depth behind their top corners. Special teams: Plenty of special teams work throughout the walkthrough. With the kicking game playing a big factor for those fighting for roster spots, the units included: Top punt block: Reggie Gilliam, Khalil Jacobs, Chad Muma, Elijah Ponder, Namdi Obiazor, Terrell Jennings Personal protectors: Mike Brown (top), Dell Pettus Kick returners: Kyle Williams and Terrell Jennings, Efton Chism III and Lan Larison, Kobe Prentice, Myles Montgomery, Channing Canada, DeMario Douglas Other notes: Offensive tackle Will Campbell wore a Rob Gronkowski-like arm brace on his left arm. The top two offensive lines remained the same: Campbell-Vera-Tucker-Wilson-Onwenu-Moses and Bryant-Rupcich-Brown-Hudson-Lomu. Gabe Jacas largely worked with the second-team defense and punt block unit. Dell Pettus mixed in behind Craig Woodson and Kevin Byard, perhaps signaling he has elevated to the No. 3 safety. They ended practice repping Hail Mary situations. The Patriots will be back on the practice fields on Thursday where they will be back in shells, which is set to begin at 10:15 a.m. ET.

title: Barion Brown could be the unsung hero of the WR room
summary: Of course, it’s important to temper expectations whenever going off of training camp performances, but I think we can all agree how exciting it’s been to see Barion Brown so far. Every day since pads were put on the players, Brown has been making play after play, and his ability to get separation is incredible. […]
full_text: METAIRIE, LOUISIANA - AUGUST 03: Barion Brown #19 of the New Orleans Saints reacts during training camp at Ochsner Sports Performance Center on August 03, 2026 in Metairie, Louisiana. (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) | Getty Images Of course, it’s important to temper expectations whenever going off of training camp performances, but I think we can all agree how exciting it’s been to see Barion Brown so far. Every day since pads were put on the players, Brown has been making play after play, and his ability to get separation is incredible. When Brown was drafted by the Saints in the 6th round, his contribution on the roster was believed to be one on special teams. He is a dangerous returner that would be a massive upgrade for this special teams unit, but it seems like the Saints viewed him as a real contributor on offense. Yesterday, after yet another excellent performance in practice, Kellen Moore spoke on what the team saw from Brown in college and made sure to mention his impact on offense. "We watched a lot of evidence of (Barion Brown) playing receiver and playing impactful plays in the SEC … You're really fired up to have this guy. He's doing a great job." Coach Moore on Barion Brown pic.twitter.com/j4Vtd4K3ir — New Orleans Saints (@Saints) August 5, 2026 The Saints have had some tough decisions to make recently because rookies/young players have outperformed expectations. For 2026, it already seems like that’s going to be Brown. When he was drafted, he was put behind 4 other guys in the WR depth chart: Chris Olave, Jordyn Tyson, Devaughn Vele, and Bryce Lance. Also, before Ja’Lynn Polk retired, it was believed that he was going to be WR4, so Brown would be all the way down at the last spot. But now, there’s no way that’s going to happen. With the consistency he’s shown in practice and the major impact he’s making, there’s a good chance Brown begins the season in the 4th WR spot, and it may not take long for him to overtake Vele. Becoming the third WR is a bit more of a long shot without injuries happening, but now it’s not out of the question. Even if he stays in that fourth spot, Brown’s ability to make big plays could make him one of the most important players on offense. He may not be able to be that consistent nearly double-digit receiving yards per game guy, but I can see a more Rashid Shaheed role for him.

title: Jeremiah wright’s injury puts Saints’ interior line depth under the microscope
summary: New Orleans Saints rookie guard Jeremiah Wright suffered an apparent shoulder injury during Wednesday’s practice, causing him to make an early exit. While the severity of the injury has yet to be determined, Wright’s departure is noteworthy because of the role he was expected to play this season. Selected in the fourth round of the […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - MARCH 01: Jeremiah Wright #OL56 of Auburn participates in a drill during the 2026 NFL Scouting Combine at Lucas Oil Stadium on March 1, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images New Orleans Saints rookie guard Jeremiah Wright suffered an apparent shoulder injury during Wednesday’s practice, causing him to make an early exit. While the severity of the injury has yet to be determined, Wright’s departure is noteworthy because of the role he was expected to play this season. Selected in the fourth round of the recent NFL Draft out of Auburn, the versatile interior lineman entered camp as one of the team’s most intriguing young depth pieces. His absence is magnified by the uncertainty surrounding starting right guard Cesar Ruiz. After showing flashes of being a dependable starter throughout his NFL career, Ruiz’s consistency has remained an issue. Injuries have also interrupted his development in recent seasons, making reliable depth behind him an important priority for New Orleans. That’s where Wright entered the picture. At Auburn, Wright developed a reputation as a physical, technically sound blocker capable of handling multiple responsibilities along the interior offensive line. Those traits made him an ideal developmental prospect and someone who could compete for playing time while serving as insurance if injuries struck the starting lineup. If Wright is forced to miss time, the Saints could lose valuable developmental reps for a rookie who was expected to push for a role throughout training camp and the preseason. Just as importantly, it would leave the team’s interior depth a bit thinner behind Ruiz at a position where durability has already been a concern. The Saints are undoubtedly hoping Wright’s shoulder injury proves to be nothing more than a minor setback. But until more is disclosed, his exit from practice serves as a reminder of how quickly depth can become a pressing issue along the offensive line.

title: Fantasy Football 2026: The biggest stories to monitor as camps open
summary: NFL training camps are underway, and the start of the 2026-27 NFL season is less than six weeks away. Can you believe it? You readers know exactly what the dog days of August signify: It’s time to get serious about fantasy football prep for redraft leagues. Lots of news and noise emerges from NFL training […]
full_text: The Giants’ offense survived the loss of the electric Nabers | Getty Images NFL training camps are underway, and the start of the 2026-27 NFL season is less than six weeks away. Can you believe it? You readers know exactly what the dog days of August signify: It’s time to get serious about fantasy football prep for redraft leagues. Lots of news and noise emerges from NFL training camps. There will be some stories and developments that matter, and plenty that don’t. Let’s put that aside for now, since we don’t know what we might hear over the next month or so. As training camps get underway, here are the stories I’m paying the most attention to, for fantasy purposes. You can find all of my preseason fantasy content, including preliminary rankings and tiers, at this link . All fantasy rankings shown are for Half-point PPR, on a points per game basis, and exclude the final week of the season. Average Draft Position (ADP) shown is also for Half-Point PPR, as of August 3. Alvin Kamara didn’t retire — Now what? How much Kamara eats into Travis Etienne’s workload is an important question. We may not get much of an answer to this before the season starts, but lots of people expected Kamara to retire, and he didn’t. He’s coming back for at least one more season, on a restructured deal. Is he dust at this point, or can he still be a factor in the passing game and at the goal line? He used to excel at both, and those high-leverage touches are what could be the difference between Top-10 numbers or something a lot lower for Etienne. I’m in on Kellen Moore’s offense in year two, but would have been a lot happier using an early pick on Etienne if Kamara wasn’t hanging around. 2. It’s only August 4, and the 49ers are already banged up. Shocker, right? Are they cursed? Is it the substation? Ricky Pearsall (PCL) is lost for the season. A guy who didn’t miss a single college game in five seasons because of injury will miss 31 across his first three NFL seasons. It doesn’t end there, though. George Kittle (achilles) opened camp on PUP, as expected, newly added Christian Kirk has a calf injury, new addition and future hall of famer Mike Evans has a quad strain, and second round rookie D’Zhaun Stribling has a hamstring issue. Even Kyle Shanahan is injured, after a bad car accident. The team just brought back Deebo Samuel, Sr. , but he hasn’t exceeded 75 catches or 1,000 yards since 2021 (and that was his only season hitting those marks).Evans will be 33 on August 21 and missed 12 games with injuries over the last two seasons. Evans isn’t the only old guy. Kittle will be 33 in October, Samuel is 30, Kirk is 29, and Christian McCaffrey is 30. Yikes. And yet, this is an offense that scores and scores… 3. Will Malik Nabers be ready Week 1, and at what strength? This has been one of the most significant fantasy stories all off-season. After months of discouraging news about his recovery from a major knee injury suffered in Week 4 of the 2025 season, which included a clean-up procedure, Nabers didn’t open camp on PUP, and now there’s speculation that he’ll be ready to go Week 1. He’s still at a major discount right now, at an ADP of overall player 39 (WR19). More positive news from camp will continue to push him up. Even if he’s ready to go Week 1, the question will be how close he is to his full strength. It’s often the year AFTER the year after an ACL tear that players get their explosiveness back. Still, Nabers is an elite talent and is already a proven producer at age 23, and if he’s a go to start the season, his ADP should climb and end up no lower than the 2-3 turn. Obviously, a healthy Nabers would be huge for second year QB Jaxson Dart . 4. Are the Cardinals going to trade James Conner or Trey Benson ? I’m asking for a friend. Actually, I’m asking for a lot of friends: The entire fantasy community. Overall #3 pick Jeremiyah Love and newcomer Tyler Allgeier should both play a lot of snaps for the Cardinals this season. But what of Conner and Benson? Both are trade candidates, and a running back injury on another team could expedite a move. Love’s ADP is a little rich for me at 31 (RB14). Arizona has the league’s toughest schedule and they’re projected to score one of the lowest point totals for the season. Plus, they had the fewest running back carries in the league last season. The big crowd in the RB room only makes it worse. 5. Will Josh Jacobs suffer any league discipline (or face legal charges)? For now, neither Rashee Rice nor Jacobs is facing a suspension relating to his off-field incidents. The Fantasy community has been watching closely for developments. Rice appears to be in the clear for this season, but the police investigation is still open on Jacobs, and it’s possible he could face a suspension at some point this season. His ADP (RB17, 37 overall) reflects that uncertainty. He finished as the RB6 and the RB9 in 2024 and 2025. 6. Where (if anywhere) will Brandon Aiyuk and/or Keenan Allen sign? Deebo is back with the 49ers as discussed above, and it sounds like Tyreek Hill’s injury recovery timeline won’t allow him to play this year. Stefon Diggs just signed a one-year deal with the Commanders. That leaves the duo above as the biggest names who remain unsigned. Teams that could be in the market: Kansas City, Baltimore, New Orleans, Indianapolis, and Buffalo, among others. 7. The progress of players returning from season-ending injuries is always important to monitor as the season approaches. The next six weeks won’t reveal how much Patrick Mahomes or Daniel Jones will use his legs this season, but it should tell us if they’re ready to go Week 1. I’ll be keeping an eye for injury recovery news related to those two, plus Nabers and Kittle who I already discussed, and Zach Charbonnet , Tucker Kraft , Alec Pierce , Michael Penix , Jr. , and others who are returning from injuries and surgeries that happened since the start of last season. That’s it for today. Keep it here for more preseason fantasy content. Coming later this month: Sleepers, and players to target and avoid at ADP.

title: Giants news: Patriots hosting former Giants guard Greg Van Roten
summary: The New England Patriots are hosting former New York Giants guard Greg Van Roten for a workout, per a report from Ian Rapoport. Van Roten, 36, spent the last two years as the Giants’ right guard, joining Jermaine Eluemunor in coming to New York from the Las Vegas Raiders. While certainly not an elite guard, […]
full_text: Greg Van Roten | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New England Patriots are hosting former New York Giants guard Greg Van Roten for a workout, per a report from Ian Rapoport . Van Roten, 36, spent the last two years as the Giants’ right guard, joining Jermaine Eluemunor in coming to New York from the Las Vegas Raiders. While certainly not an elite guard, Van Roten comported himself well once he became established in 2024 and carried that into 2025. And despite being an older lineman, Van Roten was a steady presence for the Giants and started all 34 games for them over the last two years. The Giants opted to move on from Van Roten after the 2025 season, adding Daniel Faalele as well as retaining Evan Neal and Joshua Ezeudu in free agency. There was some thought that the trio could compete to fill the right guard spot next to Eluemunor, or at least there was until Dexter Lawrence demanded his trade and the Cincinnati Bengals sent the 10th overall pick to New York. That pick turned into Sisi Mauigoa, who is in line to lock down the right guard spot and hopefully upgrade the position. It remains to be seen whether the Patriots will sign Van Roten, but he should still at least be able to be a good depth piece at guard and center.

title: NY Giants Odell Beckham feeling ‘a lot of love’ from fans, and making them dream
summary: WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — For the past couple of days, Odell Beckham Jr. has made New York Giants fans dare to dream that he can actually complete an unlikely comeback. Beckham, 33, will never again be the superstar he was for a few years after the Giants selected him in the first round of […]
full_text: Odell Beckham | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — For the past couple of days, Odell Beckham Jr. has made New York Giants fans dare to dream that he can actually complete an unlikely comeback. Beckham, 33, will never again be the superstar he was for a few years after the Giants selected him in the first round of the 2014 NFL Draft. Age and several leg injuries guarantee that. Can he, though, be productive after not playing in 2025 and playing sparingly in 2024? Maybe. Don’t get caught up in the “oh my God, Odell is taking first-team reps” hype. Yes, Beckham has taken reps with starting quarterback Jaxson Dart in the past two practices. So, too, have Jalin Hyatt and Xavier Gipson. Malik Nabers is not taking team reps. Malachi Fields has only done individual drills for the past couple of days. Darius Slayton is ramping up after double sports hernia surgeries during the offseason. JuJu Smith-Schuster missed a practice this week. The story isn’t, or shouldn’t be, that Beckham is getting a handful of training camp reps with the starters. That feels like missing the forest for the trees. The story is that Beckham has practiced every day thus far. The story is, or should be, that after the injuries and time away, Beckham is still a good player. He can still run. He still has strong, sure hands. He is still a good route runner. He doesn’t have the explosive athleticism of his youth, but he can still get open. Wednesday was Beckham’s best day. He caught passes from Dart, Jameis Winston and Brandon Allen at all three levels of the field. “I feel like I’m getting better,” Beckham said after Wednesday’s practice. “I feel like with repetition, with mistakes, unfortunately I’m one of those people who has to touch the stove to know that it’s hot and to not touch it again, so I learn from a mistake, and it’s like, all right, that’s something that I corrected. “So, I definitely feel like I’m getting better. There’s definitely been more opportunities. It’s just a combination of both. But kind of just fizzle all that out, and I’m just like – I’m just locked in the moment. I’m truly grateful for being where my feet are at and just trying to enjoy that each and every day and bring the best energy that I can.” Defensive back Ar’Darius Washington played with Beckham in 2023 with the Ravens. “He almost looks better (than 2023),” Washington said. “As far as his physical abilities and things like that, he’s still rolling. Sometimes he gets in his head, and he doesn’t make those plays. He just wants it so bad, I’ll just tell him, just relax. Be yourself. It’s going to come to you. “He’s still got the juice in the tank. Hundred percent.” Cornerback Paulson Adebo has also been impressed. “He’s been great. I think every time we line up against him, he looks good,” Adebo said. “I grew up watching him as a youngin’, so it’s definitely cool to be able to go up against him, but yeah, he definitely looks like he looks ready.” When fans are in attendance at training camp practices, every Beckham catch is greeted by a louder, more excited crowd reaction than any other player receives. Clearly, they want Beckham to make this team and help the Giants win. Beckham, who said he gets “a lot of juice” from the fans, also wants that. “It’s a lot of love,” Beckham said. “Most people don’t get a chance to double back, and this is a place that made me into a man, made me into who I am. I have so much love for this organization, this city. I’ve got New York tatted on my back; you know what I mean? And I’m from New Orleans. “So, all I ever wanted to do was win a championship for the New York Giants and just having an opportunity right now to – the end goal in mind, but stack those days, that’s all I want to do for this city, this organization, is bring one home.” Beckham did not have to put himself through this. He has fame. He has money. He has nearly 600 catches and 8,000 receiving yards. He was, during his first tenure with the Giants, arguably, the game’s best receiver. He chose this, in an effort to leave the game on his own terms. “I feel like if this comes off selfish, sorry, but this is like – this is for me. This is [to] prove to myself. It’s never really been to prove it to others, but it’s always fun when you can prove it to others,” Beckham said. “But this is for me, this is for my son, this is like – in our household, we never give up, you know what I’m saying? No matter what it is, you’re going to finish what you started. And that’s kind of all this is to me. “I take it as if God’s giving me one year, then it is what it is, but who knows what it’s going to be. I’m just trying to be present each and every day, and prove to myself that I am who I know I am.” Part of the reason head coach John Harbaugh hesitated to give Beckham this opportunity. This is what Harbaugh said after the Giants did sign Beckham to a contract: “I told him, you just can’t be okay. You’re Odell Beckham,” Harbaugh said. “You’ve got to come out here, and you’ve got to be performing at a high, high level in a workout. You’ve got to be performing at a high level in practice. “You’ve got to be a guy that’s capable that we can see would have a chance to make a difference in NFL games. You’ve got to be that kind of a player. Who knows better what that kind of a player is than Odell Beckham?” Beckham isn’t worried about that. He isn’t worried about facing the indignity of Harbaugh, a coach with whom he has a close relationship, perhaps being forced to cut him. “This is the conversation I had with Coach. Before I ever came here, he’s like, ‘You know, I’ve got a really good relationship with you, I don’t want you (to) come here, and then something happens, and you can’t make the team.’ I’m like, ‘I can live with me getting up, leaving my home, coming here and giving my best effort, and if it doesn’t work out, it doesn’t work out,’ ” Beckham said. “I couldn’t live with me feeling like I gave up on myself and I never (saw) through my dream that I’ve been chasing since I was four years old. I just couldn’t live with that. “So, it is what it is. I’m all for competition. I’ve always been like that. I feel like I rise to the occasion. And right now, I’m just trying to stay in the bag, you know what I mean? I’m trying to get better each and every day, know exactly what I’ve got to do, get open, catch the ball, score, get back to the game that I truly love.” Giants fans might remember the Victor Cruz comeback. After a year away from the game, Cruz caught 39 passes for 586 yards for New York in 2016, averaging 15.0 yards per catch. Those weren’t the numbers of his glory days, but he was productive. What sort of numbers can Beckham produce, if he can make the team? “People like to talk, ‘What are the stats?’ And all these things, and I’m like, the last time I played at the Ravens, I had 35 catches and 600-plus yards and four touchdowns. If you double that, that’s 70 catches, 1,200 yards, it’s a great season,” Beckham said. “So, it’s about how many opportunities you get, knowing that I may not be getting 10, 12 targets, what am I going to do with the five or six that I get? How can I help all the other receivers and the running backs, and how can I help this team? What can I bring? “I’m not so much caught up in what numbers are going to be, I just want to be the best me that I can be. I want to get open and create separation, catch the ball, hopefully score a lot, and have fun. That’s really all it is for me.” I wrote in the spring that the Giants should pass on a reunion with Beckham . I was wrong. He will never be the Beckham of old. He also, though, is not the old Beckham. He’s older. More mature. Mellower. A dad. He doesn’t seem like the young player who proposed to a kicking net and pretended to pee like a dog on the field after scoring a touchdown against the Eagles in Philadelphia. There are snaps to be had at the Giants’ wide receiver position. Malik Nabers is working back slowly from knee…

title: NY Giants training camp, practice No. 7: Odell Beckham has his best day
summary: WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — The New York Giants completed their third consecutive day of padded practices, the maximum allowed by the Collective Bargaining Agreement, on Wednesday. This was the best day of camp for the offense, and for wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. Winners Beckham — This was Beckham’s best day of camp. He […]
full_text: Odell Beckham | Getty Images WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — The New York Giants completed their third consecutive day of padded practices, the maximum allowed by the Collective Bargaining Agreement, on Wednesday. This was the best day of camp for the offense, and for wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr . Winners Beckham — This was Beckham’s best day of camp. He caught passes from Jaxson Dart, Jameis Winston, and Brandon Allen, and showed some burst turning a couple of those receptions upfield. Yes, Beckham received some first-team reps on Wednesday, the second straight day that has happened. I refuse to fuss about that, though. Jalin Hyatt and Xavier Gipson also got first-team reps. Jaxson Dart — After he fired a ball at Greg Newsome after a touchdown on Tuesday, Harbaugh made sure the quarterback was penalized 15 yards for taunting. You can be sure the topic was addressed during the team’s Tuesday night film session. “We have our team meeting, and all those plays come up, the different things come up. So, that’s an opportunity for coaching points. So, we went over the sequence, and everybody knows,” head coach John Harbaugh said. “So, it was good. He was great about it. He’s great about accepting responsibility and he’s a very accountable guy.” Dart responded by having a good day. He threw two interceptions, one a slightly off-target ball that safety Raheem Layne grabbed after Darnell Mooney batted it into the air, and the other a ball he tried to squeeze in to Calvin Austin that defensive back Elijah Campbell came away with. Despite that, Wednesday was probably Dart’s sharpest day of camp. Dalen Cambre — How did this young man catch only 10 passes as a college player? In his second season, Cambre has had an exceptional start to camp as he bids for one of the backup wide receiver spots. Cambre has made several highlight-reel catches in camp, including one Wednesday on a deep ball down the right sideline from Jameis Winston. “I see him make a circus catch every single day,” said Harbaugh. “And not just that, he’s doing all the other things. He’s doing special teams. He knows what he’s doing. He’s running great routes. I think he’s making a move. I think he’s done a great job and he’s got our attention.” Tae Banks — The Giants’ 2023 first-round pick has followed a solid spring with a good start to training camp, aside from a bad drop on an interception earlier this week. Banks is firmly in the mix in the competition for snaps opposite Paulson Adebo. Banks played collegiately at Maryland. Harbaugh, coach of the Baltimore Ravens for 18 years, was familiar with Banks before taking the Giants job. “We’ve known Tae for a long time. He’s from the area there, played at Maryland. We knew him coming out,” Harbaugh said. “I was really thrilled that he was on the team coming here. And I was excited to see how he did, and he’s done really well.” Dominic Zvada — The undrafted rookie placekicker took his turn in the kicking rotation with Ben Sauls on Wednesday. Zvada was a perfect 10 of 10 on field goals and extra points. Theo Johnson — The third-year tight end is a frustrating player. He will drop balls that look like they should be easy catches. Then, he will have days like Wednesday when he made two difficult catches with safety Tyler Nubin draped all over him. Calvin Austin — Like Cambre, he just keeps making plays every day. Losers Andrew Thomas — The star left tackle was not really a “loser”. Thomas, however, got yanked off the field for a play after committing a false start during a red zone session. In his media sessions, Harbaugh has not been critical of players for a high number of penalties. Taking Thomas off the field, though, shows that the veteran coach is not taking the penalties lightly. Theo Johnson under center — The Giants are experimenting with a Kansas City Chiefs-style sneak/Tush Push play with tight end Theo Johnson under center. They ran it Wednesday from their own 1-yard line. I hate, hate, hate, hate this play. It has disaster written all over it, and I hope we never see it during the regular season. Injury notes Edge defender Brian Burns and safety Beau Brade both sat out practice. Rookie wide receiver Malachi Fields only did individual work. Harbaugh said the injuries to all three players were “minor”, and that each would have played if Wednesday had been a game day. Nickel cornerback Dru Phillips left practice after a collision in the end zone with a wide receiver. I believe it was Xavier Gipson, but it was on the far end of the field blocked by players. Harbaugh said Phillips’ injury appeared to be minor, but the Giants would monitor him throughout the evening. Malik Nabers did his usual individual drills and routes on air. Wide receiver JuJu Smith-Schuster was a full practice participant a day after sitting out with knee swelling. Cornerback Jarrick Bernard-Converse was back to practice after missing a couple of days. Running back Cam Skattebo was not listed as injured, but did have a lighter workload on Wednesday. Roster moves As we reported earlier, the Giants made four roster moves . Defensive tacke Roy Robertson-Harris was placed on season-ending IR, ending hopes that he could return late this season. Second-year wide receiver Beaux Collins was waived. To fill those spots, the Giants added defensive backs D.J. James and David Long . Marty Mornhinweg pays a visit Marty Mornhinweg, former head coach of the Detroit Lions and a four-time NFL offensive coordinator, was on the field at Giants practice on Wednesday. Mornhingweg made the rounds, introducing himself to media members. Mornhingweg’s son, Skyler, is a football analyst for the Giants. Quote of the day “There’s absolutely nothing to do here. Beautiful place, but nothing to do here.” — Odell Beckham on West Virginia Mixing and matching The Giants did a lot of work on Wednesday with the units mixed up. Rather than first unit vs. first unit, there were a number of instances of the first team working against the second or third team. “You go ones against ones, you get good on good, just like you would expect. That’s more the coordinators calling what they want to call,” Harbaugh said. “If we go ones versus twos, we’re still, at this stage of camp, we’re still running our offense and defense. But the coordinator, if it’s the first offense, then he’s going to ask for some things. He wants to see more cover two, more cover three. He wants to see a blitz. He doesn’t want to see a blitz. He can help script that, but the defense still plays. It’s our calls, that kind of thing. “And then you also, we were able to run some longer periods out. So, you saw the guys out there for 12 plays, nine plays, for six no huddle plays, things like that, which become more game-like. So, that’s the balance I think of it.” Remaining Greenbrier practice schedule The Giants’ stay in West Virginia is winding down. There are only two more open practices.
