title: Proposing five big trades during 2026 NFL training camps
summary: NFL rosters are mostly locked in for 2026, but we crafted five potential win-win deals teams should consider making before Week 1.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL season might be a little more than a month away, but rosters aren't locked in quite yet. Training camp brings hope, optimism and trade talks, which is what we're focusing on here. And there are still a few roster holes to be patched -- and some trade candidates who could be dealt to fill them. So, let's play matchmaker.

 I'm proposing five deals that would make sense for both sides considering each team's depth chart, contention horizon and salary cap, along with each player's ability and contract. Is this finally the moment when the Giants move on from edge rusher Kayvon Thibodeaux ? Could Kayshon Boutte find a new home after the Patriots' wide receiver acquisitions? And is there a star defender who would fit well with the 49ers?

 Let's dive in. Here are five trades that should happen before Week 1.

 

 
 Jump to a proposed trade involving: 
 Bates | Thibodeaux 
 Coleman | Little | Boutte 

 
 

 

 49ers get a defensive boost with Bates 
 49ers receive: S Jessie Bates III , 2028 sixth-round pick 
 Falcons receive: 2027 third-round pick

 The Falcons' 2023 signing of Bates was an example of free agency gone right. The Falcons paid sticker price -- four years and $64 million -- to sign Bates, who was very effective in Cincinnati and continued that quality play in Atlanta. That was particularly true in 2023, when Bates delivered six interceptions and three forced fumbles while earning second-team All-Pro honors.

 He was good again in 2024, but he wasn't quite on the same level last season. Still, the 29-year-old Bates remains one of the best safeties in the league. (He ranked fifth in this year's survey of coaches and executives conducted by ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.)

 

 If the Falcons were expected to contend, it would make sense to keep Bates and see the original contract through. But they aren't, and with a ton of 2027 cap space even after the  Bijan Robinson   extension , the Falcons will likely be spenders next offseason. They would risk losing Bates without getting a compensatory pick in return if he walks in free agency. So it's better for Atlanta to deal him now. And while that would mean finding a replacement for Bates, the Falcons wouldn't be lacking in safety talent thanks to emerging second-year player Xavier Watts .

 It just so happens that former Falcons head coach Raheem Morris, who coached Bates the past two seasons, is now the 49ers' defensive coordinator . And he could use an upgrade at safety alongside Ji'Ayir Brown and Malik Mustapha . The timing works, as the 49ers are contenders who could use defensive help after ranking 25th in EPA allowed per dropback last season.

 

 San Francisco would be giving up real draft capital for a short-term player, but that's an indicator of Bates' skill and the fact that his contract would cost the 49ers only $13 million in 2026 -- a below-market price to sign a player of his caliber.

 
 

 Patriots satisfy the edge-rush need with Thibodeaux 
 Patriots receive: Edge  Kayvon Thibodeaux , 2027 fifth-round pick 
 Giants receive: 2027 third-round pick

 I included a Thibodeaux trade in this same story last year . One year and another first-round edge rusher later, he's now an even more obvious candidate to be dealt.

 Thibodeaux is playing on his $14.75 million fifth-year option and is set to be a free agent at the end of this season. While there was an argument for having him as a third edge rusher behind Brian Burns and Abdul Carter  in the past, New York now also has first-round pick Arvell Reese , who plays linebacker and edge. To keep Thibodeaux around at this price point to potentially be the team's No. 4 edge rusher isn't ideal.

 So the Giants need to find a trade partner who:

 
 Has a need at edge 
 Has the cap room to take on Thibodeaux's 2026 contract 
 Is an immediate contender, given his pending free agent status 
 
 New England fits the bill and then some because Thibodeaux offers long-term upside if the Patriots decide to re-sign him. Their current edge rushers are Harold Landry III and Dre'Mont Jones . At this stage of their careers (Landry is 30, Jones 29), they're better fits as No. 2 and No. 3 edge rushers, respectively, on a contending team. Thibodeaux hasn't been good enough yet to be New England's unquestioned top edge rusher, but he possesses the promise to develop into that.

 Thibodeaux's 9.9% pass rush win rate at edge last season -- below average for the position -- was similar to what Landry (10.8%) and Jones (8.6%) posted. Thibodeaux had only 2.5 sacks last season in 10 games but has shown more in the past. In 2024, he recorded a 16.8% pass rush win rate at edge (16th best), and he recorded 11.5 sacks as a rookie in 2022. Thibodeaux is also solid in the run game, and his 27.9% run stop win rate at edge last season was above average for the position.

 Giants fans will likely feel like the team should get more in this deal. But it's all about the contract, as Thibodeaux has only one year left on his deal and is getting paid pretty close to what he would probably make on the open market.

 

 

 
 

 Colts give Coleman a fresh start 
 Colts receive: WR Keon Coleman , 2028 sixth-round pick 
 Bills receive: 2027 fourth-round pick

 Coleman was already a potential trade candidate before Bills owner Terry Pegula blamed the team's former coaching staff -- as opposed to the current front office -- for pushing to draft the wide receiver with the No. 33 pick in 2024. Coleman has struggled in two NFL seasons, but it was a fairly shocking insult toward a player still on the roster.

 Buffalo doesn't have to trade him, but between his on-field struggles and the negative vibes stemming from ownership's comments, it certainly could. And the Colts would be a logical candidate to bet on Coleman at a reduced cost.

 Coleman has recorded 1.65 yards per route run over 583 career routes, along with a 48-51-49 triple-slash of open, catch and YAC scores from ESPN's player-tracking based  receiver scores . Those numbers aren't great and aren't what the Bills hoped for when they drafted him, but they're not terrible either. He definitely could still be a contributing player to a winning team with some growth.

 Indianapolis needs receiver help. After being re-signed to a $28.5 million-per-year deal , Alec Pierce underwent  ankle surgery and is not yet back on the practice field. The Colts have the promising Josh Downs in the slot, but the depth chart on the outside behind Pierce is rough, with Nick Westbrook-Ikhine and Ashton Dulin the likely next options. The Colts could use another receiver regardless of Pierce's status, so taking a chance on Coleman's upside makes sense.

 

 The Jahan Dotson trade in 2024 , in which the Eagles sent a third-round pick and two seventh-rounders to the Commanders for Dotson and a fifth-rounder, is a useful comp. Like Coleman, Dotson was entering his third year after an uneven first two seasons. But Dotson was a higher draft pick (No. 16 vs. No. 33) and was better regarded than Coleman is now, which is why I think it would cost less to acquire the latter.

 
 

 Cardinals get offensive line help with Little 
 Cardinals receive: OT Walker Little , 2027 seventh-round pick 
 Jaguars receive: 2027 sixth-round pick

 Little was Wally Pipped last year by Cole Van Lanen , who ascended into the starting lineup at left tackle after Little missed two games with a  concussion . The Jaguars kept Van Lanen at left tackle even after Little returned, then extended him in the offseason. That makes Little an expensive third tackle, due an almost fully guaranteed $11.5 million this season.

 

 Little had his best season in terms of pass block win rate in 2025 but was still only in the 27th percentile among tackles. While tackle depth is important, my guess is that the cap-strapped Jaguars would cut Little if his money weren't guaranteed. But it is. Dealing Little would be a cost-saving maneuver, so the compensation on any deal ought to be barely above -- maybe…

title: Matthew McConaughey contacts Bijan Robinson following contract extension
summary: When word got out about Robinson's new extension with the Falcons, it didn't take long for McConaughey to get in touch. In fact, it was only a matter of minutes.
full_text:
When news of Bijan Robinson 's new contract broke Tuesday, the first person the star running back heard from wasn't a teammate or a family member.

 It was actor Matthew McConaughey.

 Robinson revealed Wednesday that when word got out about his three-year extension with the Atlanta Falcons worth up to $75 million, it didn't take long for McConaughey to offer his congratulations. In fact, it was a matter of minutes.

 

 "As soon as the news hit, Matthew McConaughey hit me," Robinson told reporters. "As soon as it hit. I think it hit at like 7:56 [a.m.]. Like 7:58, he texted me.

 

 "A lot of awesome, really cool people texted me, but it was cool to see him, as soon as it hit, like, he was the first one."

 Robinson played college ball at Texas , where McConaughey is an alumnus and longtime superfan. The Falcons showed in their post of Robinson's quote a photo he took with McConaughey as a recruit on a visit to Austin. The former Longhorns running back has expressed interest in getting into acting following his playing career and was connected with McConaughey, with the two developing a friendship during Robinson's final collegiate year in 2022.

 For now, though, Robinson's talents will remain on the gridiron -- talents he's now better compensated for than he was last week.

title: Tracking 2026 NFL hold-ins: Gibbs, Vea and Tuipulotu
summary: Here is the latest on Falcons' Bijan Robinson, Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs, Bucs' Vita Vea and Chargers' Tuli Tuipulotu.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL preseason kicks off with the Pro Football Hall of Game on Thursday , with three weeks of action to follow, but there are a handful of prominent players who are still not practicing because of their contract situations.

 The start of NFL training camps brought these negotiations to a head. Players can hold out and stay away from camp until their financial situations are addressed, or they can hold in, where they report to camp to avoid fines but skip practice while waiting for a new contract. We're tracking the important hold-ins across the league, with updates from our NFL Nation writers on each situation.

 The list of stars not practicing includes Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs ,  Tampa Bay Buccaneers defensive tackle Vita Vea  and  Los Angeles Chargers outside linebacker  Tuli Tuipulotu . 

 Which player will be next in resolving his contract dispute? Are any of these four willing to miss games once the season begins? Let's examine each situation.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Gibbs | Robinson | Vea | Tuipulotu 

 
 

 

 Jahmyr Gibbs , RB, Detroit Lions 
 

 Status: Holding in, seeking a new contract 

 Aug. 4 update:  Lions coach Dan Campbell said  Bijan Robinson 's record-setting deal with the Atlanta Falcons  is " certainly not gonna hurt " the team's contract negotiations with their own star running back, Gibbs. The Falcons and Robinson agreed to a three-year extension Tuesday that includes $51 million guaranteed, setting the stage for a new deal for Gibbs, who continues to hold in and miss practices at training camp. "[Robinson's deal is] not gonna hurt, but we'll see," Campbell said. "Look, I'm anxious to get Gibbs back out there."

 Aug. 3 update: Gibbs  missed his fifth consecutive practice Monday as his apparent hold-in continues while he looks to reach agreement on a new deal during training camp. However, the three-time Pro Bowler was spotted roaming the sidelines in a gray Lions cutoff hoodie for the second straight day at the Meijer Performance Center, often chatting with teammates Amon-Ra St. Brown , Jameson Williams and Jared Goff on the sideline in between drills. While leaving the field to enter the locker room alongside team security, Gibbs was briefly approached by reporters and stated that "only time will tell" when he returns in his first official comments on his absence from practice.

 

 Aug. 2 update: Gibbs was spotted on the sidelines Sunday, sporting a hoodie as he watched his teammates practice for the first time since training camp began. Gibbs has now missed his fourth consecutive practice as he seeks a contract extension. Lions WR Jameson Williams described Gibbs as "the best of the best" following practice as they were spotted communicating in between on-field drills. Williams feels Gibbs should be the NFL's highest-paid running back. "I wouldn't even say look at the stats, look at the film," Williams said. "Nobody close. He's the best."

 July 31 update: The Lions star missed his third day of practice as the hold-in continues. Coach Dan Campbell mentioned earlier this week that Gibbs was dealing with a "little bit of a back" issue during conditioning tests but clarified that it's nothing to worry about ahead of Friday's session. "No, I don't think it's severe," Campbell said. Gibbs, who is showing up at the team facility, has continued to communicate with teammates, such as wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown . "Obviously, we're missing one of our best players on offense, which sucks, but he's still in the building," St. Brown said. "He's still at all the meetings and everything. So, I think that the players understand what's going on. Everyone kind of gets it. It's part of this business, but we're still out there practicing, doing our thing."

 July 30 update:  The running back missed his second straight day of practice Thursday as the apparent hold-in continues until he reaches a new contract extension. Campbell addressed the situation ahead of Thursday's practice, saying that he is "not even sweating it" as both sides are working to secure a long-term deal. Gibbs did complete a conditioning test Wednesday in which Campbell said he "had a little bit of a back" issue, so it's unclear if Gibbs will start practicing right away once he inks a new deal.

 -- Eric Woodyard, Lions reporter 

 

 
 

 Bijan Robinson , RB, Atlanta Falcons 
 Status: Signed a new deal 

 Aug. 4 update:  The two-time Pro Bowler and the Falcons reached agreement on a three-year extension worth up to $75 million that now will make him the highest-paid running back in NFL history, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

 Aug. 1 update:  Robinson was again at practice, though not practicing, for the fourth straight day. Robinson left the field at one point during the media video shooting period and then came back when the cameras were off. Otherwise, he was with his teammates on the sidelines like he has been since camp started on Wednesday.

 July 31 update : Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski addressed Robinson's hold-in for the first time Friday morning. He said he was confident the contract situation will be resolved amiably.

 On how he is approaching the conflict, Stefanski said: "Just coach the football team."

 "Understand that there's a business side to everything we do and there's the football side and sometimes you're living in both worlds, if you will," Stefanski said. "But just going to continue to coach the football team."

 Robinson was once again in a jersey with no helmet or cleats for a third straight day. He was on the sideline encouraging teammates after plays. At the end of practice, he did pushups with his teammates who lost a drill.

 July 30 update: Robinson was a hold-in for a second straight practice Thursday. Like Wednesday, the team's first practice of training camp, Robinson was present on the field, chatting with teammates and seemingly in good spirits. He wore a Falcons jersey but had no helmet or cleats. Robinson and the Falcons have not commented on the situation, though coach Kevin Stefanski is likely to address it Friday morning.

 -- Marc Raimondi, Falcons reporter 

 

 
 

 Vita Vea , DT, Tampa Bay Buccaneers 
 

 Status: Holding in, requesting a trade 

 Aug. 2 update: The star defensive tackle remains sidelined with a back injury, as well as his contract hold-in. Coach Todd Bowles said there is "nothing new" to report on his injury, and he is unsure if Vea will make the trip to the  New York Jets  for a pair of joint practices starting Aug. 11.

 July 31 update: Vea, who stayed indoors to receive treatment Thursday, was back out on the practice field Friday with teammates but was still sidelined with a back injury sustained during the team's conditioning test. Bowles said he does not have a timetable yet for Vea's back.

 July 30 update: While Vea was on the sidelines during Wednesday's first training camp practice and was standing alongside teammates during positional drills, he was not on the practice field Thursday. Bowles said Vea tweaked his back in the team's conditioning test Tuesday and he was getting treatment. Vea did, however, participate in an interview on the "Up & Adams Show," but he did not discuss his contract. Vea is set to earn $17 million this season, but none of it is guaranteed, along with a per-game roster bonus that is capped at $1 million total. Bowles said they are preparing for the season as if Vea will play. 

 -- Jenna Laine, Bucs reporter 

 

 
 

 Tuli Tuipulotu , OLB, Los Angeles Chargers 
 

 Status: Holding in, seeking a new contract

 Aug. 5 update:  Tuipulotu, who has been a limited participant in practice this training camp amid ongoing contract negotiations, was a full participant in Wednesday's practice. The caveat is that the practice was a walkthrough, so Tuipulotu and the other Chargers players were going at half speed. He still has yet to participate in a non-walkthrough practice 11-on-11 period, but his participation could be a…

title: 2026 Atlanta Falcons training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Falcons training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Atlanta Falcons ' camp is taking place in Flowery Branch, Georgia, and Falcons reporter Marc Raimondi has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Falcons camp. We will update this file often. How will the QB battle play out between  Michael Penix Jr . and  Tua Tagovailoa for QB1? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Falcons stories 
 
 Sources: Falcons, RB Robinson reach 3-year deal worth up to $75M 
 Falcons sign Matthew Bergeron to four-year, $96M extension 
 Falcons' Jalon Walker tore ACL, out for season 
 Wife of DC Ulbrich dies of cancer 
 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 Michael Penix Jr . explained his current situation in the clearest way possible Wednesday.

 "If I can't be on the field," Penix said, "how am I going to be the starter?"

 Penix has been on the field. He has done individual drills and 7-on-7 sessions. But what the Falcons third-year quarterback means is that he has yet to be cleared for 11-on-11 work. And until he does, there cannot be any kind of quarterback competition.

 That is not necessarily news. The Falcons coaching staff made that clear in the spring. But back then there was some expectation Penix would be fully ready for training camp. That has not been the case and Penix said it could be another several weeks before he's good to go.

 Tua Tagovailoa (tight back) took another step toward a full return Wednesday with more work in 11s. He went 5-of-7 passing. At this juncture, it's fair to say Tagovailoa will be the team's Week 1 starter unless something major changes.

 More observations: 

 
 Edge rusher Jalon Walker was officially confirmed as out for the season with a torn ACL after getting injured Tuesday at practice. It's a major blow for a pass rush that was depending him on to make a major impact. He had 5.5 sacks as a rookie last season. 
 Running back Bijan Robinson officially put pen to paper on his three-year extension, which is worth up to $75 million. He is still limited in practice and has not done any 11s as the team ramps him up. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Falcons running back Bijan Robinson returned to practice after a five-day hold-in Tuesday. Robinson got a three-year extension worth up to $75 million and is now the highest-paid running back in the NFL.

 Head coach Kevin Stefanski referred to Robinson's hold-in as "very amicable." Robinson had been at every practice on the hip of running backs coach Michael Pitre prior to actually coming back.

 "He wants to be out there practicing," Falcons running back Brian Robinson Jr . said. "You know he wants to be competing. So, I used to just tell him, 'Yo, take your time, handle your business. Whenever your time comes, it's going to come. I know you want to be out there with us, but we going to hold it down until you come back.'"

 Bijan Robinson didn't do much Tuesday. He worked a bit with the running backs in individual drills and did a play-action drill after practice with quarterback Michael Penix Jr . Pitre said they will work to ramp Bijan up over the next few days based on recommendations by the training and medical staff.

 More observations: 

 
 Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa (tight back) said he continues to make progress and expected to be practicing fully Wednesday. Tagovailoa has eased into 11-on-11 sessions the last two days, but has only thrown seven passes. He was 3-of-4 in 11s on Tuesday. 
 Quarterback Cooper Rush , who signed with the Falcons last Wednesday, got reps with the first-team offense in a two-minute drill near the end of practice. Penix has still not yet been cleared for 11s, but got reps again in 7-on-7 work Tuesday. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa participated in 11-on-11 team sessions Monday for the first time this training camp. Tagovailoa has been dealing with a tight back and was still limited. He did two series, going 3-for-3 passing in 11s with individual drills, as well.

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 Rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane continues to be the talk of Baltimore Ravens training camp after another highlight reel catch.

 During red-zone drills, Lane leapt high in the back of the end zone to grab a Lamar Jackson throw for a touchdown. The way Lane is consistently pulling in passes has drawn lofty comparisons.

 "The guy that I was around that his hands remind me of is [former NFL great] Mike Thomas ," Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle said. "Mike Thomas had these strong hands where he could pull it down in a way. You threw it in the vicinity, and you felt like he was going to go get it. There is a lot of that feeling. He is a very friendly guy to throw to."

 Doyle was in New Orleans with Thomas from 2019 to 2022 as an offensive assistant. Thomas led the NFL in receptions in 2018 and 2019.

 Now, in his first season as the play-caller in Baltimore, Doyle has been impressed with the Thomas-like catch radius of Lane, who has been the headliner through the first seven practices of camp. He made a leaping, 30-yard reception over the middle last week and then wowed fans with a one-handed catch on Tuesday.

 When Doyle left the field Wednesday, Lane approached him to say he wasn't pleased with how he messed up at practice.

 Doyle told him, "Hey, you recognized what you made a mistake on. Now, the next step is let's fix it before that happens."

 Other observations:  

 
 After watching the Ravens not practice well in the rain during the spring, Doyle was pleased with how the players performed during the steady downpour on Wednesday. "We play in the AFC North," Doyle said. "In order to win games late in the year, you are going to play in some weather games." 
 Middle linebacker Roquan Smith is reacting to the ball better than he did a year ago. Smith ended the first team drill by picking off Lamar Jackson and then lateraling the ball on the return. 
 Wide receiver Zay Flowers added 8 pounds this offseason and is up to 186 pounds. What was the reason for the added weight? "Everybody gets mad at me when I'm running sideways," Flowers said. "So [now I can] run through some more tackles." 
 

 
 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane has become the star of Ravens training camp.

 Early in team drills, Lane made an unbelievable one-handed grab along the sideline, which will go down as one of the best receptions in Ravens' camp history. After running a route to the right sideline, Lane had to reach back to catch Lamar Jackson 's 20-yard pass with his extended right hand while falling backward to the ground.

 "That was a great play by Ja'Kobi," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said. "He's continued to flash and make those type of plays. As [for] anybody, you're always searching for consistency down after down. Again, the more he shows Lamar that he's making those types of plays, the more trust they build, and that's really what training camp and what practice is all about."

 

 Later, in one-on-one drills, Lane showed his playmaking ability again, using a double move to get behind cornerback T.J. Tampa and catching a long touchdown pass from Jackson.

 This has been an outstanding start to camp for Lane, a third-round pick from USC who has become the team's No. 3 wide receiver behind Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman . On Thursday, Lane first electrified the crowd by elevating over two defenders for a leaping, 30-yard catch over the middle.

 There was a brief scare when No. 1 cornerback Nate Wiggins leapt high to pick off Jackson and then landed hard on his back after safety Jaylinn Hawkins accidentally collided with him. Wiggins didn't move for a few minutes as trainers looked at him on the field. But Wiggins got back to his feet and continued to practice, saying he got the wind knocked out of him. 
 In one of the more unusual plays of camp, Jackson was intercepted by 310-pound defensive lineman David Olajiga , who had dropped back into coverage. But right tackle Roger Rosengarten made a heads-up play by knocking the ball away from Olajiga and forcing a fumble. 
 Reserve cornerback Amani Oruwariye picked off No. 3 quarterback Skylar Thompson with aggressive play. Oruwariye closed on tight end Ty Pezza and ripped the ball away. 
 
 
 Monday, Aug. 3 
 On Monday, Ravens defensive end Calais Campbell practiced for the first time since his personal tragedy this offseason.

 Last month, Campbell's brother was charged with murder after police found their 71-year-old mother dead at home in Atlanta during a welfare check. Campbell's family told police that his brother struggled with mental illness.

 'We're excited to work him in, start to ramp him into getting ready," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said. "That'll be at a pace that's good for him."

 Campbell was not made available to reporters after practice. Last month, the Campbell family issued a statement asking for privacy while they deal with "overwhelming grief."

 Campbell's participation on Monday was limited to individual drills. The Ravens excused him from practicing for the first week of training camp.

 Campbell, 39, is entering his 19th NFL season after signing a one-year, $5.5 million contract with Baltimore in April.

 "He's a force multiplier of just how he operates and the wisdom that he brings," Minter said. "On top of, he's still a really high caliber player for his position."

 Other observations:  

 
 In the first padded practice of camp, first-round pick Olaivavega Ioane was looking to make a block downfield and he accidentally collided with running back Derrick Henry , which caused both of them to go to the ground. "Welcome to the league, huh," said Ioane, the Ravens' starting right guard. "Now I know to stay out of his way." 
 Offensive line coach Dwayne Ledford said it's going to take all of training camp for the Ravens to make a decision at starting center. Danny Pinter , Ethan Pocic and Jovaughn Gwyn are competing for that spot. "We want to make sure that we're diligent in giving everybody the opportunity that's here," Ledford said, "and just make sure we get the right guy that we want in there with that first group." 
 Pro Bowl defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike is sporting a new neck roll at practice. Madubuike, who is looking to come back from neck surgery, has suited up but has not participated in individual or team drills. Asked about the neck roll, Minter said, "Whatever makes the players feel their best and play with the most confidence -- it definitely looks like a little bit of a throwback." 
 In one-on-one drills against cornerbacks, rookie third-round pick Ja'Kobi Lane flashed again, beating Chidobe Awuzie and catching a deep pass on a fly route. Lane is off to a fast start to the second week of training camp after a strong first week. He…

 Darnell Wright agrees to record deal 
 New Bears safety Coby Bryant out 8-10 weeks with injury 
 Bears CB Johnson views 2026 as 'definitely a contract year' 
 Ben Johnson: Bears motivated to spurn 'regression' label 
 
 
 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 One day after becoming the highest-paid right tackle in NFL history, Darnell Wright got ribbed by coach Ben Johnson, who congratulated Wright on his four-year, $116 million extension ($93 million guaranteed) in front of the team before practice.

 Johnson joked that Wright "owed" offensive line coach Dan Roushar a loan. Wright agreed with Johnson's assessment and credited his position coach for helping him reach the point of his career where he's played his way into earning life-changing money.

 "[Roushar's] consistent every day in what he does and what he says," Wright said. "He's consistent in what he's telling you. ... Some coaches I've had in the past or some coaches in the league, they're not very good teachers. They see a guy with talent and blah, blah, blah, but they can't really convey what it is and teach you. You still need to be taught. So I think he is such a good teacher and he does it with such good -- he's not yelling at you, he's not screaming at you, he's not demeaning you, he's telling you what's good about the rep and he's telling you what's bad about the rep so you can see both sides.

 "If you have a coach that tells you just what you did was wrong with the rep so maybe the next rep, you just change everything. Now, you have a different result and you have no consistency to stack on top of each other, where as Dan he shows you what you did good with the rep so you can, you know, keep doing the good things and fix the bad things he tells you."

 During training camp in 2025, Roushar told reporters that he didn't see Wright playing with a consistently high motor. Wright said he appreciated the honesty and path Roushar laid for the right tackle to improve. That constructive criticism paid off as Wright earned second-team All Pro honors while playing through an elbow injury.

 Wright was the inaugural first-round draft pick by general manager Ryan Poles in 2023. The Bears traded back one spot, from No. 9 to No. 10, which allowed the Philadelphia Eagles to draft defensive tackle Jalen Carter , while Chicago snagged its franchise right tackle.

 Proving to Poles that he made the right decision is something Wright internalized over the first three seasons of his career. Seeing how the investment made by the GM went far beyond a financial commitment motivates Wright to continue to progress.

 "[Poles] really invested in me [by] helping me get more one-on-one time with the coaches, one-on-one time more with the strength staff, one-on-one time more with [assistant strength and conditioning coach] Mark [Phillipi] in there doing core strength," Wright said. "...Even when I was a young player, it's hard for you to go up to a coach and want to demand their time. I know you're a first-round pick and blah, blah, blah, so they would probably be obliged, but sometimes it's hard for a player to approach a coach and want to take all their time when they've got stuff to do ...but he was invested in me at a really early age, beyond what you'd think a GM would do."

 

 
 The Bears were in shells for a practice that lasted 90 minutes and had just a handful of team periods conducted at walk-through speed. 
 The highlight of the morning came during a 7-on-7 period when  Caleb Williams completed 9 of 10 attempts. Wide receiver Kaden Davis was on the receiving end of the best catch of the day, a one-handed sliding grab in the corner of the end zone from Williams. 
 Linebacker T.J. Edwards (calf) was activated off the non-football injury list before practice and got his mandatory 40 up-downs done as the defense looked on. 
 For a third straight day, Braxton Jones took his reps as the first-team left tackle. 
 Left guard Joe Thuney and defensive tackle Grady Jarrett were given veteran rest days. The Bears will be in pads Thursday for their fourth practice of the week. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 After the offense got off to a fast start during the Bears' first week of training camp, the defense has caught up and set the tone the last two days.

 Tuesday's two-hour practice featured a heavy dose of 11-on-11 periods and live tackling. The emphasis was on 13 personnel (3 TE, 1 WR, 1 RB), which leant itself to the offense establishing the run game early on.

 But the offense looked the sloppiest it has during any of the team's first six practices. There were dropped passes, pre-snap penalties and timing issues between quarterback Caleb Williams and his receivers.

 During the final period, the first-team offense began on its own 47-yard line trailing 28-23 with 54 seconds on the clock. After back-to-back false starts, Williams found himself being chased down by linebacker Devin Bush , who blitzed off the edge.

 Williams had three straight completions to Luther Burden III , Colston Loveland and Kalif Raymond but could not finish the drive in the end zone.

 With 3.2 seconds remaining, Williams launched a ball down the seam, where Burden went up in traffic to complete the play through multiple defenders and was subsequently blown up by Bush.

 "It was a last-minute play," Bush said. "Take a shot at the end zone. Our responsibility is to not let them in the end zone. Offense's responsibility is get the ball in the end zone. So just a competitive play and finished our practice in the two-minute drill."

 Burden was slow to get up but walked off the field on his own flanked by Williams and cornerback Tyrique Stevenson . A practice like this is an anomaly for the offense, but the lack of execution is something players know will be drilled down on in Tuesday afternoon meetings.

 "We're gonna go in there, clean up the film," Burden said. "You know, every day not gonna be a great day. I mean, you can strive for that, but it's camp. It's gonna be ups and downs. So that's the good part about it. We get to come back and watch it. We come back, be better, talk about it. Come back tomorrow, have a better day. That's what it's about."

 
 Braxton Jones was the first-team left tackle for a second straight practice. That's the first time since late last week when the Bears began rotating who would be with the starting O-line that a player got multiple days in a row with the first-teamers.

title: What are the Browns looking for in their QB competition?
summary: Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders have spent seven camp practices focused on pre-snap and post-snap techniques.
full_text:
BEREA, Ohio -- A late practice sequence on Monday encapsulated the highs and lows that can occur in the Cleveland Browns ' quarterback competition on a given day.

 Shedeur Sanders was leading Cleveland's No. 2 offense in an end-of-game situational drill: down 2, near the goal line, with about a dozen seconds remaining and no timeouts left. The objective for Sanders was to attempt a pass into the end zone but leave enough time for a field goal in case of an incompletion. Sanders held the ball too long and finally threw a pass out of the back of the end zone with no time remaining, drawing the ire of coach Todd Monken.

 About 10 minutes later, Sanders displayed his growth before the snap. Leading a two-minute drill, Sanders signaled a tight end to motion inside and block, properly setting his protection to block the defense's blitz before delivering a deep touchdown pass to wide receiver Gage Larvadain .

 The quarterback competition between Sanders and Deshaun Watson has delivered plenty of highlights and lowlights in a week-plus of practices. But most importantly to Monken, it has brought teaching moments as he installs a new offense and evaluates each passer, focusing on pre-snap operation and post-snap execution.

 

 "I think to say who's ahead is a little extreme," Monken said before Wednesday's practice, the team's seventh camp session. "But we evaluate every day where our roster is, who's where. We try not to knee-jerk react on the one day; that's hard to do. We want every day to go as smooth as it can, and it doesn't, so you have to fight that part of it. We also have to fight; we're in install. We see what you see, and we see a little more in-depth because of the film. But the reality is we're always talking about personnel and the roster; the quarterbacks just happen to be part of that."

 Sanders and Watson have been alternating first-team reps every practice since the Browns opened training camp on July 29. Each session has consisted of 7-on-7s and 11-on-11s, in addition to various situational drills. Monken said the first eight (including Thursday's) practices will center around installing the offense, adding various portions of the scheme each day. Cleveland opened with zone runs and its short passing game before expanding to longer-developing pass concepts and gap scheme runs once padded practices began Monday.

 Monken said the installation will end Thursday, and he'll then start calling plays catering to each quarterback's strengths.

 Beyond how each quarterback looks throwing the ball, Monken has also prioritized perfecting the pre-snap operation. Multiple players have said Monken's scheme heaps plenty of responsibility on the quarterback before the ball is snapped, whether it be audibling into more favorable plays or executing various cadences. Through three practices, Monken had already incorporated 10 different cadences. With those have come a bevy of pre-snap infractions, but in the eyes of the first-year head coach, it's all a part of the learning curve for a new offense.

 The pre-snap operation has been one of the biggest points of emphasis for Sanders, who in his second season has continued to display a penchant for throwing an accurate deep ball.

 "Reviewing all the film from last year and the mistakes I made, and just being able to recognize, have a better pre-snap, be able to recognize things better and post-snap, also," Sanders said of his growth. "The fact that our defense gives us a lot of different looks and everything is truly great that we're able to get that in practice."

 Monken said he has been "highly impressed" by Sanders, dating back to his performance in the offseason workout program.

 "There's a lot to take in when you're installing," Monken said. "We got through the spring, then we were gone for six weeks, and then you start back up again in a new system. I think you'll continue to see his operation and mechanics improve, and I think that's the biggest part right now is in and out of the huddle, getting to the line of scrimmage, eliminating that anxiety, his anxiety and my anxiety."

 

 Watson, who did not play in 2025 after a pair of Achilles surgeries, got off to a slow start in training camp, throwing six interceptions in the first couple of practices. But he delivered his best session to date on Wednesday, throwing multiple touchdowns during 7-on-7 red zone drills. Monken previously downplayed Watson's spate of turnovers, saying they can be positive lessons, so long as the same mistakes aren't repeated.

 "The biggest thing for me is just letting my instincts take over -- not doing anything extra, not doing anything less, just staying balanced and letting it come," Watson said. "Day to day it's getting better, and honestly, I think the biggest thing is just playing football. Whenever the preseason games come up and we're out there playing, I think that's where we can learn. Each game is just an opportunity to get better at it."

 Monken said he'll continue to alternate first-team reps between Watson and Sanders until a starter is named. For the time being, the expectation is that both passers will start one of the first two preseason games, with the Browns' preseason opener against the Chicago Bears looming on Aug. 15.

 "I don't think you're really going to know until you get through all the installs, because we're not game-planning against our own defense," Monken said. "Each day has been a different part of the pass game, so it's hard to really [tell]. And one day you go with the 1s, the other day you go with the 2s; certainly that matchup is going to be different depending on who you're going against.

 "The most important thing is, from a process standpoint, how are we operating at the line of scrimmage, where are their eyes, have they taken command of one, the huddle, and then cadence, and then understanding the concepts. I think they're all doing good, they're all fine. All of our players are working through mistakes and fighting like hell to get better."

full_text:

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Browns camp 
 
 Jerry Jeudy clarifies viral video, says he talked to Browns QBs 
 AJ Epenesa grateful to be Eagle after 'weird' Browns situation 
 Deshaun Watson: Preseason is 'great opportunity' after injuries 
 Deion Sanders gives Browns 'insight' on Shedeur Sanders

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 Quarterback Deshaun Watson had a slow start to training camp but had his best day to date on Wednesday. After two consecutive practices in pads, the Browns practiced in shoulder pads and helmets and ran extensive red zone and goal line 7-on-7 drills. Watson excelled, throwing multiple touchdowns, but he also looked more in sync and confident pushing the ball downfield in other team drills.

 "I think to say who's ahead is a little extreme," Browns coach Todd Monken said before practice. "But we evaluate every day where our roster is, who's where. We try not to knee-jerk react on the one day; that's hard to do. We want every day to go as smooth as it can, and it doesn't, so you have to fight that part of it. We also have to fight; we're in install. We see what you see, and we see a little more in-depth because of the film. But the reality is we're always talking about personnel and the roster; the quarterbacks just happen to be part of that."

 Another observation: 

 
 Sixteen players did not practice Wednesday: tight end Joe Royer (personal), cornerback Myles Bryant and Damarri Mathis , fullback Michael Burton , linebacker Carson Schwesinger , defensive tackles Mike Hall Jr ., Kalia Davis , Mason Graham , Maliek Collins (PUP), Sam Kamara and Elijah Chatman ; centers Parker Brailsford and Elgton Jenkins ; offensive tackle Izavion Miller , guard Teven Jenkins and wide receiver Jamari Thrash . 
 
 
 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Quarterback Shedeur Sanders , leading the No. 1 offense in Cleveland's quarterback competition today, led a two-minute drill that ended in a field goal.

 It marked the second straight day Sanders led a successful two-minute drill to end practice.

 "I've been highly impressed over the last four months that I've been around him with how far he's come as a player, and he's only going to continue to get better," Browns coach Todd Monken said. "There's a lot to take in when you're installing. We got through the spring, then we were gone for six weeks, and then you start back up again in a new system. I think you'll continue to see his operation and mechanics improve, and I think that's the biggest part right now is in and out of the huddle, getting to the line of scrimmage, eliminating that anxiety, his anxiety and my anxiety."

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Wide receiver KC Concepcion was at practice after avoiding a serious shoulder injury on Monday but was limited to individual drills. 
 Eleven players did not practice: tight end Joe Royer (personal), cornerbacks Myles Bryant and Damarri Mathis , fullback Michael Burton , linebacker Carson Schwesinger , defensive tackles Mike Hall Jr ., Kalia Davis , Mason Graham and Maliek Collins (PUP); and offensive linemen Kendrick Green and Teven Jenkins . 
 Safety Christopher Edmonds intercepted quarterback Dillon Gabriel in 7-on-7s; it was Edmonds' third pick in training camp, the most of any defender. 
 Browns offensive tackle Izavion Miller left practice with a member of the team's medical staff. Defensive tackle Sam Kamara also left practice on a cart. 
 The Browns claimed defensive tackle Coziah Izzard via waivers from Arizona and waived wide receiver Aaron Anderson , who left practice early with a member of the medical staff, with an injury designation. 
 Before practice, Cleveland signed cornerback Tyler Hall and waived offensive tackle Jack Conley . 
 

 
 Monday, Aug. 3 
 On the first practice with pads for the Browns, quarterback Shedeur Sanders ended the day on a high note for Cleveland's offense. Running the No. 2 offense in the ongoing quarterback competition with Deshaun Watson , Sanders connected with wide receiver Gage Larvadain for a deep touchdown on a slot fade to end a two-minute drill in the end zone.

 One play before the touchdown, Sanders found wideout Tylan Wallace on a back-shoulder fade to put the offense in scoring position. Sanders also threw an earlier touchdown in team drills after rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion got behind the secondary for a deep score.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Concepcion had an injury scare in a previous two-minute drill for the No. 1 offense when he had a hard fall while trying to make a catch and grabbed his right shoulder. Concepcion walked off the field under his own power and remained on the sideline as practice ended shortly thereafter. He is believed to have avoided a serious injury. 
 Linebacker Carson Schwesinger did not participate in practice for a second consecutive day because of what coach Todd Monken called a "minor injury." 
 In addition to Schwesinger, tight end Joe Royer (personal), defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr ., offensive linemen Kendrick Green and Teven Jenkins , wide receiver Jamari Thrash and defensive tackles Kalia Davis and Maliek Collins (PUP) did not practice. 
 Thrash, who also did not practice Saturday, was on the field before practice catching passes from a Jugs machine with a brace around his left leg. 
 Cornerback Myles Bryant left practice early with a member of the team's medical staff. 
 The Browns signed defensive tackle Travis Bell , who most recently played in the UFL, and waived running back T.J. Harden . 
 
 
 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 

 It was an opportunistic afternoon for the Browns' defense, which intercepted five passes on the fourth day of practice.

 Three of those picks were thrown by Deshaun Watson , who now has six interceptions in four practices, with  Christopher Edmonds  getting two and safety Donovan McMillon getting another. Rookie safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren made a strong play on the first interception, dislodging a ball from tight end Jack Stoll that Edmonds caught off the ricochet.

 Shedeur Sanders  was also intercepted for the first time in training camp, as he underthrew a deep pass to wide receiver Jerry Jeudy and was picked off by cornerback D'Angelo Ross .

 Dillon Gabriel was also intercepted by linebacker Reid Carrico in a red zone drill.

 The three quarterbacks, though, had success in the red zone drills, with each throwing multiple short touchdown passes.

 "It's multiple -- they're doing all types of different stuff, showing us different things," Watson said of Cleveland's defense before practice. "It's really good, especially for the quarterbacks, running backs and O-line, just protectionwise. They're showing us different things every time, and each group is getting different looks."

title: 2026 Dallas Cowboys training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Cowboys training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Dallas Cowboys ' camp is taking place in Oxnard, California, and Cowboys reporter Todd Archer has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at the Cowboys' camp. We will update this file often. Will Dallas turn around the NFL's worst defense from 2025? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Cowboys camp 
 
 Cowboys' Dak Prescott not shying away from setting lofty goals 
 Jones optimistic about Cowboys, likes 'what we put together' 
 Source: Ex-Cowboys QB Will Grier returns as offensive assistant 
 Quieter offseason has Cowboys focused on the right things 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 A year ago at this time, the Cowboys were learning about how  Javonte Williams  fit into their run game. They found out what he did well, as he rushed for 1,201 yards in 2025. Then they rewarded him with a three-year, $24 million contract in the offseason.

 As Williams enters his second season with the Cowboys, offensive coordinator Klayton Adams is looking to expand the list of what Williams does best.

 "Obviously the guy's pretty good on direct runs and he's hard to get down behind the line of scrimmage, but I think that he is a more diverse runner than he probably gets credit for," Adams said. "I think the guy does a really nice job with some of the outside zone stuff, particularly the weak side.

 "He's got really quick feet. He's able to get in and out of cuts really well. And he's one of those dudes that's not scared to run through the smoke, and that's what you're going to have to do on some of the time. I think he's good at a lot of things."

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Sometimes coaches can be inventive when it comes to putting players through drills. On Tuesday, wide receivers coach Junior Adams had CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens catching passes off the Jugs machine during a special teams portion of practice while wearing what looked like a mosquito net or beekeeper's hat.

 The goal is to limit the receiver's vision and force him to concentrate longer on the catch. Lamb dropped one pass but figured it out. The first pass went through Pickens' hands, and he was finished.

 Longtime tight ends coach Mike Pope, who had a stint with the Cowboys, said he had 478 different drills for his tight ends. He would throw ice water at shirtless players while wearing a helmet. He had them wear swim goggles to limit their peripheral vision.

 Let's see if Adams has more tricks in his bag.

 More observations: 

 
 Defensive end  Donovan Ezeiruaku was tossed from practice for fighting. Brian Schottenheimer abhors fighting in practice because if a player throws a punch in a game, he gets ejected. A lesson to be learned for Ezeiruaku. 
 With linebacker  DeMarvion Overshown battling a sore leg (a source said it was nothing to do with his surgically repaired knee), rookie Jaishawn Barham worked with the first-team defense next to Dee Winters . 
 Quarterback  Dak Prescott went 13-of-17 in team drills and would have been better if not for drops by Lamb and tight end  Jake Ferguson . He tried to stretch the field once with a throwback down the field to Pickens, who drew a flag on cornerback  Shavon Revel  at the goal line for pass interference. 
 Ferguson had two excellent catches, however, adjusting on a slightly underthrown seam ball from Prescott and later securing a lower pass with one hand before getting it under control. 
 Cornerback  Cobie Durant came up with the defensive play of the day, knocking away a deep ball from Prescott to wideout  Marquez Valdes-Scantling . Safety Alijah Clark was tangled up on the play and limped off to the medical tent and did not return. 
 

 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 No, there is not going to be a playcaller controversy when it comes to the Cowboys this season, but coach Brian Schottenheimer gave the controls to coordinator Klayton Adams for two periods in Monday's practice, including red zone work.

 The result? Four touchdowns in a six-play span, including one to Ryan Flournoy where the receiver wrestled the ball away from cornerback  DaRon Bland for the score from Dak Prescott .

 "[Bland] actually guarded it great," Flournoy said. "I just had to win on that. I dropped slant before that so I had to make it up. Yeah, definitely great defense by DB. I just had to show strong hands."

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Second-year CB Shavon Revel Jr.  had a solid day, breaking up Prescott throws to CeeDee Lamb  and Flournoy, and blanketing George Pickens on a fade in the end zone. He had a pass interference penalty, reaching too early on a throw to Pickens, but it might have been the best practice Revel has had. 
 CB Cobie Durant picked off Prescott, undercutting a throw to Lamb near the goal line in which he dropped off another receiver and came up with the interception. 
 TE Jake Ferguson was back at practice after missing Saturday for personal reasons. He displayed strong hands on a TD catch in the back of the end zone while being covered by S Markquese Bell . 
 NFL officials were on hand for practice, but backup QB Joe Milton III took it into his own hands when an official did not throw a flag on rookie CB Devin Moore on a contested throw to Lamb in the end zone. The pass came on the defensive sideline, so perhaps there was some influence there, but Moore was aggressive on the play in a good way. 
 Prescott was 12-of-21 in team drills Monday after starting 3-of-7 with the Durant pick. 
 TE Princeton Fant left practice early after colliding with RB Israel Abanikanda . 
 

 
 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 The red zone is an area the Cowboys want to see a lot of offensive improvement in in 2026, and Saturday's practice had plenty of work from inside the 20.

 Dak Prescott had touchdown passes to CeeDee Lamb on the post, two to Ryan Flournoy (dig, slot fade) and a bullet of a throw low to the outside that receiver  George Pickens  corralled for the score.

 There was one interception when a Prescott checkdown was tipped by running back  Jaydon Blue into the arms of safety  Malik Hooker .

 Prescott finished the day unofficially 11-of-18 in team drills.

 Last year, the Cowboys converted a touchdown on 37-of-65 red zone drives. So, what makes a good red zone offense?

 "Finishing in the end zone, executing when you need to, third downs, sometimes on first (down)," Lamb said. "Just being able to not really bat ourselves in the foot, those self-inflicted wounds or penalties that'll really bring us back or kill our momentum. And again, finishing in the end zone."

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 It's hard not to notice rookie linebacker  Jaishawn Barham . He is seeing some work with the first-team defense so far. He is active in the run game, filling holes, but he also showed good feel for zone work, knocking down a Prescott pass near the goal line. 
 With Jalen Thompson (hip flexor) and P.J. Locke (knee) not practicing, safeties Alijah Clark and Markquese Bell shared the work with the first-team defense. 
 The catch of the day belonged to undrafted rookie Camden Brown on a fade from Sam Howell . The pass to the back pylon was in a perfect spot and Brown controlled the ball as he was going to the ground. 
 Brandon Aubrey went 5-for-6 on field goal attempts, missing wide right from 44 yards. 
 T.J. Bass has yet to play center in a game in his career, but he is currently the backup to Cooper Beebe . So far, no off-kilter shotgun snaps. Bass' versatility is a plus for the…

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Denver Broncos camp is taking place in Englewood, Colorado, and Broncos reporter Jeff Legwold has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Broncos camp. We will update this file often as we track the Broncos' push toward getting to the Super Bowl after falling one game short last season. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Broncos camp 
 
 Payton to talk to Taysom Hill about interest in Broncos 
 Broncos QB Bo Nix won't be afraid to run on repaired ankle 
 How will Broncos' Sean Payton adjust to not calling plays? 
 Cooper practices Wednesday despite legal troubles 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle left Wednesday's practice and did not return. The Broncos' main offseason addition slowed down during a play in a team period and walked off to the locker room. He did not return to practice. Coach Sean Payton said after the workout that Waddle would be "fine" after the initial exam by the team's medical staff. "But we'll evaluate him ... he had some muscle tightness," he added.

 Payton has said repeatedly "we'll be smart" about returning players to practice after injuries. With the Broncos still nine days away from their preseason opener, Waddle could be held out of some practice time in the remainder of the week. Courtland Sutton was also given his second consecutive off day, so Marvin Mims Jr ., Troy Franklin and Pat Bryant got the bulk of the work with the starters after Waddle left the field. Payton said Sutton would practice Thursday.

 More observations: 

 
 Franklin and Bryant each had explosive plays in team drills Wednesday and Franklin might have had his best day of camp overall. The receiver combination of Sutton, Waddle, Mims, Franklin and Bryant -- if healthy -- looks like it will be the top five, so the Broncos would have to keep six receivers for another wideout to make the 53-player roster at the end of the preseason. 
 The Broncos again showed their cornerback depth, as Kris Abrams-Draine intercepted Bo Nix in an 11-on-11 period. 
 Sam Ehlinger took snaps with the second-team offense during multiple practice periods Wednesday and continues to push Jarrett Stidham for the backup quarterback job. Ehlinger re-signed with the Broncos this offseason after spending 2025 on the practice squad. He turned down multiple chances to sign with a team with an active roster spot a year ago. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 Edge rusher Nik Bonitto limped off the practice field Tuesday after he suffered what appeared to be a lower left leg injury in a 9-on-7 run-game drill. Bonitto left the field with a trainer as well as one of the team doctors and did not return. After practice, Broncos coach Sean Payton would say only "he'll be fine, no updates."

 

 Bonitto has led the team in sacks in each of the past two seasons -- 13.5 in 2024 and 14.0 in 2025 - helping the Broncos lead the league and establish single-season franchise records in each campaign. Jonah Elliss and Jonathon Cooper took most of the snaps with the starters at the edge spots after Bonitto left practice, with second-year man Que Robinson getting more work throughout the day as well.

 It was the second consecutive day the Broncos had a starter leave practice. Center Luke Wattenberg , who dealt with a shoulder injury last season, left Monday's practice and did not practice Tuesday.

 More observations: 

 
 Add Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle to the list of those who have noticed Marvin Mims Jr .'s work this training camp. Mims made another leaping grab Tuesday -- this time in one-on-ones -- and Waddle was quick to praise it all after practice. "Man, Marv -- I'm a big fan of Marvin Mims, I'm not going to lie. He's very explosive, I love watching him work, love being in meetings (with him), picking his brain. Marvin's a big play always ready to happen, you've got to respect that kind of speed." 
 Wide receiver Courtland Sutton was held out of practice Tuesday for rest, as Payton had said this week he would begin to give some of the veteran players scheduled days off. Sutton was the first, but Payton said he has a group of players who have been scheduled for days off in the weeks to come. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton lamented with a laugh about how fans "certainly only cheer for one side of the ball" when watching the team's practices. But on Monday, cornerback Riley Moss made the kind of defensive play that gets folks on their feet.

 During team drills, Moss jumped alongside wide receiver Courtland Sutton on a deep throw from Bo Nix up the left sideline and snatched the ball away from Sutton as the two hit the ground. Few players in the league get tested more in practice and in games than Moss given that he plays across from four-time Pro Bowl selection Pat Surtain II -- the league's Defensive Player of the Year in 2023. But Sean Payton said Moss' play Monday is indicative to the kind of camp Moss is having as the corner enters the last year of his rookie deal.

 "Man he competes his tail off, I love that about him," Payton said. " ... He's moving around well right now."

 Moss continues to play at a high-enough level to continue to hold off Jahdae Barron  -- Denver's first-round pick in 2025. Safety Talanoa Hufanga said Monday that Moss is "one of the most athletic corners I've ever been around."

 More observations: 

 
 Considering that he was the 20th pick of the 2025 draft, Barron's progress is often a topic of queries pointed at Payton. The Broncos continue to carve out snaps for the second-year defensive back, even as Moss continues to improve. Barron is currently lining up at outside corner in some sets, as the nickel in others and plays at linebacker in the dime. If the Broncos do not re-sign Moss to the market-value deal he might command next offseason, Barron is poised to be next in line. 
 On a team with few roster spots available and almost no traditional camp battles for starting jobs, Sam Ehlinger continues to push Jarrett Stidham to be the team's No. 2 quarterback. Ehlinger has consistently moved the offense via limited snaps in team drills in and while Stidham continues to get most of the work with the second-team offense behind Nix, Ehlinger's work in the preseason and the practices to come will bear watching. 
 Center Luke Wattenberg walked off the field after being knocked down in one-on-one drills and did not return. After practice Payton said Wattenberg "should be fine," but Wattenberg did miss time last season with a shoulder injury. 
 
 
 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 After the Broncos tinkered with the idea this offseason to move Jonah Elliss from outside linebacker to inside linebacker, the first three days of training camp have reaffirmed the decision to leave Elliss right where he is as part of the team's pass rush.

 No matter the future of Jonathon Cooper , who was arrested twice on domestic violence charges this offseason, Elliss is expected to push for more playing time. He has been consistently impactful in practices. And coach Sean Payton has said he is glad they didn't move Elliss inside.

 "For me, it felt like man, we're taking a position that's harder to find and moving him to a position that we think might be a little bit easier to replace," Payton said. " ... I just think we felt like man, he's really ascending as an edge player."

 Elliss continues to push for more than 318 snaps he played on defense last season.

title: 2026 Detroit Lions training camp: Latest intel, updates

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action.  Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Lions camp 
 
 Ex-All Pro LB Devin White joins Lions on 1-year deal 
 Campbell: Robinson deal won't 'hurt' contract talks with Gibbs 
 Campbell: CB Arnold's release 'unfortunate' but for the best 
 
 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 The Lions held a 2 ½-hour practice session in humid conditions. All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell wasn't pleased with the performance of the defense during red-zone drills and was brutally honest in his assessment. He also took accountability for his "fair share of mess ups" as they're looking to improve to reach their standard ahead of Week 1.

 "Not very good. I'll be completely honest with you," Campbell said. "What caused it? I feel like there's obviously communication and technique. It's really simple. Like football is simple, but it's hard to do. It's easy to talk about and hard to do."

 Campbell feels they will continue to get better.

 More conversation:  

 
 Running back  Jahmyr Gibbs returned to practice, taking part in the walkthrough portion and stretches for the first time all training camp, before working on the side with a team trainer. However, he didn't participate in any individual drills during the session as he seeks a new deal. A crowd of media members swarmed Gibbs as he strolled off the practice field to enter the locker room after signing autographs, but he carefully avoided reporters and flashed a thumbs-up sign to the group after being asked if he was close to reaching a contract extension soon. 
 CB De'Shawn Rucker (ankle) and DT Mekhi Wingo (groin) left practice early to be evaluated for potential injuries. Several other players were limited due to cramping from the heat on a humid day. 
 The Lions placed TE Miles Kitselman on reserve/injured and signed WR Tarik Black . 
 

 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Tuesday marked Day 2 of padded practices and veteran LB Devin White continued to get acclimated to the defense alongside guys like All-Pro Jack Campbell . White was signed as a free agent on Aug. 1 to add depth after rookie linebacker  Jimmy Rolder went down with a hamstring injury earlier in camp. He has received limited reps in practices so far but has been doing additional conditioning drills on the side with trainers to keep in shape. "Right now, they've got a plan for me and I'm trusting in the plan," White said. "So, whenever they're ready for me to stop doing reps on the side, running and getting more reps in the team period, I'm going to be ready for it."

 More observations: 

 
 Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs missed his sixth straight practice as his hold-in for a contract extension continues but was on the field watching. Ahead of Tuesday's practice, the Atlanta Falcons reached a record-setting three-year extension with RB Bijan Robinson worth up to $75 million, which now likely sets the stage for Gibbs to reach an extension soon. Campbell feels it's "certainly not gonna hurt" with the process of negotiating. "It's not gonna hurt. But we'll see. Look, I'm anxious to get Gibbs back out there," Campbell said. "Every day that goes by, that's another day that you feel like you miss with him and getting him out there with the guys and him doing his part. But there again, it'll get done when it gets done." 
 LB Malcolm Rodriguez left practice early to be evaluated for an ankle injury. 
 The Lions have placed TE Anthony Firkser on injured reserve list and signed TE Zach Horton . Firkser will miss time with a fractured fibula after being carted off the field in practice on Monday. 
 Lions RB Sione Vaki missed Tuesday's practice after getting poked in the eye and suffering a broken nose during a freak accident at practice Monday, according to Campbell. Vaki will also miss time. "We think he'll be OK," Campbell said. "He's just gonna need a minute here. It's just one of those freak things. Somehow a hand gets through the face mask. It was unbelievable."﻿ 
 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 The Lions started padded practices on Monday for the first time in training camp. Head coach Dan Campbell anticipated the intensity increasing with pads on. That sentiment proved correct as players showed more aggression in training for Day 5.

 "I told the players last night that by the end of this week, this roster will begin to separate itself," Campbell said. "This is where we'll find out. We're about to get four really, really good days of pads, and this is Day 1 just to kind of break them in for the other three."

 More observations: 

 
 Star running back Jahmyr Gibbs missed his fifth consecutive practice as his hold-in continues while looking to reach a new deal. However, he was spotted roaming the sidelines for the second straight day, chatting with teammates  Amon-Ra St. Brown , Jameson Williams and Jared Goff on the sidelines. "I think it's good to see. He got a little work inside and to be able to come out and be around the guys, I think that's always gonna be important," Campbell said of Gibbs. "Look, he's still part of us and our players love him. We love him and he's a part of what we do, so it's always good to see him." 
 Injured Lions safeties Kerby Joseph (knee) and Brian Branch (Achilles) were both spotted doing individual rehab/conditioning drills on the side with trainers during practice. 
 Lions rookie LB Jimmy Rolder (hamstring) will be "out for a while," but Campbell says it's not a season-ending injury. 
 Lions rookie edge Derrick Moore is expected to miss 7-10 days with a "minor strain" in his groin. 
 The Lions signed TE Nick Muse and released WR Tarik Black . 
 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 2 
 The Lions signed free agent linebacker  Devin White to add depth after rookie Jimmy Rolder exited Friday's practice early with a leg injury. Rolder, a fourth-round selection out of Michigan, was off to promising start but could miss some time. Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard still feels Rolder will "absolutely" contribute this season, but the defense could also benefit from White's veteran presence.

 "The urgency's real this year. It's not just lip service," Sheppard said ahead of Sunday's practice. "And, that's what we did. The front office and Dan do a great job going out and it's nonstop. It's always evolving. How can we get better? How can we improve?

 "And like I said, it's not just, 'Oh, go out and get this flash guy.' No. How can we improve the competitive depth situation right now as far as training camp is concerned? And, Devin definitely does that with his championship pedigree."

 

 More observations: 

 
 DT Alim McNeill returned to practice after leaving early on Friday to be evaluated for a neck injury. 
 TE Miles Kitselman (leg) and DE Derrick Moore (groin) left practice to be evaluated for their injuries. 
 RB Jahmyr Gibbs missed his fourth consecutive practice as he awaits a new deal but was spotted outside with the team for the first time since camp started. Lions WR Jameson Williams described Gibbs as "the best of the best" following practice as they were spotted communicating in between on-field drills. Williams feels Gibbs should be the NFL's highest-paid running back. "I wouldn't even say look at the stats, look at the film," Williams…
