title: 2026 Green Bay Packers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Packers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Green Bay Packers ' camp is taking place in Green Bay, Wisconsin, and Packers reporter Rob Demovsky has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Packers camp. We will update this file often. Will the revamped WR corps help QB Jordan Love and the offense take another step? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news out of Packers' camp 
 
 Micah Parsons: Playing vs. Cowboys in Week 6 'realistic' 
 Packers RT changes last name to Bako-Bewele to honor heritage 
 Packers star TE Tucker Kraft activated off PUP after ACL recovery 
 Better, worse or the same: Packers defense 
 Packers CEO: Team needs financial bump to stay competitive 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 While much has been made about rookie kicker Trey Smack 's early struggles in training camp (see Monday's camp report), special teams coordinator Cam Achord explained why those practice kicks are only a small part of the evaluation.

 
Some of that has to do with the wind. Smack kicked in one especially windy day on Ray Nitschke Field, and Achord -- who is new to town -- was surprised at the difference in the wind on the practice field compared to inside Lambeau Field.

 
"We go in there and it's like, wow, you don't feel anything," Achord said. "So I don't put as much stock on the practice stuff as I will in the stadium stuff."

 
Lambeau Field has tricky winds of its own, but Achord said he believes gusts of 25 miles per hour outside "really feels like a light breeze almost inside. Whereas at practice you're out there and you're looking at the flags and it's moving. You're like, whoa, it's a tough day to kick."

 
Add into the mix that regular long snapper Matt Orzech has been unavailable because of a calf injury and holder Daniel Whelan is getting used to putting the ball down the way Smack likes it, which coach Matt LaFleur said is different than how previous kicker Brandon McManus wanted it held.

 
Achord was asked to explain the nuances of holding and didn't just explain it, he demonstrated it in the Packers' media auditorium. That demonstration can be seen here:

 

 Achord, defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon and offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich spoke to reporters on Wednesday, when the players were off.

 More observations: 

 
 Achord might be the only Packers coach ever to wear cleats to practice. He said he started wearing them in 2018, when he joined the Patriots' staff because he likes to get hands on with his players: "I got tired of getting thrown on the ground doing gunner releases with Matt Slater," he said. " Justin Bethel broke my nose. ... I'm 165 pounds and they're athletes, and I tell them like, quit pulling me like you're gonna pull a coach. I was like, pull me like you're gonna pull the freaking vise, yank. So they started yanking and broke my nose, fell down. So after that, I started wearing cleats just for better grip." 
 LaFleur has rarely played veteran starters during the preseason but with a new defensive coordinator in Gannon, might LaFleur want his players to get some exhibition game reps? Said Gannon: "I'll probably punt that one to Matt what we're going to do. How do I say this the right way to you guys? I think that our players have earned the right to play our stuff and get really good at it and go play." 
 Gannon on his plans for Micah Parsons when he returns from his ACL rehab: "We were talking the other day, he could see himself in a bunch of different spots in different calls, so that's kinda cool. Then it will be our job to make sure he gets his touches, which he will." 
 Six practices in, and MarShawn Lloyd is still healthy. That's an accomplishment for the third-year pro, who has played in exactly one NFL game and missed all of last season after getting injured on the first day of padded practices last summer. Asked whether his confidence in Lloyd has grown, offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said: "Every day he's out there and doing it, I have a little bit more. ... But I think this preseason's going to be a huge telling point of what we can do with him this year." 
 The Packers have a closed (to the public) practice Thursday and then hold their annual Family Night on Friday at Lambeau Field, where they will practice in front of a full stadium of fans. 
 

 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 If there were any questions about how new defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon plans to come up with a pass rush until Micah Parsons returns from his torn left  ACL, the first six training camp practices have offered a glimpse.

 
It's been blitz, blitz, blitz.

 
"Linebackers, safeties, corners, nickels," cornerback Benjamin St-Juste said. "Pretty much everybody."

 
St-Juste, who has been working mostly with the No. 2 defense, had what would have been a sack if tackling was allowed. He also had one on Monday. So did rookie cornerback Brandon Cisse , who has been working with the No. 1 defense. Another cornerback, Jaylin Simpson , had a QB pressure during Tuesday's practice.

 
"Feel like Micah Parsons a little bit," Simpson said.

 
It's not just the corners. Safety  Evan Williams got into the act with a sack of Jordan Love and a pressure to force an incompletion, while safety  Kitan Oladapo got home and forced a scramble. Linebacker Edgerrin Cooper has also been a regular blitzer.

 
Gannon was not blitz heavy as coach of the Cardinals the past three seasons. They ranked 19th, 17th and 32nd in the NFL in blitz rate. Before that, as the Eagles' defensive coordinator, Gannon's units ranked 22nd and 30th in blitz percentage. But he might have to be now -- at least until Parsons is available.

 
"He's got the personnel here to do it," St-Juste said."

 More observations: 

 
 It was the first day for one-on-one pass block/pass rush drills, and in the featured matchup, new left tackle Jordan Morgan blocked Lukas Van Ness on three straight reps. Van Ness tried a power rush, a speed rush and an inside move, and Morgan turned away all three. Morgan, however, did lose a rep against Barryn Sorrell . 
 Speaking of Sorrell, the second-year edge had perhaps his best day. He not only went 2-0 in the one-on-one drill, but he had a pick-six of Love on a backside screen for Josh Jacobs . Sorrell perfectly timed the play, and plucked Love's pass out of the air. "They ran a play like two plays later, and I was out there and I told Josh, 'Not again. Not again,'" Sorrell said. "Then next thing you know, it happened." 
 No wonder defensive tackle Anthony Campbell is so good at batting down passes (see Sunday's and Monday's camp reports). He won all four of his reps in the one-on-one pass rushing drill Tuesday. 
 Short on tight ends because of injuries, the Packers signed two of them: McCallan Castles and Drew Biber . They have been without Luke Musgrave (neck), Luke Lachey (foot) and RJ Maryland (hamstring) plus Tucker Kraft (ACL recovery) has been limited to individual drills only. The Packers then waived/injured Lachey and Maryland. Without Musgrave and Kraft, Josh Whyle , who had five catches in eight games last season, has worked as the No. 1 tight end. 
 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 

 Patience may be the operative word when it comes to kicker Trey Smack . The rookie had another uneven day on Monday, the first practice in full pads and the second in which the Packers kicked field goals during live periods.

 After going 3-for-5 in windy conditions on Sunday, Smack had a 5-for-8 day in slightly calmer…

title: Texans' Ryans uses Artemis II space launch to set expectations
summary: Houston's coach used NASA's trip around the moon as inspiration to rally his team.
full_text:
HOUSTON -- Before training camp began, DeMeco Ryans set the tone for his team with a different approach.

 The Houston Texans  coach delivered a speech with a picture of Artemis II towering over him in bold letters. The names from NASA's crew of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover (pilot), Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen sat beneath Ryans as he talked about the launch on April 1 and flight around the moon, marking the first time since Apollo 17 in 1972.

 Ryans used the 10-day mission to fly around the moon before returning safely to Earth as an example of how the crew "went further" than anyone else. But he also highlighted how they laid the groundwork for years to make that moment possible.

 He compared the takeoff to what Houston could do this upcoming season. How this team could reach heights that it never has. Not only reaching the AFC Championship Game for the first time in franchise history, but winning the Super Bowl. 

 

 "The preparation that it took for Artemis II to launch, it took three years for that mission to take place, and that's the beauty of it," Ryans said. 

 Owner Cal McNair has been on record saying Houston wants to play "in the very last game," and All-Pro defensive end  Will Anderson Jr . called the Texans a "Super Bowl team" this offseason.

 "When you guys asked me about expectations, the only thing I know is high expectations," Ryans said. "That's why we do what we do to achieve the ultimate goal."

 But with the Texans' lofty goals comes the mentality of daily submission to the process.

 "The expectation is to take it one day at a time, one play at a time," quarterback C.J. Stroud said. "And then see where we are at the end of camp."

 The roster has the necessary pieces on both sides of the ball to reach the heights the franchise has failed to capture in years prior.

 Houston has a capable quarterback who has played at a Pro Bowl level at times. The running game has a lead back in David Montgomery , a more physical offensive line with the addition of first-round pick Keylan Rutledge  (center), offensive tackle Braden Smith and former All-Pro guard Wyatt Teller . Wideout Nico Collins is a multiple time Pro Bowler.

 

 The defense is highly decorated with three All-Pros in cornerback Derek Stingley Jr ., Danielle Hunter  and Anderson. There are three other Pro Bowlers in linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair , cornerback Kamari Lassiter and safety Calen Bullock . Each level has difference-makers, which helped them allow the fewest yards (277.2 per game) and second-fewest points (17.4) in the NFL last season.

 But the coaches and players have left those achievements in the past, shifting their focus toward a Super Bowl while putting a massive emphasis on the daily process.

 "You just have to realize that it's a marathon," Lassiter said. "It's a long season. Training camp is the beginning, but every day you want to get better. If we have a common goal, and we're all trying to reach that goal, you take each and every day with a sense of gratitude and you attack it like you don't have the next one."

 The push for goals never met is what's fueling this season, but they won't rush through the importance of the process.

 "You want to do things, you want to go places you've never been before, there's a lot of preparation in the background to prepare to launch," Ryans said. "We don't launch tomorrow. You don't just get there just by talking about it. You got to put the work in, and that's the main message."

title: 2026 Houston Texans training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Houston Texans training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Houston Texans ' camp is taking place in Houston at at NRG Park., and Texans reporter D.J. Bien-Aime has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Texans camp 
 
 Tank Dell returns to practice for first time since 2024 
 Houston bringing back former No. 1 pick Clowney 
 Texans have 'productive' contract talks with Stroud 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 Wideout Tank Dell made his return to the practice field, participating in limited capacity. It marked the first time he engaged in any sort of team padded practice since Week 16 of 2024 after the 2023 third-round pick suffered multiple torn ligaments and a dislocated kneecap against the Chiefs.

 He caught a few passes from quarterback C.J. Stroud during individual drills and ran full speed routes.

 Dell didn't do much more after that, but this is the step in the right direction. Coach DeMeco Ryans won't rush Dell back and said "Tank is on the right plan." The goal is have him ready for team 11-on-11 contact reps. He still has a ways to go, but this is positive progress.

 Other observation:  

 Wideout Jayden Higgins continue to flash throughout practice. He made another impressive catch with Derek Stingley Jr . in coverage. It was a tightly contested catch but that's always a positive because it's against an All-Pro corner.

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 Texans wideout Jayden Higgins is starting to blossom as he's entering Year 2. When Pro Bowl wideout Nico Collins  was asked about Higgins' progression he said "He's hooping right now, and I can't wait to see him rock out when it really matters."

 During Tuesday's practice, Higgins made multiple catches with All-Pro cornerback  Derek Stingley Jr . in coverage. One of those receptions occurred during a team third-down period for a 20-yard gain. The other one was during 1-on-1s -- where Stingley tried to aggressively jam Higgins, but he avoided the powerful jab and broke free for an easy toss from quarterback C.J. Stroud .

 Early in camp, Stroud said he expected Higgins to have a "dominant" Year 2, and so far we are starting to see it.

 Other observation:  

 Linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair was slow to get up after a collision with tight end Dalton Schultz . Al-Shaair was fine shortly after.

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 

 This was Day 1 of padded practices, and the defense shined. Quarterback C.J. Stroud  was forced to hold the ball longer than he would like as the secondary coverage was stout.

 Stroud occasionally scrambled more than usual to buy time to make throws and the defensive line forced a few sacks. Safety Calen Bullock intercepted Stroud.

 Also coach DeMeco Ryans used exotic blitzes throughout the day, and the offense sometimes had answers and other times didn't. Ryans deemed the first day in full pads as "successful." 

 Other observation: 

 First-round pick Keylan Rutledge is adding an extra juice of aggression to the unit. He got into a mini tussle with defensive end Danielle Hunter after a successful run play by running back Woody Marks .

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Saturday's padless practice featured more back and forth from the offense and defense. Some periods the defense dominated and others, the offense was able to counter their blitzing.

 The Texans start padded practices on Monday and that will be a "big part" of the evaluation process for the team according to coach DeMeco Ryans.

 The fourth-year head coach said: "There's a lot of all-stars in shorts," and later added the staff wouldn't be fooled by what players have done without pads.

 Another observation: 

 
 Cornerback Derek Stingley Jr collided with linebacker Henry To'oTo'o and was slow to get up, but he shook it off and was back on the field. 
 

 

 Friday, July 31 
 It was mainly walk-throughs for the Texans. It's a theme that's been consistent for coach DeMeco Ryans throughout the offseason -- where he has focused on helping his team mentally work toward executing deep in the playoffs.

 "I've grown as a head coach," Ryans said in June. "For me, it's more so now about how much smarter can we play as a team. How can we be more elite on our execution? Our communication, can it be louder? Can we echo it more? Can we truly be tied together every time we line up? That's what I've seen when I talk about the process of us this year being better."

 Saturday's practice will be the first day with fans in attendance since training camp has opened. That will be a longer practice with more intensity compared to today's practice that was roughly a little over an hour.

 

 

 Thursday, July 30 
 The passing attack was centered around the quick game time to throw on Day 2 of practice. Quarterback C.J. Stroud was quick and decisive with his throws with all but one of his throws being made under 2.8 seconds, and his only rep over three seconds was when he extended the play and tried to find wideout Jayden Higgins in the back of the end zone.

 It fell incomplete, but the majority of his throws came with precision and decisiveness. Stroud was able to connect a few times with Higgins, who's development in Year 2 will be huge for the offense.

 Other observation:  

 
 Backup cornerback Alijah Huzzie was able to make a nice interception off of backup QB  Davis Mills  -- where took the ball away from the intended receiver. 
 
 
 Wednesday, July 29 
 The Texans were more forthcoming regarding contract discussions than normal. General manager Nick Caserio said there's a "possibility" the team and quarterback C.J. Stroud can reach a contract extension. Stroud isn't focused much on contract discussions; he's letting his agent handle it as he is "keeping the main thing the main thing."

 Stroud is going into Year 4 and is eligible for an extension for the first time in his career. Coach DeMeco Ryans said he doesn't get into a lot of deep discussions with guys when it comes to contract situations.

 But he added, "I truly believe you get the contract by what you do on the field. It doesn't matter what you say, what I say. It's about how you perform on the field, and if you're worthy of getting a contract and you deserve it, it'll happen for you."

 Other observation: 

 
 CB Kamari Lassiter intercepted Stroud with a diving catch and then punted the ball in celebration. That was the most exciting play on a relatively quiet morning.

title: Can Colts recapture '25 magic? Taylor deal reflects optimism
summary: The Colts believe they can recapture their early-season success from 2025, but they couldn't do it without Jonathan Taylor.
full_text:
WESTFIELD, Ind. -- If you want to know about an NFL team's priorities, it can be instructive to simply examine where it spends its money.

 For the Indianapolis Colts , their 2026 offseason spending was directed toward the pieces of their roster that represent their biggest reasons for optimism.

 In the spring, Indianapolis signed receiver and deep threat extraordinaire Alec Pierce to a four-year, $116 million deal. Days later, the Colts agreed to a new contract with rejuvenated quarterback Daniel Jones at two years for $88 million.

 And, on Thursday, the Colts locked up another critical offensive piece, with big-play running back Jonathan Taylor agreeing to terms on a two-year extension worth $44 million. The contract is the third-largest deal for a running back in NFL history.

 Their philosophy isn't difficult to decipher.

 In Weeks 1 through 10 of 2025, the Colts were 8-2 and playing at a level rarely seen even when Hall of Fame quarterback Peyton Manning starred for the team. Indianapolis led the NFL in offensive expected points added (103.8), points per game (32.1), yards per game (396.9) and yards per play (6.4) before falling off a proverbial cliff late in the season.

 

 They had seemingly perfected a formula with proven success in the NFL: Running an efficient passing game with Jones at the controls, mixing in explosive deep shots to Pierce, who led the NFL in yards per catch, then allowing Taylor to bludgeon defenders until they inevitably yielded one of his breakaway runs.

 Likewise, the Colts were running away from opponents, posting a league-high 11.5-point margin per game.

 But a seven-game losing streak to end the season represented a stunning unraveling fueled by a season-ending injury to Jones and the loss of key defensive players.

 The Colts, however, are holding out hope they can recapture who they were before that collapse. And in their estimation, they will do that by doubling down on their offensive stars.

 "What we saw in that first half is we were, in a record way, dominating offensively," principal owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon said after the season.

 That formula likely would not have worked had any of those pieces been missing. That is why, even amid a season that is seen as make-or-break for the Colts -- with coach Shane Steichen and general manager Chris Ballard considered to be on the hot seat and several veteran players facing uncertain futures -- locking up Taylor proved to be a priority.

 Without Taylor in the backfield, Jones' play-action passing would be much less potent. Without Taylor, defenses would be more comfortable dropping defenders into coverage to safeguard themselves against Pierce's speed. Without Taylor, linebackers might've been more likely to focus on rookie tight end Tyler Warren , who was dominating the middle of the field.

 So much could have been different if not for Taylor, already the second-leading rusher in Colts history behind Hall of Fame back Edgerrin James. Even in an era when running backs are often taken for granted, Taylor is the piece that made it all come together.

 

 His ability to turn 3-yard rushes into 5-yard gains, and to make mere chunk plays into game-breaking runs that broke opponents proved to be the Colts' secret sauce.

 When Taylor got bottled up on an inside run against the Atlanta Falcons last season in Week 10, then somehow bounced outside for an 83-yard touchdown, it left even his teammates in awe. The play was all Taylor.

 "He's our home run hitter," former Colts linebacker Zaire Franklin marveled afterward. "He's our knockout punch. He's the best weapon in the league."

 Taylor is among a group of backs who believe they are changing perceptions of the position as a collective afterthought. Derrick Henry , Saquon Barkley , Bijan Robinson , Jahmyr Gibbs and others are making the NFL rethink its attitudes toward running backs.

 For the Colts, there is no attitude adjustment necessary. They demonstrated Thursday just how important Taylor is to their offensive formula.

title: Colts WR Josh Downs sees opportunity approaching
summary: Downs' production took a downturn in 2025, one the Colts studied and plan to remedy.
full_text:
WESTFIELD, Ind. -- Even on a day the Indianapolis Colts amassed 519 yards of offense, ran 77 plays and played six additional minutes of overtime, you practically needed a microscope to find receiver Josh Downs in the final box score.

 There was no greater example of the limited opportunities that came Downs' way in 2025 than the Colts' November win over the Atlanta Falcons .

 Downs had two pass targets from quarterback Daniel Jones , finishing with one reception for 3 yards. For further perspective, consider that Downs had more punt-return opportunities in the game (three) than he did pass-catching chances.

 "Last year we had a kind of a packed room with a lot of good receivers in there," Downs said on another day in which he established himself as one of the stars of the Colts' ongoing training camp. "... But it teaches you patience, teaches you to just be grateful for what you get. And I just keep working. I was still doing all the stuff I was doing the years before. Just got to just keep going, keep your head down and stay on the grind."

 But the 2026 season should not test Downs' patience in a similar fashion. The time for patience has passed.

 This is Downs' moment.

 "I'm trying to show I'm a really good receiver," Downs said.

 He averaged 787 receiving yards and 103 targets in his first two seasons (2023-2024) and seemed to be an ascending player. But myriad factors impacted Downs' usage last season, when he had a career-low 566 yards on 58 receptions: The emergence of rookie tight end Tyler Warren , the role of now-departed receiver Michael Pittman Jr ., and the downfield feats of Alec Pierce , who led the NFL in yards per catch, all played a role.

 Downs was relegated to a garden-variety slot receiver in an offense that otherwise was employing an aggressive passing game. Accordingly, his per-catch average dropped from 11.3 yards over his first two seasons to 9.8.

 But there is an effort underway to reprioritize Downs in 2026. Some of that is happening organically; Pittman has been traded and Pierce is still rehabbing from offseason surgery. But some of it seems more deliberate, with the Colts in recent months emphasizing just how good Downs was in his first two seasons and vowing not to forget.

 "I'm a big Josh Downs fan," general manager Chris Ballard said.

 Said coach Shane Steichen: "There's guys that have got to step up, and Downs is going to be one of those guys."

 The 2026 season is going to look different in big and small ways for Downs.

 And that goes beyond just the amount of usage he's expected to see. How he's specifically used is likely to change, including where he lines up on the field. Downs has been primarily a slot receiver, but that could be less true this season. He's played 67.1% of his career snaps in the slot and just 40 of his 198 career receptions have come when he was lined up as a perimeter receiver.

 But the Colts are now more convinced he can play a bigger role on the outside, allowing them to utilize more two-receiver, two-tight end formations. Downs is much smaller than an ideal outside receiver (5-foot-9, 171 pounds), making him susceptible to press coverage. But the Colts can help him evade that by putting him in pre-snap motion or lining him up off the line of scrimmage. That's something another undersized Colts star, T.Y. Hilton , provided a blueprint for during his impressive career.

 Steichen confirmed the Colts' intent, describing Downs as "a guy that can play inside and outside now for us, and his role is going to improve this season."

 Further, the Colts believe Downs can add more explosiveness to his game. He showed an ability to stretch the field on deeper routes in his first two seasons. But those were much rarer last season. His share of receptions that netted 20 yards or more in his first two seasons was 14.3%; it dropped to 6.9% last season.

 Now, with Pierce expected to play a more varied role after being primarily a deep threat, there likely will be chances for Downs to show his downfield chops.

 The timing of all this is fortuitous for Downs. He's entering the final season of his rookie contract and is looking to get paid like the star he believes he is.

 "I feel like I'm just as good as some of the best guys in the league and I'm excited for more opportunities," he said.

 His chance to prove it is here.

title: 2026 Jacksonville Jaguars training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Jaguars training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Jacksonville Jaguars camp is taking place in Jacksonville, Florida, and Jaguars reporter Michael DiRocco has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Jaguars camp. We will update this file often. How much will we see Travis Hunter on both sides of the ball in camp? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Jaguars' camp 
 
 Jaguars' Travis Hunter feeling faster after 10-pound weight gain 
 
 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 Talks between the Jaguars and receiver  Parker Washington 's camp on a contract extension remain active, but the fourth-year player out of Penn State isn't focusing on when a deal could get done and isn't upset that an agreement hasn't yet been reached.

 "It's there and it's a conversation, but my focus is just coming out here and I need to make plays for Trevor [Lawrence]," Washington said Thursday. "So that's my mindset and that's how I'm going to attack it. I'm not going to step on my agent's toes. They can have those conversations. I'm going to come out here and do my job."

 Jaguars general manager James Gladstone said early in the offseason the team was working on extensions with Washington and tight end Brenton Strange . They reached a deal with Strange, signing him to a three-year extension worth up to $48 million in June, but have yet to finalize anything with Washington.

 Washington was asked about his reaction to the four-year, $140 million extension  with $108 million guaranteed that receiver Zay Flowers agreed to with Baltimore and said he was happy for Flowers, who was the 22nd overall pick in 2023.

 "The receiver market is a little crazy and you see guys getting their opportunities and getting paid, I mean, that's cool," said Washington, whom the Jaguars drafted in the sixth round in 2023. "But like I said, for me, I just want to go out here and be my best self and just attack it."

 

 More observations: 

 
 OL Emmanuel Pregnon was injured during 11-on-11 and received treatment off to the side. He remained at practice but did not participate in any more team work. 
 S Preston Hodge intercepted QB Joey Aguilar and LB Ventrell Miller punched the ball away from RB Ameer Abdullah and recovered the fumble in 11-on-11 work. 
 The Jaguars will have a mock game on Friday morning at the team's practice facility. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Very good day for the defense on Tuesday in the Jaguars' second day in full pads.

 Safeties Antonio Johnson and Eric Murray and cornerback Jarrian Jones intercepted passes, Jones broke up another in the end zone, and linebacker Branson Combs broke up a pass on the goal line. Cornerback Jabbar Muhammad also had tight coverage on Travis Hunter on a throw into the end zone and forced an incompletion.

 Johnson's interception came off Trevor Lawrence while Murray and Jones picked off Nick Mullens .

 More observations: 

 
 Hunter had 17 snaps (10 defense, 7 offense) in 11-on-11 work. He has totaled 86 snaps (51 defense, 35 offense) through six practices. 
 LB Jared Bartlett was taken off the field after suffering a leg injury, which leaves the team down two linebackers ( Jack Kiser suffered a right knee injury on the first day of camp). The team is also limiting  Foyesade Oluokun 's snaps in team work, so the Jaguars could be looking to add at that spot. 
 RB Chris Rodriguez Jr . did not participate in Tuesday's practice as part of the team's plan to ramp up his participation. Rodriguez, who missed almost all of the spring with a left foot injury, did participate in Monday's practice. 
 DE Arik Armstead had a veteran day off on Tuesday, his second of camp. 
 

 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Anton Harrison , who has started 48 games at right tackle since being drafted 27th overall in 2023, has spent the past three practices working at left tackle as part of the Jaguars' philosophy of cross-training offensive linemen.

 Coach Liam Coen didn't rule out that being a permanent change, though.

 "If that ends up sticking, then hopefully that's a good thing for us," Coen said after Monday's practice. "And I think he's put together five good practices so far that you're pleased with seeing the consistency."

 Monday's practice was the first in full pads and Harrison won all four of his one-on-one pass rush reps, including two against defensive end Josh Hines-Allen , the franchise's sack leader (61).

 Cole Van Lanen was the team's starting left tackle at the end of the 2025 season and the Jaguars signed him to three-year, $51 million extension in January. However, he has yet to practice because he's still recovering from a knee injury he suffered in the regular-season finale. He is expected to return at some point in camp.

 Walker Little  -- who lost the starting job at left tackle to Van Lanen last season -- had been the left tackle for the first two camp practices and is now working at right tackle.

 

 More observations: 

 
 WR Brian Thomas Jr . has followed up his impressive spring with a good start to camp. He had the play of the day on Monday with a one-handed catch down the sideline in 11-on-11. CB Montaric Brown had sticky coverage but Thomas grabbed Trevor Lawrence 's throw with his right arm while fending off Brown with his left. 
 Relatively quiet day for CB/WR Travis Hunter . He had 13 snaps in 11-on-11 (seven on defense and six on offense). He was targeted once by QB Nick Mullens , but there was a miscommunication on the route. Hunter cut the route short while Mullens threw long. 
 

 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 2 
 Travis Hunter had one of the most impressive training camp practices of his career on Sunday, making two catches on offense and intercepting a pass on defense.

 His first catch came on a deep over route on a throw from Trevor Lawrence . He had a step on cornerback Jarrian Jones when he caught the ball and accelerated down the sideline for what would have been a big gain.

 He made his second catch, also from Lawrence, over his left shoulder down the right sideline with a defensive back on his back.

 "The deep reception was awesome to see," offensive coordinator Grant Udinski said. "He's continued to progress from a route technique fundamental standpoint, but also a knowledge of the offense and just the system in general.

 "When he has the ball in his hands, he can create something special. He can make guys miss. He has a great awareness of defenders and space out there on the field, but he also has great ball skills. So those things kind of pop off the tape."

 Hunter intercepted Nick Mullens ' pass to tight end Quintin Morris , jumping in front of the throw and returning the ball for what would have been a touchdown.

 More observations from the day: 

 
 RB Chris Rodriguez Jr . participated in 11-on-11 work for the first time in camp. His snaps were limited but he did get two carries as part of a gradual ramp-up of participating that coach Liam Coen said would be the plan. Rodriguez missed the spring after undergoing surgery on his left foot. 
 WR Parker Washington had one of the plays of the day when he made a sliding catch in the end zone on a deep throw from Lawrence during an 11-on-11 move-the-ball period. 
 The Jaguars will be in full pads for the first time on Monday.

title: 2026 Kansas City Chiefs training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Chiefs training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Kansas City Chiefs ' camp is taking place at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, Missouri, and Chiefs reporter Nate Taylor has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Chiefs camp. We will update this file often. Can coach Andy Reid get the Chiefs back into the playoffs? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive into all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Chiefs camp 
 
 Rookie wideout Cyrus Allen an early star of Chiefs training camp 
 Chiefs' Reid: Eric Bieniemy's wife out of ICU, 'doing great' 
 Chiefs' Mahomes fully cleared for camp, feeling 'amazing' 
 As training camp opens, Chiefs point to brighter future in 2026 
 
 
 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 Rashee Rice , the Chiefs' No. 1 receiver, participated in 11-on-11 repetitions, a positive sign that his acclimation process is going well. In May, Rice underwent surgery on his right knee to remove loose debris that was causing inflammation. Since camp began, the Chiefs have been cautious with Rice's participation.

 Most of Rice's work was during the red zone period, where he had several short receptions, including a bubble screen on the perimeter and a touchdown in the back of the end zone. When Mahomes targeted Rice in the back corner of the end zone, Rice couldn't make a leaping, contested catch against cornerback Nohl Williams .

 It's clear Rice will need time to get into true football shape, as he showed fatigue before the long-drive drill, the final 11-on-11 repetitions. During that period, Rice was held out of the first-team offense's 12 repetitions.

 "He got a lot of good reps today, which is important," Reid said of Rice. "We've just got to ease him back in and just keep working. We know he's a good player. He actually got better as the practice went on, so that was a good thing."

 Other observations:  

 
 Linebacker Drue Tranquill missed his first practice of camp with lower back spasms. During the second half of Wednesday's work, Tranquill did some light strength work off the side with the training staff. 
 The other players who missed Wednesday's on-field session were cornerback Kristian Fulton (hip), linebacker Jeffrey Bassa (strained groin), defensive end Ashton Gillotte (strained right hamstring), defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee) and receivers Cyrus Allen (left shin) and Xavier Worthy (sprained right shoulder). 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 For the second consecutive day in pads, Kahlil Benson , the undrafted rookie right tackle from Indiana, performed well, even better than Monday, after once again receiving all of the repetitions with the first-team offense.

 In the first 11-on-11 period, Benson showed strong run-blocking skills by executing a double-team to move defensive tackle Khyiris Tonga back. The repetition finished with Benson also blocking linebacker Nick Bolton , which created more space on the right side of the field for running back Kenneth Walker III . A few minutes later, Benson blocked defensive end Felix Anudike-Uzomah in pass protection for quarterback Patrick Mahomes to connect with receiver Tyquan Thornton for a completion for more than 30 yards.

 "He's done great," Walker said of Benson. "We've got pads on now and you get to see how well he's doing out there. He's going to have a great impact on this team."

 Benson's work, on the field and in meetings, has pushed him to have true competition with Jaylon Moore , the five-year veteran, for the starting right tackle role.

 In the final 11-on-11 period, Benson didn't lose any of the five repetitions with the first-team offense. His matchups included Anudike-Uzomah, pass rusher Chris Jones and rookie defensive end R Mason Thomas .

 "We'll give you a chance here to learn, but if you start making [mistakes] consistently, then we've got a problem," Reid said Monday of Benson. "But he's been doing a good job. There's a hiccup here or there, but he fixes them normally."

 More observations: 

 
 The players who missed Tuesday's practice were cornerback Kristian Fulton (hip), defensive end Ashton Gillotte (strained right hamstring), defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee) and receivers Cyrus Allen (left shin) and Xavier Worthy (sprained right shoulder). 
 Receiver Rashee Rice (right knee) participated in 7-on-7 repetitions for the second straight day, this time catching a short pass from Mahomes against zone coverage. For the first time in camp, cornerback  L'Jarius Sneed , a six-year veteran, participated in 1-on-1 drills and 7-on-7 repetitions. 
 Joe Bleymaier said he has talked with offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy the past few days. For more than a week, Bleymaier, the pass game coordinator, has taken over Bieniemy's duties as offensive coordinator during his absence. He left the Chiefs after his wife, Mia Bieniemy, 57, was hospitalized in stable condition last week after being allegedly shot by the couple's son, Elijah Zion Bieniemy, 27, at the family's home in Virginia. "We miss EB, obviously," Bleymaier said. "It was great to hear from him, just on a personal standpoint. You're so devastated for him. He's been reaching out more and more lately with some of the football stuff, so that's kind of brought a little sense of normalcy back. As far as the [acting] offensive coordinator, calling in the plays and just making sure some of the administration stuff is handled has been the biggest thing." 
 One of Mahomes' best repetitions was during the first 11-on-11 period, when he, under center Creed Humphrey , rolled to the right on a play-action pass, completing an intermediate throw to Thornton while on the move. "We're not going to put any limitations on what Patrick can do rather than maybe emphasizing what we're going to try to do more," Bleymaier said of Mahomes, who had surgery in December to repair the torn ACL and LCL in his left knee. "We're really trying to eliminate holding him back -- or 'Let's not put him in this situation.' Everything is open. -- under center, rolling left or right, the whole playbook." 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 

 Among young players, the biggest winner from the Chiefs' first padded practice was rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods , the second of the Chiefs' first-round picks.

 In the 1-on-1 period, Woods had highlight repetitions, winning quickly in both of his matchups against backup guard Hunter Nourzad , a three-year player. When Woods went against right guard Trey Smith , a two-time Pro Bowler and a five-year veteran, the teammates split their two repetitions. The rookie used his quickness to push Smith back by gaining leverage using his right hand.

 "Peter is really talented, man, in terms of his hand utilization, speed, power," Smith said after practice. "He's really sort of the full package type of guy. He's young and he's figuring out the game, but he has a willingness to learn.

 "I've really enjoyed the way he's stepped into this program. He definitely has an outstanding future. I'm just really excited to help him in his development where I can."

 Selected with the 29th pick, which the Chiefs gained from the Los Angeles Chargers through the trade involving cornerback Trent McDuffie , Woods has been impressive in creating havoc at times for running backs by bursting through the offensive line just a second after the snap. The Chiefs are hoping Woods can be effective in 1-on-1 matchups while playing next to star pass rusher Chris Jones .

The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action.  What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Chargers camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 
 Latest from Chargers camp 
 
 Players with the most at stake during Chargers' training camp 
 Tracking 2026 NFL hold-ins: Tuipulotu 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 Outside linebacker Tuli Tuipulotu , who has been a limited participant in practice this training camp amid ongoing contract negotiations, was a full participant in Wednesday's practice. The caveat is that the practice was a walkthrough, so Tuipulotu and the other Chargers players were going at half speed. He still has yet to participate in a non-walkthrough practice 11-on-11 period, but his participation on Wednesday could be a sign that things could be headed toward a resolution.

 Other observations:  

 
 After an injury scare Tuesday scare to the same left leg in which he sustained a season-ending patellar tendon rupture last year, left tackle Rashawn Slater was a full participant in practice Wednesday without any limitations. 
 Branson Taylor and Trevor Penning rotated at left guard, continuing the five man race for this starting job. Rookie Jake Slaughter continues to play center with the second group. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 The Chargers had their first major injury scare Tuesday as left tackle Rashawn Slater appeared to sustain an injury to his left leg at practice. Slater went to the medical tent with a trainer and then did some on-field testing but didn't return to practice. Branson Taylor and Trey Pipkins III rotated at tackle in his absence.

 Slater ruptured the patella tendon in his left knee during last year's training camp, which forced him to miss the entire season. He appeared in good spirits after practice, walking around and taking pictures with his family.

 Quarterback Justin Herbert said that Slater told him he was healthy enough to return to the field.

 "He said he wanted to be out there, so I think that's okay," Herbert said.

 

 Other observations: 

 
 OLB Tuli Tuipulotu participated in one 7-on-7 rep but did not take part in the remainder of team drills, marking his sixth straight practice with limited participation as his contract situation remains unresolved. 
 Coach Jim Harbaugh said that Kayode Awosika is leading the competition to start at left guard, but added that Pipkins, Jake Slaughter and Taylor are all in the mix. Harbaugh said that he'd like to name a starter after the next ten practices. 
 The offense came out sharp, with Herbert completing his first eight passes before safety RJ Mickens broke up a pass. From there, the offense and defense traded wins throughout the rest of practice. 
 S Kendall Williamson intercepted Herbert on a pass that was intended for wide receiver Ladd McConkey . "That was nice. He snagged it," Derwin James Jr . said. 
 OLB  Nadame Tucker  had one of his best practices of camp, consistently generating pressure and recording three would-be sacks. 
 DT Teair Tart was disruptive throughout, including what likely would have been at least one sack. The Chargers' interior defensive line generated pressure throughout the day.

 Monday's practice was one of the better days for the defense, as they were constantly disruptive throughout. Undrafted cornerbacks Rodney Shelley and Avery Smith were among the stars. Smith continued his strong start to camp with another good day, as he intercepted quarterback DJ Uiagalele i and had an impressive pass breakup on a Justin Herbert pass. Shelley was sticky in coverage throughout and had a few pass breakups, celebrating after each.

 The rookies will have their first NFL training camp practice in pads on Tuesday at the University of San Diego, a chance to affirm the way they've been playing.

 

 Other observations:

 
 Edge rusher  Tuli Tuipulotu continued to not participate in team drills, continuing his limited participation as his contract situation remains unresolved. 
 Rookie Jake Slaughter and Kayode Awosika split reps at left guard as the competition for that spot continues. 
 Second-year wide receiver  KeAndre Lambert-Smith , who has been quiet so far, made one of the top highlights of the day with impressive downfield catch while cornerback Deane Leonard was draped in coverage. 
 Quentin Johnston also produced another offensive highlight, tracking a perfectly placed deep ball from Herbert over the outstretched arms of safety Derwin James Jr. along one sideline. 
 
 
 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Coach Jim Harbaugh declined to say whether outside linebacker Tuli Tuipulotu 's absence from team drills at practice is contract-related, saying only the situation is being "handled internally" and repeatedly describing Tuipulotu as "ramping up."

 Tuipulotu hasn't taken part in team drills amid contract negotiations since camp began this week, as he is heading into the final year of his rookie contract. He finished sixth in the NFL in sacks last season.

 Without Tuipulotu again Saturday, rookie Akheem Mesidor flashed, looking explosive coming off of the edge throughout practice.

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Saturday marked perhaps the highest-energy practice as the Chargers offense had its best day this week. Wide receivers Ladd McConkey and Derius Davis caught deep passes that energized the crowd at the Chargers facility. 
 Cornerback Donte Jackson was active in coverage with a couple of pass breakups, causing fans to cheer in reaction. 
 
 

 Friday, July 31 

 Friday's practice was at half-speed, walkthrough pace, but the most significant development came at left guard.  Trey Pipkins III  began with the first group blocking for quarterback Justin Herbert , the first time he's done so this week. Throughout camp and the offseason program,  Kayode Awosika , Trevor Penning  and rookie Jake Slaughter have rotated at left guard, with Awosika getting most of the reps with Herbert.

 Coach Jim Harbaugh said earlier this offseason that the race for a starter at left guard would be between these four players. This is the first time that Pipkins has gotten reps with the top group.

 Still, offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel cautioned against looking too much into the rep distribution, noting that the real evaluation will come with padded practices next week.

 "It's much different when you have 300 pounds of mass on your edge," McDaniel said, "and a subtle 6-inch step determines whether or not you can actually execute that block."

 Other observations:  

 
 Tuli Tuipulotu continued not to practice amid ongoing contract negotiations. He went through individual drills, worked off to the side with a trainer and watched practice. 
 Wide receivers Quentin Johnston and Ladd McConkey said that McDaniel has changed the way they run routes, particularly by emphasizing how quickly they finish the top of a route and locate the football. "We weren't all the way used to running routes like that," Johnston said. 
 

 
 

 Thursday, July 30 
 Tuli Tuipulotu didn't practice for the second straight day amid ongoing contract negotiations, but he did more on the field work with teammates than on the opening day of camp. On Thursday, Tuipulotu wore a helmet and jersey and went through individual drills with the team before working off to the side with a trainer. On Wednesday, he was in a…

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Los Angeles Rams  camp is taking place at Loyola Marymount University in L.A. Rams reporter Sarah Barshop has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Rams camp. We will update this file often. Can the Rams live up to the hype? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Rams camp 
 
 Myles Garrett out third straight day with soreness 
 Rams' McVay: No Aaron Donald update, but 'trending upwards' 
 Puka Nacua says it 'never crossed my mind' to not take part in camp 
 Rams unveil two new alternate uniforms for 2026 
 
 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 The Rams had a familiar face at their team facility this week, as Aaron Donald's name appeared on the NFL's transaction wire on Wednesday as a player taking part in a tryout for the team.

 The workout had to be reported to the league because it was supervised by a member of the Rams' football staff. Defensive coordinator Chris Shula said he was not at the Woodland Hills facility for the tryout, but said he talked to defensive line coach Giff Smith afterward.

 Last week, Rams head coach Sean McVay said he doesn't expect Donald to make a decision about coming out of retirement until after the team returns to its facility in Woodland Hills. The Rams' final practice at LMU is scheduled for Friday.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Defensive end Myles Garrett returned to practice on Wednesday after missing the last four practices with a little "lower body soreness." Garrett said he feels good and that the Rams were just trying to make sure he got back "100%." 
 Garrett was asked whether he feels like he can play with more "freedom" during practices in Los Angeles. He said that was a good way to describe the way the coaching staff allows players to play. "Not being punished or critiqued for trying to make a play," Garrett said. "There's guidelines and boundaries you got to stay within in the defense, but as long as we put ourselves in the right spots, they're all for it." 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 
 The Rams finished their second training camp block on Monday with what head coach Sean McVay called more of an unscripted practice. Matthew Stafford and  Stetson Bennett IV  took all of the quarterback reps for the Rams, with rookie Ty Simpson only taking part in individual drills.

 The first-team offense and the secondary exchanged several standout plays, including a pass breakup on receiver Puka Nacua by cornerback Trent McDuffie . Later, Stafford found wide receiver Davante Adams for a completion down the sideline.

 "I thought there was especially some really good back and forth with the ones," McVay said after practice. "Some really good plays on both sides, but that's what we're looking for is good quality play where you can really see guys playing through the cycle of the snap."

 McVay pointed to "some big breakups down the field" by McDuffie and cornerback Jaylen Watson .

 "Guys made plays on both sides and it felt like it was a quality operation," McVay said.

 More observations from the day: 

 
 
 McVay said he hasn't determined how he will allocate reps during the preseason between the quarterbacks other than Stafford not playing in any preseason games. Last year, Stafford and Jimmy Garoppolo sat out of the preseason while Bennett started the first two preseason games.

 
 
 Rams tight end Davis Allen is dealing with a quad injury. McVay said the Rams will give Allen "some time" before he returns to practice because it's a soft tissue injury. "You don't want to rush him back," McVay said. "He's played a lot of football and it'll give ... some of these other tight ends an opportunity to get snaps they wouldn't otherwise. But Davis is going to be a big part of what we do this year."

 
 
 Garrett (lower body soreness) did not practice for the fourth straight day. The Rams will re-evaluate him after the Tuesday off day.

 
 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 2 
 Coach Sean McVay praised quarterback  Stetson Bennett IV 's growth from last training camp, pointing out "the ownership of the offense" he has now.

 Bennett got the majority of the second-team reps last training camp while Matthew Stafford was dealing with a back injury and Jimmy Garoppolo was with the first team.

 "But then once Matthew came back, he didn't get any reps at all," McVay said. "And so for his ability to come in and to be able to run the one offense the way that he has, I've been really pleased with him."

 McVay said quarterbacks coach Dave Ragone "deserves a ton of credit" for the way he has worked with Bennett.

 "[Bennett has] played really well through the offseason program and up until now," McVay said. "And that's been a real positive for us."

 Bennett, a fourth-round pick in 2023, is competing with rookie first-round pick Ty Simpson to back up Stafford this season.

 More observations from the day: 

 
 The Rams held a jog-through on Sunday, meaning players were in T-shirts and shorts on the practice field. It was one of Stafford's scheduled days off of practice. 
 Defensive end Myles Garrett did not practice for the third straight day, as he is dealing with "a little soreness in his lower half," McVay said. The head coach said the Rams are just erring on the side of caution and that he is not concerned. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Rams running back Kyren Williams , who is entering his fifth NFL season, said he changed the way he worked out. While Williams has always prided himself on his versatility, he said he didn't do wide receiver drills this offseason. Instead, he focused on drills specific for a running back.

 "[In the past] I would work out and do a lot of receiver workouts and do a lot of different things because I want to be as versatile as I can," Williams said. "But this year I honed in on running back. I honed in on really training to be running back, training, like I said, those pad levels, those cuts. And when I am cutting, sinking my body. Because if I cut straight up, I'm not going nowhere.

 "My superpowers, when I'm low to the ground, I have both my feet in the ground and I'm playing it and I'm explosive."

 Williams said that is an area where he felt he "needed to get better at."

 "And I think it's been showing here [at] camp," Williams said.

 

 Another observation: 

 
 Myles Garrett did not practice for the second straight day. A team spokesperson said it was a scheduled rest day for the defensive end. 
 

 
 Friday, July 31 
 The Rams practiced in pads on Friday for the first time during training camp. It was a scheduled day off for quarterback Matthew Stafford , allowing for backup quarterback candidates Stetson Bennett IV and Ty Simpson to take the reps.

 Rams head coach Sean McVay said even in a padded practice, it can be tough to judge a quarterback's performance without looking at the tape because they are not being tackled. Still, McVay said, "I thought both Stetson and Ty did a nice job."

 "Stetson has really taken incredible strides, done a lot of good things, and I think Ty has improved tremendously from the spring until now as well," McVay said.

 McVay said he's seen that growth for Simpson in the way he is calling the plays in the huddle and even some things "mechanically about being able to speed up his release, some of the timing and rhythm in terms of with his lower half being married up with the routes."

 

 Other observations:

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Miami Dolphins  camp is taking place in Miami Gardens, and Dolphins reporter Marcel Louis-Jacques has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Dolphins camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Dolphins camp 
 
 Dolphins top pick Proctor embracing NFL learning curve 
 Miami, All-Pro LB Jordyn Brooks reach 3-year, $51.3M extension 
 Dolphins, Aaron Brewer reach 3-year, $52.5 million extension 
 Why Miami's rookies can thrive 
 
 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 

 Pressure, pressure and more pressure was the key word for the Dolphins in Thursday's practice. The team shed its shoulder pads, looking to ease back into work following Wednesday's off day, but it didn't stop coach Jeff Hafley's defense from attacking its offensive counterparts throughout team drills.

 Linebacker Jackson Woodard was a constant presence around the ball, while defensive end Chop Robinson continued his strong camp -- albeit against a banged up right side of the Dolphins' offensive line. Thursday also marked another strong performance from rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez ; defensive coordinator Sean Duggan said he could tell the game is starting to slow down for Rodriguez and the other rookie linebackers, Kyle Louis and Trey Moore .

 More conversations: 

 
 Running back Jaylen Wright broke of a couple strong runs during team drills. Speaking to the media earlier this week, he sounded calm and at peace with his career to date and ready to attack the best opportunity he's had for regular playing time since entering the league in 2024. 
 Linebacker Willie Gay Jr . intercepted quarterback Cam Miller and returned it for a long gain. We've seen Gay stand out at training camp before, the Dolphins are hoping his momentum carries into game day this preseason, and the regular season. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 If you were building a basketball team out of Dolphins players, defensive tackle Zach Sieler -- all 6-foot-6, 300 pounds of him -- might be a choice at power forward. But coach Jeff Hafley said the nine-year veteran is actually more of a point guard on the team's defensive line.

 Despite his 25.5 sacks over the past three seasons, Hafley said Sieler's ability and willingness to take on blockers and open rush lanes for his teammates really pops on tape.

 When asked about the comparison after Tuesday's practice, Sieler said it all comes down to being selfless and a team player.

 "You've got to be a leader, you've got to be vocal -- but you can't be selfish," he said. "The better we do as a unit, the better we'll do as a team ... If someone's making plays one day and you're not, the plays will come. Don't stress, because when you stress and try to force a play, that's when bad things happen."

 More observations: 

 
 Defensive end Chop Robinson goes through stretches where he's simply unblockable -- his speed off the line of scrimmage has given the Dolphins' offensive tackles fits all summer, and continued to do so Tuesday. Fellow defensive end Josh Uche also had a pair of sacks in team drills. 
 Right tackle Austin Jackson , tight end Greg Dulcich and safety Lonnie Johnson Jr . did not participate in Tuesday's practice because of what Hafley described as "day to day" injuries. Neither player is expected to miss much time, but rookie UDFA DT Rene Konga will miss the entire season with an undisclosed injury suffered Monday. 
 Quarterback Malik Willis threw an interception to Zayne Anderson on the first play of the team's red-zone drill, but followed it up the next play with a touchdown pass to running back De'Von Achane . 
 

 

 
 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Malik Willis still isn't scrambling in team drills as the Dolphins want him to focus on making plays from the pocket in training camp, but he's displaying a keen ability to evade pressure and keep his eyes downfield.

 On multiple occasions during Monday's practice, Willis kept a play alive and found a receiver downfield. He spun away from pressure and found a wide open Malik Washington over the middle for an explosive gain, and lofted another off-platform throw to rookie tight end Seydou Traore -- who came down with a one-handed catch for a first down.

 Willis did throw an interception off a tipped pass, but the ball placement certainly could've been better. He also missed a throw to a wide open Caleb Douglas , who got hands on the ball but couldn't come down with it. But Willis has flashed some touch over the past few practices.

 More observations: 

 
 Linebacker Tyrel Dodson returned an interception for a touchdown in team drills, tracking the ball after it deflected off tight end Cole Turner 's hands. In Turner's defense, the ball from Willis was far too low. 
 Cornerback Ethan Bonner intercepted Quinn Ewers ' first pass of the team's game-winning drive drill, again off a deflected pass. 
 Both Willis and Ewers led their groups into field goal range during game-winning drive drills, and both kickers attempted field goals with each unit. Riley Patterson was good from 50 yards before missing from 43 yards, while Zane Gonzalez made both kicks. Both kickers were good from 52 yards on their third attempt. 
 Safety Lonnie Johnson Jr. appeared to suffer a lower body injury after thudding running back Jaylen Wright in team drills. He was attended to on the sideline and didn't return. 
 Tight end Greg Dulcich did not practice Monday for an unspecified reason, and the group's production tapered off without him. 
 Defensive end Chop Robinson blew by right tackle Charlie Heck on back-to-back plays to start the game-winning drill. The first one was credited as a sack, but Willis got the ball off just in time on the second play, hitting tight end Ben Sims over the middle for a first down. 
 

 
 Sunday, Aug. 2 
 The Dolphins' offense woke up in a major way in an exciting practice in front of fans Sunday morning. Running back De'Von Achane kicked things off with an explosive run on the first play of team drill, while wide receivers Tutu Atwell , Kevin Coleman Jr ., and AJ Henning each had receptions of at least 50 yards.

 Coach Jeff Hafley has introduced "competitive" practice segments in which the "loser" endures some sort of punishment; Sunday, that meant the defense owed Hafley 20 pushups after practice.

 "(Last practice) we beat the offense, today they got us back," rookie cornerback Chris Johnson said. "So we're looking forward to taking the lead back tomorrow."

 

 More observations: 

 
 Johnson turned in yet another strong performance, intercepting a Quinn Ewers pass early on in team drills. The 2026 first-round pick out of San Diego State has trained at both cornerback spots this summer and is destined for a big role this season. 
 Henning turned in his best practice in a Dolphins uniform, dating back to last season. He was the intended receiver on Johnson's interception, but made up for it with 50-plus yard receptions from both Ewers and Cam Miller -- the latter being an over-the-shoulder grab in stride on the final play of practice. 
 Despite the explosive passing plays, arguably the best throw of the day might have been a 10-yard pass from Malik Willis , where he perfectly lofted the ball to tight end Cole Turner just over linebacker Jordyn Brooks ' reach. Impressive touch from Willis, especially while on the move. 
 

 

 Friday, July 31 
 Wide receiver Caleb Douglas turned in his best day of practice yet, and it's…

title: 2026 Minnesota Vikings training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Vikings training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Minnesota Vikings ' camp is taking place in Eagan, Minnesota, and Vikings reporter Kevin Seifert has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Vikings camp. We will update this file often. Who will win the starting quarterback battle between incumbent J.J. McCarthy and free agent addition Kyler Murray ? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Vikings stories 

 
 What McCarthy-Murray QB battle means for Vikings' locker room 
 Vikings, O'Neill reach $96M extension 
 Top Vikings storylines after minicamp, from QBs to new GM 
 Will Vikings start Caleb Banks, other rookies on defense? 
 Jefferson says decision on Vikings starting QB 'coach's call' 
 
 

 Wednesday, Aug.5 

 The Vikings haven't won a playoff game since 2019 and have three playoff victories in the past 25 seasons. So during his annual training camp meeting with reporters, co-owner/president Mark Wilf was asked about the patience his family has exhibited during its tenure as owners.

 "We try to be patient as an ownership, and that we know [leads to] ultimate success," he said. "But of course, patience isn't infinite. We understand that, but I feel really good about the direction of this football club and we're going to get to those benchmarks."

 Mark and Zygi Wilf hired general manager Nolan Teasley this spring to work with fifth-year coach Kevin O'Connell. Of their early interactions, Mark Wilf said: "I just think they work well together. I had an opportunity to watch them interact, and I just see how comfortable they are with each other. They have different characteristics but from my perspective, it's working well. And I think coach can focus on what he has to focus on. Nolan can focus on what he focuses on and they share and they collaborate and everyone in the building feels that."

 

 More observations: 

 
 Facing pressure during a two-minute drill, quarterback Kyler Murray made a smart decision: He lofted a jump ball for receiver Justin Jefferson . Predictably, Jefferson extended over cornerback Isaiah Rodgers and safety Theo Jackson to make the catch and scoot into the end zone. Murray also had a key scramble during the drill, keeping the drive alive. 
 Receiver Jordan Addison jammed his thumb Tuesday. O'Connell said tests revealed no serious injury. During practice, Addison was in full pads and ran routes during individual drills. But he did not have a pass thrown in his direction, and he worked out on a side field during team drills. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 As members of the 2023 draft class begin getting contract extensions, Vikings receiver Jordan Addison  said Tuesday that he is focused on "being where my feet are."

 Four receivers were drafted between picks No. 20-23 that year, and two of them -- Seattle's Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Baltimore's Zay Flowers -- have agreed to new deals. Addison and the Vikings have had to navigate two arrests and one citation during his time in the NFL, and Addison said: "I'm just putting in the work in right now, going through camp, making sure I'm becoming a better receiver, and I feel like everything is going to take care of itself."

 Addison leads the 2023 class with 22 career touchdown receptions. He ranks eighth with 175 receptions and fourth with 2,396 receiving yards.

 "He loves football," Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell said. "He's a great teammate. Clearly he was a young player when he came into the NFL. I think he's learned, matured and he knows exactly what's out in front of him. He knows what's important to him. I'm proud of his growth and development in that phase as well and I think there's a lot of folks in this building that deeply, deeply care about Jordan and what's best for him on and off the field moving forward, and you can count me as one of them."﻿

 More observations: 

 
 The Vikings had a relatively light practice Tuesday in shells, one day after their first full-pads practice of summer. Quarterback J.J. McCarthy elicited murmurs from fans in the stands after overthrowing three consecutive passes in the red zone against no defense, but he came back later with two strong throws on deep outs to receivers  Myles Price  and Dontae Fleming . 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Neither Kyler Murray nor J.J. McCarthy took a step forward Monday during the fifth practice -- and first in full pads -- of their competition to win the Minnesota Vikings ' starting quarterback job. The pair roughly split first-team snaps during 11-on-11 team drills, with Murray getting 10 and McCarthy eight.

 Murray found Justin Jefferson crossing across the field after evading the pass rush, but he also threw high over the middle to receiver Jordan Addison . On the play, Addison and cornerback Isaiah Rodgers collided in the air, flipping Anderson and sending Rodgers sprawling.

 The practice ended with a rough two-minute sequence for both quarterbacks. In five snaps, McCarthy went 0-for-3 with two tipped passes and an interception on a throw to Jefferson that cornerback Byron Murphy Jr . stepped in front of. Murray took over for two snaps with the second team, going 0-for-2 with a pass behind tight end Josh Oliver on the first and a miscommunication on the second.

 More observations from the day: 

 
 
 Receiver Tai Felton , a third-round draft pick in 2025, made the catch of camp in 7-on-7 drills, leaping high to grab a Murray pass in the back corner of the end zone. Felton has been working as the No. 4 receiver behind Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison and Jauan Jennings .

 
 
 Cornerback James Pierre returned to practice after sitting out at the end of last week. Rookie running back Demond Claiborne was in full pads but worked out on a side field for players who are rehabilitating injuries."

 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Quarterback Kyler Murray had by far his best day of training camp Saturday, pinpointing a series of downfield throws in traffic while taking the majority of the Vikings' first-team reps as his competition with J.J. McCarthy continues.

 Murray was on the field for 16 of the first-team offense's 22 snaps in 11-on-11 team drills. McCarthy took the other six. Murray hit receiver Justin Jefferson on a deep dig route over the middle and he threw another perfectly placed pass on his next series that receiver Myles Price dropped. All three of Murray's passes to Jefferson were complete, and Price's drop was Murray's only incompletion among seven passes in team drills.

 McCarthy did not find similar success while working mostly with the second team against the first-team defense. He threw one pass on the run that rookie linebacker Jake Golday tipped, and was intercepted by linebacker Blake Cashman . McCarthy's best throw of the day came during a stint with the first team, but tight end T.J. Hockenson was unable to come up with the ball in traffic in the end zone.

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 At one point Saturday, the Vikings had three rookies working in the same package on their first-team defense: defensive linemen Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange , along with Golday. 
 Cornerback James Pierre was not in uniform for Saturday's practice. Rookie running back Demond Claiborne was not seen in team drills.
