 Rain pushed the Vikings' third practice of training camp indoors Friday, and the condensed area left them working at close to a walkthrough pace. But their quarterback competition continued, and for the first time J.J. McCarthy (32) got…

title: 2026 New England Patriots training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Patriots training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The New England Patriots ' camp is taking place in Foxborough, Massachusetts, and Patriots reporter Mike Reiss has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Patriots camp. We will update this file often. Will Drake Maye  start another MVP-like campaign in Year 3? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive into all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Patriots camp 
 
 A.J. Brown on injury: 'Thumb out of place, you keep going' 
 Patriots' Brown knows Vrabel's rip comes from 'great place' 
 Kraft: Patriots' Gonzalez has offer to be 'highest-paid' CB ever 
 Too many receivers? A look at the Patriots' crowded WR room 
 
 
 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 If the Patriots are indeed considering the possibility of trading wide receiver Kayshon Boutte , their walk-through practice Wednesday was a reminder about why they should reconsider. An unexpected absence can change the receiver outlook quickly.

 Big-bucks free agent signing Romeo Doubs was not present Wednesday, opening the door further for Boutte -- who has had a strong training camp -- to carve out a larger niche as a "comforting" option for quarterback Drake Maye .

 Doubs' absence likely isn't anything serious. He appeared slightly hobbled in recent days, so it simply might be a much-needed rest day. But as Maye recently pointed out, the Patriots are going to need all their receivers, and no one has made more plays down the field than Boutte through 10 practices.

 Maye described him as a "comforting receiver to throw to" and noted his quiet demeanor and how he's "going to be in the right spot and make a play on the football."

 Maye was asked about how Boutte after Wednesday's walk-through, saluting his professionalism despite being mentioned in media-based trade rumors on a regular basis.

 "I think the way Kayshon has approached it -- he's here now, he's where his feet are at. I'm having fun throwing to him out there in practice. He's doing a great job. He makes plays when the football is in the air, and I think that speaks for itself. I've had a lot of great times with Kayshon and I'm looking forward to keep getting better each and every day."

 More observations: 

 
 TE CJ Dippre , who opened training camp on the physically unable to perform list, was in uniform for the first time. He could face an uphill climb for the TE3 role behind Hunter Henry and Eli Raridon , as undrafted free agent Tanner Arkin has been one of the surprise stories of training camp. 
 With RB Terrell Jennings returning to practice Monday, he has quickly established himself as the leading candidate for the RB3 role behind Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson , in part due to his special teams presence. At running back, Jennings is competing against 2025 undrafted free agent Lan Larison , 2026 seventh-round pick Jam Miller and 2026 undrafted free agent Myles Montgomery . 
 There continues to be notable movement at linebacker, where Chad Muma has consistently been the top backup in training camp, and rookies Khalil Jacobs (more of a middle linebacker) and Namdi Obiazor (weakside linebacker) are pushing veteran free agent signing K.J. Britt for reps on defense and special teams. 
 The slower-paced walk-through provided further context on health/injury-based situations, as CB Carlton Davis III remained out of practice since appearing to injure his hamstring July 28. In addition to Davis and Doubs, the other players not present were WR Cameron Dorner , G Caedan Wallace and FB/TE Jack Westover . Meanwhile, ST captain Brenden Schooler remains on the non-football injury list and OLB Harold Landry III remains on the PUP list. 
 

 

 
 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Rookie outside linebacker Gabe Jacas answered questions from reporters Tuesday for the first time since missing the entire spring and signing a contract two days into training camp, saying he wasn't looking back.

 "First and foremost, I just want to say how grateful I am to be here," the second-round pick from Illinois told the assembled media after the ninth practice of training camp. "It was a long journey, but I'm just glad to be part of this organization. It's a blessing to be at practice and run around."

 Jacas underwent a procedure on his left knee in May, which led to his absence and contract impasse. His contract includes an injury waiver that protects the team if his knee isn't healthy through his first three seasons.

 He returned to practice for the first time Saturday and has been gradually increasing his workload since, which also includes one-on-one punt-protection work with coach Mike Vrabel. When asked about his knee, Jacas said he's "100%" and that he doesn't have long-range concerns.

 The Patriots have had eight-year veteran Dre'Mont Jones and second-year player Elijah Ponder as their starting outside linebackers in training camp, with nine-year veteran Harold Landry III  -- a starter in 2025 -- opening on the physically unable to perform list.

 The 6-foot-4, 261-pound Jacas, who wears Vrabel's old No. 50, projects as a top backup.

 "I will tell you this, he looks like an outside linebacker," Vrabel told Sirius XM NFL Radio. "I saw him in uniform and said, 'Well, this is kind of what they're supposed to look like.'"

 

 More observations: 

 
 Ponder had a pass breakup after dropping into coverage and getting in a passing lane to make life hard on QB Drake Maye , who was looking for TE Hunter Henry . 
 Backup QB Tommy DeVito had one of the highlight plays, delivering a deep pass (40ish yards) to WR Mack Hollins along the right sideline (CB Channing Canada closest in coverage). 
 Two-minute offense, which culminated with bringing the field goal unit onto the field, was part of the end-of-practice script. The first- and second-unit offenses were successful. 
 Kicker Andy Borregales was 7-of-7 overall. 
 Undrafted LB Khalil Jacobs (Missouri) repping ahead of veteran LB K.J. Britt on the punt-protection unit was notable, as Jacobs has also been getting some reps ahead of Britt on defense recently. 
 Second-year WR Kyle Williams , who had hobbled off Saturday and didn't participate Monday, returned to what looked like a full workload. 
 WR  Kayshon Boutte 's knack for tracking the football down the field showed up again, with him adjusting to snare a deep pass from DeVito. 
 Punt return was the primary special teams focus of the day, with Marcus Jones ,  DeMario "Pop" Douglas , Romeo Doubs , Efton Chism III and Kobe Prentice the returners. 
 Former quarterback Brian Hoyer was present, watching practice from the field with his son, Garrett. 
 Former receiver Danny Amendola was present and then took part in a USAA "combine" event. "Guys look good, man. I love the receiving corps. Drake Maye looks great," he told reporters. "Guys are flying around, the energy was high, it was great to see." 
 

 

 

 
 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Wide receiver Romeo Doubs ' transition from the Green Bay Packers to the New England Patriots has flown a bit under the radar since the arrival of A.J. Brown in early June.

 So, in a sense, it was fitting that on the day Doubs was scheduled to visit reporters after practice that Brown was once again dominating headlines (he dislocated his left thumb but practiced through it).

 He seems just fine with it.

 "The process has been really good," the soft-spoken Doubs said . "I love where I am, I love where our team is, I love the intensity of camp practices and things of that nature."

 Though Brown is the clear-cut No. 1…

title: 2026 New Orleans Saints training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Saints training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  New Orleans Saints ' camp is taking place in Metairie, Louisiana, and Saints reporter Katherine Terrell has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Saints camp. We will update this file often. Kellen Moore enters his second season as head coach, and expectations are higher after  Tyler Shough  impressed while starting the final nine games of the 2025 campaign. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Saints news 
 
 Drew Brees' greatness, as seen through eyes of teammates, coaches 
 Saints place WR Ja'Lynn Polk, 24, on reserve/retired list 
 Saints starting DT Bryan Bresee to have season-ending ACL surgery 
 The legacy of Taysom Hill in New Orleans: 'There's only one' 
 WR Chris Olave signing four-year extension 
 
 
 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 Wide receiver Barion Brown , a sixth-round pick in April's draft, has seemed to find his stride since the pads came on. Brown has taken advantage of the one-on-one drills vs. defensive backs and made several nice catches during that period Wednesday. He also had a 36-yard catch-and-run from Spencer Rattler over safety Jordan Howden in the two-minute drill to end practice. That play helped the Saints get into field goal range.

 Brown was the third receiver the Saints drafted this year and he came in with the potential to make the team as a kick returner. Saints coach Kellen Moore said they saw more than that when they drafted Brown, who played at Kentucky and LSU.

 "We watched a lot of evidence of him playing receiver and playing impactful plays in the SEC for a number of years, not just the LSU year, but the Kentucky years. And when you watch all that exposure and get to know Barion, you're really fired up to have this guy," Moore said.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Cesar Ruiz was back at practice following the birth of his son, which he described as the best experience of his life. 
 Running back Kendre Miller is dealing with a back issue that has kept him limited in the past two practices. Christen Miller has a toe issue and Jeremiah Wright left early with a shoulder ailment. 
 The Saints worked the two-minute drill to end practice. The scenario was that the offense was down 3 with less than two minutes and one timeout. Both the first- and second-team offenses kicked a field goal to tie. 
 Tanner Brown  made 5 of 6 field goals, with a miss from 39 yards. He also kicked the two-minute field goals. Charlie Smyth is now 15-for-16 in camp and Brown is 17-for-19. 
 Linebacker Kaden Elliss , who is sometimes used as a pass rusher, worked in one-on-one drills against the OL. That drill is usually OL vs. DL but Moore said Elliss wanted to do the drill to get more reps. 
 

 
 Monday, Aug. 3 
 The Saints' offense bounced back in the team's first day in pads. It was a run-focused day featuring some usage of 12 and 13 personnel (sets with two and three tight ends).

 Saints quarterback Tyler Shough and the offensive unit had a solid end to practice when he completed a pass to Alvin Kamara , hit Travis Etienne Jr . near the sideline and connected again with Etienne, who found running room thanks to a hole opened up by Erik McCoy .

 Shough also had completions to Jordyn Tyson and Juwan Johnson (the last one coming with pressure from several defensive linemen). Rookie wideout Barion Brown had what might have been the play of the day, catching a deep pass down the sideline from Spencer Rattler while going against cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. 

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Charlie Smyth made five of six field goal attempts, missing his first kick of camp (wide right from 55 yards). Smyth kicked a 44-yarder again after his miss and made it. 
 Quincy Riley and Isaac Yiadom  substituted in with the first team at outside cornerback. Linebacker Danny Stutsman also got first-team reps. 
 The Saints practiced one-on-one individual drills for the first time. Tyson did not participate in those to limit his overall reps for the day, but Bub Means had a few solid reps. 
 Cesar Ruiz had another excused absence after the recent birth of his child. 
 Coach Kellen Moore did not say whether the Saints planned to bring in another receiver after the unexpected retirement of Ja'Lynn Polk . 
 

 
 Sunday, Aug. 2 
 The Saints' defense had a solid showing in a day that involved a lot of 11-on-11 red zone work. It specifically shined in the final period of the day. Linebacker Pete Werner punched the ball out of running back  Travis Etienne Jr .'s hands after he caught a pass from Tyler Shough ; safety Jonas Sanker blitzed and had a pressure to force an incompletion; and Chase Young had a pressure on an end zone interception from Shough that was caught by Julian Blackmon .

 On the first play of team drills, Shough made a nice downfield throw from the Saints' 35-yard line to Chris Olave in the end zone, but it was hard to tell if Olave, working against Quincy Riley , came down with the ball in bounds.

 More observations from the day: 

 
 The Saints practiced in their indoor facility because of a rainstorm, so practice was closed to fans. 
 Saints coach Kellen Moore said defensive tackle Bryan Bresee will have surgery for a torn ACL . 
 Tanner Brown rotated in as kicker and went 5-for-5 in field goals. So far he has missed one field goal in camp and Charlie Smyth has missed none. 
 Shough was knocked to the ground at one point in 11-on-11 drills, marking the second time this has happened in the first week of practice despite his red noncontact jersey. 
 Cesar Ruiz and Ja'Lynn Polk were excused absences again. Ruiz recently posted on social media that he and his wife welcomed their first child. 
 Edge rusher Michael Heldman , who signed with the Saints as a UDFA, had a nice series with the third team where he had two pressures on Zach Wilson in four plays, including one where the ball fell incomplete. 
 Rookie wideout Bryce Lance had back-to-back touchdowns while working with Spencer Rattler and the second team in 7-on-7s. 
 

 

 
 Friday, July 31 
 Chris Olave was a full participant in practice for the first time this offseason after agreeing to a contract extension on Thursday . For the first two days of camp, Olave did only individual position drills as they worked out the final details of the contract.
 "It was kind of a deal where we kind of had to meet halfway [because of] the injuries and everything that happened," Olave said of the extension. "The uncertainty in the future, especially with the blood clot and concussions. We kind of met halfway. They did a great job of communicating that. And I feel like, my agent and them came to a good deal for both of us."

 On Friday he participated in 11-on-11 drills, at one time lining up outside rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson . Olave and Tyson have been establishing their chemistry throughout the offseason, including a cohesive charity event set for Saturday. They showed off their bond in front of fans for the first time Friday.

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Guard  Cesar Ruiz and wide receiver  Ja'Lynn Polk were excused from practice for personal reasons. Dillon Radunz subbed in for Ruiz with the first unit 
 Nose tackle  Davon Godchaux was given a rest day, while cornerback  Kool-Aid McKinstry had a light practice after tweaking his ankle the day before. Isaac Yiadom got snaps in McKinstry's place. 
 Charlie Smyth went 5-for-5 on field goals again on Friday. Smyth is kicking with a cast on his thumb…

title: Drew Brees' greatness, as seen through eyes of teammates, coaches
summary: The former Saints and Chargers QB will be enshrined in the Pro Football Hall of Fame on Saturday, and those who know him share tales of what makes him "the GOAT."
full_text:
NEW ORLEANS -- Saints quarterback Tyler Shough got more than he bargained for when he called Drew Brees for advice on setting up an offseason workout in California this summer.

 Shough expected Brees to make an appearance at the throwing sessions he helped set up. What he got was a workout in which he carried kettle bells next to the 47-year-old Brees and struggled not to get shown up by a man almost twice his age.

 "I have to do a heavier weight than him," the 26-year-old Shough jokingly recalled. "So I grab the heavier ones, and me and Drew are walking and he's just [stoic] and I'm trying not to die."

 Some of the younger players in attendance at those workouts were in awe of Brees. Running back Travis Etienne Jr ., who grew up in Louisiana watching Brees play, had to get a picture of him to mark the moment.

 

 "That's like our hero, fans growing up and watching him. And especially for Trav, it was really cool," Shough said. "He's like, 'Man, that's Drew Brees over there.'"

 Brees can no longer throw with his right arm 20 years after Dr. James Andrews put in more than 10 anchors to repair his shoulder. He suffered a 360-degree labrum tear and partial rotator cuff tear in his final appearance with the Chargers, the team that selected him with the 32nd pick of the 2001 NFL draft.

 The shoulder injury closed the door on his Chargers career and led him to New Orleans, where he would spend 15 record-setting seasons, win Super Bowl XLIV and uplift a city recovering from Hurricane Katrina.

 Brees will become the fifth primary Saints player to be enshrined in the Pro Football Hall of Fame on Saturday (Noon, ET). All-Pro tight end Jimmy Graham , franchise receiving leader Marques Colston and franchise rushing leader Alvin Kamara are among the players who attribute a portion of their success to him, and they are among a group of more than 10 players and coaches who spoke to ESPN about what made Brees a Hall of Fame quarterback.

 Those who know Brees say his brilliance was never about arm strength, even in his early years. Brees thrived because of his work ethic, leadership and consistency.

 He missed one game due to injury in his first 13 seasons with the Saints, although a thumb injury and broken ribs cost him nine games in his final two seasons.

 Even as his arm strength diminished in his final seasons, he carried the Saints to one more playoff appearance in the 2020 season. His last game was a loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in front of a crowd of less than 5,000 people due to COVID-19 restrictions. He announced his retirement on Instagram on March 14, 2021 .

 "The greatest tip of the hat you can give somebody is 'I gave everything to the game.' I knew he didn't have anything more left in him after that last year," Saints defensive end Cameron Jordan , who played with Brees from 2011 to 2020, said.

 Here's a snapshot of the qualities that made Brees a Hall of Famer, through the eyes of those who had a front-row seat:

 

 
 Attention to detail 
 Brees often said he never wavered in how he prepared each day. His teammates said that was true whether it was a record-breaking game or a practice. Jordan said training camp practices used to feature relentless trash-talking from defensive players who were certain they were going to get the best of Brees that day.

 If the defense did win the rep, Brees would repeat the play and tweak the smallest detail, sometimes scooting a receiver over an inch. Brees was also famous for taking "mental reps," often running through games in his mind while alone in the indoor facility on Saturdays.

 Jordan: Next thing you know, it's a touchdown. And you're like, what? There shouldn't be any difference. ... Same play, same player. All of a sudden it's a better read. It's just Drew's mind, the way he was able to process the game was next level.

 Erik McCoy (Saints teammate with Brees, 2019-20): In here on his own on Saturdays after everybody has left, just walking through the game on the field, like the first 15 [plays], going through a whole drive. ... The attention to detail was crazy. And I think that's why he's my GOAT.

 Benjamin Watson (Saints teammate with Brees, 2013-15, 2018): On Saturday you come in and you have meetings, then you have your walk-through. ... I was in the weight room and in the facility, obviously there's windows to the indoor practice field and it was kind of dark in there. And I see this figure out there at midfield doing some sort of motion repetitively. And he was pointing at different things and just walking back and forth. And somebody was like, "Yeah, that's Drew in there." I was like, "What is he doing?" ... "Well, he's going through all of the calls." So Drew, as you know, would be in there kind of in the shadows, going through all of his offensive playcalls and going through all of his progressions ... I mean, it had to be an hour ... just by himself visualizing everything he was about to do.

 Dennis Allen (Saints assistant coach with Brees, 2006-10, 2015-20): He wanted to win everything. Watching a guy play the game the way he played the game and you watched him after every throw that he made, he went through the rest of his progression -- not once, not a few times during practice, every time during practice.

 

 
 Accuracy 
 Brees retired with a completion percentage of 67.7%, an NFL record at the time. He still holds four of the top 10 spots for single-season completion percentage, and his final season ranks 14th.

 Those accomplishments didn't happen by accident. Brees was relentless about studying film, and it was almost impossible to beat him to the practice facilities in the mornings. He studied both opponents and his own teammates to figure out how they preferred him to throw the ball. When he threw a pass, he wanted that pass to land in a specific spot every time.

 Lance Moore (Saints teammate with Brees, 2006-13): First guy in the building, last guy out type of cliché, but it matters.

 Josh Hill (Saints teammate with Brees, 2013-20): You could be in the building anytime during the week and say you came at 7 a.m. on Wednesday [and saw him]. Come the next Wednesday at 7 a.m., [he's at the] same spot. Just ultimate focus.

 Alvin Kamara (Saints teammate with Brees, 2017-20): Drew was just a perfectionist. ... He wanted the ball to look a certain way coming out of his hand. He wanted it to land a certain way. He wanted it to hit a receiver in stride. It was just his detail. It was obsessive.

 

 Jimmy Graham (Saints teammate with Brees, 2010-14): I remember sometimes we'd be in the red zone and he scrambled around. He gets it out quick and the ball would maybe be on my hip or the ball would be somewhere where he thought that I wouldn't like it. And in the end, I end up catching it. I would score a touchdown. And we get to the sideline, the first thing he said was, "Hey, listen, awesome catch. I'm so sorry for that throw." And I look at him and I'm like, "Dude, what are you talking about? We just scored." But for him, perfection was everything.

 Allen: If they had a play that he didn't like the outcome, he didn't like the timing or the placement of the ball or whatever the case may be, the moment we had the next break, he had whoever that receiver was and he was working that play again. And so, to me, that's what makes Hall of Famers special. They are willing to do things that not everybody else is willing to do.

 Graham: There is and was and probably will never be an offense more complex and more demanding on a quarterback than a [former Saints coach] Sean Payton offense. The amount of calls and the amount of changes to these calls that could happen, I still don't understand how we did it. ... I mean, the amount of studying he did, I've never met a guy who's literally at the facility at 5:30 in the morning and stays till 9:30, 10. And this even happened when I was in Seattle and Green Bay. I would get a random text from Drew. It would be late in Seattle. So I can…

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The New York Giants camp is taking place at The Greenbrier in White Sulphur Springs, West Virginia, and Giants reporter Jordan Raanan has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Giants camp. We will update this file often. How will the Giants handle increased expectations and a new coach? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Giants camp 
 
 Cam Skattebo admits doing 'dumb things,' will save backflips for TDs 
 Nabers 'looked good' in 1st practice since knee injury 
 Giants have spoken with Skattebo after Fanatics Fest flip 
 2026 New York Giants training camp preview 
 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 It was another up and down day for the Giants' offense. It really has been the story of training camp in West Virginia.

 Quarterback Jaxson Dart and Co. were pedestrian again on Wednesday, even against the second-team defense. He threw a pair of interceptions early, before tossing three touchdown passes and rushing for two more in red-zone drills.

 Coach John Harbaugh thought it was a good response after Dart let the frustration get the best of him one day earlier.

 "The football response absolutely was there. Yeah, he stepped up," Harbaugh said. "A lot of third down stuff we did. Fourth down stuff, fourth down in the red zone to win the game, things like that.

 "Yeah, he had a heck of a practice. It was impressive."

 Dart and the first-team offense have yet to fully hit their stride this summer. And there are some built-in excuses. Dart is learning a new offense. He's also without his No. 1 receiver in Malik Nabers , who still isn't taking part in team drills as he recovers from a knee injury. Still, it would be nice to see them put together a complete practice before leaving West Virginia.

 
 Second day in a row Odell Beckham Jr . had a strong practice. This time he had four catches in live drills. He continues to get open and make it a tough decision for the Giants whether to find a roster spot for the veteran receiver. 
 Outside linebacker Brian Burns , wide receiver Malachi Fields and safety Beau Brade all sat out Wednesday's practice with what Harbaugh called "minor" deals. Wide receiver  JuJu Smith-Schuster  (knee swelling) returned to practice after sitting out the previous day. 
 Rookie Dominic Zvada went a perfect 10 of 10 kicking field goals. He's now 28 of 31 on field goals at training camp and has to be the leader in the clubhouse to be the Giants' kicker this season. 
 The Giants signed two players: CBs D.J. Jones and David Long. In order to make room, they waived wide receiver Beaux Collins with an injury designation after he was banged up this week and placed defensive lineman Roy Robertson-Harris on injured reserve after tearing an Achilles in the spring. That ends Robertson-Harris' season with the Giants. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 In his quest to make the roster, Tuesday was an important practice for Odell Beckham Jr . For the first time this summer he worked with the first-team offense for most of the day.

 Beckham caught a pair of passes and had another would've-been touchdown grab in a strong performance.

 Beckham worked alongside Darnell Mooney and Braxton Berrios on a day when Darius Slayton and Malachi Fields seemed to have their workloads limited. Malik Nabers continues to participate in individual drills but mostly stands around and watches when the team breaks into live periods.

 "Just probably worked out that way [Tuesday]," coach John Harbaugh said of Beckham working with the first team. "He ... I don't know, worked out that way."

 Regardless, Beckham continues to get open consistently. He might not look like Prime Odell, but he still can play and create separation.

 More observations: 

 
 Wide receiver  JuJu Smith-Schuster  sat out practice with knee swelling, according to Harbaugh. Smith-Schuster is also fighting for a roster spot. Look out for wide receiver Dalen Cambre . He had another strong day with three catches in live drills, including a touchdown from Jameis Winston on a rub route at the goal line. Cambre worked his way onto the Giants' roster in the second half of last season and played well on special teams. 
 The penalties that plagued the Giants on Monday were again a problem early in Tuesday's practice. They committed five more penalties in the second padded practice of the summer, including four in the first few live drills. 
 Rookie guard Francis Mauigoa had his ups and downs in one-on-ones. He got the better of Abdul Carter on their first matchup but was spun around after they immediately ran it back. Mauigoa did recover. Still, Carter beat him cleanly at the onset. 
 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 

 It was a rough day for the Giants' offense in pouring rain on the first day in full pads. The performance was really an extension of the early part of training camp for Jaxson Dart  & Co.

 A lot of penalties. Too many mental mistakes. Not enough positive plays. 
 
Dart threw an interception into the hands of safety Jevon Holland when the ball slipped out of the quarterback's hand while throwing. The Giants failed to score a touchdown on any of their drives and committed nine offensive penalties, everything from delay of games to endless false starts to holding by a wide receiver.

 "I think two things," coach John Harbaugh said. "I mean, I think you've got the elements a little bit, and you've got the first day in pads. So, it's not really unexpected, but we'll be working on it."

 Harbaugh added that he generally believes the offense is ahead of the defense early in camp. That seems not to be the case with his sloppy Giants as they digest new schemes.

 Other observations:  

 
 It was another strong practice from first-round pick Arvell Reese . The rookie linebacker had a run stop early in practice and later a sack when he beat left tackle Andrew Thomas . "The rookie has been impressive. Kid has a real chance to be special," veteran defensive tackle DJ Reader said. 
 Cornerback Deonte Banks is flashing early this summer. The former first-round pick has provided sticky coverage on receivers throughout camp. Monday's practice was no different. He tipped a pass that resulted in an interception by linebacker Micah McFadden . Banks later had Darius Slayton blanketed but dropped an interception that hit him in the chest. After some struggles, maybe Banks has it figured out? 
 
 
 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 It has been a quiet start to training camp from Odell Beckham Jr .

 Until Saturday.

 On the day when the Giants had their largest crowd of the summer at The Greenbrier in West Virginia, Beckham made the biggest play of the day. And received the biggest ovation of the summer to date.

 The veteran receiver made a leaping grab over a defender in the back of the end zone for a touchdown from quarterback Jameis Winston during 11-on-11 drills. It sent the crowd of approximately 2,000 fans into a frenzy and served as a reminder of what used to be.

 It was a big play for Beckham, who is battling for a roster spot with several other veterans. Braxton Berrios has stood out the most of the group this camp, until Saturday.

 "There's a lot of really good football players in our room right now," wide receiver Darius Slayton said. "From a competition-level standpoint, it's ... raised the competition level."

summary: Follow our daily updates from Eagles training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Philadelphia Eagles camp is taking place in the Jefferson Health Training Complex, and Eagles reporter Tim McManus has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and -- of course -- the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Eagles camp. We will update this file often. How will quarterback  Jalen Hurts fare in the reimagined offense? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Eagles news 
 
 Epenesa grateful to be Eagle after 'weird' Browns situation 
 Eagles' Nolan Smith apologizes for 'unacceptable' speeding arrest 
 Eagles, DT Carter agree to four-year, $152M extension 
 Eagles coach Nick Sirianni adjusting to offseason changes 
 
 
 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 The Jalen Hurts - Dontayvion Wicks connection continues to shine. The highlight Wednesday came during 7-on-7s with Hurts tossing a precision pass deep down the left sideline for Wicks, who corralled it with defensive backs Jonathan Jones and Andre Sam bearing down on him. Hurts said Wicks was "trying to beat down the door" this offseason to get extra reps in with him and complimented his attack mindset.

 "When you talk about adversity, you learn a lot about the guys around you this time of camp. It's humid, it's sticky, it's hot. You see who's got that anger to them, who's got a little bit of rage in them -- for the best," Hurts said. "He's got it. That's exciting to see."

 

 Other observations:  

 
 Eagles receivers DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon both missed practice due to hamstring injuries for a second straight day. Right tackle Lane Johnson was absent for the fourth straight practice for personal reasons. 
 The linebacker corps looks to have some good depth to it behind presumed starters Zack Baun and Jihaad Campbell . Jeremiah Trotter Jr . has enjoyed a strong camp. He put himself in perfect position to extinguish a Saquon Barkley toss run. DC Vic Fangio also told reporters not to "sleep" on veteran Chance Campbell when putting together their "lists," seemingly referring to the 53-man roster projections. He has looked solid as well. 
 New offensive coordinator Sean Mannion has dialed up a healthy amount of designed runs for Hurts, generally to good results, including one Wednesday with Dallas Goedert as an escort that produced a chunk gain down the left side. Hurts said it's too early to know how those kind of plays will mesh with the new offensive scheme but the bet here is Hurts uses his legs a little more than last season based off what we've seen at camp. 
 

 
 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Eagles receivers DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon both missed practice with hamstring injuries. The team is not expressing any long-term concern with either player. Still, these are meaningful reps -- especially for a rookie. Lemon missed minicamp as well with a hamstring injury. He has served primarily as the starting slot receiver when healthy but hasn't produced many splash moments to date. It's important Jalen Hurts gets as many snaps as possible with his skill players as the offense breaks in a new system in the post A.J. Brown era.

 Other observations:  

 
 Standout right tackle Lane Johnson was absent (excused/not injury related) for the third straight practice. The team declined to provide further details given that it is a personal matter. Rookie Markel Bell received first-team reps in his absence and appeared to hold his own. 
 With a number of starters missing, it wasn't a big surprise the offense sputtered. Penalties made for a clunky, rhythmless practice with few highlights. 
 It's important to note that new plays are being installed in the early portion of camp, so it makes sense why the offensive operation can look rough in spots. It's no coincidence that the offense's breakout day on Monday was a review of plays that had been installed previously. In other words, patience is required. 
 Linebacker Jihaad Campbell had perhaps his strongest showing of the summer. He sliced into the backfield to stifle a pitch to Saquon Barkley . Moments later, he fired in on a blitz and delivered a hit on would-be blocker Tank Bigsby that sent Bigsby flying to the turf. 
 In that same series, DT Byron Young got free on a pass rush, forcing a Cam Jurgens holding penalty. Between Jalen Carter , Jordan Davis , Moro Ojomo , Young and others, the defensive tackle spot appears to be in superb shape. 
 
 
 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Quarterback Jalen Hurts had his best day of camp to date. It started with a deep sideline throw to Dontayvion Wicks followed by a dot to Elijah Moore down the right seam. Hurts lit it up in the red zone, finding DeVonta Smith for a pair of touchdowns before running in for another score moments later, leading to a leaping celebration with Saquon Barkley and other teammates. There was one notable blemish on the day -- a short pass to Moore that was jumped by Quinyon Mitchell for a pick-six -- but the practice was defined by sharp, on-time throws, including one deep over the middle that led to a highlight diving catch by Darius Cooper .

 Other observations: 

 
 Right tackle Lane Johnson (excused/not injury related) was absent for a second straight practice. Rookie receiver Makai Lemon did not participate in team drills after taking part in individual drills earlier in the session. 
 The second-team defense got work against the first-team offense. Credit linebacker Chance Campbell for sniffing out a Barkley run to the outside and darting into the backfield to make a stop. 
 Andy Dalton appeared to outplay Tanner McKee as the battle for the No. 2 QB spot continues. Dalton fired a completion over the middle to Johnny Wilson with Jihaad Campbell looming in coverage. McKee underthrew Wilson later in the session and appeared to hold onto the ball for too long at times in the red zone. 
 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 The Eagles' defense flexed its muscles, making for some tough sledding for Jalen Hurts  & Co. over the one-hour, 40-minute session. Hurts had two passes batted at the line of scrimmage to start the session -- first by Zack Baun , then Jalen Carter . That set the tone for a day defined by heavy pressure and little flow to the pass game.

 Carter, fresh off signing a mega-extension , was a problem, and the same can be said for Jalyx Hunt , who has spent much of training camp to date in the backfield.

 Other observations: 

 
 Jeremiah Trotter Jr . got the nod at starting linebacker in Jihaad Campbell 's absence (excused/not injury-related) and made his presence felt, showing good anticipation to disrupt the short-to-intermediate passing game. 
 Safety Andrew Mukuba and rookie receiver Makai Lemon collided over the middle of the field going after what proved to be a Hurts incompletion. Fortunately, no one was injured on the play. Lemon has seen plenty of action as the primary slot receiver but has had a relatively quiet start to camp. 
 Receiver Dontayvion Wicks had another quality practice. He made a contested catch over the middle and muscled through Michael Carter II for some yards after the catch. 
 

 

 Thursday, July 30 
 New Eagles receiver Dontayvion Wicks made the play of the day and may have earned more of Jalen Hurts ' trust in the process. Near the end of Thursday's practice, Hurts unfurled a pass deep down the field to Wicks, who was double covered by defensive backs Cole Wisniewski and Jakorian Bennett . Wicks elevated over both of them and secured the catch.

 The former Packer is trying to solidify his spot as the No. 2 wideout in this offense alongside DeVonta Smith .…

title: 2026 Seattle Seahawks training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Seahawks training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Seattle Seahawks ' camp is taking place in Renton, Washington, and Seahawks reporter Brady Henderson has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Seahawks camp. We will update this file often. What is new with the defending Super Bowl champions? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp previews for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Seahawks camp 
 
 WR Tory Horton healthy after cracking tibia last season 
 Seattle Pro Bowl DL Williams confirms deal talks 
 Seattle's Nick Emmanwori has ankle surgery, expected to play W1 
 Who are the Khoslas? Meet the family set to buy the Seahawks 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 What does it mean to be a technician as a pass-catcher?

 Jaxon Smith-Njigba provided a few examples during an almost-unstoppable performance Wednesday.

 In one early period, as a deep ball from Sam Darnold was on its descent, the NFL's reigning receiving champion and AP Offensive Player of the Year deked an in-phase cornerback by momentarily gearing down, creating enough last-second separation to haul in the pass uncontested. On a later touchdown catch, the Seahawks' new $168.6 million man slow-played his release on a wheel route from the slot, perfectly timing the traffic before accelerating into a void between the corner and safety. He found the end zone again on a quick slant at the goal line.

 Whether he actually did make another highlight-reel grab while falling out of bounds was in question. An official called it incomplete before coach Mike Macdonald overruled him.

 Either way, Seattle's 10th practice of camp was JSN's best.

 "It was great to see him come alive," Macdonald said. "Some of those in high-leverage situations, too. ... There's defensive attention on where he's at at all times, too, so for him to be able to make those plays, it's great for the Seahawks, great for him."

 Smith-Njigba made this kind of dominance almost routine last season on his way to a league-high and franchise-record 1,793 receiving yards, which was the eighth-highest total in NFL history. That was with Klint Kubiak calling the offensive shots. Now it's up to new coordinator Brian Fleury, a first-time playcaller, to find the best way to utilize Seattle's star receiver.

 "He can get open from wherever, doing whatever, doing all the things from all the places," Macdonald said. "But how do we optimize it? How do we move him around? Where is he in the progression? He's going to be No. 1 in the progression on a lot of plays, but when is it best for him not be that? Those are the things that we're always going to be working through.

 "Today was a really cool step for us and our offense."

 

 
 Tuesday's season premiere of "Hard Knocks" showed Macdonald's mic'd up reaction to the fights during Friday's practice. He was disappointed in outside linebacker Derick Hall for throwing down offensive lineman Bryce Cabeldue from behind, and he felt fullback Brady Russell crossed a line with a verbal dig he took at Hall moments later. Based on what Macdonald and Hall said Wednesday, it's all been smoothed over. "Things get out of control sometimes, but at the end of the day, we all love each other here," Hall said. "We're a team, we're a brotherhood, and at the end of the day, it happens out here, we go in the locker room and hug it out, 'Hey man, I apologize. That was beyond the line of where we are trying to go and what we're trying to get,' and we move forward. I think that's what we do really well here." 
 OLB Jared Ivey has returned to practice after missing several days with an undisclosed injury. Still sidelined are WR Jake Bobo , CB Julian Neal , DL Mike Morris , LBs Jamie Sheriff and Chris Paul Jr ., and RB Jacardia Wright . OT Bobby Hart did not practice after going down Tuesday. 
 Backup LB Tyrice Knight delivered a highlight play when he reached down to intercept a low pass that had bounced off the hands of WR Tory Horton . It'll he hard for Knight to reclaim the starting job he lost last season to Drake Thomas -- who played his way into a two-year, $8 million deal -- but Macdonald has sounded open to finding ways to get Knight on the field. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 As Brian Fleury prepares to call plays for the first time, Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald is trying to help his new offensive coordinator by hindering him.

 "Mike is doing a great job of putting me through the wringer in terms of challenging situations," Fleury said Tuesday. "We go through different ones every day. For some reason, we're always down by a touchdown with 50 seconds left and no timeouts. I don't know who's burning through the timeouts, but it definitely helps me adjust to those situations."

 When Klint Kubiak left to become the  Las Vegas Raiders ' head coach a day after Seattle's Super Bowl LX victory, Macdonald initially thought he'd likely find his next OC by promoting from within. He wanted offensive continuity, and when he interviewed Fleury -- who came from a similar West Coast system in San Francisco to what the Seahawks ran under Kubiak -- he realized how aligned they were in their vision and mentality.

 It was enough to make up for his absence of playcalling experience, but as Fleury readily admits, "doing it for the first time at this level is going to present some challenges."

 While much of Seattle's playbook will remain the same, one likely change will be an increase in shifts and motions. The time those can take off the play clock increases the need for an offense to operate efficiently between each snap. That begins with Fleury getting his playcalls out on time.

 "I try to make it harder on myself," Fleury said. "There's a lot of thought that'll go into it beforehand, going into a game. You'll have stuff all laid out on your sheet, but I try and challenge myself at times just to think off the top of my head and see if I can get it out on time for the sake of the quarterbacks and the playcall. We're practicing all the time."

 More observations: 

 
 After Riq Woolen 's departure in free agency, No. 3 cornerback is among the jobs that's up for grabs on Seattle's defense. The competition is on between incumbent Nehemiah Pritchett and free agent addition Noah Igbinoghene . "I think Nehemiah's doing a great job and I think as we go, you'll see who else shows up and just wait for the opportunity," defensive coordinator Aden Durde said. "I think the games and when we go against different people, that will really show itself. When we put pads on and you have to tackle and you have to play our style, we'll find out." 
 Igbinoghene, a 2020 first-round pick who can play inside and on the perimeter, blew up a run play Tuesday when he blitzed from the slot. "I think he's shown up a lot on early-down football, coming up, hitting the run, doing some great things in man," Durde said. "I think he's shown some great things." 
 Third-round pick Julian Neal could enter the No. 3 cornerback competition, but he has missed the past week with an undisclosed injury. Macdonald has described it as a "shorter-term" issue. 
 Also still sidelined Tuesday were WR Jake Bobo , DL Mike Morris , LBs Jamie Sheriff and Chris Paul Jr ., and FB Robbie Ouzts . RB Jacardia Wright didn't practice after injuring his foot Monday. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 The play of the day on Monday was one that Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald had been wanting to see.

 With Seattle's No. 1 offense facing the No. 2 defense in an 11-on-11 session, Sam Darnold found Rashid Shaheed…

title: 2026 San Francisco 49ers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from 49ers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The San Francisco 49ers camp is taking place in Santa Clara, California, and 49ers reporter Nick Wagoner has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at 49ers camp. We will update this file often. What does  Mike Evans  look like as a top receiver on the 49ers? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive into all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp previews for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 
 

 Latest news from 49ers' camp 
 
 What's next for 49ers receivers Aiyuk, Deebo and Pearsall? 
 Deebo Samuel on reunion with 49ers: 'Just matter of time' 
 WR Ricky Pearsall to have season-ending knee surgery 
 VP Paraag Marathe exits to focus on soccer clubs 
 Police: Shanahan not charged in crash at officer's discretion 
 49ers GM Lynch focused on 'players that are here,' not WR Aiyuk 
 

 
 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 Two years ago, the 49ers canceled joint practice sessions with the Saints because, by the time they got to them, they had 23 players not participating for injury reasons. By the end of Wednesday's session, the Niners were without 20 players on their 90-man roster.

 Some of those absences -- DE Nick Bosa , LB Dre Greenlaw and DT Osa Odighizuwa -- aren't serious and were more about getting past some general soreness. But questions still abound after rookie OL Carver Willis (concussion), FB Kyle Juszczyk (broken finger) and WR Jacob Cowing (hip flexor strain) were added to the injury report Wednesday.

 When asked whether next week's joint sessions with the Titans might be in jeopardy, assistant head coach Chris Foerster indicated that such a move hasn't been something that has come across his desk.

 "We have injuries, we have dings and bumps and bruises where guys are missing practices, but it has yet to come up in anything I've heard," Foerster said. "It doesn't mean it hasn't been discussed ... but that's not come up this week."

 More observations: 

 
 Wide receivers Mike Evans (quad), Christian Kirk (calf) and De'Zhaun Stribling (hamstring) again sat out practice Wednesday. All three did at least some running and conditioning work on the side during the session. 
 OL Brett Toth is also a new addition to the injury report with an undisclosed ailment. 
 In a bit of good injury news, rookie DT Gracen Halton returned from the knee bone bruise he'd been dealing with. Halton's fresh legs seemed to help him, as he was effective in one-on-one pass-rush drills and team work. 
 The Niners released defensive linemen Kevin Givens and  Cameron Sample  on Wednesday to make room for DE Ogbo Okoronkwo and WR KhaDarel Hodge . Okoronkwo, who played under defensive coordinator Raheem Morris with the Rams, is wearing No. 59. Hodge is wearing No. 0. 
 Quarterback  Brock Purdy had a sharp day despite playing musical chairs with wide receivers. In one red zone drill, he accounted for three straight touchdowns, finding running back Patrick Taylor Jr . and receiver Junior Bergen for scores before using his legs to score on a designed run. He also led a touchdown drive in the move-the-ball period, which ended on a deep connection with WR Jordan Watkins . 
 Tight end  Luke Farrell  had a nice day, too. Farrell hasn't offered much as a pass catcher in his time with the Niners, totaling 11 receptions last season. But he and Purdy were in sync Wednesday. 
 The Niners are back at it Thursday and then have a walkthrough set for Friday. 
 
 
 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 The injuries continue to mount for the 49ers, particularly at wide receiver. On Monday, they added veteran Mike Evans to the list as he did not practice because of a quad strain.

 The injury is not believed to be serious and Evans did some work on the side during the session, but it again left the Niners a bit short-handed. With  Ricky Pearsall (knee) done for the season, rookie De'Zhaun Stribling battling hamstring tightness and Christian Kirk out for the better part of the past week with a calf strain, the team's projected top four wideouts were not available Monday.

 Kirk and Stribling also did some work on the side and should be back soon, but the situation bears watching given the number of injury issues that always seem to plague this team at that position group.

 More observations: 

 
 Mike Brown, the title-winning coach of the NBA's New York Knicks, watched practice Monday. His son Cameron is the Niners' defensive quality control coach. 
 Alex Smith, the former 49ers quarterback and current ESPN analyst, was also in attendance. 
 Running back Kaelon Black (adductor) was another addition to the injury report after he missed the second half of Saturday's practice. 
 Defensive tackle C.J. West and edge rusher Romello Height returned from injuries to participate Monday. 
 WR Deebo Samuel continues to show off fresh legs in camp as he was again quite involved in the offense. With all the injuries at receiver, there's an opening for Samuel to establish a role beyond returning kicks. 
 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 While no definitive date has been set for coach Kyle Shanahan to return to full-time duty, he seems to be taking the necessary steps in that direction.

 Before Saturday's practice, Shanahan addressed the team for the first time since his July 14 car accident, according to general manager John Lynch. Then, during practice, Shanahan emerged on the field before team drills and stayed through the end of the session. At one point late in practice, he even stood behind the offense, offering real-time feedback rather than standing next to Lynch in the deep middle of the field.

 "He's doing better," Lynch said. "He got a nice welcome, and it was good to have him up there. We'll continue to do kind of like a phased approach. So that was one threshold. He wanted to get up there. He was cleared to do so. So we'll see where it goes from there."

 More observations: 

 
 Some new additions to the injury report: rookie WR De'Zhaun Stribling (hamstring tightness), DL Romello Height (elbow) and DL Cameron Sample (knee) did not participate. DL Keion White (adductor), DL Mikail Kamara (knee) and RB Kaelon Black (undisclosed) did not finish the practice after starting it. Kamara's ailment seemed the most serious as he was taken off on a cart. 
 WR Deebo Samuel took part in one-on-one drills but was limited to about 10 snaps in team drills. He made a trio of catches, including one over the middle for a big gain from QB Brock Purdy . 
 It was a rough day for the offense in general as it could never quite get on track. Purdy overthrew a handful of pass catchers as did Mac Jones . Nobody seemed to get in sync as it went on. Perhaps a sign of fatigue a week into training camp. 
 

 

 Friday, July 31 
 During the team meeting before Friday's first fully padded practice, assistant head coach Chris Foerster emphasized to the 49ers the importance of protecting one another. In that message, Foerster asked his team to be competitive but not fight.

 "I did a great job with that one," Foerster said, laughing.

 In fact, the Niners' first padded practice did end with a couple of skirmishes, the second of which devolved into a full-fledged fight. On the play, tight end Jake Tonges appeared to push off linebacker Fred Warner then catch a pass from QB Brock Purdy . Although there was a flag thrown on Tonges on the play, Warner ran over to Tonges and got in his face, seemingly taking exception at how Tonges got open. The two exchanged words and shoves before OT Colton McKivitz ran in to stand up for Tonges. That led to LB Dre Greenlaw coming in and McKivitz ending up on the…

title: 2026 Tampa Bay Buccaneers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Buccaneers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' camp is taking place at the Advent Health Training Center in Tampa, Florida, and Buccaneers reporter Jenna Laine has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Bucs camp. We will update this file often. We are looking at who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football, and which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Bucs camp 
 
 Mayfield felt 'disrespected' and 'undervalued' by contract offers 
 History says Vea, Mayfield will play with Bucs this season 
 Vea requests trade from Bucs after stalled talks 
 2026 Bucs training camp preview 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 Tempers flared as the Bucs put on pads for the second straight day -- this time at their annual night practice. Rookie inside linebacker Josiah Trotter , the Bucs' second-round draft pick and son of NFL great Jeremiah Trotter, had multiple tackles for a loss during Monday's first padded practice. He followed that up with a tackle for a loss during 11-on-11s Tuesday.

 Trotter could be seen jawing with starting right guard Cody Mauch , starting left guard Ben Bredeson , starting right tackle Luke Goedeke and backup swing tackle Justin Skule . Fellow inside linebacker Alex Anzalone had to restrain Trotter as he took him to the sideline. Anzalone could also be seen pointing at the offensive line and chirping as they huddled up, appearing to support his younger teammate and directing everyone to get back to work.

 While coach Todd Bowles stopped practice to address the team, he praised the 21-year-old challenging for the starting MIKE role. "He had a heck of a day yesterday and he buckled some guys," Bowles said. "If they start playing like that yesterday, he shouldn't need the extra energy today. He's probably a guy you really don't want to mess with either."

 He added, "Once you put your helmet on and you go on the field, all is fair game as long as you're doing it the right way. He plays with the right temperament and he plays the right way."

 Other observations:  

 
 During one-on-one drills, rookie outside linebacker Rueben Bain Jr . used a nasty hand swipe to blow by starting right tackle Luke Goedeke , drawing gasps from fans in attendance. Mind you, Goedeke is no slouch and is making $22.5 million a year. Bain also had what would have been a sack of quarterback Jake Browning . 
 Rookie wide receiver Ted Hurst III hauled in a Baker Mayfield red zone touchdown in the corner of the end zone with Zyon McCollum in tight coverage. Defensive tackle Calijah Kancey came flying at Mayfield on that play however, and it would have very likely been a sack. Still, it was good work for Hurst, who also caught a 20-yard pass downfield from Mayfield. 
 Wide receiver Tez Johnson left the practice field early to get treatment for what Bowles said was a groin injury that he sustained while running. Wide receiver David Sills V also left practice early, but Bowles did not have specifics immediately after practice. He was, however, seen with an ice pack on his knee. 
 The team was without its top three wide receivers as  Chris Godwin Jr .,  Emeka Egbuka  and Jalen McMillan all sat out. Godwin has been getting maintenance days in camp, while McMillan - who was spotted wearing a compression sleeve on his left calf - banged his knee in practice, according to Bowles, which forced him to miss Monday as well. Egbuka is still dealing with soreness and "tweaked something," Bowles said, and the team is "trying to keep him off the turf." 
 Rookie  Dean Patterson , an undrafted free agent out of Georgia Tech and FIU (he's also from nearby Lutz), maximized his opportunities in a depleted wide receiver room, hauling in two touchdowns from Browning. 
 Cornerback Ayden Garnes , an undrafted free agent out of Arizona, closed out practice with an interception off quarterback Jalon Daniels . He also picked off Mayfield during one-on-ones Monday on a pass intended for Kameron Johnson . With Benjamin Morrison and Jacob Parrish both missing time, he's gotten a lot more opportunities and is pushing for the last cornerback spot. 
 The team has Wednesday off and will return Thursday at their regular 8:30 a.m. practice time. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Wide receivers Jalen McMillan and Emeka Egbuka were not practicing for the team's first day in pads -- due to being, as coach Todd Bowles put it, "a little sore." Cornerback Jacob Parrish , last year's starting nickelback who is competing for a starting outside cornerback spot, also missed practice with what Bowles said was soreness.

 More observations from the day: 

 
 The Bucs have brought back two-time Olympic hurdling champion Roger Kingdom, who served as the team's speed and conditioning coach under Bruce Arians and is part of a coaching staff revamp that also included members of strength and conditioning department. "Obviously, we're stretching and running and doing dynamic warmups and those type of things, trying to stop some of the soft-tissue injuries," Bowles said. "He does a good job aiding in that and making sure guys are doing what they're supposed to do, as far as running form-wise and the way they're supposed to run. It's really helped us out." 
 The team was forced to practice indoors due to heavy rain for the second straight day. Bowles joked, "I think I've been here about eight years, and this is the second time in a row we've gone indoors. Every other year we've been outside." They'll do it a third day in a row Tuesday as it's a night practice. 
 There's been no movement on Pro Bowl nose tackle Vita Vea 's contract since his 'hold in' began at the start of camp. but the team just installed his image on one of four corners of Raymond James Stadium's exterior, along with quarterback Baker Mayfield , wide receiver Chris Godwin and safety Antoine Winfield Jr . 
 
 
 
 Sunday, Aug. 2 
 Bucs coach Todd Bowles clarified that the hamstring injury that has plagued outside cornerback and 2025 second-round draft pick Benjamin Morrison -- forcing him to miss the start of training camp -- is actually a different hamstring than the one that limited him last season.

 Morrison missed all of preseason last year and played in 10 regular-season games -- with three starts -- as a result of a quad injury and then a right hamstring injury. On top of this, Morrison underwent bilateral hip surgery. He is competing for a starting spot on the outside with Zyon McCollum and Jacob Parrish but has yet to participate in team periods in camp, making his evaluation a tough one and raising concerns over depth at that position.

 "Hopefully he gets some work in this coming week," Bowles said of Morrison. "I would like to see. He was out here moving around better, but I'll see what the trainer says."

 Monday will mark the team's first padded practice of camp.

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Safety Antoine Winfield Jr . picked off quarterback Baker Mayfield on a deep ball pass intended for wide receiver Jalen McMillan , whom he battled on a contested catch. 
 WR  Tez Johnson , who hauled in a deep ball touchdown from QB  Jake Browning  earlier this week and punctuated it with a celebratory backflip, pulled in a touchdown from Mayfield on a crossing route during a red zone period. 
 All-Pro left tackle Tristan Wirfs remains sidelined with a hamstring injury, but like Pro Bowl nose tackle Vita Vea , he was spotted on the sideline during the indoor practice.  Benjamin Chukwuma , who started two games last season, has been getting reps in Wirfs'…

title: Will WR Stefon Diggs be a fit with the Washington Commanders?
summary: The Commanders have signed Stefon Diggs to a one-year contract worth up to $12 million. Here's what it means for him and the team.
full_text:
ASHBURN, Va. -- The Washington Commanders had one big question on offense: Who would be the No. 2 receiver? They answered it Wednesday.

 It's Stefon Diggs .

 The Commanders signed him to a one-year deal worth up to $12 million Wednesday, filling a spot on the depth chart that had remained a topic of conversation since they started practicing again in the spring.

 

 Diggs will slide into the receiver spot opposite Terry McLaurin , giving quarterback Jayden Daniels another proven target. The sides had been talking for some time, so there had been mutual interest in getting a deal done with someone who grew up in Maryland -- and then played collegiately at Maryland -- as Diggs had.

 But this wasn't about a homecoming -- it was about getting another target for Daniels and the offense. Washington has changed coordinators, promoting David Blough after parting ways with Kliff Kingsbury, who had spent the past two seasons in Washington. The Commanders drafted wide receiver  Antonio Williams in the third round and have been pleased with his progress.

 However, another piece was needed, and Washington added him Wednesday.

 ESPN Commanders reporter John Keim and analytics writer Seth Walder break down what it means for Diggs and Washington, and grade the deal. 

 

 

 Why Diggs and not other WR options? 

 It was either Diggs or bust for Washington -- nobody used those words, but one team source said he was the only free agent they were interested in signing at this time.

 They had Deebo Samuel last season, but he's best used in the slot -- and they drafted someone for that role who excites them in Williams. So Samuel wasn't an option before he signed with San Francisco.

 Keenan Allen is also a free agent, but he averaged only 9.6 yards on 81 receptions, and only 7.4% of his catches were for 20 yards or more. That ranked 46th among receivers with at least 45 receptions last season -- and it happened to be the lowest of his career. In other words, they wanted someone who could add explosiveness, and Allen's game didn't offer that ability.

 Tyreek Hill suffered a dislocated left knee and tore multiple ligaments and said in a video posted on X that "I have no power in my left leg at all, so I'm trying to regain all the power back in my left leg."

 Another veteran, Brandin Cooks , has averaged 2.2 yards after the catch the past three seasons combined with only 17.3% of his catches in that span going for 20-plus yards.

 But Diggs has remained productive and can play inside and outside. He also averaged a career-best 2.77 yards per route run and 4.2 yards after the catch, his best total since 2019. He has surpassed 1,000 yards in the last seven seasons in which he played at least 10 games. And Patriots players and coaches praised his leadership last season en route to a Super Bowl appearance.

 Washington lost out on other possibilities in the offseason. It had wanted to sign Alec Pierce , but he opted to re-sign with Indianapolis before free agency; one league source said Pierce would have signed with the Commanders -- had he come free.

 They also tried, but failed, to sign Romeo Doubs . And Carnell Tate would have been an option had he been available with the seventh pick. In other words, they had kept searching for more at the position. -- Keim 

 

 What does this do for the Commanders' offense? 
Washington improved its receiver depth compared to a year ago, but that didn't mean it had built a strong, proven group. The Commanders had more viable players, but needed another option alongside McLaurin.
 

 This move might not transform the offense but it does make it better for sure. Diggs gives them an immediate boost as a second receiving target, someone who can play in the slot or the Z -- also known as flanker -- position. With New England last season, he ran 171 routes when aligned wide and 191 when in the slot.

 In 21 games last season, Diggs had five games with more than 100 yards, but those were the only games in which he topped 70. In his last five games, including the postseason, he managed 153 receiving yards.

 With the Patriots, Diggs was the primary target. He should benefit from not being the No. 1 option in Washington.

 Diggs just needs to be a solid target who can be productive -- and have a big game on occasion. Washington has McLaurin to provide explosiveness. 

 Diggs also will be the most accomplished receiver McLaurin has played with since arriving in Washington in 2019. No other receiver has surpassed 1,000 yards here in that time; and only Samuel, who played here last season, has ever surpassed that figure in his career. He did it once.

 The Commanders have been pleased with Williams, particularly on underneath routes. The Commanders also signed tight end Chig Okonkwo to provide more dynamic play as well.

 Diggs adds insurance, too, in case McLaurin has another year like 2025, when he missed seven games with a quad injury. -- Keim 

 

 Why did the Commanders wait so long to sign him? And does his delayed start hurt his chances to make an early impact? 

 There were multiple reasons. At one point, Brandon Aiyuk appeared to be a possibility -- Washington was just waiting for him to be released from the 49ers. The Commanders would have been interested, according to multiple team sources. But he has yet to be cut.

 So that likelihood diminished this summer, putting them more on a path to Diggs, who was always going to be the more expensive option.

 Also, with Diggs not in camp, others -- notably rookie Williams -- have gotten more reps -- and a better chance for Washington to see what it had in its receiving corps. Williams in particular will play a key role, and there are similarities in how he'd be used along with Diggs.

 It's also possible that Diggs wanted to see what other opportunities arose -- or the money just wasn't right. But he had made it known that he would like to play in Washington.

 Two years ago, Washington signed Noah Brown a week before the season began. In 12 games played, he caught 35 passes. Diggs is a far more accomplished receiver, but that season Brown had been in Houston's camp until being cut.

 But, Quinn said, "the veteran player will know how to practice, what to do." The key will be where he's at physically, but they won't know that until they have a chance to assess him.

 "Once you get that assessment, you can add more [for them]," Quinn said. -- Keim 

 

 

 Does this mean Brandon Aiyuk isn't going to Washington? 

 That possibility had diminished before this signing, in part because Aiyuk remains with the 49ers on the reserve/did not report list. He has yet to apply for reinstatement. The 49ers can keep him on this list when the season begins and he won't count against their salary cap.

 But Aiyuk also made a series of Instagram posts this summer, including some that targeted Daniels, with whom he had been close since playing together one season at Arizona State.

 As one team source said, "you never say never," but even if Diggs had not signed with Washington, the Commanders at best would be wary of bringing in Aiyuk.

 But the Commanders do have the cap space. If he's ever free, they could always meet with him and revisit the situation. Aiyuk hasn't played since October 2024, but he is only 28 and averaged 14.6 yards per catch in his first five seasons with 25 touchdowns -- and a 1,342-yard season three years ago.

 

 How would you grade the signing? 
 Grade: A-

 By signing Diggs, the Commanders filled one of the most glaring holes across the entire league. Prior to this acquisition, the team's second outside wide receiver options were essentially noncompetitive. Diggs changes that.

 At 32 years old, he isn't the player he once was, but he showed last season in New England that he can still be a productive part of an efficient offense.
